papers.abstract: We investigate holographic mutual information in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasma within the framework of gauge/gravity duality. Considering both parallel and perpendicular strip configurations, we analyze the effects of temperature, anisotropy, strip lengths, and separation distance on the correlation structure between subsystems. For strips with equal lengths, we show that increasing temperature suppresses mutual information and reduces the size of the correlated region in the phase diagram. We find that the parallel configuration exhibits a monotonic behavior. However, the perpendicular configuration displays a more complex behavior resulting from the competition between the effects of energy density and pressure. Similar qualitative features are observed for strips with unequal lengths. Our results suggest that the directional dependence of the energy density and pressure plays an important role in the behavior of mutual information and may explain the nontrivial directional effects observed in the phase structure.
papers.authors: Mehri Rahimi, Masoumeh Tavakoli, Behrouz Mirza

papers.title: The sharp uniqueness threshold for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on regular trees
papers.abstract: We study Gibbs uniqueness for the $q$-state antiferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite rooted $d$-ary tree and the infinite $(d+1)$-regular tree, where $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. An edge has weight $p\in[0,1]$ if its endpoints have the same color and weight $1$ otherwise. We prove that there is a unique Gibbs state if and only if $p\geqslant p_c:=\max\{0,1-q/(d+1)\}$, except when $(q,p)=(d+1,0)$, thus completes the uniqueness thresholds for all $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. Our proof use a convex potential for the tree recursion and show that it strictly decreases away from the uniform distribution. Together with the result of Gu, Wu and Yang, our theorem gives the exact critical power law whenever $p_c>0$.
papers.authors: Wei Wu, Yicheng Xu, Kuan Yang

papers.title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
papers.abstract: We study the scalar Schr\"odinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|\Omega_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|\Omega_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.
papers.authors: Humberto Belich Jr., Edilberto O. Silva

papers.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
papers.abstract: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.
papers.authors: Sebastian Garcia-Saenz, Yizhou Lu, S\'ebastien Renaux-Petel

papers.title: Emergent cloud patterns from stochastic jump models of parcel microphysics
papers.abstract: Warm clouds organize into bands, cells, and intricate wave networks, yet the dynamical mechanisms connecting these forms remain difficult to isolate. To bridge unresolved parcel microphysics and cloud organization, we formulate a spatial jump-process model of cloud-water and rain-water anomalies in an activated regime and analyze its mean-field closure. Eliminating fast supersaturation adjustment from droplet growth and vapor transport supplies a screened environmental kernel, which we couple to a cubic Stuart-Landau oscillatory law. Averaging over Poisson parcel episodes and closing third-order moments yields a pseudoparabolic Ginzburg--Landau equation (PGLE), whose mixed space--time derivative encodes dynamic inertia, slowing fine-scale relaxation. Unlike diffusive amplitude equations, the PGLE splits into a regularized nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian sector and a pseudoparabolic Allen--Cahn gradient sector governed by a conserved Noether charge, alongside an open-system liquid-water budget separating conversion from vapor exchange, fallout, and triad-driven domain-mean oscillations. Exact stability criteria show how dynamic inertia and amplitude-dependent frequency shifts (twist) control modulational loss of synchrony and resonant cross-carrier sideband gain above a critical twist threshold. Numerical integrations show that increasing twist transforms undulatus-like bands into defect-rich asperitas-like waves via defect proliferation, while subcritical competition consolidates cellular patterns into rolls. Even without twist, random anomalies evolve into a persistent cellular exclusion scale and actinoform-like spiral arms, while 1D wave breakup reorganizes into a two-frequency combination-tone spectrum. The jump model identifies omitted fluctuation moments for calibration against large-eddy simulations.
papers.authors: Micka\"el D. Chekroun, Ilan Koren, Honghu Liu

papers.title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
papers.abstract: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincar\'e-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.
papers.authors: Wanting Hou, Wei Liu, Hong-Chao Liu, Jun Xiong, Zhiyuan Ye

papers.title: Phase information and measurement in the Stochastic--Quantum correspondence
papers.abstract: The recently proposed stochastic-quantum correspondence establishes a connection between general stochastic processes and quantum dynamics, in which stochastic transition probabilities admit compatible representations on a Hilbert space, known as quantum lifts. We ask how the predictive information represented by off-diagonal degrees of freedom in the quantum lift is encoded within the stochastic description. We introduce the notion of a family of context-dependent stochastic processes and show that their continuation probabilities encode this predictive information. In particular, suitable continuations allow the intermediate lifted quantum state to be reconstructed entirely from system configuration probabilities. This perspective also clarifies the nature of quantum measurement: active continuations make basis-dependent quantum probabilities accessible as configuration probabilities, while a separate physical interaction records the realized configuration and introduces measurement disturbance. Although the rooted quantum probabilities alone do not guarantee that every stochastic realizer of the idealized recording interaction faithfully records the system's pre-measurement configuration, we show that at least one faithful stochastic realizer always exists.
papers.authors: Jason Doukas

papers.title: Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations
papers.abstract: Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an arbitrary TDI combination and compare the analytic and Monte Carlo numerical results for the optimal combinations A, E, and T. Finally, we analyze the responses of multiple types of TDI combinations, classify them into ordinary and {\zeta} types according to their low-frequency behavior, and give the low-frequency response expressions of the individual combinations. The results can be used to evaluate the sensitivity of space-based gravitational-wave missions such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin to the mass and coupling parameters of ultralight scalar-field dark matter.
papers.authors: Wenqiu Tang, Pan-Pan Wang, Yuezhe Chen, Rui Luo, Cheng-Gang Shao

papers.title: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count by low-energy subspace sampling
papers.abstract: On current digital quantum devices, standard one-qubit-per-variable encodings restrict quantum optimization algorithms to problem sizes where classical solvers typically excel. To avoid this constraint, we introduce Quantum Subspace Sampling Descent (QSSD), an iterative heuristic that decouples the number of problem variables from qubit count, while preserving knowledge of the problem's global structure. QSSD drives the energy descent using a fixed-angle Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm as a low-energy sampler. As the angles are precomputed, each iteration requires just a single circuit execution. We test QSSD on IBM Heron and Nighthawk quantum devices with up to 152 qubits on instances of higher-order unconstrained binary optimization and Max-cut problems. On the largest instance with 10000 variables, QSSD reaches an approximation ratio above 0.95 with 100 circuit executions. We provide both exact and heuristic classical baselines, namely greedy, branch-and-bound solver, and simulated annealing. While our approach still does not match the performance of the best classical baseline, it shows promise in a slower runtime scaling with problem size given a fixed budget. This suggests a regime of large problems where subspace sampling on quantum devices could become competitive, as we also demonstrate how improvements in hardware will lead to better algorithm performance. QSSD is thus a practical heuristic for combinatorial optimization problems that helps bring quantum optimization a step closer to utility.
papers.authors: Mateo Alonso, Gonzalo Bl\'azquez-Gil, Pablo D\'iez-Valle

papers.title: Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals from Higher Residue Pairings
papers.abstract: We develop a method for constructing differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from multivariate intersection numbers, without fibration. The large-$\varepsilon$ expansion of the intersection pairing, with $\varepsilon$ the dimensional regulator, is given by Saito's higher residue pairings, which localise at the critical points of a potential and admit closed multivariate formulae. In the Lee-Pomeransky representation, applying these formulae to Feynman integrals requires analytic regulators $\delta$ on the coordinate hyperplanes, and the physical limit $\delta \to 0$ is not manifest. Assuming that the regulated critical points are analytic in $\delta$, we show that, as $\delta \to 0$, they organise into sectors labelled by sets of pinched propagators. We derive closed formulae for the leading and first subleading higher residue pairings in this limit, written entirely in terms of unregulated sector data. These suffice to reconstruct differential systems at most linear in $\varepsilon$, including canonical ones, bypassing integration-by-parts identities. We apply the method to the massless planar four-point ladder families up to four loops and obtain their canonical differential equations, which are new at four loops.
papers.authors: Giacomo Brunello, Vsevolod Chestnov, Ben Page

papers.title: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation
papers.abstract: We present a trace distance estimator with optimal sample complexity. Specifically, the trace distance between two unknown $d$-dimensional quantum states can be estimated to within additive error $\varepsilon$ using \[ \Theta\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\left\{1,\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\right\}}\right) \] samples of each quantum state. This matches the lower bound of Wang (2026). The estimator combines tomography and polynomial approximation, with variance bounds from quantum Fourier analysis.
papers.authors: Ziyun Chen, Minbo Gao, Qisheng Wang

papers.title: On Lipschitz equicontinuity of random Schr\"odinger operators on lattices
papers.abstract: We consider random Schr\"odinger operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We prove that the density of states is uniformly bounded in the coupling strength for a dense set of single site probability distributions.
papers.authors: Jan Fischer, David Hasler

papers.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
papers.abstract: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.
papers.authors: Oxana Shaya, Zahra Baghali Khanian

papers.title: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and its control power
papers.abstract: We propose a controlled quantum teleportation protocol for an arbitrary unknown qutrit using a nonmaximally entangled channel, with Charlie holding a qubit and Alice and Bob each holding a four-level particle. With the aid of an auxiliary qubit, the receiver can recover the input state probabilistically with unit fidelity. We derive the overall success probability and show that it is independent of the input state. To quantify the controller's authority, we obtain analytical expressions for the optimal average teleportation fidelities with and without the controller's cooperation, keeping the sender's joint measurement fixed and averaging uniformly over pure qutrit input states with all measurement outcomes included. Their difference defines the control power of the protocol. For the shared states considered here, we determine a controller measurement basis that simultaneously maximizes the control power and the teleportation success probability for a given shared state. These results clarify the role of the controller's measurement in controlled teleportation with unequal local dimensions.
papers.authors: Xiao-Xu Li, Feng-Li Yan, Ting Gao

papers.title: The infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation
papers.abstract: In the extended Bloch representation (EBR) of quantum mechanics, the Born probabilities of a measurement with N outcomes are the relative volumes of N regions of a simplex-shaped abstract membrane, whose points represent the "hidden" measurement interactions. However, when N tends to infinity, the volumes vanish and the uniform membrane concentrates at the center of the unit ball. We show that this problem can be solved by renormalization: if the radius of the generalized Bloch ball grows like N, the distances of the measurement interactions from the facets of the simplex become independent exponential random variables. This is the only growth with a non-degenerate limit, and the limit membrane, which cannot live in the limit of the generalized Bloch space without privileging some of the outcomes, is the projective limit of the finite-dimensional membranes and, once renormalized, the only distribution compatible with the Born rule. For a pure point spectrum, the regions of the membrane become cones, the particle representing the state recedes to infinity, and the lines along which the membrane collapses become parallel. For a continuous spectrum, a further magnification yields a Poisson point process and the Born rule for probability densities. We also show that the uniform membrane is the only one compatible with the Born rule in finite dimension, and that the mechanism can be read, in every dimension, as a race between independent exponential clocks.
papers.authors: Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi

papers.title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors
papers.abstract: Trotter formulas approximate quantum dynamics by discrete steps, but errors in measured observables can be much smaller than worst-case estimates. We investigate how this suppression depends on the degree of randomness in the input states. We show that the mean absolute observable-error bound for state 2-designs can be exponentially smaller in qubit number than the tight bound for state 1-designs. To characterize this error transition from 1-design to 2-design, we use the excess frame potential to quantify the ensemble's second-moment distance. We quantify departures from these random-state statistics through the frame potential, a measure of pairwise state overlaps, and identify the accessible observables most sensitive to the resulting deviations in mean-square error. Extending the analysis to a Hamiltonian trajectory whose frame potential decays as $1/T$ before saturation, we also obtain a sufficient $p$th-order Trotter number $\mathcal O(T^{1+3/(4p)})$ for evolution time $T$. These findings connect input-state statistics to the visibility of Trotter errors, giving a theoretical guarantee and foundation for practical quantum simulation.
papers.authors: Yue Cao (QICI Quantum Information and Computation Initiative, School of Computing and Data Science, The University of Hong Kong, Pokfulam Road, Hong Kong SAR, China), Tianfeng Feng (QICI Quantum Information and Computation Initiative, School of Computing and Data Science, The University of Hong Kong, Pokfulam Road, Hong Kong SAR, China), Jonathan Allcock (Tencent Quantum Laboratory, Shenzhen, China), Chenfeng Cao (HK Institute of Quantum Science and Technology, The University of Hong Kong, Pokfulam Road, Hong Kong SAR, China), Qi Zhao (QICI Quantum Information and Computation Initiative, School of Computing and Data Science, The University of Hong Kong, Pokfulam Road, Hong Kong SAR, China)

papers.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
papers.abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.
papers.authors: Gefei Cai, Shengzhi Jin, Xin Sun, Baojun Wu

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.
papers.authors: Rafael Rocha de Farias

papers.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
papers.abstract: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.
papers.authors: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya

papers.title: Classifying exact local-equilibrium solutions of the Boltzmann equation
papers.abstract: We provide a complete classification, in a \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, of all hydrodynamic states and external forces for which a local equilibrium distribution constitutes an exact solution to the Boltzmann kinetic equation. We demonstrate that the temperature \(T\) must be spatially uniform, that the velocity field is the sum of a rigid translation, a radial expansion or compression, and a rigid rotation, and that the external acceleration must be conservative, though time-dependent within a reference frame that translates and rotates along with the fluid. The density profile is then determined by the external potential, while its temporal dependence is governed by any temperature function \(T(t)\) that can be generated through an appropriate adjustment of the external acceleration. We recover the classic ``harmonic breather'' and obtain solutions involving static forces that exhibit algebraic cooling, similar to Haff's law, despite the occurrence of elastic collisions. Our classification identifies the exceptional circumstances under which local equilibrium is exact and provides rigorous criteria for evaluating kinetic and hydrodynamic approximations.
papers.authors: Nagi Khalil, Jorge Bravo-Gadea

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
papers.abstract: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $\Lambda$-deuteron and $\Lambda$-$\alpha$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.
papers.authors: Sumit Choudhary, Tarunpreet Kaur, Harjeet Kaur, Harpreet Singh

papers.title: Reflection positivity of discrete and Brownian loop-soup occupation fields
papers.abstract: The intensities guaranteeing reflection positivity of loop-soup vertex occupations on every reflection-symmetric finite graph with positive semidefinite cross-conductance matrix of rank $r$ form the real Wallach set $\W_r$. For the renormalized occupation field on the massless planar Dirichlet strip, the exact set is $\bigcap_{r\geq1}\W_r=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$.
papers.authors: Yves Le Jan

papers.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
papers.abstract: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. The analysis of continuous wave EPR measurements revealed a spin concentration of $c_{\mathrm{V1}}=1.47\pm0.3\times10^{14}$, $c_{\mathrm{V2}}=5.6\pm1.12\times10^{13}$ and $c_{\mathrm{X}}=1.03\pm0.21\times10^{13}$ spins/cm$^{3}$. Additionally, electron spin coherence $T_2$ and relaxation times $T_1$ have been measured on the central and on the satellite spectral lines, resulting in longer $T_1$ and $T_2$ for the satellite transition, compared to the central one, with maximum values of $42.8\pm1.3$~ms and $0.708\pm0.004$~ms respectively at $T=80$~K. We reveal, that decoherence is mainly caused by nuclear and electron spin diffusion.
papers.authors: Irene Don\`a, Michele Segantini, Gianluca Marcozzi, Nguyen Tien Son, Takeshi Ohshima, Ha Duong Ngo, Boris Naydenov

papers.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
papers.abstract: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.
papers.authors: Matteo Bruno, Simone Speziale

papers.title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.
papers.authors: Soumen Pari

papers.title: Romans Mass from a $\mathrm{GL}(1,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.abstract: We construct an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary whose edge modes are the dilaton and form fields of type IIA supergravity, including the Romans mass. The bulk action is the Chern--Simons functional of the superalgebra of the doubled formalism, completed by two brackets that are invisible in ten dimensions; it is unique up to normalization, contains no potentials, and the metric enters only through a boundary term. The Romans mass is the boundary value of a zero-form, like the other field strengths: it is varied, and its equation of motion is an eleven-form Gauss law with no ten-dimensional counterpart. The boundary term breaks the $GL(1,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $O(1)$: the dilaton is the edge mode on $GL(1,\mathbb{R})/O(1)$, and $(-1)^{F_L}$, which reverses the Romans mass, becomes a gauge symmetry. The holonomies of the flat connection are monodromies of the dilaton and of $(-1)^{F_L}$, fixed classically by the D8-brane charges when the mass is nonzero, and the hypersurface dual to the $O(1)$ holonomy can end on reflection seven-branes. Since no field is self-dual, the reduction gives Romans' action off shell, while other boundary conditions of the same bulk give massless type IIA and dual formulations.
papers.authors: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal

papers.title: Holographic Spread Complexity of a Probe Particle with General Initial Data
papers.abstract: We investigate the holographic spread complexity of a massive particle probing global AdS$_3$ with general initial data. By constructing an adapted Hamiltonian, we map each bulk geodesic to a boundary Krylov dynamical pair, whose dynamics are governed solely by the conserved chiral charges. We find that, for generic initial data, the original identification $\dot{C}\sim p_\rho$ fails; instead, both the complexity and its growth rate depend nonlinearly on the bulk Noether charges. We systematically analyze this nonlinear encoding via several perturbative expansions. We further investigate two refined variants: the symmetry-resolved spread complexity, which restores the bulk radial $\pi$-periodicity, and the chiral spread complexity, which admits an exact closed form approaching the standard complexity at small angular momentum. Finally, by directly quantizing an effective AdS$_2$ theory, we obtain a new holographic interpretation of spread complexity in terms of the lapse function.
papers.authors: Zekun Qian, Zhehan Li, Jia Tian

papers.title: Noncommutative $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed beta functions of first and second kind : beta gamma relations, shift identities and symmetrisation
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of the beta functions attached to the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba, for structure functions whose deformed numbers are generated by two deformation functions $\phi_{1}>\phi_{2}>0$. Working with the Jackson type series representation of the deformed integral, we define a first kind beta function on $[0,1]$ from the deformed power $(1\ominus\phi_{2}t)^{y-1}$, extended to complex exponents, and a second kind beta function on the half line from $(1\oplus\phi_{1}t)^{-x-y}$. The first kind function equals $\phi_{1}^{(y-1)(2x+y-2)/2}\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x)\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(y)/\Gamma_{\mathcal{R}(p,q)}(x+y)$ for all complex arguments with positive real parts; we derive its general shift identity, its exchange defect $\phi_{1}^{(y-x)(x+y-1)/2}$, a commutative symmetrisation unique up to a constant, its asymptotics and a deformed Euler integral for a deformed Gauss hypergeometric function, which yields a deformed Gauss summation. The second kind function is evaluated through Ramanujan's ${}_{1}\psi_{1}$ summation and involves a second deformed gamma function, differing from the first one by a one periodic theta quotient, so that its exchange defect persists in the one parameter case. We prove a Bohr Mollerup type characterisation and a multiplication formula for the deformed gamma function, show that it is logarithmically convex on the positive half line if and only if $\phi_{1}\geq1$, obtain the joint logarithmic convexity of normalised beta functions with a deformed Tur\'an identity, and compute the moments of the associated deformed beta distributions. Gauge invariance covers the Jagannathan Srinivasa Rao, Chakrabarti Jagannathan, generalized $q-$Quesne and Hounkonnou Ngompe deformations, and every identity is confirmed numerically to thirty digits.
papers.authors: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba

papers.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
papers.abstract: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance? We determine the optimal second-order coding rates for input dimension $d\ge2$, erasure probability $0<p<1/2$, and fixed infidelity (one minus fidelity) $0<\varepsilon<1$. For $n$ channel uses, the optimal base-two logarithmic code size is \begin{equation}\tag{A}\label{eq:abstract-rate} n(1-2p)\log_2d +2\sqrt{np(1-p)}\log_2d\,\Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon) +O((\ln n)^2), \end{equation} where $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $\Phi^{-1}$ is its quantile function. The square-root term is the second-order correction. This formula holds for entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication. Quantum error measures failure to preserve entanglement. Private error compares the actual output with a correctly decoded uniform message independent of an optimized environment state. The achievable Gaussian term and a matching quantum expansion below infidelity one half were established recently. We prove matching upper bounds for every fixed infidelity, including private communication, with the displayed remainder. The proof bounds one code's average performance across all loss patterns of a given size; binomial fluctuations then determine the Gaussian correction. It combines tests of correct and secret communication with tensor-product averaging and a classical polynomial identity. Arbitrary mixed encoders and collective decoders are allowed. Requiring the private error bound for every message preserves the Gaussian term. Fixing the ideal environment state to the actual marginal instead changes the quantile to $\Phi^{-1}(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon})$. Thus the precise privacy criterion affects communication at second order.
papers.authors: Mark M. Wilde

papers.title: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits
papers.abstract: Preparing thermal states on noisy quantum hardware requires circuits that remain shallow at low temperatures. Even when accurate classical state representations are available, compiling them into suitable circuits can be costly. We introduce PP-VarQITE, combining Pauli propagation with variational quantum imaginary-time evolution to determine circuit parameters entirely classically, with target temperatures encoded in the angles of a fixed circuit architecture. In numerical studies of Ising and frustrated Heisenberg models, we recover low-temperature energies and correlations using up to 100 qubits. Across the frustrated chain and two-dimensional lattice, our circuits are approximately two to ten times shallower than the lowest-depth circuits from sequential tensor-network compilation. These shallow circuits enable us to prepare a 48-site frustrated chain and a $7\times7$ Ising lattice using 96 and 98 qubits on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum processor. We reproduce the development of dimer order and lattice-wide correlations from high to low temperatures, with the lattice circuits requiring at most 42 two-qubit layers. Through classical circuit design, we demonstrate low-temperature state preparation at circuit sizes beyond the practical reach of statevector simulation.
papers.authors: Cenk T\"uys\"uz, Simon Deconihout, Enrico Rinaldi, Michele Grossi

papers.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.
papers.authors: Leila Shahkarami

papers.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
papers.abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.
papers.authors: Miguel A. L. Marques, Irene D'Amico, Stefano Pittalis

papers.title: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Quantum coherence and quantum correlations are two fundamental features of quantum systems and are closely related in various quantum information tasks. In general, due to the existence of correlations, the amount of coherence in a bipartite state should be no less than that in the reduced states. We focus on what types of states have an equal amount of coherence in the global state and the local states. For such states, the basis-dependent correlations (the difference between the coherence of a bipartite state and its reduced state with respect to a set of standard orthogonal local bases) vanish. Based on the Tsallis relative entropy coherence measure, we prove that block-diagonal product states exhibit vanishing basis-dependent correlations. Furthermore, we establish an equivalence between the absence of basis-dependent correlations and the block-diagonal product structure in a special case. We then consider the coherence measure based on quantum Fisher information and show that block?diagonal product states again lead to vanishing basis-dependent correlations, while in the two-qubit case the vanishing condition constrains the state to a broader block-diagonal-like product structure. These results provide a structural characterization of bipartite states with vanishing basis-dependent correlations under different coherence measures.
papers.authors: Zi-Han Chen, Hui Zhao, Shao-Ming Fei, Zhi-Xi Wang, Mei-Ming Zhang

papers.title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
papers.abstract: In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model. The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$. Concentration of the matrix extent along a fixed number of principal directions fewer than nine at large $N$ requires the total extent relative to a corresponding reference scale to diverge in probability. It also requires relative noncommutativity to be suppressed more strongly than the inverse of $N$, in every fixed finite moment of order at least one. These bounds apply to the full quantum wave function, including off-diagonal matrix degrees of freedom, and constrain the quantum structure of D0-brane bound states and the possible large-$N$ matrix geometries in Matrix theory.
papers.authors: Tetsuyuki Muramatsu

papers.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
papers.abstract: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites. For bosonic atoms, we further show how the tautochrone dynamics is shaped by lattice inhomogeneity, phase-space structure, and on-site interactions.
papers.authors: Georgios K. Simopoulos, Georgios E. Pavlou, Ioannis Kiorpelidis, Georgios A. Siviloglou, Konstantinos G. Makris

papers.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
papers.abstract: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(\alpha\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(\alpha\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.
papers.authors: Sudipta Sahu, Rathan Samala

papers.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
papers.abstract: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.
papers.authors: Andrea Pelissetto, Davide Rossini, Ettore Vicari

papers.title: Exact Mass Multipoles of Distorted Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the Weyl-distorted Schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. Starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. For a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $\beta$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $\alpha_{2}$. We use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. Leading-order approximations in $\alpha_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $\alpha_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. A simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. As a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $\alpha_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. Finally, truncating the series in $\beta$ at its first $\beta$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|\beta|,|\alpha_{2}| \leq 1/8$.
papers.authors: Brennen Black

papers.title: Relaxation dynamics of the impurity momentum in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
papers.abstract: We consider a single mobile impurity coupled by a repulsive contact interaction to a gas of free spinless fermions of equal mass in one dimension. Using the determinant overlaps between the interacting eigenstates and free-fermion states, we derive closed determinant formulas for the matrix elements of the impurity momentum operator and of its square between arbitrary Bethe-ansatz eigenstates of a finite system. At infinite coupling we prove a selection rule: both operators have vanishing matrix elements between distinct eigenstates that share the same rapidity, and every eigenstate carries the per-particle share of the total momentum. For an impurity injected into the Fermi sea we have the following: at infinite coupling the average impurity momentum relaxes completely in the thermodynamic limit, while at finite coupling relaxation remains incomplete. The closed-form matrix elements turn the spectral representation of the average impurity momentum into explicit finite sums over eigenstates. We evaluate the post-injection dynamics, resolve the quantum-flutter oscillations and the approach towards the diagonal-ensemble value, and map the stationary momentum as a function of the injection momentum and the coupling. Finally, we analyse the thermodynamic limit and its asymptotics as an integral over Fredholm determinants.
papers.authors: Felipe Taha Sant'Ana

papers.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
papers.abstract: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron. In this work we recast the neuron from a measurement-based circuit to a differentiable computational unit. This neuron is benchmarked against other classical, spiking, and quantum models on an LHC di-jet latent space. We show that under noise perturbations the QLIF network retains $0.95$ of its clean accuracy, while accuracy retention for twelve classical models falls to $0.74$-$0.85$. The QLIF anomaly scores respond $3.5$-fold less to the noise perturbation than any of the control model's scores. We compare against a periodic classical control that reproduces the QLIF effect, isolating it to the $\sin^2$ membrane map. This membrane map is a native regulariser that decouples robustness from model capacity supplied by the qubit state space. We demonstrate this through several benchmarks and ablation studies to characterise the performance landscape of the quantum-neuromorphic model space.
papers.authors: Dean Brand, Donovan Slabbert, Chanelle Matadah Manfouo, Francesco Petruccione

papers.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
papers.abstract: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, reversing a target coupling leaves the single-site energy slopes at uniform occupation unchanged, yet a collective mode of the residual interactions switches the favored diagonals from aligned to opposed. On 32 held-out twelve-site targets, the simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots averages 69.82\% with residual detunings and 24.31\% with a tuned uniform pulse. By scoring the pooled samples under the original objective, we can use these native layouts to search for ground states of a Hamiltonian that none implements alone.
papers.authors: Zecheng Shen

papers.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
papers.abstract: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). At a high level, we modify the protocol such that the receiver proves that they are following honestly some crucial steps of the protocols, without revealing extra information to the sender. This yields a tighter security bound against a malicious receiver. For practical scenarios with a fixed security target, this approach reduces the amount of required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude, depending on the specific parameters. Furthermore, the benefits of our approach become particularly pronounced at higher qubit error rates, and our proposal even extends the maximum tolerable error rate of the quantum channel from approximately 3.5% to about 9%. The ZKP, however, introduces a substantial computational overhead, estimated to significantly exceed the acquisition time of the protocol, which is usually the primary bottleneck. To address this limitation, we also introduce a variant that serves as a tunable trade-off between the protocol with and without our modification. This enables precise adjustment of the computational overhead while still retaining significant, albeit moderately reduced, efficiency gains.
papers.authors: Alex Bredariol Grilo, Lucas Hanouz, Anne Marin

papers.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.
papers.authors: Erkka Haapasalo, Pekka Lahti, Juha-Pekka Pellonp\"a\"a

papers.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
papers.abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.
papers.authors: Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Fedor \v{S}imkovic IV, Prachi Sharma, Carlos L. Benavides-Riveros, Werner Dobrautz

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
papers.abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.
papers.authors: Zhi-Rong Deng, Jie Yang

papers.title: Compressional-shear wave interference and wave suppression at exceptional-point gaps
papers.abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) in complex elastic materials signify the coalescence of compressional and shear modes and bound a frequency gap where waves become evanescent. While their effects on wave propagation have been extensively studied, the physical mechanisms underlying their existence remain elusive. In this Letter, employing a transfer matrix formulation combined with Bloch's theorem, we demonstrate that the gaps bounded by EPs in layered media originate from destructive interference between the compressional and shear wave fields. We further reveal that the corresponding wavenumbers satisfy a Bragg-like condition with the unit cell thickness, causing the total wave field to become stationary, forming a standing wave. Finally, a finite layered medium is considered, where this mechanism is shown to manifest as forbidden wave propagation for both modes in the gap. These results provide a direct physical interpretation of EPs.
papers.authors: Gabriel N\'u\~nez, William J. Parnell, Rapha\"el C. Assier

papers.title: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics
papers.abstract: The generation of optical higher-order sidebands, which produces new frequencies with regular spectral separation, holds significant promise for applications in optical communication and quantum metrology. We investigate second-order sideband generation and tunable slow-fast light effects in a parity-time (PT)-symmetric cavity optomechanics and propose an enhanced magnetometer scheme. We demonstrate that the PT-symmetric structure, an external magnetic field, and the photon tunneling strength provide powerful and flexible control over both the second-order sideband efficiency, as well as the broadening and switching of slow-fast light propagation. Operating in the PT-symmetry-protected phases, our magnetometer based on the second-order sideband achieves a theoretical sensitivity at the picotesla level, surpassing the performance of previous optomechanical approaches. Our results offer new strategies for magnetic field sensing and optical transmission control, paving the way toward applications in quantum sensing and optical information storage.
papers.authors: Yuguo Su, Tianshun Tan, Yiying Yan, Hengyan Wang, Elijah Omollo Ayieta, Szabolcs Kelemen, Slobodan Radosevic, JunYan Luo, Yi-Xiao Huang, Xingyu Zhang

papers.title: The polarization bundle of a bending ray: nested projections and helicity Chern numbers
papers.abstract: We consider a ray propagating in a weakly anisotropic, possibly absorbing medium. The transverse planes of the propagation directions form a rank-two complex vector bundle $E_\perp$ over the sphere $S^2$ of directions. The polarization states are the points of $Z=\mathbb{CP}(E_\perp)$. Projecting the flat derivative of $\mathbb{C}^3$ onto $E_\perp$ gives a connection $D$, the complexified Levi-Civita connection of $S^2$, whose holonomy is the Rytov rotation. Projecting $D$ onto a polarization line gives the connection of the tautological line bundle over $Z$, whose holonomy is the Pancharatnam--Berry phase. For the horizontal distribution defined by $D$, the curvature of this bundle is $i\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the vertical part, $i s_3\,\omega$ on the horizontal part, and zero on the mixed part. Here $\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the Fubini--Study form, $\omega$ the area form of $S^2$, and $s_3$ the circular Stokes parameter. The Rytov rotation, the Pancharatnam--Berry phase and the Chern numbers $c_1(L_\pm)=\mp 2$ are all obtained from this curvature. Restricted to the helicity sections, it gives the obstruction to a globally smooth circular Jones vector, although the circular polarization states are globally defined.
papers.authors: Didier Felbacq, Emmanuel Rousseau

papers.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.
papers.authors: Alan Zhang, Ye Zhou

papers.title: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems
papers.abstract: The transfer tensor method (TTM) extrapolates open quantum system dynamics from short-time trajectories by encoding memory effects in a discrete hierarchy of transfer tensors. Standard TTM relies on time-translational invariance (TTI) of the dynamical maps, which is broken by time-dependent driving or coherent control. We generalize TTM to time-inhomogeneous and periodically driven systems with a two-time transfer tensor hierarchy $\mathcal{T}(n,k)$. For driving with period $t_0$, sub-stroboscopic sampling ($\Delta t = t_0/N_c$) restores a block TTI, $\mathcal{T}(n+mN_c, k+mN_c) = \mathcal{T}(n,k)$, so that only $N_c$ starting-time branches must be learned. Averaging over the driving phase (or start time), termed temporal homogenization, restores single-index TTI at the price of phase-induced memory that combines non-additively with that of static disorder. We study two systems. (i) In an inhomogeneously broadened two-level ensemble driven beyond the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), the phase-induced memory scales with the square of the Rabi coupling and the disorder-induced memory with the square of the inhomogeneous width. The phase-induced memory is frame dependent: in the drive's rotating frame it arises solely from counter-rotating terms and vanishes under the RWA, whereas in the lab frame it largely survives the RWA. (ii) In a driven tight-binding chain at the Dunlap--Kenkre condition, the clean chain is stroboscopically frozen, whereas sub-stroboscopic tensors show that dynamical localization is enforced by delayed, period-commensurate refocusing in the memory kernel, in contrast to the immediate backflow of Anderson localization. A generalized outgoing pseudoflux tracks the non-monotonic dependence of the spreading on disorder: moderate disorder breaks the refocusing and lets the particle spread over a larger but finite region, whereas strong disorder confines it.
papers.authors: Ferdos Fessahaye, Rajesh Dutta, Michelle Anderson, Chern Chuang

papers.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
papers.abstract: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input. First, for every $\epsilon\in(0,1/4)$, $\mathsf{AND}_n/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree $O(\log(n/\epsilon))$, improving the previous $O(\log^2(n/\epsilon))$. This is optimal up to constant factors for inverse-polynomial error, by a lower bound of Krishan and Vishwanathan, and refutes two superlogarithmic-degree conjectures of Krishan and Sarma. Second, for every Boolean function $g$ computed by a depth-$d$, size-$s$ $\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ circuit, $g/2$ has an $\epsilon$-approximating torus polynomial of degree at most $C_m^d(\log s)^{\max\{1,\mu-1\}d}\log(1/\epsilon)$, where $\mu$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $m$ and $C_m$ depends only on $m$. This improves the bound $(\log s)^{O_m(d^2)}(\log(1/\epsilon))^{O_m(d)}$ of Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao, making the exponent of $\log s$ linear in the depth and the dependence on $\log(1/\epsilon)$ linear. Both proofs sample terms of a Fourier expansion and approximate them by low-degree torus polynomials. A torus approximation of degree $D$ can be written as a linear combination of at most $(n+1)^D$ parities, called a periodic Fourier representation, which is known to give a non-adaptive measurement-based quantum computation with linear side-processing using one qubit per parity. Hence every $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ function can be computed with quasipolynomially many qubits and inverse-polynomial error probability on every input. Conversely, we prove that a periodic Fourier representation with $r$ parities and error probability $\epsilon$ gives a torus approximation of degree $O(\log(r/\epsilon))$, so the two notions are equivalent.
papers.authors: Shuhei Osaki, Ryuhei Mori

papers.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
papers.abstract: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
papers.authors: Yiming Pan, Jiapeng Yang, Hao Geng

papers.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
papers.abstract: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function. At genus one the closed free energy follows from the pencil as a sum of logarithms of critical-value velocities. The two theories differ through the origin of the curve, which the D theory counts as two canonical directions, and through the pairing of every point with its reflection. We follow the origin contribution through the free energies to genus three, the one-holed torus and the torus one-point amplitudes, and in the primary range the latter reproduce the formulas conjectured from worldsheet numerics for both series.
papers.authors: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar

papers.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
papers.abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.
papers.authors: Oleksandr A. Voloshyn, Mykola I. Serov, Olena O. Vaneeva

papers.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
papers.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $\beta_f^-(q)=\beta_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-\nu_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $\nu_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.
papers.authors: Fumihiko Nakano, Xu Xia

papers.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.
papers.authors: Jae-Hyun Baek, Byung-Sun Won, Jon-Lark Kim

papers.title: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
papers.abstract: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $\rho_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_\rho$ ebits per pair. We show that this cost is robust under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. For every $R>S(A|B)_\rho$, a single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on $\rho_{AB}$ and $R$, merges every weakly almost i.i.d. source along $\rho_{AB}$ with vanishing error. The net entanglement cost is at most $nR$ ebits for all sufficiently large blocklengths $n$. This guarantee also covers the Wasserstein and Mazzola--Sutter--Renner subclasses. Each class contains the exact i.i.d. source, so $S(A|B)_\rho$ is optimal for universal merging within each class. More generally, the same protocols achieve vanishing error whenever the two-pair marginal of the permutation-averaged source converges in trace norm to $\rho_{AB}^{\otimes 2}$.
papers.authors: Nilanjana Datta

papers.title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
papers.abstract: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively. Analytic limits and numerical results instead support a candidate square-root correction based on L-entropy, which vanishes in the holographic complete-leg prescription considered here. We discuss the possibility of a common multipartite information bound in general conformal junctions.
papers.authors: Yan Liu, You-Jie Zeng

papers.title: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
