papers.title: Efficiency enhancement in a two-detector Unruh quantum Otto engine
papers.abstract: We investigate efficiency enhancement in an Unruh quantum Otto engine (UQOE) consisting of two initially uncorrelated Unruh-DeWitt (UDW) detectors. The detectors undergo uniform acceleration with different magnitudes and couple locally to a massless scalar field prepared in the Minkowski vacuum. We choose a diagonal free Hamiltonian for the UQOE and define its work and heat with respect to the proper time of one of the detectors. Consequently, the coherence terms generated through the interaction with the scalar field do not directly contribute to the work and heat of the UQOE. Instead, the efficiency enhancement arises from the relative proper-time weighting of the detectors' local population changes. We identify operating points that satisfy the conditions of initial-state passivity, cycle closure, and energy conservation. The efficiency is higher than that of a conventional UQOE, and the state of the UQOE after the heat absorption stage is separable. We further investigate the influence of detector separation on cycle closure and efficiency. Although the local population responses are independent of separation at fixed control parameters, the nonlocal coherence terms depend on separation and impose additional constraints on state cycle closure. Restoring closure generally requires retuning the cycle parameters, which can indirectly modify the achievable efficiency enhancement. Our results demonstrate that, within the second-order perturbative framework and the adopted energy convention, entanglement generation is not necessary for efficiency enhancement. They also clarify the distinct roles of local population changes and nonlocal coherences in the thermodynamic operation of a two-detector UQOE.
papers.authors: Yongjie Pan, Baocheng Zhang, Qingyu Cai

papers.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
papers.abstract: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. We answer this question systematically through a Go theorem and a no-go theorem. The Go theorem answers it affirmatively: we construct an explicit model in which coupling a system to a zero-temperature Gibbs environment via a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, with only short-range Hamiltonians, activates a time crystal in a stationary state that shows none in isolation. This coupling reproduces a Lindblad master equation satisfying three conditions---time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, time-translation covariance, and detailed balance---that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. The no-go theorem shows that, for every Lindblad master equation satisfying these conditions and every stationary state, dissipation can never contribute to activation; only an environment-induced Hamiltonian term can. Indeed, the periodic two-time correlation function of any such time crystal coincides with that of the isolated system with the open-system Hamiltonian, the sum of the bare isolated Hamiltonian and the environment-induced Hamiltonian, in the thermodynamic limit. These results reveal both the possibility and the origin of time crystals in open systems without external resource supply.
papers.authors: Yuri Ogami, Hiroyasu Tajima

papers.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
papers.abstract: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
papers.authors: Matheus G. Barbosa

papers.title: Large particle number asymptotics for point-interacting bosons in the plane
papers.abstract: We consider $N$ bosons in two dimensions interacting via point interactions, modeled by the TMS Hamiltonian. We prove that their ground state energy has the asymptotic behavior $-e^{C N }$ for large $N$, for an explicit constant $C$ related to the sharp constant in the Ladyzhenskaya-Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Such asymptotic behavior was predicted in the physics literature, based on a variant of the mean-field approximation.
papers.authors: Rupert L. Frank, Robert Seiringer

papers.title: $\Phi$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $\Phi$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $\Phi$-Stages, each augmented by a $\Phi$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $\Phi$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $\rho>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $\rho\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)
papers.authors: Ioannis Tsioulis, Anastasios Tefas, Nikolaos Stergioulas

papers.title: Reflective algebras over factorizable Hopf algebras
papers.abstract: The reflective algebra $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$, introduced by Laugwitz, Walton and Yakimov, is a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra constructed from a quasitriangular Hopf algebra $(H,R)$ and a left $H$-comodule algebra $A$. We study the structure and factorizability of finite-dimensional reflective algebras. When $(H,R)$ is factorizable, we show that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is isomorphic, as a quasitriangular left $H$-comodule algebra, to $A\otimes H$ equipped with the trivial left $H$-coaction on $A$ and the universal $K$-matrix induced by $R_{21}R$. In this case, we also classify all universal $K$-matrices on $R_H(A)$. Finally, we prove that $(R_H(A),K_{\mathrm{ref}}(A))$ is factorizable if and only if $(H,R)$ is factorizable and $A$ is simple as an algebra.
papers.authors: Rei Sugitani

papers.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
papers.abstract: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $\phi$ such that no primary lighter than $\phi$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssim\Delta_\phi\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $\Delta_\phi$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $\Delta_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $\Delta_\phi$ has two sharp minima near $\Delta_\phi=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.
papers.authors: Yu Nakayama

papers.title: Two-scale band geometry and ballistic transport for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with bounded limit-periodic potentials. If the nested periodic approximants satisfy $\|V-V_n\|_\infty=o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, with $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, then the rescaled Heisenberg position has a nonzero strong limit on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. In contrast to earlier continuum results requiring exponential accuracy in $p_{n+1}$, the exponential weight here involves only $p_n$; the ratios $p_{n+1}/p_n$ may be unbounded. Folding identifies each ordered large-cell band, away from symmetry momenta, with a fixed translated small-cell band. This confines near-collisions of all bands to a common neighborhood controlled at the smaller period. A period-uniform quadratic-form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a graph-norm comparison linear in the potential error then give the limiting velocity. Moments of orders $0<r\le4$ have two-sided ballistic growth as a corollary. An explicit example separates the two approximation conditions.
papers.authors: Moises Gomez Solis

papers.title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: Many questions about interacting quantum systems ask which member of a Hamiltonian family $H(\mathbf{q})$ has the lowest ground-state energy, rather than for the ground state of one Hamiltonian. A pointwise scan answers this with one many-body solve per candidate. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) instead holds all $N_q$ candidates in a coherent register and searches them with a ground-energy threshold oracle, replacing $N_q$ solves by $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ coherent oracle calls. We identify static-field (Hubbard-Stratonovich) families as a broad class in which this minimum is a rigorous variational bound that the parent ground state does not reveal, and we make the oracle robust to imperfect ground-state preparation by fixed-point amplitude amplification. The measured search constant places the crossover against a pointwise quantum scan at $N_q \approx 220\xi^2$, where $\xi$ is the overhead of a coherent call. We test the search on realistic sd-shell (USDB) static quadrupole landscapes with up to $10^6$ grid points and on a Hubbard ring with competing orders. It pays where competing minima trap local descent, needing about four times fewer energy queries than multistart descent for oblate-prolate coexistence in $^{28}$Si, and not on smooth single-well landscapes. Circuit-level simulations validate the complete pipeline on a schematic model. The gain concerns the number of energy queries; any advantage of the quantum solver itself is separate.
papers.authors: Abhishek, P. Arumugam

papers.title: Enhanced SiV-phonon coupling in dissipation-diluted diamond nanomechanics
papers.abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.
papers.authors: Guanhao Huang, Amberly Xie, Chang Jin, Evelyn Hu, Marko Lon\v{c}ar

papers.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding
papers.abstract: What is the intrinsic reason of emergence of macroscopic order parameter out of microscopic systems? In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. We present three examples of classical spin systems: two-dimensional ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a two-dimensional spin model with competing stripe orders, and the fully connected Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model. In all of these examples, proper macroscopic order parameters including the replica overlap emerge automatically through communication informatics of CPC, only from observed spin configurations. We call the learned macroscopic coordinate the collective predictive order. Furthermore, for the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, the equilibrium distribution of the collective predictive order yields an emergent potential with the symmetry and thermal evolution characteristic of a Landau potential. Notably, the emergence of the collective predictive order does not refer to any structure of microscopic Hamiltonians/Lagrangians. Thus our ``Atom-as-an-Agent" (AaaA) principle offers a completely data-driven method for the emergence of macroscopic order, that is, machine learning physics.
papers.authors: Koji Hashimoto, Tadahiro Taniguchi

papers.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
papers.abstract: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.
papers.authors: Yulia A. Ageeva, Andrey K. Sharofeev

papers.title: Geodesic Efficiency of Counterdiabatic Charging in a Quantum Battery
papers.abstract: We investigate an open quantum battery consisting of a resonator acting as the energy-storage unit, a frequency-tunable two-level system acting as a controllable mediator, and an external coherent drive serving as the energy source. In the dispersive regime, the dynamics reduce to those of a driven harmonic oscillator with a tunable effective coupling. Starting from the vacuum state, the resonator remains in a coherent state under a Lindblad master equation describing photon leakage at zero temperature. We derive a counterdiabatic (CD) driving protocol that compensates for dynamical lag and ensures that the system follows the prescribed reference trajectory. As a result, the energy stored in the resonator increases monotonically without transient oscillations, allowing the battery to reach the target ergotropy at the prescribed final time $t_f$. The CD trajectory follows a geodesic in the coherent-state phase space and achieves near-unity geodesic efficiency over a broad range of pulse durations, whereas unassisted charging exhibits markedly lower efficiencies. Finally, we show that the CD protocol saturates the quantum speed limit for the charging process.
papers.authors: F. Ahmadi, S. Salimi

papers.title: Graviphoton mixing with KK modes in the 2D effective theory of charged black holes
papers.abstract: We study the effects of massive Kaluza--Klein modes on the two-dimensional low-energy effective theory obtained by the $S^2$ reduction of four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory on a Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole background. We retain the first excited ($l=1$) Maxwell Kaluza--Klein modes in addition to the massless sector. The background electric flux mixes the Maxwell Kaluza--Klein scalars with the graviphotons, and tree-level exchange of the massive scalars generates a correction to the graviphoton kinetic term proportional to the square of the black hole charge. Within the leading local approximation, we also perturbatively evaluate the one-loop correction to the graviphoton kinetic term and find no dependence on the black hole charge. We find that near extremality, the charge-dependent tree-level correction becomes parametrically comparable to the classical graviphoton kinetic term.
papers.authors: Yoshihiko Abe, Tetsutaro Higaki, Yu Miyauchi

papers.title: Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Switch Networks: Memory Limits and Achievability
papers.abstract: We study the minimum persistent memory required to distribute a graph state through a quantum switch. Specifically, consider a central switch that assists $n$ remote users in distributing a graph state, using independently generated user-switch Bell pairs. Since Bell-pair generation is probabilistic, different links generally succeed at different times. When a Bell pair is generated, the qubits may need to be stored in memory while waiting for other links to succeed. Recently, new protocols have been proposed to reduce this storage overhead by processing and releasing some switch qubits before all Bell links are available. However, these protocols do not characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required at each stage. Moreover, the local-cover method in the state-of-the-art Piecemaker protocol is computationally expensive for general target graphs. In this work, we characterize the minimum persistent switch memory required after any subset of users' Bell links are generated and processed. We then develop an online stabilizer-transition protocol that attains this limit, which can be implemented in polynomial time in the number of qubits $n$ and does not require information about future Bell-link successes. Moreover, when one Bell link succeeds per round of duration $\Delta t$, for the path graph $P_n$, Piecemaker requires the cumulative switch-qubit storage time $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ and peak memory of at least $\left\lfloor n/2 \right\rfloor$ \textit{for any arrival order}, while under some arrival orders, our protocol requires only $(n-1)\Delta t$ and retains just one persistent switch qubit. More generally, for tree graphs, our protocol can reduce the $\Theta(n^2\Delta t)$ cumulative storage time in Piecemaker to $O(n\log n\,\Delta t)$ for some arrival orders.
papers.authors: Lei Hu, Alptug Aytekin, Stavros Mitrolaris, Mohamed Nomeir, Subhankar Banerjee, Sennur Ulukus, Saikat Guha

papers.title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
papers.abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory (DFT) to include a temperature dimension. The formalism unifies established hybrid functionals with information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation DFT, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. It further gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set of different organic molecules. The results clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.
papers.authors: Florian Matz, Paul G. Graf, Markus Penz, Christian Schilling

papers.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
papers.abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.
papers.authors: Rishabh Batra

papers.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
papers.abstract: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
papers.authors: Piotr \'Cwikli\'nski

papers.title: A mathematical perspective on nonplanar on-shell forms
papers.abstract: On-shell forms are differential forms on the Grassmannian which arise in particle physics. They are defined using bipartite graphs with $n$ distinguished ``boundary'' vertices. Mathematical investigation of on-shell forms has largely focused on the case where the graph is planar, in which case one can utilize combinatorial tools pioneered by Postnikov in the study of the totally nonnegative Grassmannian. In this article, we investigate on-shell forms for arbitrary graphs. We first discuss how to extend various tools from the planar case to arbitrary graphs. We then prove a determinantal formula for a class of on-shell forms which first appeared in physics literature. We explain the relation between this class of forms and the hypertree divisors of $M_{0,n}$, introduced by Castravet--Tevelev.
papers.authors: Artyom Lisitsyn, Elizabeth Pratt, Melissa Sherman-Bennett, Jaroslav Trnka

papers.title: Plunge bounds for Fourier concentration operators: geometry, smoothing, and wave packets
papers.abstract: We prove a single-logarithm bound for the eigenvalues in the plunge region of Fourier concentration operators, removing the extra logarithmic factor in the Kulikov--Dam Larsen bound for two general admissible sets throughout each fixed exponential window. For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $\Lambda_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,\beta)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $\beta>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\le\beta c$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.
papers.authors: Ahmadreza Azimifard

papers.title: Analytic construction of dimension-dependent steering witnesses from generalized equiangular measurements
papers.abstract: In this work, we construct a dimension-dependent family of generalized equiangular measurements (GEAMs) that gives explicit steering witnesses in every prime dimension $d$. The construction consists of \(d-1\) mutually unbiased measurements and an additional normalized family of \(2d-1\) Hermitian operators, which is a $(1,2d-1)$-POVM {(POVM denotes a positive, operator-valued measure).} For odd prime dimensions, we reduce the noncentral operators to three-dimensional invariant subspaces and solve the central operator in a two-dimensional subspace. We combine complementary Gershgorin bounds from two unitarily equivalent matrix representations to obtain a fully analytic asymmetric interval for {a parameter} that guarantees positivity. The {qubit and qutrit cases} are treated separately. Finally, using a maximally entangled realization and the local-hidden-state bound for GEAMs, we obtain an explicit steering inequality and a sufficient criterion for quantum violation in every prime dimension.
papers.authors: Adam Rutkowski, Katarzyna Siudzi\'{n}ska

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy and Holographic Entanglement Entropy in DGP Brane Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the relation between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity with gravitational dynamics localized on the brane. We first consider the DGP brane model, in which an Einstein-Hilbert term is included in the brane action, and demonstrate that the gravitational entropy of a braneworld black hole agrees with the holographic entanglement entropy for general stationary spacetimes. We then generalize the brane-localized Einstein-Hilbert term to higher-curvature gravitational theories. For Lovelock gravity and $f(R)$ gravity on the brane, we derive the corresponding expressions for gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy and show that the two entropies also coincide for general stationary spacetimes. These results establish the equivalence between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity for a broad class of gravitational theories and contribute to a deeper understanding of holography in braneworld settings.
papers.authors: Takamasa Kanai

papers.title: PyCC: A Reference Quantum Chemistry Python Package for Education, Validation, and Rapid Prototyping
papers.abstract: PyCC is a Python-based quantum chemistry package that emphasizes coupled cluster and related methods. Developed over the last five years, PyCC's purpose is to provide a clear reference implementation that will serve as a validation suite for production code, a platform for rapid prototyping and testing of new methods, and an educational resource for newcomers to the field. The package covers both closed- and open-shell single-determinant references in spatial- and spin-orbital formulations for the coupled cluster hierarchy through triples-including methods such as CC3, as well as for MP2 and CI methods. PyCC provides a broad range of molecular properties such as analytic first and second energy derivatives including gradients, Hessians, polarizabilities and atomic polar tensors, as well as non-energy-derivative properties, such as velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors and diagonal Born-Oppenheimer corrections, plus dynamic linear response functions, and excitation energies. The package includes a number of unique capabilities, such as real-time CC propagation (up through CC3), atomic axial tensors for simulating vibrational circular dichroism spectra at the MP2, CID, CISD, and CCSD levels, and local correlation methods including perturbation-aware correlation domains. The code is designed around a shared Wavefunction base and a method-agnostic derivative layer that enables a new method to inherit the full energy-derivative property set once it supplies its reduced densities and their first-order responses. PyCC is fully open source and available on GitHub under the BSD 3-clause license.
papers.authors: T. Daniel Crawford, Benjamin G. Peyton, Zhe Wang, Aparna Krishnan, Brendan M. Shumberger, Jose Madriaga, Joshua Atta-Kumi, Aaron De Clercq, Ritvik Prabhu

papers.title: The monatomic limit of polyatomic gases: the Dirac prescription and an application to a new hierarchy of moments
papers.abstract: In the kinetic theory of a polytropic gas, internal molecular modes are described by a power-law density of internal states, making the monatomic limit singular. We show that the normalized limit $a\to-1^+$ is equivalent to replacing integration over internal energy by a Dirac mass at zero energy, and derive the first-order correction. We apply this prescription to the classical full-energy moment hierarchy arising from the non-relativistic limit of the relativistic hierarchy of Arima, Carrisi, Pennisi and Ruggeri. For every finite truncation order, we establish the independent and exhaustive monatomic trace identities and derive the number of surviving fields. In particular, the known reduction from polyatomic ET15 to Kremer's monatomic ET14 is recovered. We also prove that the limiting spectrum of the unreduced polyatomic characteristic pencil splits into the spectrum of the reduced monatomic system and a lower-order polyatomic spectrum with a shifted internal-energy parameter. Equilibrium characteristic velocities are obtained using the linearized maximum-entropy prescription, without assuming a nonlinear closure away from equilibrium. We show that, at fixed truncation order, the largest characteristic velocity is non-increasing with the number of molecular degrees of freedom and attains its maximum at the monatomic endpoint. Finally, the symmetric-hyperbolic principal-subsystem argument yields the previously known Boillat--Ruggeri lower bound for the new hierarchy, implying unbounded growth of the maximum characteristic velocity with truncation order.
papers.authors: Tommaso Ruggeri

papers.title: Antipodal Self-Duality for Generalized Fishnets from Integrability
papers.abstract: Antipodal self-duality (ASD) is a remarkable property that relates an amplitude to itself, after performing a suitable kinematic map and reversing the letters of the symbol (more precisely, acting with the antipode of the Hopf algebra of the de Rham analogs of multiple polylogarithms). ASD has been seen in only one process in planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and its physical origin is unknown, motivating a search for ASD in other contexts. Recently, ASD was found to hold for square fishnet integrals in a strongly-deformed version of planar $\mathcal{N}=4$. In this paper, we investigate the properties of polynomials in ladder integrals under the ASD transformation that leaves the square fishnet invariant. Our basic building blocks are determinants of certain matrices of ladder integrals, that are labeled by partitions or Young diagrams, and automatically obey the Steinmann relations. We employ integrability-based representations of such determinants, which are essentially matrix-model integrals, and the theory of symmetric polynomials to find many more ASD quantities -- linear combinations of determinants whose coefficients are expressed using the combinatorics of partitions. As a byproduct, we provide an alternate proof that square fishnet integrals obey ASD.
papers.authors: Lance J. Dixon, Claude Duhr, Francesca C. Fernandes, Victor Mishnyakov

papers.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
papers.abstract: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.
papers.authors: Tatsuhiko Shirai

papers.title: Anomalous Hardening of a Fluctuation-Induced Gap
papers.abstract: In a mean-field picture, a gap opened by quantum fluctuations grows with them. This can fail if the fluctuating mode is critical and its displacement compensates its coupling to the degenerate states. A single parameter sets the gap response: above a universal threshold, the gap hardens as the critical fluctuations weaken. Whenever the parameter is nonzero, overcompensation beyond the critical point drives a secondary phase transition. In a quantum Rabi ring with synthetic flux, exact diagonalization shows the gap of a photonic Landau level rising by 15% as the critical variance falls by 25%.
papers.authors: Shu He, Liwei Duan

papers.title: Semiclassical reconstruction of the Toda pole lattice via analytic continuation of the Probabilistic Approach
papers.abstract: We develop a probabilistic construction of Toda field theory correlators from the Coulomb gas representation. Reinterpreting $n$-point functions of primaries as $w$-moments of random variables with respect to a Gaussian measure, we derive constraints on the Toda momenta and coupling constant. $L^2$ and $L^p$ convergence conditions for the associated random variables, triviality constraints on the correlators, and local integrability conditions for the cross-moments are derived. These constraints define an extended region of convergence for the Toda correlators and provide a systematic, probabilistic interpretation of the Seiberg bounds. We proceed to analytically continue the moment indices by employing a Mellin-Barnes representation of the random variables. The local convergence boundaries become meromorphic local integrability divisors, and, in the semiclassical $b\to0$ limit, these divisors reconstruct the Liouville charge pole lattice. For $A_n$ Toda theory, we show that natural $W_n$-closure conditions in this semiclassical limit select rank-one, Virasoro-like submodules inside the full Toda theory. On these slices, the scalar integrability conditions reduce to Liouville-like divisors and recover the corresponding Toda charge pole lattices.
papers.authors: Jacques Distler, Bahaa Elshimy

papers.title: Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
papers.abstract: We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. M\"oller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=\xi-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.
papers.authors: Fran\c{c}ois Golse, Jakob M\"oller

papers.title: Contact Large Deviations of Stochastic Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: A dissipative system distributes over its state space, and its rare events are measured on an exponential scale by a rate function. This paper shows that one contact form carries both. On the bundle of jets of probability densities over the state space, the constraint function of the contact potential is a first integral of the characteristic field, so the action is affine in the elapsed time along each characteristic and the contact probability measure of a Lagrangian section has that action as its exponent at every finite time, with no path integral, no variational problem over curves and no coercivity hypothesis. The rate function is the deficit of the action below its supremum, and is therefore a transported conserved quantity rather than the value of a limit; its amplitude is invariant and its non-degeneracy is decided by the initial section alone. Large deviations form the concentration regime of this finite-time structure and require one condition, the smooth convergence of the endpoint map of the characteristic flow to a diffeomorphism. The drift and the fluctuation tensor are the first two coefficients of the same potential, the second confined to the iso-density surfaces by the degeneracy condition, so the fluctuation is constrained by the invariant density rather than chosen beside the drift. The entropy production is an observable of the same measure, and a fibre involution yields a Gallavotti--Cohen-type duality between the forward and the reversed ensembles under a separation condition on the tilted action.
papers.authors: D. Y. Zhong

papers.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $\pi$ pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single $2\pi$ pulse yields a $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(Z)$ gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a $\text{C}_2(Z)$ fidelity of $0.996$ estimated with $T_2^\ast=1.5$~s and a gate duration of $T \approx 4\text{~ms}$. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of $10^{-4}$ for $\mathbb{N}=2,3$ and $10^{-3}$ for $\mathbb{N}=4$, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as $25\hbar/T$.
papers.authors: Yan Lu, Xiao-Feng Shi

papers.title: Shadow and Polarized Images of Schwarzschild-MOG Black Hole Illuminated by Thick Accretion Disk
papers.abstract: Recent EHT polarimetric observations provide a powerful probe of near-horizon physics and modified gravity. We investigate the shadow and polarization images of a static Schwarzschild-MOG black hole illuminated by geometrically thick, optically thin accretion flows. Adopting a phenomenological model and the Hou disk model, and solving null geodesics and relativistic radiative transfer, we study how the MOG parameter, inclination angle, anisotropic synchrotron emission, and flow geometry affect the total intensity and linear polarization. It is found that the MOG parameter mainly enlarges and brightens higher-order photon rings and broadens the shadow, while the inclination angle breaks axial symmetry and enhances polarized emission inside the shadow. The Hou disk model suppresses off-equatorial radiative interference and localizes polarization signals within higher-order rings. Electric vector position angle (EVPA) patterns are mostly azimuthal but vary rapidly near lensed images. These results provide theoretical diagnostics for constraining MOG with EHT/ngEHT polarimetric observations.
papers.authors: Cheng Hu, Huan Ye, Hong Lei, Zi-Chao Lin

papers.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
papers.abstract: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
papers.authors: Valery Shchesnovich

papers.title: Modular flow and the area operator
papers.abstract: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, the Jafferis-Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Suh (JLMS) formula relates the boundary modular Hamiltonian to the HRT area operator and the corresponding bulk modular Hamiltonian. In standard discussions of a holographic code built from perturbative excitations on a fixed classical background, the $A/4G$ term dominates over the bulk modular Hamiltonian in the limit $G \to 0$. However, this setup is insufficient to describe the action of boundary modular flows that change the classical background. In contrast, our recent discussion of `large' codes provides a useful framework to obtain a JLMS formula that relates bulk and boundary modular flows acting on appropriate states in the code. Here, one sees that the bulk modular Hamiltonian is not in fact subdominant when the modular flow defined by one state acts on another state peaked around a sufficiently different classical background. Instead, the bulk modular Hamiltonian can be of order $1/G$ and can dominate over the $A/4G$ term. Nevertheless, we show that if the two states have the same classical background except for data conjugate to the HRT area then, under mild assumptions and over a large range of flow parameters, the modular-flowed state is described by a classical background given by the HRT-area flow alone.
papers.authors: Xi Dong, Donald Marolf, Pratik Rath

papers.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
papers.abstract: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.
papers.authors: Joshua Laux, Eric G. Cavalcanti

papers.title: Analytic motions of spinning particles in Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter spacetime
papers.abstract: The motion of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime with a cosmological constant is studied within the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism, working to linear order in the particle's spin. By exploiting the symmetries of the background, the radial and latitudinal dynamics are reduced to first-order equations governed by a spin-deformed quintic polynomial. A complete classification of the real root structure of this quintic is carried out, from which the allowed orbital types for spinning particles in the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter and Schwarzschild-de Sitter geometries follow directly. The parameter dependence of the root structure and of the stable circular orbit interval is analyzed. In particular, for values of the cosmological constant beyond the Stuchl\'ik limit, where spinless particles admit no bound orbits, spinning particles can still remain bound. The radial motion is expressed piecewise in terms of Lauricella hypergeometric functions, with the simple positive real roots of the quintic acting as branch cuts. The latitudinal motion consists of small oscillations about an equatorial plane, and its phase, governed by the same quintic, admits an analogous analytic representation.
papers.authors: Rui-Hui Lin, Xing-You Zhou, Chao-Jun Feng

papers.title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
papers.abstract: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.
papers.authors: Ryan A. Lanzetta, Ian Moult, Yifan Wang

papers.title: Quantum Landau Damping with Coulomb Repulsion in the Whole Space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the large time behavior of solutions to the linearized Hartree equation near a stable equilibrium which is homogeneous in space and investigate the quantum Landau damping. This allows us to get time decay of the electric field, uniformly in the Planck constant, as well as the uniform-in-time convergence of the quantum density towards the classical density as the Planck constant converges to 0.
papers.authors: Dongfen Bian, Emmanuel Grenier, Laurent Lafl\`eche, Quoc Hung Nguyen

papers.title: A loss-limited optimum for fixed uniform multi-pass quantum sensing per absorbed photon
papers.abstract: Multi-pass schemes send a photon through a sample several times to learn more about it. When the sample rather than the light is scarce, the natural figure of merit is the information gained per photon the object absorbs. We show that three properties fix the loss-limited optimum of every fixed scheme in which a single photon passes repeatedly and uniformly through the sample and is detected once at the end: a payoff that grows as the square of the pass number, the same survival probability on every pass, and no dose from a photon already lost. They force a single trade-off function $h(x)=x^2/(e^x-1)$, where $x$ is the number of passes times the loss per pass. Its maximum, 0.648, sits at $x_{\rm opt}=1.594$. The multi-pass optima of Koppell and Kasevich and of Yu et al. are two instances, and the loss-limited ceiling of interaction-free interrogation is a third when its payoff is counted as conclusive detections. Phase sensing of a weakly absorbing object is optimal at $m_{\rm opt}=x_{\rm opt}/(\epsilon+\alpha)$ passes; the absorption $\alpha$ and the parasitic loss $\epsilon$ enter the optimum only through their sum, but the damage counts only $\alpha$. N00N states and their loss-robust generalisations do worse per absorbed photon, and optimising over photon and pass number returns a single recycled photon; Gaussian probes and chains tailored pass by pass lie outside this class and can exceed its ceiling by a bounded factor. Absorption estimation gains nothing, for any scheme. Above the crosstalk crossover of the mode sorter, detecting a faint companion below the Rayleigh limit costs the companion a dose independent of its faintness; below it, and under direct imaging at any separation, the dose grows without bound as the companion fades. Among single photons and path-entangled number states, the gentlest measurement of a fragile sample is also the simplest: a single photon, recycled.
papers.authors: Christoph F. Wildfeuer

papers.title: Sourced stationary Dirac bound states around Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Ultralight bosonic fields can form macroscopic clouds around rotating black holes, whereas the existence of analogous stationary fermionic configurations is constrained by their intrinsic spin. Here we study stationary bound states of massive Dirac fields supported by an external source on Kerr backgrounds, in the test-field approximation, with a kinematic extension to Kerr--Newman, they are not fermionic condensates in the many-body sense. By mapping the Kerr--Dirac system to a globally integrated sourced radial problem, we isolate the boundary constraints dictated by horizon causality. The angular sector shows that for $|m|=1/2$ the regular boundary branches prevent the field density from vanishing on the rotation axis, whereas modes with $|m|\ge3/2$ vanish there, the reconstructed Kerr density is only mildly oblate. Precisely at the kinematic synchronization locus, the Frobenius matrix of the Dirac operator is non-defective and devoid of logarithmic divergences. Regularity on the future horizon nevertheless selects the ingoing solution, and an exact radial flux identity shows that this solution carries a positive flux, which excludes source-free normalizable states at all frequencies. The exclusion of source-free synchronized states demonstrates that a black hole's capacity to support macroscopic stationary fields is governed not merely by superradiant kinematics, but by the interplay between horizon regularity and the positivity of the Dirac flux.
papers.authors: Sen Guo, Peng-Yu Chen, Yi-Han Huang, Xin Li, Yu Liang, Kai Lin, Lin Wen, Li-Fang Li

papers.title: C-infinity Compact-Support Wormholes with Exact Schwarzschild Exterior in Trace-Coupled Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct static, spherically symmetric wormholes in trace-coupled gravity with $f(R,T)=R+\lambda T^2$. Smooth deformations of Schwarzschild vanish to all orders outside a finite core, producing an exact Schwarzschild exterior without a thin shell. Under two explicitly assumed anisotropic-fluid closures, the matter reconstruction reduces to a cubic equation for $\chi=\lambda T/(4\pi)$. The vacuum boundary selects a locally unique root; its simple continuation must remain separate from the singular inversion surface. We distinguish root folds from vanishing $1+\chi$ and terminate numerical continuation when the selected root coalesces. Regular examples have either positive or negative throat density. On every regular branch the physical radial null energy condition fails at the throat; for the undeformed-redshift family it fails throughout the open core. The nonvacuum sector has finite support, whereas the exterior retains the Schwarzschild Weyl field and mass $M$. Reproducible phase maps, convergence tests, and high-precision tail checks support these conditional existence results. No dynamical stability or microphysical matter model is asserted.
papers.authors: Mushtaq Ahmad, M. Farasat Shamir, Ahdab K. Althukair

papers.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.
papers.authors: Kohei Fujikura, Toshifumi Noumi, Shintetsu Yamazaki

papers.title: Quark Stars in $f(T,\mathcal{T}) $ Gravity: Structure, Stability, and Observational Constraints
papers.abstract: Quark stars-hypothetical compact stars made entirely of deconfined quark matter-offer a clean testing ground for gravity beyond general relativity. We study their structure in $f(T,\mathcal{T})$ gravity, a teleparallel theory in which torsion is coupled directly to the trace of the energy-momentum tensor through a single constant coupling. Using the standard MIT bag description of quark matter, we solve the modified stellar structure equations and follow how the mass, radius, compactness, and surface redshift respond as the coupling is varied across its full admissible range. The maximum mass turns out to depend on the coupling in a non-monotonic way: it rises above the general relativity value, peaks near 2.02 solar masses at a moderate positive coupling, and then falls steeply as the coupling approaches a critical value at which the structure equations become singular. The two-solar-mass pulsar constraint is satisfied within a finite window of positive couplings. All configurations on the candidate stable branch satisfy causality and remain below the standard general-relativistic compactness and surface-redshift benchmarks.
papers.authors: Takol Tangphati, Ayan Banerjee, Izzet Sakalli, Sayantan Ghosh, Aseel Smerat

papers.title: Qubit-qubit-qutrit quantum correlations in $H \to f \bar f V$
papers.abstract: We perform an extensive analysis of the quantum correlations carried by the qubit--qubit--qutrit pure state arising in the decay of a massive scalar into a fermion--antifermion pair and a massive gauge boson, $H \to f \bar f V$, specialising to the Higgs boson decay $h \to \tau^- \tau^+ Z$. Working with the exact tree-level spin state and its systematic expansion around the massless-fermion limit, we obtain analytic control over the entire phase space: the bipartite entanglement measures, the genuine $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entanglement structure (the Miyake classification), as well as the Bell-inequality violations and the non-stabiliserness (magic) are all mapped and reproduced by compact formulas. The bipartite measures exhibit a monogamy-like trade-off between the fermion pair and the fermion--boson pairs. The state is genuinely $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entangled over almost the entire phase space, most strongly in the collinear regions. We derive, for the first time, semi-analytical expressions for the tight $4 \times 4 \times 2$ Bell inequalities of the $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ system, generalising the optimisation previously available only for three qubits, and find that the local-hidden-variable bound is violated over the entire phase space, reaching within a few per cent of the quantum bound at the upper endpoint of the di-tau mass spectrum. We further extend the stabiliser R\'enyi entropy and the non-local magic to systems with unequal local dimensions, and show that the near-endpoint state carries almost exactly one bit of non-local magic, which peaks at $\log_2 \frac{27}{7} \simeq 1.95$ in the collinear regions. The differential decay rate concentrates precisely in the most nonclassical region of the phase space.
papers.authors: Micha{\l} Banacki, Misaki Ohta, Abhyoudai S. Shaleena, Pawe{\l} Caban, Micha{\l} Eckstein, Kazuki Sakurai, Michael Spannowsky, Pawe{\l} Horodecki

papers.title: A broadband, individually addressable 2D-3D photonic integrated circuit for trapped-ion qubit control
papers.abstract: Trapped ions provide a high-fidelity platform for quantum information processing, yet delivery of multiple, distinct wavelengths across large networks of interaction zones remains a bottleneck. Conventional free-space light delivery lacks scalability, while on-chip grating couplers suffer from narrow operational bandwidth that increases circuit footprint and optical interfacing complexity. Here we show a broadband photonic integrated circuit capable of addressing individual ion locations. The circuit combines a planar waveguide lens with a micromirror fabricated using two-photon polymerization at wafer scale. Optical characterization demonstrates three individual addressing spots from $\lambda = 405$- $880\,\mathrm{nm}$ with $-25\,\mathrm{dB}$ average intensity crosstalk at $5\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ pitch. We trap $^{40}\mathrm{Ca}^{+}$ above the mirror to demonstrate preferential repumping and utilize $^{138}\mathrm{Ba}^{+}$ ions to characterize optical crosstalk far away from the mirror. Charging of the dielectric and silicon structures currently limits a full experimental demonstration of the devices' capabilities but could be mitigated in future designs. This monolithic photonic architecture could bring broadband addressing in an on-chip modality to trapped-ion technology. More broadly, combining additive manufacturing with established quantum device fabrication techniques could open new possibilities for implementing advanced quantum architectures.
papers.authors: Yiyang Zhi, Daniel Klawson, Bingran You, Michael Bareian, Elijah Mossman, Chun-Yuan Fan, Arkadev Roy, Ke Sun, Jason Lee, Sung Cheol Yoon, Qiming Wu, Lai Jiang, Wenjun Ke, Weiwei Wu, Sirui Tang, Zachary Wall, Jiaxiang Wang, Louis Paul Romero, Sam Vizvary, Steven Diaz, Eric R. Hudson, Wesley C. Campbell, Hartmut Haeffner, Ming C. Wu

papers.title: Revealing the conformal symmetry of the discrete series scalars in dS${}_2$
papers.abstract: On two-dimensional manifolds with nonzero constant Ricci curvature, there exists an infinite sequence of scalar fields with nonzero mass parameter that admit a pair of (anti-)holomorphic currents. After suitably defining the theory in de Sitter space ($\mathrm{dS}_2$), correlation functions of these currents obey global conformal Ward identities. We address the question of how this global conformal symmetry manifests as an action on the scalar field. An essential step is in leveraging an equivalent description of the scalar field in terms of a conformal Killing tensor. Through this, we find a conformal symmetry transformation that acts locally on the conformal Killing tensor, but non-locally on the scalar field. We show that the equation of motion transforms covariantly with respect to these conformal transformations, and further find a traceless stress tensor in both $\mathrm{dS}_2$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_2$, locally defined in terms of the conformal Killing tensor, which generates the global conformal isometry transformations.
papers.authors: Lukas W. Lindwasser

papers.title: Comments on holographic spread complexity
papers.abstract: We revisit the holographic proposal relating the growth rate of spread complexity to the radial momentum of a bulk probe, aiming to identify its underlying assumptions and clarify how classical probe dynamics emerges from quantum dynamics. By quantizing AdS probes directly and using the extrapolation dictionary, we provide a more general derivation of the proposal within the probe approximation for the specified class of states. In particular, we discuss a probe analogue of the classical complexity observables appearing in the ``complexity=anything'' (CAny) framework and examine how such an observable can be quantized. Since probe dynamics is not intrinsically tied to the AdS/CFT correspondence, we also examine the proposal in flat and de Sitter spacetimes. In flat spacetime, the physical Hamiltonian does not preserve the coherent-state structure, and spread complexity measures the dispersive broadening of the wave packet rather than classical momentum. In de Sitter space, generic semiclassical wave packets in the static-patch energy representation show the same dispersive behavior. By contrast, coherent states adapted to the principal-series representation can exhibit exponential growth of spread complexity, with a growth rate that has the same time dependence as the classical radial momentum. These examples indicate that a semiclassical limit alone is not sufficient for a momentum--complexity relation.
papers.authors: Zhehan Li, Jia Tian

papers.title: Conformal line defects from matter-coupled 5D N=4 gauged supergravity
papers.abstract: We study a number of holographic solutions describing conformal line defects within $N=2$ SCFTs from matter-coupled $N=4$ gauged supergravity in five dimensions. For $SO(2)_D\times SO(3)$ gauge group, the gauged supergravity admits two supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua with $N=4$ and $N=2$ unbroken supersymmetries. It turns out that only solutions that are asymptotic to the $N=4$ vacuum are possible leading to line defects within the dual $N=2$ SCFT. In gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times ISO(3)$ gauge group, we find similar solutions with the $N=2$ SCFT appearing in the IR while the UV field theories correspond to six-dimensional $N=(0,2)$ field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a hyperbolic space $H^2$. The solution with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry is also uplifted to eleven dimensions via a consistent truncation on $H^2\times S^4$. Finally, for gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times SO(3)\times SO(3)$ gauge group that admits two $N=4$ supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua, we find a solution describing a line defect that interpolates between these two vacua as well as a solution with only one asymptotic $AdS_5$ geometry.
papers.authors: Parinya Karndumri

papers.title: CORTET: Robust generation of simulation-ready tetrahedral meshes of the fetal cerebral cortex
papers.abstract: Every human brain folds differently, and such natural variation confounds the search for imaging biomarkers of neurodevelopmental disorders. Physics-based simulation can help determine the causal mechanisms that underpin this variability. Yet every simulation must be initiated from a volumetric mesh of the brain's interior, tetrahedral or hexahedral, and it is the worst element in that mesh, not the average, that decides whether the simulation runs at all. Building that mesh from fetal MRI currently requires labour-intensive manual intervention. We therefore present CORTET (CORtical TETrahedral meshing): a fully automated pipeline that converts a triangulated cortical surface into a solver-ready tetrahedral mesh whose worst-element quality meets a strict quality target with no manual repair. By benchmarking against a general-purpose tetrahedral mesher on the same input surfaces, we isolate the pipeline's contribution from that of the input geometry, and we validate quality across a cohort of nearly 200 fetal subjects spanning the folding period. A mesh taken straight from the pipeline sustains a numerically stable morphoelastic folding simulation of a real fetal subject.
papers.authors: Davood Shahsavari, Irina Grigorescu, Katherine R. Long, Jiaxin Xiao, Kaili Liang, Nashira Baena, Aakash Saboo, Saga N. B. Masui, Yourong Guo, Vanessa Kyriakopoulou, Alena Uus, Martin J. Bishop, Emma C. Robinson

papers.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
papers.abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their sensitivity to noise is expected to decrease exponentially with increasing separation between the Majoranas, a suppression known as topological protection. Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot-superconductor arrays provide a tunable platform in which separated Majorana zero modes can emerge at the ends of the chain, even in two-site chains. These minimal-chain modes are known as poor man's Majoranas and retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but have only limited protection. A key outstanding challenge is to move beyond identifying such modes in electrical transport measurements and achieve coherent qubit control in the time domain. Here, we demonstrate a Majorana parity qubit by realizing coherent coupling between two-site Kitaev chains. Since total fermion parity is conserved, the system separates into global even and odd parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both manifolds with equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot, as predicted for isolated Majorana zero modes. We further show that the oscillation frequency and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in close agreement with our model for short, partially protected chains. Our results establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes in minimal Kitaev chains.
papers.authors: Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo, Antonio Lombardi, Juan D. Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, Vincent P. M. Sietses, Florian J. Bennebroek Evertsz', Pablo Cova Fari\~na, Alberto Bordin, Ghada Badawy, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven

papers.title: Seven- and eight-loop critical exponents of the three-dimensional Ising model
papers.abstract: We determine the critical exponents $\eta$, $\nu$, and the correction-to-scaling exponent $\omega$ of the three-dimensional Ising universality class by resumming the recently computed seven- and eight-loop renormalization-group series in the $\epsilon=4-d$ expansion [O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{97}, 085018 (2018); O.~Schnetz, \textit{Phys. Rev. D} \textbf{107}, 036002 (2023)]. The resummation combines conformal mapping with a homographic transformation, while the resummation parameters are optimized according to two complementary criteria. This approach yields precise estimates of the critical exponents together with quantitative uncertainty estimates. We find that the error bar on $\eta$ decreases rapidly with increasing loop order, whereas this is the case neither for $\nu$ nor for $\omega$. Unexpectedly, although the estimated values are accurate in absolute terms, their slow convergence with the loop order leads to a slight but systematic tension with the conformal bootstrap estimates that are currently considered as the benchmark. We discuss several possible origins of this behavior and its implications for high-order resummations of perturbative renormalization-group series.
papers.authors: D. Shapoval, Yu. Honchar, B. Delamotte, M. Dudka, Yu. Holovatch

papers.title: Bootstrapping "black holes" at low impact parameter
papers.abstract: We use the stringy dispersion relation to obtain a numerical upper bound on the radius of a uniformly absorptive disk in a six-dimensional gravitational effective field theory. Near the boundary of the allowed region of low-energy couplings, the bound is of order the Schwarzschild radius. The dispersion relation connects those couplings to the partial-wave spectrum. In the calculation, we fix the eikonal contribution in a specified high-energy region at large impact parameter and vary the real parts of the remaining elastic $S$-matrix elements within the bounds imposed by unitarity. The real part of each element sets an upper limit on its absorption probability, so the radius bound applies to any unitary amplitude satisfying the same assumptions. Near the boundary, a strongly absorptive disk of the classical trapped-surface radius is excluded if it must extend down to low collision energies. Raising the minimum energy lifts this exclusion. The angular momentum at the edge of the absorptive core grows approximately as $s^{0.7}$, where $s$ is the squared center-of-mass energy. This is close to the $s^{2/3}$ scaling expected for an edge at a fixed multiple of the Schwarzschild radius in six dimensions. The corresponding dimension-dependent scaling also describes full-amplitude bootstrap results in nine to eleven dimensions. In the extremal spectra, the band's outer edge stays at roughly the same impact parameter as the collision energy increases, about 5-6 EFT cutoff lengths $M_{\rm EFT}^{-1}$ at weak gravity.
papers.authors: Diptarka Das, Aninda Sinha

papers.title: Revealing precision bounds on neutrino oscillation parameters with quantum estimation theory
papers.abstract: Quantum estimation theory provides ultimate precision bounds on parameter estimation, independent of experimental setups. In this article, we apply this theoretical framework to neutrino oscillations, aiming to clarify some subtle issues and reveal the maximum achievable precision of oscillation parameters. First, taking the example of two-flavor oscillations, we clarify how the quantum Fisher information (QFI) depends on the choice of bases when the basis transformation itself involves the parameters in question. Then, for three-flavor oscillations, we compute the QFI matrix for electron and muon neutrino states in the flavor basis and derive analytical expressions and numerical results for both diagonal and off-diagonal elements. The implications of off-diagonal correlations for multiparameter estimation are discussed, including the compatibility of optimal measurements, the Holevo bound, and the spectral analysis of the QFI matrix, from which we show that a single neutrino channel leaves exactly two parameter combinations unconstrained. The quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bounds on the precision of oscillation parameters for typical reactor and long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments are obtained as vacuum, state-level benchmarks, which establish a theoretical reference for the ultimate precision achievable in future neutrino oscillation experiments.
papers.authors: Jihong Huang, Tommy Ohlsson, Sampsa Vihonen, Shun Zhou

papers.title: From spectral structure to sensing limits in quantum thermometry
papers.abstract: The precision of a quantum thermometer is fundamentally constrained by the spectral structure of the probe itself, and a systematic mapping between the configurations of energy levels and thermometric performance provides relevant information to design optimized devices. In this work, we establish such a mapping by analyzing a broad class of quantum systems, ranging from finite spin ensembles and degenerate atoms to confining potentials, quantum walks, and continuous-spectrum models. We derive exact scaling laws for the quantum Fisher information, revealing two distinct high-temperature universality classes: finite-spectrum probes exhibit a $T^{-4}$ decay, while unbounded or continuous spectra yield a slower $T^{-2}$ decay. At low temperatures, we show that sensitivity, though universally exponentially suppressed, can be enhanced arbitrarily by engineering degenerate excited states or a quantum walk on a fully connected topology. By contrast, specific quantum walk topologies provide a distinct enhancement mechanism based on gap engineering, whereby an optimal network size yields an optimized $T^{-2}$ low-temperature scaling. Furthermore, power-law spectra enable tunable scaling of thermometric performance with system size, offering a design principle for optimal probes in specific temperature windows. Our results contribute to transform spectral information into a resource for quantum thermometry, providing both fundamental bounds and practical guidelines to tailored temperature sensing.
papers.authors: Youssef Aiache, Simone Cavazzoni, Abderrahim El Allati, Paolo Bordone, Matteo G. A. Paris

papers.title: Inner sublattice competition: a minimal mechanism for reentrant localizations in Aubry-Andr\'e lattice
papers.abstract: We construct a double mosaic Aubry-Andr\'e (DMAA) model with two independent quasiperiodic potentials assigned to corresponding even and odd sublattices of the AA lattice, and show that the competition between them gives rise to multiple localization-delocalization transitions under single-parameter tuning. Such reentrant localizations are verified by comprehensive numerical characterizations including the inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension, and real-space wavefunction distributions. Simulations based on a continuous polariton model yield consistent results, confirming the experimental feasibility of the predicted phenomena. This inner sublattice competition mechanism works in a minimal way for reentrant localizations without additional ingredients or dynamical modifications such as long-range hopping, mixed quasiperiodic and random disorder, or non-Hermitian gain and loss, offering a concise route to engineer reentrant localization based on the canonical AA lattice family.
papers.authors: Hangdong Qiu, Yunhua Wang

papers.title: What makes spacetime spin in string theory?
papers.abstract: Type II string theory in the absence of orientifolds requires the target spacetime $X$ to admit a spin structure. We show that this familiar requirement arises directly from the consistency of the worldsheet GSO projection. The obstruction is a mixed global anomaly between $(-1)^{\text{F}_L}$ and the target space background data, detected by the spin bordism group $\Omega_3^{\mathrm{spin}}(B\mathbb{Z}_2\times X)$.
