It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.
papers.authors: Di Wu, Shuang-Qing Wu

papers.title: Dynamics of R\'enyi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
papers.abstract: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on R\'enyi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for R\'enyi-2. Focusing on R\'enyi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ans\"atze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher R\'enyi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of R\'enyi evolution in deterministic systems.
papers.authors: Riccardo Senese, Pasquale Calabrese

papers.title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
papers.abstract: Local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is fixed by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits, which span the permutation-symmetric subspace with one Dicke state per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and maps onto a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size, fully quantifying the preparation process. In one dimension we solve it in closed form. Its slowest rate, $\Lambda_{\rm pair}=2[1-\cos(\pi/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is the full Liouvillian gap. For any such scheme, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations and thus needs a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure gives the final state for any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates the shot noise of removal and correlations between pairs. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus all governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.
papers.authors: T. D\"orstel, T. C. Lang, T. Iadecola, J. H. Wilson, M. Buchhold

papers.title: Attainable and unattainable gauge-dependent quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $\theta_\ast=\Omega/(\Omega+\omega)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.
papers.authors: Wangjun Lu, Qing Yu

papers.title: Universality in Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
papers.abstract: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.
papers.authors: Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina

papers.title: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
papers.abstract: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts 512 quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1620,160]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ time-domain waveforms with exact parameter and temporal derivatives via automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained jointly on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 109 SXS evaluation waveforms (106 physical systems) over $[-1500,100]M$, it achieves a mean balanced relative strain error of 0.0305 and a mean finite-window detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of 0.1536%, outperforming SEOBNRv5PHM, NRSur7dq4v2, and IMRPhenomTPHM across common support, with compiled batched float64 inference reaching 445 waveforms/s on an A100 GPU.
papers.authors: Jameson Dong

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.
papers.authors: Joe Wiedemann, Roman Kolevatov, Jianyang Fu, Joelle-Marie Begin, Nate Otto, Felix St-Amour, Lyman Page, Henry LeDuc, Peter Day, Saptarshi Chaudhuri

papers.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
papers.abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.
papers.authors: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, Edson Otoniel

papers.title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In the sampled configurations, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the ISCO. For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. The resulting image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.
papers.authors: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, Edson Otoniel, Muhammad Israr Aslam, Francisco S. N. Lobo

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.
papers.authors: Julien Malartre

papers.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
papers.abstract: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(\alpha'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.
papers.authors: Mohammad R. Garousi

papers.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
papers.abstract: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states, which concentrate at a particular $R$-charge. This division has a precise mathematical meaning as two different types of cohomologies of the Higgs branch target space. We argue that a natural probe of BPS chaos in these models is the Berry/Chern curvature. In the case of the Gepner model, we use localization techniques in an auxiliary two-dimensional CFT to compute the curvature, its RMT properties, and deviations from it.
papers.authors: Micha Berkooz, Trivko Kukolj, Ohad Mamroud, Josef Seitz

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.abstract: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.
papers.authors: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

papers.title: Imaginary elements and crystals for quantum groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of stable imaginary elements in quantum groups and use crystal basis theory to construct explicit one-parameter families of such elements for all finite types. We show that all of Leclerc's examples of imaginary elements are stable imaginary. Using the generalized quantum Schur--Weyl duality, we also construct explicit examples of corresponding imaginary modules over quantum affine algebras of untwisted affine types.
papers.authors: Kyu-Hwan Lee, Euiyong Park

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers under conditions on local mixing and local energy estimates. We verify these conditions for one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature and for finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.
papers.authors: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu

papers.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
papers.abstract: We derive the primordial $\langle\zeta\zeta h\rangle$, $\langle\zeta hh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.
papers.authors: Y. A. Ageeva, M. A. Stepanov

papers.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
papers.abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_{\chi})$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.
papers.authors: Yumeng Wu, Jie Xiao

papers.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
papers.abstract: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.
papers.authors: John F. Dawson

papers.title: Optical appearance and radial stability of thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics and relate optical appearance to local radial stability. Finite magnetic self-energy fixes the seed mass and links the charge to the nonlinear scale. Transparent disks illuminate both exteriors, and independent Maxwell rays reach a static observer. For the standard Born--Infeld magnetic subset, static emitters are compared with circular motion outside the innermost stable orbit and an inward plunge below it. The wormhole--black-hole intensity difference separates light transmitted from the opposite disk from emission removed by throat excision. The illuminated inner edge depends on the admitted disk crossings rather than the throat radius alone. Increasing charge contracts the critical curve in the sampled family. Motion suppresses the face-on intensities and produces an azimuthal brightness contrast at inclination. A broad outer shoulder arises from partial compensation between decreasing emissivity and increasing circular frequency weights, before the profiles recover a decaying weak-field tail. All nine prescribed throats satisfy a local radial stability test for a calibrated modified cosmic Chaplygin law describing an effective exotic layer. An analytic identity establishes radial instability at the selected unstable photon orbit for any finite density-only constitutive slope. The resulting images relate transmitted radiation and emitter kinematics to the material support of the throat, providing a controlled comparison with the matched seed black hole.
papers.authors: Jonathan A. Rebou\c{c}as, Edson Otoniel, Muhammad Israr Aslam, Rabia Saleem

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
papers.abstract: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.
papers.authors: Arsen R. Melikyan, Aleksandr Pinzul

papers.title: Deglobalising the fit: how to search for physics beyond vacuum General Relativity in LISA catalogues
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna will observe up to $\sim 10^{7}$ overlapping signals, which have to be characterised simultaneously with a \emph{global} fit. This is a challenge for model comparison since rerunning the global fit for every model of interest, including deviations from vacuum General Relativity, is computationally demanding. An alternative is a two-step post-processing strategy: a first global fit with vacuum models only, after which selected target sources are reanalysed under a different model with all other sources subtracted. We show that in this strategy a beyond-vacuum effect in a target source can be partly absorbed by the overlapping \textit{nuisance} sources in the first fit, subtracted with them, and never reach the reanalysis. In the linear-signal approximation, the loss in reported detection significance is captured by a single number, the \emph{masking ratio} $\mathcal{R}\in[0,1]$: a deviation the global fit would detect at $n_\sigma$ is reported by post-processing at $\mathcal{R}\,n_\sigma$, and, for a single beyond-vacuum parameter, bounds in null tests are reported too tight by the same factor. We show how to compute $\mathcal{R}$ from the posterior samples of the vacuum global fit, and give an algorithm that ranks the nuisance sources by how much of the effect each can absorb, so that only the most correlated ones need to be refitted with the target. We validate our method with full Markov-chain Monte Carlo inference on a toy model of 21 overlapping chirping sinusoids, one of which carries a small non-linear chirp that represents the missed physics. Using our post-processing recipe, we are able to recover the global-fit result on the beyond-vacuum parameter to within $0.15\sigma$ by refitting only 4 of the 20 nuisance sources. This method can serve as a basis for tests of General Relativity in realistic LISA mock datasets.
papers.authors: Francisco Duque, Jonathan Gair

papers.title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
papers.abstract: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.
papers.authors: Matteo Braglia, Gabriele Franciolini, Nadir Ijaz, Marco Peloso

papers.title: Local failure of disjoint additivity
papers.abstract: Local Gauss constraints can prevent commuting regional algebras from generating the full algebra assigned to their union. We investigate disjoint additivity on the full magnetic physical subspace of finite-group quantum-double models while keeping the original lattice edge supports fixed. Every finite non-Abelian group exhibits a counterexample on vertex-disjoint regions contained within a contractible disk on a regular square torus. For a fixed eight-edge loop and a specified peripheral contact family, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and the selected contacts cover all four interior faces of the loop. Leaving an inner face uncovered restores additivity; for the same loop, so does any second region avoiding the specified testing neighborhood. A peripheral projector restricts the exterior tests on a loop transition, allowing their product to preserve the constraints even when the loop factor does not. We construct union observables that deterministically separate orthogonal relative-sign superpositions that yield identical outcome statistics under every measurement whose effects lie in the generated regional algebra. For a separate wrapping pair, we also determine the complete matrix-block inclusion, identifying missing center-orbit coherences, and construct an independent regular-torus counterexample for the eight-dimensional Kac-Paljutkin Hopf algebra.
papers.authors: Yi Liang

papers.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. These are double affine versions of the quantum affine wreath algebras of Rosso and Savage. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite cyclic group, we obtain new double affine versions of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the supercentre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.
papers.authors: Niccol\`o Mattarei

papers.title: Quantum-classical algorithm interpolation for spatial search
papers.abstract: Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time $\mathrm{HT}$. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We derive a parameterised family of hybrid quantum-classical spatial search algorithms that continuously interpolates between the classical and fully coherent quantum regimes, trading off circuit depth for total query complexity. For any $\gamma\in[0,1]$, our algorithms use circuits of depth $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{\gamma/2})$ and find a marked vertex with constant success probability at total cost $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma}\mathsf{S} + \mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma/2}(\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{C}))$, where $\mathsf{S}$, $\mathsf{U}$, and $\mathsf{C}$ denote the setup, update, and checking costs, respectively. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.
papers.authors: Diogo Ramos, Duarte Magano

papers.title: Experimental Demonstration of 7-Dimensional N-Vector Model with Dimensional Inflation and Annealing
papers.abstract: We report the first experimental realization of a physical system described by a high-dimensional Hamiltonian comprising up to seven dimensions. Our setup is based on a holographic optical computer, which realizes a dimensional inflation by spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower dimensional systems. We demonstrate an $N$-vector model, with applications in field theory and computing. The approach is scalable and enables table-top implementation of high-dimensional theoretical models, and novel methods for combinatorial optimization. We experimentally demonstrate dimensional annealing: by dynamically reducing the number of dimensions, the ground state of an Ising model is found in complex graphs by an adiabatic evolution from high-dimensional spaces.
papers.authors: Daniele Veraldi, Marcello Calvanese Strinati, Paolo Charlesworth, Matteo Spaziani, Silvia Gentilini, Davide Pierangeli, Claudio Conti

papers.title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
papers.abstract: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed; the data are real analytic and asymptotically flat, with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.80480168\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=\pi k^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. A scaling symmetry of the mode problem generates further solvable families, whose simplest member has the elementary seed function $q=\frac12\log[1+4a^2\rho^2/(\rho^2+z^2+a^2)^2]$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.
papers.authors: Piotr Koc

papers.title: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
papers.abstract: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of between triangles on wax tablets and in the sky, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of transformation (i.e. rotation, affine canonical transformation) on the page and within the atom. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.
papers.authors: Tzula B. Propp, Chris S. Jackson

papers.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
papers.abstract: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We compute the complete one-loop triangle at general masses, with its collider signal in closed form to all orders in the squeezed-limit expansion, and give the triple-exchange bispectrum at arbitrary heavy masses as a double series that converges at every physical shape. The loop reduction also applies at strong mixing.
papers.authors: Amara McCune

papers.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
papers.abstract: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tilde\Omega_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta$, with $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta'=q\theta+\pi(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tilde\Omega_I=2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.
papers.authors: Rin Takada

papers.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
papers.abstract: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, gravitational characteristic conditions reduce to inequalities in two local invariants. In five dimensions, they imply $R_h^2>\tilde\alpha$ for regular marginal spheres on the GR branch and the sharp Kretschmann bound $\tilde\alpha^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. Under the stated finite-domain hypotheses, spherical continuation places the first characteristic degeneration on a smooth background. Within this setting, a future marginal sphere formed while the characteristic conditions hold throughout the preceding evolution forces their later failure. For every allowed radius, separately chosen complete smooth data form marginal spheres with mass arbitrarily close to the sharp lower bound; in six dimensions both radius and mass can be arbitrarily small. At sufficiently large scale, complete nonspherical data with weak curvature contain marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ metrics under a spectral condition. These surfaces are outermost and strictly stable. A separate Berger family has arbitrarily small area at one common ADM mass; formation from untrapped data remains open. Exact nonspherical developments have smoothly convergent initial data but tidal tensors that fail to converge to the reference values at a chosen time after the reference core loses hyperbolicity. Under local geometric uniqueness for developments of the same data on overlaps connecting the initial slice to the observers, classical existence on a common region and continuous dependence of the tidal tensor cannot both hold. The constructed solutions themselves extend smoothly. Fixed time averages converge on the controlled interval, but this does not establish a predictive effective-field-theory continuation.
papers.authors: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja

papers.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: A streaming algorithm can keep classical or quantum memory, and its input arrives in adversarial or random order. Each resource alone is known to beat the basic model exponentially, but it was not known whether random order can help a quantum algorithm. We compare the four models by exponential space separations: every pair is separated on some problem and tied on another, and the two models with one resource each beat each other on different problems, one direction for random inputs, by concurrent work of Bouland, Ding, and Jain. The new phenomenon is that quantum memory and random order together can be exponentially stronger than each alone. We show this on a streaming version of Hidden Matching in which the bits of $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ arrive many times and $m\le\sqrt{N}$ matching requests must be answered on arrival. In random order a quantum algorithm uses $O(\log N\log m)$ space, while classical algorithms need $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$, and quantum algorithms need $\Omega(m)$ when all data comes before the requests. Two properties explain this. Consumability: answering a request destroys the quantum state. Replenishment: the state can be rebuilt from bits that keep arriving, which random order supplies and a data-first order does not. We prove that one quantum message answering $m$ Hidden Matching requests needs $\Omega(m)$ qubits, a conjecture of Gilboa, Jain, and McClean, for $m\le N^{1/2-\delta}$. The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.
papers.authors: Nadezhda Voronova

papers.title: Beyond ideal cavities: quantifying the impact of cavity dissipation on light-matter strong coupling
papers.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities promises to reshape molecular reactivity and properties in a non-invasive and tunable way, yet cavity experiments remain notoriously difficult to interpret and reproduce, highlighting the need for accurate theoretical predictions. Significant progress has been made through ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) methods, but these generally assume ideal, lossless cavity fields, an approximation commonly justified by the assumption that cavity losses are negligible and by the need to keep the methods computationally tractable. Here we show that this approximation is far from innocent: incorporating cavity dissipation through the experimentally accessible quality factor Q reduces the Rabi splitting of p-nitroaniline by more than 10% and red-shifts the minimum polaritonic gap by 0.24 eV, even when the system remains firmly in the strong-coupling regime. This implies that convergence towards the ideal-cavity limit requires quality factors substantially larger than those needed to establish strong coupling itself. Our approach, based on a damped harmonic oscillator description of the cavity field and a time-dependent unitary transformation yielding a real Hermitian Hamiltonian, is demonstrated here within the quantum electrodynamics coupled-cluster singles and doubles framework (QED-CCSD). Its general formulation allows straightforward integration into existing ab initio QED frameworks without increasing the computational cost of the underlying methods, providing a practical and efficient route to quantitatively account for realistic cavity conditions in first-principles simulations of molecular systems in cavities.
papers.authors: Giovanna Bruno, Enrico Busani, Lorenzo Gialli, Rosario Roberto Riso, Enrico Ronca

papers.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
papers.abstract: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,\Delta)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $\Delta$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.
papers.authors: Ziyuan Wang, Shaojie Wang, Jiaju Zhang

papers.title: Optimal Resource Scaling for Early Fault Tolerant Iterative Quantum Phase Estimation under Cost Error Tradeoffs
papers.abstract: The iterative quantum phase estimation algorithm (IPEA) is better suited for NISQ and early fault-tolerant hardware compared to the original algorithm, which requires the inverse quantum Fourier transform. However, current error mitigation and correction implementations lead to imperfect unitaries, causing erroneous phase feedback in IPEA. To improve the reliability of phase bits is to repeat the k^th iteration for the 2^k-th power of the unitary $N_k^*$ times, followed by a majority decision. However, due to variations in their circuit complexities, different iterations incur varying resource costs ($w_k$) and different per-shot error probabilities ($q_k$). Given tight resource constraints, we ask what the optimal number $\{N_k^*: 1\le k \le L\}$ of shots per bit is: $$\arg \max_{\{N_k\}} \mathbb{P}(\text{all } L \text{ bits correct}) \text{s.t.} \sum_{k=1}^L w_k N_k \le W$$ We construct upper and lower surrogate objectives via concentration and anti-concentration inequalities and prove an asymptotic optimality guarantee for whenever the budget satisfies $W = \sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}(\ln L + \omega(1))$, where $c_k=-\ln\left(2\sqrt{\left(1-\frac{q_k}{2} \right) \frac{q_k}{2}}\right)$, which, for $q_k\ll 1$, is proportional to $\ln\frac{1}{q_k}$. Optimizing the tractable lower surrogate yields a true success probability within a $(1-o(1))$ factor of the exact optimum. We observe that when resources are abundant, $W \gg \ln(L)\sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}$, optimal allocations are proportional to $\ 1/c_k$. However, when resources are sufficient but not abundant, $(\ln(L)+\omega(1))\sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\le W \le O\left( \ln(L)\cdot \sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\right)$, an additional $-\frac{1}{c_k}\ln\frac{w_k}{c_k}$ correction accounts for error propagation from less-significant to more-significant bits.
papers.authors: Mrudula A Mahindrakar, Avhishek Chatterjee

papers.title: Measurement-induced dynamics and emergent symmetries of particles moving in a one-dimensional lattice
papers.abstract: Continuous measurements simultaneously reveal and modify the dynamics of a quantum system. In this work we consider the tunneling motion of particles between the sites of a one-dimensional lattice. We investigate how weak continuous probing of the occupation of a single lattice site induces entanglement and selects definite values for system properties such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry. Our simulations show how continuous measurement can steer systems of two and three particles, with no prior permutation symmetry, into stable bosonic, fermionic and parastatistical symmetry sectors.
papers.authors: Salvatore Di Lorenzo, Klaus M{\o}lmer

papers.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.
papers.authors: Matteo Tedde, Davide Girolami

papers.title: Asymptotic Throat as a Minimal Geometric Alternative to the Singularity in Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: A basic question in the study of regular black holes is whether the Schwarzschild singularity can be replaced by a geodesically complete interior while retaining a single horizon. An asymptotic throat offers a minimal geometric realization of this possibility. The areal radius approaches a finite, nonzero limit at a future internal infinity, without requiring a change in spatial topology or a bounce. We extend the geometric analysis beyond monotone contraction to interiors in which the areal radius oscillates about its limit. For both null-type and spacelike-type inner ends, we derive a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for causal geodesic completeness and criteria for bounded curvature in parallel-propagated frames. Explicit examples of both types have complete inner ends and satisfy all four standard energy conditions at sufficiently large exterior radii. Applying these criteria to the oscillatory solution of the B\"ohmer--Vandersloot model of effective loop quantum gravity, we find a causally complete spacelike-type inner end. Its scalar curvature invariants converge to those of the limiting Nariai-type solution. Along each radial null geodesic, however, a parallel-propagated curvature component is unbounded along a sequence of turning points as the affine parameter tends to infinity.
papers.authors: Yi-Bo Liang, Hong-Rong Li

papers.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
papers.abstract: Axis bending of a mode-evolution coupler realizes the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol [Opt. Express 34, 1214 (2026)]. We identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, which in a real two-mode supermode basis is purely $\sigma_y$: exactly the form of the CD term, and the one form that detuning and coupling cannot supply. Equating the two gives the axis slope in closed form, as a ratio of two matrix elements at a single cross section, or $\dot{x}_0=\dot\theta/(\gamma\Delta\beta^{2})$ in coupled-mode variables. It agrees with a numerical offset search to 0.3% and is shown to be the earlier curvature condition viewed from the Kramers-Henneberger frame. Beam propagation simulations compare the bent coupler directly with the unitary-transformation realization built from the same reference structure: the two reach supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000 against 0.886 for the untreated coupler, show comparable bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, and differ inside the device by the frame transformation that relates them.
papers.authors: Yu-kai Lee, Shuo-Yen Tseng

papers.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
papers.abstract: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.
papers.authors: Suraj Gavhale, Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov, Oem Trivedi

papers.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
papers.abstract: Two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions arise from differential recursions with rational initial data: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. At order $p=3$, their rational coefficients yield the triangles OEIS A140136 and A336110, together with a positive palindromic numerator triangle for the odd sector. In general, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn companions, and an explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual series. The Narayana quadratic ($p=2$) and the $S_4$-symmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia quartic ($p=3$, with two tetrahedral edge resolvents) serve as explicit low-order benchmarks. For every $p \ge 3$, we prove that the distinguished reduced generating function has exact algebraic degree $2(p-1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x,h^{p-1})$ and that every Horn companion is algebraic. Over $h$, the rational uniformization lifts to the Fermat curve $s^{p-1}+w^{p-1}=1$ of genus $(p-2)(p-3)/2$ with generic monodromy and Galois group $S_{2(p-1)}$. This uniform cover establishes the universal boundary factorization at $H=h^{p-1}=0$ and explains the cubic characteristic factor $\mathcal{A}_p^3$ (carrying a projective $S_3$ action) in the discriminant via $(2,3)$-cusp geometry, illustrated by exact sextic and octic equations and higher-order slices. Conversely, a nonexact differential on the Fermat curve combined with full $S_{2(p-1)}$ monodromy proves that the distinguished self-dual function is transcendental for all $p \ge 4$. The complete factorization of the generic reduced discriminant remains open.
papers.authors: S. Voloshyn

papers.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
papers.abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.
papers.authors: M. A. Rajabpour

papers.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.abstract: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.
papers.authors: Shi Gu, Qiang Wen, Haocheng Zhong, Yiwei Zhong

papers.title: Coherence-generating power deviation: Fluctuations and input selectivity beyond average coherence generation
papers.abstract: Coherence-generating power (CGP) tells how much coherence a quantum process produces on average from incoherent inputs, but an average can hide where that coherence comes from. We introduce the coherence-generating power deviation (CGPD), the standard deviation of the generated Hilbert--Schmidt coherence over the uniform simplex of incoherent states. CGPD turns coherence generation into a landscape: a small value signals robust production across input populations, whereas a large value reveals selective conversion of particular population imbalances. By representing unitary coherence generation as a quadratic response on population space, we obtain exact first and second moments in arbitrary finite dimension. We prove that every nontrivial unitary generator must fluctuate, and we separate this unavoidable isotropic fluctuation from excess anisotropy. The resulting distinction between average strength and input selectivity has direct consequences for benchmarking, reliability guarantees, input-ensemble susceptibility, and four-copy measurement protocols; it also extends naturally to unital quantum channels. Matched quantum-walk and quasiperiodic-transport examples show that topology and localization can leave CGP unchanged while substantially changing CGPD, revealing structure invisible to the mean alone.
papers.authors: Kyoungho Cho, Jeongho Bang

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Slowly Rotating Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study slowly rotating, nonlinearly charged black holes in arbitrary spacetime dimension $d \geq 4$, using a generalized Lense--Thirring ansatz. Working to linear order in the rotation parameters, we solve the Einstein--nonlinear electrodynamics (NLE) field equations for restricted theories ${\cal L}({\cal S})$ depending on single invariant. We provide an extension of the four-dimensional "No Go theorem" proven in ArXiv:2203.01919 and demonstrate the uniqueness of Maxwell theory in $d \geq 4$. Similar to four dimensions, it is proven that the standard rotation generating trick fails to produce full rotating solutions for any nontrivial NLE in higher dimensions. We identify a family of NLE theories admitting slowly rotating solutions with vector potentials encoding rotation effect in Maxwell-like manner; in four dimensions this reproduces the previously found RegMax theory, while in $d\geq4$ we obtain the corresponding electric potential in closed form and the associated Lagrangian implicitly as a function of the radial coordinate.
papers.authors: Tayebeh Tahamtan

papers.title: Coherent Floquet quantum reservoirs for molecular property prediction
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses observables of a driven quantum system to make predictions from a sequence of inputs. The robust subharmonic response of discrete time crystals (DTCs) has motivated their use as quantum reservoirs. Here we develop a DTC-QRC architecture for molecular property prediction in which successive graph events or surface-hopping frames drive a fixed Floquet reservoir. An adjustable reset probability controls how long earlier inputs influence the state, and measurements of the final polarizations and pair correlations yield a feature vector of fixed dimension. Weak reset favors classification of inhibitor activity and blood-brain barrier penetration from long graph prefixes, whereas forecasting electronic gaps in ethene favors greater weight on recent nuclear motion. With nonlinear decoding, DTC-QRC outperforms an echo-state network on these tasks at matched input lengths and readout widths. For gap forecasting with this decoder and final-state readout, the dissipative reservoirs share a low-error drive window near the DTC transition reported for related spin chains. Dephasing lowers prediction performance in both molecular applications. In six-qubit classification without programmed reset on the Quafu superconducting quantum cloud platform, pair correlations retain more of their noise-free predictive power toward the DTC side, and the full readout performs best near the transition among the drives tested. The architecture provides a common framework for molecular screening and time-resolved property prediction using quantum reservoir computing.
papers.authors: Luofei Wang, Da Zhang, Congren Wang, Yiming Li, Yuxiao Yang, Xuan Zhang, Xuefeng Cui, Zhang-Qi Yin

papers.title: Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
papers.abstract: We develop a systematic framework for timelike entanglement in a two-dimensional free real scalar field, connecting spacetime density matrices with Lorentzian twist-operator correlators through independent microscopic and continuum calculations. Extending Gaussian diagonalization to generally non-Hermitian reduced operators, we determine their complete nonzero spectra in the generic regular case, together with all integer R\'enyi moments. The real-time replica construction relates these moments to twist correlators, with quantitative agreement in both magnitude and phase for the full four-point function on a circle, the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary two-point functions, and the massive form-factor predictions. In the massless continuum theory with Dirichlet boundaries, we further establish a finite causally connected window in which all integer moments are real, while the even moments are strictly positive for arbitrary initial states. For Gaussian states, all integer moments are strictly positive, and the resulting R\'enyi entropies are real. These results demonstrate that causal connectedness alone is not sufficient for a nonzero imaginary part of timelike R\'enyi entropy.
papers.authors: Hao-yu Wang, Wu-zhong Guo

papers.title: The phase coordinates transformation in Moyal noncommutative framework 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator and Painlev\'e second equation
papers.abstract: This work aims to explore the physical application of Moyal noncom- mutative formalism with the the presentation of new transformations which connect the old canonical coordinates to purly noncommuting phase coordi- nates through the parameters describe the Moyal noncommutative deforma- tion. These transformations are consistent with the Moyal noncommunica- tive brackets and build sixteen components traceless anti-symmetric tensor. This formalism incorporates space-space and space-momentum noncommu- taivity rather then noncommutativity (Heisenberg quantum commutation ) only for the canonical coordinates. The transformations imply to construct noncommutative analogs of 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its superintegrability and Painlev\'e second equation. The associated deformed Hamiltonians additionally involve some extra symmetries and reveal a deep physical understanding of about the additional symmetries with noncommunicative structure. The Painlev\'e second noncommutative coordinates transformation are also efficiently applied to generate the first Yablonskii Vorobev polynomial with Painlev\'e second parameter transformation.
papers.authors: Irfan Mahmood

papers.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
papers.abstract: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $\gamma$, scaling as $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} - \beta_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $\beta$-$\gamma$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $\sigma_{2\gamma-\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $\sigma_{\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $\gamma$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $\sigma_\beta\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $\gamma$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $\sigma_{\gamma}\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.
papers.authors: Mohsen Khodadi, Salvatore Capozziello

papers.title: Classification of abstract Bose field models
papers.abstract: We classify a class of abstract Bose field models in quantum field theory up to unitary equivalence. The class includes abstract free Bose field models, abstract van Hove--Miyatake models, and infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models. Moreover, as an application of our classification, we classify quadratic interaction models. In particular, our results answer a question of A. Arai concerning the classification of infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models.
papers.authors: Yasumichi Matsuzawa

papers.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
papers.abstract: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.
papers.authors: Jianan Wang, Long Cui, Bin Wu

papers.title: Teleparallel formulation of $E_{8(8)}$ Exceptional Field Theory
papers.abstract: The potential of $E_{8(8)} \times \mathbb{R}^+$ exceptional field theory, suited for studying three-dimensional maximally supersymmetric compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, is derived in teleparallel formulation. This means that, starting from an ansatz of the most general combination of the quadratic scalar contractions of the intrinsic torsion, which is manifestly invariant under generalised diffeomorphisms, one selects the potential by imposing the invariance under infinitesimal rotation of the maximal compact subgroup of the duality group. The teleparallel formulation makes manifest at geometric level the preeminent role of the intrinsic torsion in studying compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, where the intrinsic torsion is identified with the embedding tensor of the resulting gauged supergravity.
papers.authors: Davide Rovere

papers.title: Fermion mass hierarchies in a three-generation Clifford model
papers.abstract: We examine whether an algebraic model of three fermion generations based on the complex Clifford algebra $\mathbb C\ell(10)$, in which an $S_3$ family symmetry relates the generations, can reproduce the observed mass hierarchies of the charged leptons and down quarks. Taking the internal Gram matrix as the fermion kinetic metric, we show that the original Yukawa interaction, with complex coefficients, gives precisely those ordered mass triples $0\leq m_1\leq m_2\leq m_3$ for which $m_3\leq m_1+2m_2$. This restriction excludes the observed hierarchies in both sectors and persists when the right-acting Higgs operator is allowed to range over the full Clifford algebra. This obstruction motivates a second Yukawa contraction in which a projector, constructed from the difference between an internal charge operator and its family average, acts from the left. The resulting interaction preserves the gauge and family symmetries and uses the same three Higgs doublets. With both contractions present, there is a fixed coupling ratio at which the two successive mass ratios in a single sector become arbitrarily large along a real vacuum path. Separately, a rational interval calculation establishes that one real Higgs vacuum, with different coupling ratios in the two sectors, reproduces the chosen running masses of the charged leptons and down quarks. A softly broken three-doublet potential realises this vacuum as a global minimum at tree level. The additional neutral scalars have flavour-changing couplings, and their exchange at a common mass of $2000\,\mathrm{TeV}$ satisfies the neutral-meson mixing criterion and the $\mu\to3e$ contact-interaction test considered here.
papers.authors: Ye Zhou, Niels Gresnigt

papers.title: The inverse eigenvalue problem for Partial Transposes of Two-Qubit States and Sharp Entanglement Bounds from Their Low-order Moments
papers.abstract: The negativity of a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho$ can be determined without full state tomography by measuring sufficiently many partial-transpose (PT) moments on multiple copies of $\rho$. When the available copies allow only low-order PT moments to be estimated reliably, how tightly do these moments bound the negativity? For two-qubit states, we answer this question by solving the inverse eigenvalue problem for their partial transposes: an ordered eigenvalue list $(x,y,z,-q)$, with $x\ge y\ge z\ge0$, $q>0$, and $x+y+z-q=1$, occurs as the spectrum of $\rho^{\Gamma_B}$ for some two-qubit state $\rho$ if and only if $q\le y$ and $qy\le xz$. The quantum steering ellipsoid of the $X$ state constructed to prove sufficiency gives a geometric interpretation of the two equality cases. We use these inequalities to determine the exact range of negativity compatible with the two lowest nontrivial PT moments, $p_2=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^2]$ and $p_3=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^3]$. We also compare our sharp negativity bounds with estimates from several existing methods and quantify how much the inverse eigenvalue constraints narrow the negativity interval as a function of $p_3$ at fixed $p_2$. Beyond negativity, we extend this approach to derive attainable bounds for the maximal CHSH value and directional coherent information at fixed $p_2$ and $p_3$. Our result establishes the strongest possible bounds on the negativity of an unknown two-qubit state from just two experimentally accessible PT moments, and shows the potential for obtaining similarly sharp bounds from low-order PT moments by solving the corresponding inverse eigenvalue problem for higher-dimensional bipartite states.
papers.authors: Ruoting Dou, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen

papers.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction \xi of the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming \xi\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
papers.authors: M. G. Belyakova, R. Nevzorov

papers.title: Brans Dicke scalar-tensor gravity and unimodular FRW cosmology with Coleman-Weinberg potential
papers.abstract: As an alternative gravity theories with respect to General Relativity, the Brans-Dicke scalar-tensor model is well known, in which the Brans-Dicke parameter the controls the best fit observational, and so its cosmological model is studied in the literature well. On the other side, the Coleman-Weinberg self-interaction scalar field potential coming from radiation corrections of Feynman diagrams is used to describe the best fit cosmic inflation phase and reheating phase. We study inflation in unimodular Brans-Dicke gravity with a Coleman-Weinberg potential. We investigate the observational constraints on the Brans-Dicke parameter \(\omega\) and identify its allowed range in light of current cosmological data. Also, in the slow-roll regime, we derive inflation parameters and study the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ in terms of the model parameters, and determine the region of the parameter space allowed by observations. Comparing these predictions with the P-ACT-LB-BK18 constraints, we find that the model is consistent with the data at the $95\%$ CL level for $77\lesssim\omega\lesssim1148$ and within the $ 68\% $ CL for $134\lesssim\omega\lesssim272$.
papers.authors: Manda Malekpour, Hossein Ghaffarnejad

papers.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
papers.abstract: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.
papers.authors: Hari Krishnan SV, Andreas Winter

papers.title: 3D trapping of a meta-atom in an intensity minimum
papers.abstract: High-refractive-index particles have recently attracted a growing interest in optical manipulation, enabling to engineer optical forces through electromagnetic Mie resonances. Unlike standard silica particles, which exhibit trap frequencies mainly determined by material density, resonant meta-atoms formed by high-index particles enable qualitatively new trapping behaviors. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trapping of resonant silicon particles in an optical standing wave. A direct comparison of silicon and silica highlights the fundamental differences in their optical force scaling and trapping dynamics. Beyond conventional trapping at intensity-maxima, we demonstrate deterministic and stable three-dimensional trapping of silicon nanoparticles in optical intensity minima, a regime that remains inaccessible for silica particles. Drawing a mesoscopic analogy with blue-detuned atom trapping, our results establish meta-atoms as a versatile approach to further extend the optical manipulation tool box towards accessing novel trapping regimes e.g. in close proximity to a surface.
papers.authors: Bin Lu, Adeel Afridi, Nadine Meyer, Romain Quidant

papers.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
papers.abstract: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev.
