A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.
papers.authors: Kedar Mal, A. N. Agnihotri, Sugam Kumar, Wolfgang Quint, Manuel Vogel

papers.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $\Delta$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[\Delta]=(V/V')\Delta'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $\Delta n_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|\Delta n_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $\Delta n_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.
papers.authors: Ekapob Kulchoakrungsun, Phongpichit Channuie, Daris Samart

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.
papers.authors: Md Rezwanul Islam, ASM Shihavuddin

papers.title: History-Dependent Mode Selection in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
papers.abstract: We study finite-rate mode selection among competing Landau-unstable modes in a holographic superfluid. The first mode to reach a prescribed amplitude need not be the instantaneously fastest-growing one. Time-dependent linear evolution on the driven homogeneous background closely reproduces the modal amplitudes obtained from full bulk evolution. Protocols with identical present driving conditions can reverse the relative ordering of two modes. For the controlled histories studied here, the change in their logarithmic amplitude ratio is well approximated by the excess accumulated differential QNM gain.
papers.authors: Bo-Xuan Ge

papers.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
papers.abstract: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.
papers.authors: Arpit Raj, Johannes Mitscherling, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

papers.title: Algebraic versus physical uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators
papers.abstract: We give explicit determinant counterexamples to the uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators from their degrees and simultaneous pair zeros. At seven points the solution space has dimension seven; Bose symmetry removes six directions and leaves the Hodges line. At eight points a two-dimensional Bose-symmetric space remains. Regular integer-spinor configurations distinguish these deformations from the Hodges numerator. On the eight-point plane, collinear factorization, the leading positive-helicity soft coefficient and ordinary BCFW decay each select the Hodges line. For $n\ge5$, we prove two results on the full fixed-degree, common-denominator ansatz, without pair-zero conditions. Complete collinear residue functions on all pairs determine at most one numerator; Bose symmetry makes one channel sufficient. The splitting law and a normalized lower-point amplitude supply the boundary function, starting from an explicit five-point seed. With Bose symmetry, $O(Z^{-1})$ decay under one fixed same-helicity shift at generic conserving kinematics also selects the Hodges line. Normalized collinear and soft data fix the eight-point scale; the homogeneous shift condition leaves one constant per multiplicity.
papers.authors: Lin Mai, Yaobo Zhang

papers.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
papers.abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.
papers.authors: Manuel A. Mart\'inez S\'anchez, Christoph Adam, Danial Saadatmand

papers.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
papers.abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.
papers.authors: Marcin Rudzi\'nski, Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andrei B. Klimov, Luis L. S\'{a}nchez-Soto, Karol \.Zyczkowski

papers.title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
papers.abstract: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = \rho$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $\alpha_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /\delta_n)$, where $\alpha_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $\delta_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.
papers.authors: Sidan A, Tom Banks, Willy Fischler

papers.title: Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
papers.abstract: Mapping anisotropies in the gravitational-wave background (GWB) requires choosing a basis to represent the sky intensity, such as pixel and spherical harmonic bases. Each introduces a truncation---e.g., a number of pixels or a maximum multipole l_max---often set by a naive counting argument that relate the number of measurable modes to the number of independent cross-correlations, N_pair, in a pulsar timing array (PTA). However, such truncations can lead to reconstruction artifacts, as they do not reflect the true information content of the PTA response. Increasing the value of truncation parameters spans the observable space better but reveals poorly constrained modes, making the inverse problem ill conditioned and requiring regularization. A natural approach is to restrict the reconstruction to a well-measured subspace via principal maps, defined by the dominant eigenmodes of the detector response (or Fisher) matrix. However, these maps are not a fundamental parametrization of the sky but, rather, are derived from an underlying representation---such as a pixelization or a spherical harmonic expansion. While their explicit form depends on basis choice, they can span the \textit{same subspace} when the underlying representation is sufficiently complete. Here, we show that reconstructed anisotropy maps via different bases are equivalent, provided they retain the same information content, i.e., span the same principal subspace. As illustrative cases, we consider a toy model for PTA configuration and several GWB anisotropy shapes: point source, an extended source with deterministic anisotropy, and a statistical isotropic background, along with its summary statistic---the angular power spectrum. Although the reconstructions are equivalent, their computational costs can differ. We conclude with brief comments on the construction of principal maps for ground-based interferometers.
papers.authors: Deepali Agarwal

papers.title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Quantum Control
papers.abstract: We develop certified lower bounds on structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margins for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for the trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the nominal connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method whose finite runs return lower bounds on the distance to the first threshold contact. The fidelity may touch the threshold without falling below it. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that the returned bounds vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.
papers.authors: S. P. O'Neil, F. C. Langbein, C. A. Weidner, E. A. Jonckheere, S. Schirmer

papers.title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
papers.abstract: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $\Gamma/2\pi=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $\omega_0/2\pi=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $\omega_0\Gamma$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.
papers.authors: Azusa Sawada, Hina Nakano, Kanta Watanabe, Gaku Ohashi, Shota Okumura, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

papers.title: Quantum resetting with memory
papers.abstract: We introduce a quantum stochastic resetting protocol with uniform memory, in which each resetting event returns the system to a state visited at a time chosen uniformly from its entire history. The resulting dynamics is nonunitary, non-Markovian and a direct quantum generalization of the classical preferential relocation model. Working in the energy eigenbasis, we derive the exact evolution of every density-matrix element for an arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonian and show that the Hamiltonian enters the dynamics only through the corresponding Bohr frequencies. This leads to a natural distinction between two classes of quantum systems: gapped and gapless. In \emph{gapped systems} (systems with a discrete energy spectrum), while the diagonal elements remain unchanged, the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in the energy eigenbasis decay algebraically with a continuously varying exponent and with an amplitude that oscillates periodically in $\log t$. The system therefore approaches a stationary state that is independent of the resetting rate and retains a strong memory of the initial state. In \emph{gapless systems} (systems with a continuous energy spectrum), arbitrarily small Bohr frequencies prevent stationarity. Instead, the position distribution spreads on the universal (ultra-slow) scale $\log(rt)/r$, independently of the initial state and of the details of the Hamiltonian. We illustrate these results with a two-level system, a harmonic oscillator, and a free quantum particle, and contrast them with their classical counterparts.
papers.authors: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar

papers.title: Later Information Can Outperform Earlier Information in Query-Assisted Quantum State Discrimination
papers.abstract: Classical partial information about the states can increase the success probability in quantum state discrimination. An important aspect is its timing, whether it is given before or after the measurement. One might expect that later information is less useful than earlier information, because earlier information can still be stored and exploited at a later stage. Surprisingly, we show that the classical information can be more useful if it arrives after the measurement. We present a framework for state discrimination in which the sender provides classical information in response to a request from the receiver, which we refer to as a query. In some cases, nonorthogonal states can be perfectly discriminated when the query is allowed to depend on the measurement outcome. We give a general method for finding the optimal strategy in this setting, which turns out to be the standard minimum-error discrimination problem for an auxiliary ensemble. We show that for any number of states greater than two, there exists a qubit ensemble exhibiting an advantage of later information.
papers.authors: Hanwool Lee, Teiko Heinosaari

papers.title: Directional Anisotropic Sensitivity Curves for Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract: After two decades of observations, pulsar timing array collaborations have reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background, most likely sourced by an inspiraling population of supermassive black hole binaries. Because that population is finite, anisotropy in the background is inevitable, producing hotspots on the sky that track the loudest binaries. Building on the Fisher formalism for anisotropic backgrounds, we recast the directional Fisher information as effective sensitivity curves on the sky, distinguishing the radiometer and full-Fisher estimators, along with a sky-weighted curve that reduces the anisotropic sky to a single spectrum and recovers the standard isotropic curve in the isotropic limit. We implement five sky-decomposition bases: pixel, spherical harmonic, square-root spherical harmonic, radiometer, and principal-map. We demonstrate the framework on a simulated array modeled on the International Pulsar Timing Array: characterizing the angular response, analyzing the Fisher structure, quantifying the detectability of injected anisotropic hotspots, and forecasting future-array sensitivity. The framework is released as an extension to the sensitivity software package hasasia.
papers.authors: Daniel J. Oliver, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Martine M. Maggi, Jeremy G. Baier, Kyle E. Gourlie

papers.title: Quantum States over Spacetime Can Hide Setting-Dependent Dynamics
papers.abstract: Determining whether correlations across quantum events arise from one physical process is essential for interpreting quantum states over spacetime (QSOSTs). Yet separately realizable settings can share the same unconditional QSOST without admitting a common process, because compression hides distinctions between underlying dynamics. Using least positive lifts, we derive an exact joint-domination criterion for conditioned data to admit a common deterministic parent. A reset-dephasing example and a sparse interferometric witness make this obstruction testable under trusted readout assumptions. We further establish a minimum-five-reference theorem: for two laboratories with qubit inputs and outputs, any four fixed local product-unitary reference groups cannot universally identify deterministic processes from exact joint data, whereas a specified set of five suffices. These results establish when reconstructed temporal correlations support interpretation as alternative readouts of one stable quantum process, making preparation-readout separation a testable physical property.
papers.authors: Jianqi Sheng

papers.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
papers.abstract: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ (leading) and $\Delta=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $\Delta=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $\Delta=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.
papers.authors: Manizheh Botshekananfard, Elif B\"u\c{s}ra G\"uraks{\i}n, Vasileios A. Letsios, Gizem \c{S}eng\"or

papers.title: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
papers.abstract: After decades without a fully self-consistent thermodynamic formulation, recent proposals for Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetime have yielded several inequivalent descriptions, each satisfying its own first law and Smarr relation, leaving unresolved which formulation is physically preferred. In this Letter, we introduce a two-horizon diagnostic whose left- and right-moving thermodynamic temperatures are fixed via the harmonic mean relations before the thermodynamic variables are chosen. For uncharged Taub-NUT spacetime, the left-moving first law closes with the mass and NUT charge, whereas, within the restricted homogeneous class examined here, the right-moving first law requires an additional thermodynamic secondary hair $J_n = mn$. This result supports a bi-hair thermodynamic organization of the NUT parameter through $N = n$ and $J_n = mn$. Furthermore, this two-horizon framework offers a new opportunity toward addressing similar thermodynamic non-uniqueness in other two-horizon NUT-charged systems when the first law and Smarr relation alone do not identify a physically preferred formulation.
papers.authors: Di Wu, Robert B. Mann, Shuang-Qing Wu

papers.title: Investigating planar Proca metamaterials in nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.
papers.authors: Widervan de Deus Morais, Stamatios Strikos, Ronaldo Thibes, Jos\'e Abdalla Helay\"el-Neto

papers.title: Les Houches lectures on Spinfoam Path Integrals
papers.abstract: In these lecture notes for the Les Houches School on Loop Quantum Gravity 2025, which took place in September 2025, we give a pedagogical review of the basics of the spinfoam framework for a quantum gravity path integral. While spin network states in loop quantum gravity describe the quantum geometry of the 3d space as dynamical networks of entangled quanta of volumes, spinfoams define transition amplitudes for those spin networks using the reformulation of general relativity as an "almost-topological" field theory and tools from quantum BF theory and topological state-sums. The lectures were a short format of three times one hour and a half, only allowing to cover the basics and offer a glimpse of more advanced lines of research. We introduce spin foam path integrals for increasing spacetime dimensions starting with 2d BF theory, then build up to 3d quantum gravity with the Ponzano-Regge state-sum and the Turaev-Viro invariant, and finally the quantization of general relativity in four dimensions.
papers.authors: Oleksandra Hrytseniak, Etera R. Livine, Valentine Maris

papers.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.
papers.authors: Masaki Yamada

papers.title: On Leray's Theoreme de Structure for a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations: an improvement of the result
papers.abstract: In this note we furnish a new result concerning the well known th\'eor\`eme de structure by Leray related to a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. We are able to furnish a new estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity.
papers.authors: Paolo Maremonti

papers.title: Approximate Virtual Quantum Recovery
papers.abstract: The recovery of quantum information after subsystem loss is a central challenge in quantum information processing. However, some quantum states remain beyond the reach of any recovery strategies. Here we identify the algebraic origin of virtual irrecoverability, the \emph{ghost information}---correlations present in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. We introduce a scalar measure to quantify its magnitude and prove a universal error floor below which no virtual recovery map can operate, irrespective of resource investment. In such cases only \emph{approximate} virtual recovery is available. We derive upper and lower bounds on the sampling overhead for approximate virtual recovery. Moreover, we show that conditional mutual information, the standard entropic diagnostic, does not determine the sampling overhead. Our work thus establish an algebraic framework of information recovery beyond entropic criteria.
papers.authors: Yuan Liu, Linhan Lin, Ke-Mi Xu

papers.title: Analytical Criteria for Potential-Well Formation in Non-Minimally Coupled Scalar-Tensor Theories: A Necessary Condition for Instability
papers.abstract: Although the existence of a potential-well does not necessarily imply instability, its formation is a necessary prerequisite for the existence of unstable bound states. We investigate the formation of an effective potential-well for scalar-field perturbations in two non-minimally coupled scalar-tensor theories, involving couplings to the Ricci scalar and the Einstein tensor. In the context of the near-horizon approximation, we derive an analytical expression for the threshold coupling in each model at which the extremum of the effective potential reaches the event horizon. We use this criterion for the stationary, spherically symmetric black holes in this paper, in particular for a number of regular black holes spacetimes. We examine the dependence of the threshold couplings on the scalar field mass, angular multipole number, and the background parameters. At this distinguished coupling, the real part of the near-horizon quasi-normal mode frequencies vanishes, yielding purely imaginary frequencies. We further demonstrate that the universal area spectrum of spherically symmetric black holes can be recovered from the near-horizon frequency spectrum without invoking the highly damped-mode approximation. Remarkably, this spectrum is independent of the specific non-minimal coupling scheme.
papers.authors: Majid Karimabadi, Davood Mahdavian Yekta, S. A. Alavi

papers.title: A wormhole with two black holes
papers.abstract: We report on a new three-parameter stationary solution of the four-dimensional vacuum Einstein equations, which describes a Lorentzian wormhole harboring two antipodal co-rotating black holes. These are hung from one of the two spacelike infinities by two semi-infinite cosmic strings with positive or negative tension. We evaluate the Komar masses and angular momenta of the two black holes, and check that these obey the usual Smarr relation, as well as the generalized first law for a system of collinear black holes and cosmic strings. While free from Misner strings, this spacetime allows closed timelike curves within a bounded volume. The metric also admits a naked ring singularity for almost all values of the parameters.
papers.authors: G\'erard Cl\'ement

papers.title: Group Theory and the CFT Distance Conjecture: $\mathcal{N}=2$ Tensionless Strings Have No (Co)Weight
papers.abstract: We perform a systematic survey of the Hagedorn behaviour at infinite-distance points in the conformal manifold of four-dimensional large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ Superconformal Field Theories admitting a Lagrangian description. Many properties of these theories can be understood in terms of the Lie algebra encoding the shape of their quiver. We find that in the overall-free limit, the Hagedorn temperature is determined by the largest eigenvalue of an affine or finite Cartan adjacency matrix. This defines two types of universality classes of theories sharing the same high-energy exponential growth of states characteristic of string-like spectra. The first and largest is the affine case, corresponding to orbifold and orientifold projections of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills, and all share the same temperature. The others fall into universality classes following an ADE classification with a temperature set by the dual Coxeter number, and can be obtained by deforming the affine case. Our results apply to all large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ quivers with any classical gauge symmetry, including those with matter charged beyond bifundamental representations. We further discuss the string-theoretic construction of these theories and some of the holographic implications, as well as how our methods extend to broad families of theories with less supersymmetry. We also consider limits where only part of the theory becomes free, and find lower and upper bounds on the exponential rate predicted by the CFT Distance Conjecture. Both these bounds and the Hagedorn temperature are set by the same eigenvalue, and when the quiver has a single gauge node the lower bound is saturated, giving a natural explanation for the three universality classes recently found in the literature.
papers.authors: Florent Baume, Fabio Mantegazza

papers.title: Superconformal mechanics from N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models
papers.abstract: We investigate two-particle variants of the N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models. Oving to translational invariance, the center-of-mass degrees of freedom and the associated fermions decouple, yielding specific systems of superconformal mechanics. Additional bosonic spin variables are straightforwardly incorporated into the supercharges and the Hamiltonian. For the Euler-Calogero-Moser model, the two-particle supersymmetry exhibits an unexpected extension from $Osp(N|2)$ to $SU(1,1|N)$ superconformal symmetry, whereas the Calogero model reduces to purely $Osp(N|2)$ superconformal mechanics. Finally, we demonstrate that introducing a larger number of fermions into the system provides a consistent pathway to overcoming well-known pathologies with higher supersymmetries inherent to these framework.
papers.authors: S. Krivonos, A. Sutulin

papers.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\to\gamma_\varepsilon(8\pi\nu)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $\gamma_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.
papers.authors: Kabiru Michael Adeyemo, Mohamed Majdoub, Subha Pal

papers.title: Poisson-Lie T-duality and D-brane Configurations of $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ Backgrounds
papers.abstract: We construct a non-Abelian dual pair for the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ background via Poisson-Lie T-duality on a semi-Abelian double. Using a specific parameterization of the six-dimensional Lie group ${A}_2 \times {A}_2 \times A_2$, we formulate the original $\sigma$-model incorporating the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ metric with a vanishing Kalb-Ramond field ($B$-field), and derive its dual background, which features a non-vanishing $B$-field and a physical singularity. We investigate the conformal properties and test the generalized supergravity equations for the complete geometry; although a generalized Killing vector exists, the full background fails to satisfy these equations. We then analyze the asymptotic structure and coordinate domains, revealing distinct exterior and interior sectors separated by curvature-singular boundaries, alongside an asymptotic approach to the original background. Finally, we investigate the transformation of $D$-brane boundary conditions under Poisson-Lie T-duality for the semi-Abelian Drinfeld double $({\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 , 6{\A}_1)$. By analyzing seven classes of gluing matrices, we examine the eigenvalue spectra, identify candidate dual D-brane configurations, and construct the corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann projectors. We also investigate the integrability of the Neumann distributions and determine the associated gauge-invariant two-forms and world-volume field strengths, providing a systematic framework for studying the geometric and boundary condition properties of the dual branes.
papers.authors: Ali Eghbali

papers.title: A Small-Throat Boundary Condition for the Tunneling Wave Function of the Universe
papers.abstract: We propose a small-throat prescription for the wave function of a closed universe in the semiclassical approximation, motivated by the idea that universe creation may be obtained as the decoupling, or pinch-off, limit of a tunneling geometry connected to another universe through a small throat. Instead of retaining the parent-universe side explicitly, we describe the remaining half-geometry by a minisuperspace model with boundary conditions imposed at the throat. To model the finite throat, we introduce a small radiation component parametrized by $\epsilon$ in a closed minisuperspace model with a positive cosmological constant. The radiation term produces two turning points, an inner one $q_-\sim O(\epsilon)$ and an outer one $q_+\sim H^{-2}$, where $q$ is the square of the scale factor. Our prescription imposes the Neumann condition $\dot q(0)=0$ on the classical solutions and restricts the initial size $q_i=q(0)$ to the small-throat domain $0<|q_i|<\sqrt{\epsilon}/H$. This domain contains the inner turning point $q_-$ and excludes the unsuppressed outer-turning-point saddle at $q_i=q_+$. We choose the steepest-descent lapse contour through the inner tunneling saddle in the semiclassical approximation. Taking the limit $\epsilon\to0$ after this finite-throat saddle problem has been defined, the inner turning point approaches $q_i=0$, and the saddle action reduces to that of the standard tunneling saddle. Other choices of lapse contour can instead select Hartle-Hawking-type growing branches. In this sense, the tunneling exponent and outgoing WKB phase can be obtained as the limiting form of tunneling from an arbitrarily small universe, rather than by imposing a boundary condition directly at a vanishing geometry.
papers.authors: Masaki Yamada

papers.title: Unbiased Estimation of Conditional Covariance for Quantum Optomechanics
papers.abstract: Continuous measurements can prepare macroscopic mechanical oscillators in conditional quantum states, but their covariance is difficult to verify. For each quadrature, the conventional retrodictive estimator is unbiased exactly when the conditional and future-likelihood variances are equal, and it needs a separate rule for the position-momentum cross covariance. Here, we derive an estimator that recovers all three independent covariance entries using one exact identity for linear-Gaussian models. It combines the forward trajectory, a future-likelihood center, and the smoothed trajectory. Using these three trajectories, we reconstruct the covariance of the center-of-mass motion of a 7.71-mg suspended mirror. This covariance describes a thermally squeezed conditional state with a principal-variance ratio of $4.7\pm0.7$. The reconstructed covariance and the measured bias difference between the conventional and three-trajectory estimators agree with the model predictions within propagated uncertainties. Varying the upper band edge resolves changes in all three covariance entries. For upper edges up to 1 kHz, the measured changes agree with the finite-band predictions. Every experimental record covers only a finite frequency band; these results show how such records can be used to characterize conditional mechanical states and provide a basis for future tests of macroscopic entanglement.
papers.authors: Katsuta Sakai, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

papers.title: Nonlinear Causality and Strong Hyperbolicity of Einstein-Israel-Stewart Theories of Transient Relativistic Fluid Dynamics
papers.abstract: We present the first complete analysis of nonlinear causality and local well-posedness for a very general class of bulk and shear viscous theories of relativistic transient fluid dynamics, which encompasses (i) the original Israel-Stewart theory derived from entropy-current arguments, (ii) approaches derived from kinetic theory, and (iii) resummed gradient-expansion based formulations as particular subcases. Our work establishes, for the first time, simultaneously necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for causality, alongside sufficient conditions guaranteeing strong hyperbolicity, in the full nonlinear regime. These results are rigorously proven for both systems coupled to Einstein's equations featuring a dynamic metric and on a fixed background, with or without a cosmological constant, and include baryon conservation (in the absence of heat/diffusion currents). The conditions are purely algebraic, require no simplifying spacetime symmetry assumptions or a specific equation of state, and allow all transport coefficients to depend on the dissipative currents. We also demonstrate that the normalization, orthogonality, symmetry, and tracelessness physical constraints on the dynamical variables are properly propagated during the lifetime of the solutions. Our results provide a readily usable toolset with which one can investigate the domain of applicability of relativistic viscous fluid dynamics in numerical and phenomenological studies in heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics.
papers.authors: Ian Cordeiro, Enrico Speranza, F\'abio S. Bemfica, Marcelo M. Disconzi, Jorge Noronha

papers.title: Weak-field charged-scalar dynamics in Melvin--Kerr spacetime: an effective Kerr spectral problem
papers.abstract: We study the local weak-field reduction of the charged Klein--Gordon equation in the neutral-seed Melvin--Kerr geometry and the auxiliary Kerr spectral problem defined by that reduction. At fixed radius and fixed scalar charge, the metric has no term linear in the magnetic parameter $b$. In the chosen gauge the first-order Maxwell potential is $A_\mu=b\,g_{\mu\phi}$, so its interaction with an azimuthal mode $m$ is absorbed into $\mu_{\rm eff}^{2}=\mu^{2}+2qbm$. This identity applies to both separated equations and leaves the gauge-invariant horizon phase in the Kerr form. Extending the truncated equation to all exterior radii and imposing Kerr outgoing boundary conditions defines an auxiliary spectrum, evaluated with Dolan's continued-fraction method. Its linear magnetic response is the complex mass derivative of the Kerr spectrum. Numerical examples for the fundamental $\ell=1,2$ branches illustrate this relation, including the continuation through negative effective mass squared. The tabulated modes remain damped, and their real-frequency shifts have opposite signs for the two positive-frequency azimuthal sectors in the surveyed range. We separate numerical accuracy within the auxiliary problem from local weak-field power counting and the unresolved exterior boundary problem. No matching to the exact magnetized exterior is performed; consequently these frequencies are not established approximations to global Melvin--Kerr resonances.
papers.authors: Haryanto M. Siahaan

papers.title: Possibility of the antibottom-strange molecular pentaquarks near $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ thresholds
papers.abstract: The molecular states in coupled channel system of $B_s^0N- B\Lambda- B^*\Lambda- B\Sigma- B^*\Sigma$ are investigated within one-boson-exchange model that includes $S$-$D$ wave mixing and a tunable short-range $\delta(r)$ term. Bound, resonant, and virtual states are searched by analytically continuing the $S$ matrix in the complex energy plane. In the single-channel analysis, the $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ systems with $J^P=1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ are found to be attractive and form three bound states with reasonable cutoff region, corresponding to $1/2^-( B\Sigma)$, $1/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$, and $3/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$ . When coupled-channel dynamics is included, these states evolve into near-threshold poles that produce enhancements in the $B_s^0N$, $ B\Lambda$, and $ B^*\Lambda$ invariant mass spectra. The pole below the $ B^*\Sigma$ threshold in the $J^P=1/2^-$ system depends strongly on the treatment of the short-range $\delta(r)$ term and becomes a virtual state when this contribution is removed, while the other two resonant poles and their line shapes are only moderately affected. The influences of $B^{(*)}\Sigma^*$ channels on these states are also investigated. For representative parameter region, the predicted masses of these states lie in the $6.44-6.70$ GeV region and have widths of a few to several MeV. The pole coupling and partial-width analyses indicate that the invariant mass spectrum of the $B_s^0N$ and $ B^{(*)}\Lambda$ channels are the best place to hunt the predicted states. These results support the existence of near-threshold molecular pentaquark $P_{ \bar b s}$ and provide useful guidance in future experimental searches.
papers.authors: Jian-Kang Zhao, Nijiati Yalikun

papers.title: 70 years of Double-Logarithmic Approximation
papers.abstract: Existence of Double-Logarithmic (DL) contributions to scattering amplitudes in QED was discovered by V.V. Sudakov in 1956 and total summation of DL contributions to electron-photon scattering resulted in appearance of famous Sudakov exponentials. Then, thanks to contributions of V.G. Gorshkov, V.N. Gribov, G.V. Frolov and L.N. Lipatov, the pattern of calculations in Double- Logarithmic Approximation (DLA) was constructed. Since then, DLA has become one of basic ways of describing various high-energy processes in the framework of QED, QCD and theory of EW interactions. In the present paper, we remind the history of DLA and present a brief overview of application of DLA to various objects like form factors, scattering amplitudes, DIS structure functions.
papers.authors: B. I. Ermolaev

papers.title: Stroboscopic Ergodic Averages and Radial Symmetry in the Vortex Model
papers.abstract: We study the point-vortex model in the plane in the case of $N$ vortices of equal positive circulation, and we investigate the long-time behaviour of the empirical vorticity measure. We conjecture that, for almost every initial datum, the time average of the empirical measure exists and is invariant under rotations about the centre of vorticity. We prove the conjecture for $N=3$ by exploiting the integrability of the system. For $N\ge 4$ we reduce the problem to a question about a measure-preserving dynamical system on the shape space: after replacing time with a suitably chosen rotation angle as independent variable, radiality is equivalent to the independence of stroboscopic ergodic averages from the initial phase along a single trajectory. We formulate this reduction as a general ergodic problem, discuss its scope through elementary counterexamples, and verify the required hypotheses in explicit regions of the phase space for $N=3$ and $N=4$.
papers.authors: Emanuele Caglioti, Marco Cecchini

papers.title: Constraining dark energy with complementary probes of large-scale structure
papers.abstract: To observationally pin down the nature of dark energy, it is essential to consistently model cosmological perturbations in the presence of dark energy alongside the background expansion and constrain this joint theory space with a large array of complementary probes. Here, we achieve this by constraining a model in the Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy (EFTofDE) framework by supplementing probes of the expansion history with several probes of large-scale structure: redshift space distortions (RSD) from DESI DR1, $3\times2$pt measurements from DES Y3, and the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect from cross-correlating CMB temperature anisotropies with galaxy number counts or CMB lensing. We demonstrate the complementarity of different probes which leads to strong improvements on constraints on DE perturbations. For our most constraining dataset combination that supplements CMB+BAO+SNe probes with DESI DR1 RSD, DES Y3 $3\times2$pt and ISW cross-correlations between CMB temperature and galaxy counts, we find an improvement in the Figure of Merit (FoM) for the DE perturbation parameters $\{c_B, c_M\}$ by a factor of 2.69. We show the phenomenological implications of these constraints by mapping them to the present-day values of the phenomenological functions $\{\mu(z), \Sigma(z)\}$, where we see an FoM improvement by a factor of 3.37. We find a significant interdependence between the posteriors of $\{w_0, w_a\}$ and $\{c_B, c_M\}$, caused by the theoretical prior imposed by the gradient stability condition within the EFTofDE framework. Finally, we compute the significance of deviation from $\Lambda$CM for the EFTofDE model when constrained with CMB+BAO+SNe datasets, finding it to be at 2.9$\sigma$. This significance is nontrivially similar to the significance for the $w_0w_a$CDM model for the same dataset combination which we find to be 3.1$\sigma$.
papers.authors: Neel Shah, Kazuya Koyama, Johannes Noller, Lanyang Yi

papers.title: Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative trace-norm propagation of chaos for finite-dimensional quantum mean-field systems governed by Belavkin equations under continuous diffusive measurements. Our results concern random reduced states conditioned on the observation records of the entire particle system, rather than states averaged over these records. We allow arbitrary one-particle density matrices, general measurement operators, and both perfect and inefficient detection. Two regimes of initial data are considered. For initial states approaching a tensor product in trace norm, without requiring permutation invariance, we establish explicit convergence rates, improved from an inverse fourth-root to an inverse square-root rate when the one-particle initial state is faithful. More importantly, for permutation-invariant initial states, convergence of the two-particle marginal to a product suffices for propagation of chaos, even when the full initial state remains far from a tensor product. Quantitative convergence rates are obtained in this setting, including a sharper estimate under faithfulness. Our proofs combine purification, fully observed dilation, and uniform stability of linear Zakai equations with a relative-entropy method for the joint observation law and conditional quantum state. The latter controls the interacting dynamics through entropy-production estimates and extends to arbitrary-rank initial states by regularizing only the reference dynamics. These results provide a rigorous foundation for low-dimensional approximations of continuously monitored interacting quantum systems, including those with initially correlated states.
papers.authors: Gaoyue Guo

papers.title: Electrical-Circuit Simulation of the Uhlmann Phase
papers.abstract: The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this work, we reformulate the Uhlmann parallel-transport condition as a linear matrix differential equation and vectorize it to obtain an effective dynamical generator. This generator can be directly mapped onto the admittance matrix of a classical RC circuit, thereby translating the Uhlmann dynamics into the evolution of circuit node voltages. We illustrate the mapping using the equatorial-loop model and, via a rotating-frame transformation followed by a real decomposition, derive a time-independent, real-valued dynamical system suitable for analog implementation. LTspice simulations of the resulting active RC network faithfully reproduce the Uhlmann geometric phase and its topological transition at the critical purity, demonstrating that classical electrical circuits offer a simple and accessible platform for probing mixed-state geometric phases.
papers.authors: Yu-Huan Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

papers.title: Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Mutually Unbiased Operator Frames
papers.abstract: We develop an operator-frame formulation of entropic uncertainty relations in the Hilbert-Schmidt space of operators. For general continuous indexed operator frames, we derive an entropic uncertainty relation for the associated coefficient distributions by combining endpoint norm estimates with Riesz-Thorin interpolation. We then identify a distinguished class of mutually unbiased operator frames, defined through constant-modulus trace overlaps. Under suitable structural conditions, the corresponding coefficient amplitudes are related by a bilinear Fourier transform, leading to a stronger Hirschman-Beckner-type entropic uncertainty relation. As canonical realizations, we consider Weyl displacement operators and Wigner kernels, as well as Cartesian dyadic frames generated by position and momentum eigenstates. These examples recover familiar continuous-variable Fourier dualities while extending entropic uncertainty relations beyond measurement outcomes to operator representations themselves.
papers.authors: Jesni Shamsul Shaari, Stefano Mancini

papers.title: Non-relativistic limits of $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and S-duality
papers.abstract: We investigate non-relativistic limits of four-dimensional maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory (4d MSYM) and their relation to the nonperturbative $\operatorname{SL}(2;\mathbb Z)$ S-duality of the relativistic theory. We construct a general family of non-relativistic limits using a Type IIB brane set-up with a D3-brane and $(p,q)$-strings and show that the resulting theories are topological deformations of supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills theory or quantum mechanics on the moduli space of BPS monopoles. The deformations of the Galilean Yang-Mills theory are the familiar $\theta$-term and a coupling to the monopole charge, while in the moduli space theory the only deformation is a $\theta$-term. This family of theories fit together into a three-dimensional moduli space with nontrivial topology, on which $\operatorname{PSL}(2;\mathbb Z)$-valued dualities act in a richer and more complex way than in the relativistic parent theory. In the Abelian case, we establish the duality directly using the path integral, while in the non-Abelian case we support our claim by matching the one-particle spectrum as well as the Galilean spacetime symmetries and electric/magnetic invertible one-form symmetries.
papers.authors: Hyungrok Kim, Joseph Smith

papers.title: Hybrid Stars with Post-Merger Rotation Profiles
papers.abstract: We study the effect of differential rotation on hybrid stars with the first-order deconfinement phase transition from hadronic to color superconducting quark matter. The differential rotation is introduced within a realistic, four-parameter phenomenological rotation law, in which the maximum angular velocity of the rotating configuration is shifted away from the center. We focus on two classes of differentially rotating solutions, namely quasi-toroidal (type C) and quasi-spherical (type A), and study the changes in the star global properties and angular velocity profiles due to the presence of a phase transition. We show that when increasing the angular momentum $J$ the turning points of the $J=const$ sequences shift towards lower energy densities, shrinking considerably the region where differentially rotating neutron stars with phase transitions exists. Interestingly, for both type A and type C solutions, the angular velocity profile is continuous throughout the star despite the discontinuity in the energy density. Moreover, we show that for the differential rotation law we study, at the crossing points where the mass-radius curves for different equations of state intersect, the rotational profiles of the solutions are very close despite large differences in the energy density profiles. This reveals a possible degeneracy between the post-merger remnant properties for models with and without phase transitions, emphasizing the need for complementary multi-messenger observables to distinguish between them.
papers.authors: Kalin V. Staykov, Violetta Sagun, Lorenzo Cipriani, Daniela D. Doneva, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev

papers.title: EMRI Dephasing from a Torsion-Inspired Near-Zone Kerr Deformation: Motivated by Spin-Polarized Dark Matter
papers.abstract:
Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive probes of weak conservative perturbations in the strong-field region of massive black holes. We study a phenomenological EMRI model motivated by Einstein--Cartan gravity in which a spin-polarized dark-matter spike is described by a Weyssenhoff fluid. After torsion is eliminated algebraically, the local spin contribution contains a repulsive exterior source $U_{tt}^{m spin}\propto-\sigma_0^2/r^3$. Solving the corresponding static linearized field equation, however, does not produce a global $1/r^3$ metric perturbation; the response contains a mass renormalization, a logarithmic $r^{-1}$ tail, and an $M/r^2$ term. We therefore introduce $g_{\mu
u}^{m eff}=g_{\mu
u}^{m Kerr}+\alpha h_{\mu
u}^{m eff}$ only as a local near-zone matching ansatz, not as a complete rotating Einstein--Cartan black-hole solution. Within this torsion-inspired deformation we compute circular equatorial inspirals and analytic-kludge waveforms. The fiducial model can produce large phase shifts in an idealized adiabatic calculation, but the forecast is optimistic and does not include a full LISA/Taiji response, Teukolsky/self-force fluxes, eccentricity, inclination, or high-dimensional parameter degeneracies. The results should be read as constraints on an effective near-zone operator rather than as a prediction of minimally coupled Einstein--Cartan dark matter.
papers.authors: Jingxu Wu, Liangyu Luo, Daniil Stepanenko, Jie Shi

papers.title: No classical particle limit for massless quanta
papers.abstract: We investigate whether relativistic massless classical particles may emerge as the classical limit of massless quanta. To address this question independently of any specific dynamics, environment, or pointer basis, we develop an axiomatic and operational framework for the coarse-graining approach. In this formulation, a candidate classical phase space is taken as the outcome space of a POVM subject to minimal classicality and covariance requirements. Applying this framework to the Poincar\'e group, we prove a no-go theorem for massless particles: the covariance requirement is incompatible with the operational conditions for classicality. Conversely, we show that the obstruction can be avoided for massive particles by constructing coarse-graining schemes satisfying the minimal classicality requirements. The no-go theorem leaves open field-like limits of massless quanta, such as the emergence of the electromagnetic field, while ruling out classical massless particles, such as classical photons.
papers.authors: Riccardo Falcone, Simon Fuchs

papers.title: Quantum Otto engine powered by an anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model under independent local magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We study a quantum Otto heat engine whose working substance is an anisotropic two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ model. Independent local magnetic fields are used to control each spin individually. The influence of the longitudinal coupling, anisotropy, transverse coupling, and local fields on the net work output and efficiency is systematically examined. Reducing the longitudinal coupling is found to markedly improve both the maximum work and the peak efficiency. The engine performance reaches an optimum at a particular value of the anisotropy parameter. A local work analysis clarifies how work is produced during the cycle. Because of the asymmetric local fields and the intrinsic spin-spin interaction, the two qubits play markedly different thermodynamic roles; the interaction term itself contributes crucially to the total work. We further analyze the variation of quantum entanglement, quantified by concurrence, along the cycle. The results indicate that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes is closely correlated with the efficiency enhancement. This work offers new insight into the operating principles and control of quantum Otto heat engines.
papers.authors: Meiru Li, Maimaitiyiming Tusun, Fang Zhao, Hasiyatihan Abudoula, Tongcheng Wei

papers.title: A Dynamical Spacetime Hypothesis for Quantum Entanglement with a Proposed Experimental Test
papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement is a central resource of quantum information science, yet its correlations are ordinarily treated as properties of the quantum state rather than as the outcome of an underlying physical process. Here we explore the hypothesis that these correlations are mediated dynamically by a field propagating locally at finite velocity through an extension of ordinary spacetime, extending the kinematic proposal of Physical Review Research 7, 013261 (2025) to a constrained bulk-field dynamics. Motivated by the constraints imposed by no-signaling on finite-speed hidden-influence models, we consider a warped five-dimensional spacetime with an additional timelike coordinate. We show that the five-dimensional Einstein equations determine the warp factor within a symmetric ansatz, requiring a positive bulk cosmological constant. We show that null trajectories propagating through the additional timelike dimension can project onto arbitrarily large spatial distances at the same ordinary time, although these trajectories do not themselves connect separated points on the brane. Spectral analysis of a minimally coupled bulk scalar reveals a tachyonic four-dimensional continuum. We isolate a normalizable zero-mode sector with stable, retarded effective dynamics in ordinary brane time and obtain an exact solution for a suitably distributed source. Building on these results, we formulate an equal-time contextual coupling and Bohm-Bub-inspired outcome dynamics as additional hypotheses, subject to Born-rule compatibility and multipartite no-signaling. We propose an experiment involving two independently prepared Bell pairs to test for departures from their expected statistical independence. Under specified assumptions on the field covariance and detector response, we derive a conditional inverse-square decay of correlations between the two pairs joint measurement outcomes at large separations.
papers.authors: Marco Pettini

papers.title: Soft information from neural-network logits and correlation-aware matching gaps
papers.abstract: To utilize quantum error-correcting codes, a decoder must infer the logical sector from the measured syndrome. Beyond producing a hard logical decision, some decoders provide soft information that estimates the reliability of that decision. For minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), a common confidence measure is the complementary gap. Neural-network decoders trained with binary cross entropy naturally output a different confidence score, the logit, whose usefulness for post-selection has already been demonstrated. Here, we compare the logit of a pretrained graph neural-network (GNN) decoder with the complementary gaps of uncorrelated and correlation-aware MWPM, evaluated on identical syndromes from rotated-surface-code memory experiments under circuit-level noise. Incorporating correlations substantially improves matching-based hard decisions, post-selection performance, and calibration, reversing the GNN's advantage at larger code distances while leaving it superior at smaller distance. Exchanging confidence scores shows that their ability to rank logical failures is decoder-relative. An exact-posterior comparison at small distance, together with larger-distance log-loss measurements, further shows that neither score universally provides the closer approximation to posterior soft information. These results reveal that much of the apparent advantage of learned confidence over the standard matching gap arises from correlations omitted by the matching model. Nevertheless, learned logits provide useful soft information without requiring an explicit detector error model or competing-sector matching calculations at inference, offering an alternative where matching-based confidence is costly or unavailable.
papers.authors: David Dentelski

papers.title: Enabling quantum communication in ultra-large-scale networks
papers.abstract: The recent development of small-scale quantum networks poses the question of which network-level mechanisms could enable quantum communication to operate at scale in a future Quantum Internet. The question can be answered within a well-established framework where a quantum network is mapped into a classical weighted graph, and communication reliability is assessed using methods from network theory. Previous work relied on this framework to determine sufficient conditions for viable network-wide communication only on special network topologies, such as regular lattices, and to devise communication protocols applicable only to small- and moderate-sized real networks. Here, we overcome both limitations by introducing a family of quantum communication protocols that scale to networks with hundreds of millions of nodes. We show that the competition between increasing communication distance and path redundancy determines their large-scale behavior, and that degree heterogeneity can provide sufficient redundancy to sustain communication in small-world networks. These conclusions are supported by a systematic analysis of both real network topologies and synthetic networks, and an analytical treatment in the limit of infinitely large random scale-free graphs.
papers.authors: Filippo Radicchi

papers.title: On the large N convergence of the supermembrane matrix model
papers.abstract: In this paper, the large N behavior of a supersymmetric matrix model is compared with its exact continuum description. We prove that the complete spectrum of a $SU(N)$ regularized compactified M2-brane theory in the semiclassical approximation converges, in the large $N$ limit, to the exact spectrum in the same approximation. To this end, we concentrate on the large $N$ limit of a supersymmetric matrix model describing a supermembrane with central charge on a toroidally compactified target space. We analyze, on the one hand, the supermembrane model formulated on a differentiable compact torus, with structure group given by the area-preserving diffeomorphisms, and, on the other hand, its associated regularized $SU(N)$ model. We emphasize in our analysis the structure of the local and global constraints of the regularized model, which generate the $SU(N)$ algebra and reproduce the area-preserving diffeomorphism algebra in the large N limit, together with the topological information associated with the central charge condition and the topology of the model. We explain the role of the central charge in the compactified supermembrane and how it allows a top-down $SU(N)$ regularization. It is known that its $SU(N)$ regularized model has a purely discrete spectrum with finite multiplicity. We prove that, in the semiclassical approximation, the spectrum of the Hamiltonian of the supersymmetric matrix model converges in the large-$N$ limit to that of the Hamiltonian of the supermembrane (M2-brane) with central charge.
papers.authors: M. P. Garcia del Moral, P. Le\'on, A. Restuccia

papers.title: Existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle, helping to establish the universality of the C-type route to chaos in families of non-invertible maps of the plane. Families of two-dimensional non-invertible maps, with at least two parameters and critical points of fold type, exhibit a distinct type of critical scaling, the C-type. An accumulation of parameter values leads to an infinite collection of coexisting attracting cycles of periods $4^n$ or $2\cdot 4^n$. Asymptotically, period quadrupling is accompanied by parameter-space scaling and state-space scaling governed by particular universal constants. Kuznetsov et. al. explained this phenomenon in terms of a stationary orbit of period two of the renormalisation group (RG) transformation for period-doubling. We prove the existence of the corresponding renormalisation two-cycle in a Banach space of analytic maps and gain rigorous bounds on the corresponding universal state space scaling constants. This result provides a further step in proving a series of outstanding conjectures concerning distinct universality classes for period-doubling. It extends the recent results for unidirectionally-coupled maps (the FS-type) to bidirectionally-coupled maps, and generalises the framework from fixed points to periodic orbits of the corresponding renormalisation operators. It also provides a further step in establishing the conjectured picture that the C-type universality class is born from the FS-type class via a period-doubling bifurcation in the dynamics of the RG transformation itself. The proof relies on rigorous computations to establish that a variant of Newton's method for the two-cycle is a contraction map. The C-type scaling regularity is known to occur in a number of dynamical systems of interest, perhaps most notably in biologically-plausible models of nephron blood pressure autoregulation.
papers.authors: Zainab Rahman, Maria Pickett, Andrew Burbanks

papers.title: Fracton Topological Holography
papers.abstract: Topological Holography (TH) is a framework of representing $(d-1)$-dimensional quantum systems with a $d$-dimensional sandwich, consisting of a topological order bulk, a gapped top boundary and a dynamical bottom boundary. Dualities and non-invertible symmetries are represented by the change of top boundary in the TH framework. Existing studies have focused on sandwiches with liquid topological bulk, in this paper we examine some fracton bulks, where we call the framework Fracton Topological Holography (FTH). In particular, the X-cube FTH induces the transverse field plaquette Ising model (TFPIM) version Kramers--Wannier duality, the duality between TFPIM and the two-dimensional $90^\circ$ quantum compass model, and the self-duality of quantum compass model. Haah's code FTH induces a duality of transverse-field generalized Ising models (TFGIMs). The two examples illustrate at least a part of type-I fracton (X-cube) and a part of type-II fracton (Haah's code) models can be used to construct FTH sandwiches. Moreover, we construct an explicit Sequential Quantum Circuit (SQC) switching the top boundary of X-cube sandwich, realizing the TFPIM version KW duality.
papers.authors: Yu-Tao Hu, Jie-Yu Zhang, Peng Ye

papers.title: Propagation of Regularity for Schroedinger Equations with Time Dependent Potentials
papers.abstract: The dynamics of Schr\"odinger equation with time dependent potentials of general time dependence is considered. It is shown that for localized in space potentials, there is propagation of regularity which is uniformly bounded in higher Sobolev norms. Unlike the cases where the solution scatter, and then propagation is proved via a standard bootstrap argument, the solutions considered here have a part that does not scatter, as expected in general. For this we introduce propagation estimates that work directly in (e.g.) $H^2(\mathcal{R}^3).$
papers.authors: Avy Soffer

papers.title: Symmetry-Protected Bipartite Entanglement in Hopf-Linked Quantum Rings
papers.abstract: We study two interacting electrons in Hopf-linked quantum rings, one electron on each ring. In the absence of the inter-ring interaction, the two lowest orbital states on each ring have the same energy. For the ideal geometry, the Fourier coefficients of the three-dimensional Coulomb kernel satisfy $V_{1,0}=-V_{0,1}$, making the positive-parity block of the four-state Hamiltonian diagonal in the Bell basis. Unitary symmetries of the full orbital Hamiltonian preserve the parity sectors under virtual transitions. For pure states odd under ring exchange followed by a half-turn on each ring ($\mathcal Y=-1$), the Schmidt weights occur in equal pairs, giving at least one bit of entanglement between the rings. An elliptic deformation changes the Coulomb selection rule to first order while preserving the link. Finite-basis diagonalization shows that higher orbitals can reduce the probability of obtaining the encoded Bell pair by projection onto the two lowest orbitals of each ring even when the entanglement between the rings remains close to one bit.
papers.authors: V. Yogesh, Prosenjit Maity

papers.title: Deformed seminorms, anisotropic sectors and Phragm\'en Lindel\"of principles for $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$\allowbreak difference operators
papers.abstract: We study the deformed derivative of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba on spaces of holomorphic functions, with the induced geometry and growth principles. The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $\rho$ into those on the disc of radius $\rho/\beta$, $\beta$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/\phi_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carath\'eodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fr\'echet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragm\'en Lindel\"of and Lindel\"of principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $\theta\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.
papers.authors: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba

papers.title: Two Operational Principles Single Out Quantum Theory
papers.abstract: Within a finite-dimensional causal operational-probabilistic theory (OPT), we show that adding just two postulates, local equivalence and purification, suffices to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory as a whole, without separately assuming quantum rules for states, measurements, composites, or transformations. This resolves the question raised by Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti (CDP) [Phys. Rev. A 81, 062348 (2010)]. The key step is to establish homogeneity of state cones by combining infinitesimal cone-preserving deformations obtained from these postulates with geometric optimization. CDP purification requires every normalized state to be purifiable and purifications of the same state on any common ancilla to be related by a reversible channel on that ancilla. Our alternative assigns each system one operationally equivalent ancilla that purifies all its normalized states, requiring such reversible equivalence only there. Together with local equivalence, this condition also yields quantum theory.
papers.authors: Kenji Nakahira

papers.title: Optimal work extraction in measurement-based quantum Otto engines: Non-adiabaticity and generalized measurements can be beneficial
papers.abstract: Measurement-based quantum heat engines have attracted significant interest as alternatives to conventional thermal engines, as they replace the hot thermal reservoir with quantum measurements, thereby offering greater controllability and simpler implementation. Motivated by these advantages, we investigate a measurement-driven quantum Otto engine with a qubit working substance and study the optimal work extractable from such engines along with the corresponding efficiency, including whether their performance can surpass that of conventional quantum Otto cycles. We analyze the engine in both the infinite-time (adiabatic) and finite-time (non-adiabatic) regimes, considering two distinct implementations obtained through optimization over all projection-valued measurements (PVMs) and over all two-outcome positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). We show that measurement-based engines can outperform conventional quantum Otto engines within specific parameter regimes and that POVM-based engines can yield higher optimal work extraction than PVM-based ones. Furthermore, by incorporating the thermodynamic cost associated with resetting the auxiliary system required for POVM implementation, we demonstrate that the resulting net work output can still exceed that of PVM-based engines under suitable conditions on the spectral gaps and cold bath temperature. We also identify regimes in which non-adiabatic implementations can yield higher work output and efficiency than their adiabatic counterparts. Our study provides operational guidelines for designing improved measurement-driven quantum Otto engines.
papers.authors: Arunabha Das, Sayan Mondal, Debarupa Saha, Ujjwal Sen

papers.title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing.
