While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees through joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. We present GeneCS, a resource-efficient synthesizer of code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, designed for the backend of fault-tolerant quantum compilers. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS reduces ancillary qubits and checks by over 85\% on average for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while the optimized constructions exhibit logical-error-rate behavior comparable to the baseline under BP-OSD (belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding). On surface-code stress tests with more than $10^4$ physical qubits, one independent synthesis run takes about one second on average. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication for modern QLDPC (quantum low-density parity-check) codes and heterogeneous code systems.
papers.authors: Junyu Zhou, Ali Javadi-Abhari, Gushu Li

papers.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
papers.abstract: A systematic study of chiral effects is presented using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established, beyond the identification of their coefficients. In particular, we can appreciate how these effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. The consistent and covariant anomalies are both encapsulated in master formulae for the currents which result from a careful treatment of the regularisation. It is finally found that, at finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.
papers.authors: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

papers.title: Worst-Case Sample Complexity Bounds for Distributed Inner Product Estimation with Local Randomized Measurements
papers.abstract: We study distributed inner product estimation for $n$-qubit states using local randomized measurements, for which rigorous worst-case guarantees are less understood. We first reduce the minimax kernel optimization to Hamming-distance kernels. Within this class, unbiasedness fixes a unique kernel. For this kernel under local Clifford sampling, we prove a fourth-moment bound for arbitrary inputs. This yields a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{5.25^n})$ copies per party at fixed additive error and failure probability. For the same kernel under local Haar sampling, we prove a local twirling identity that compares its fourth moment with the Clifford fourth moment. A direct bound on the Haar fourth moment shows that $\mathcal(\sqrt{4^n})$ copies per party suffice. We also show that independent single-qubit Pauli shadows have a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{7.5^n})$ for large $n$.
papers.authors: Zhenyuan Huang, Kun Wang, Ping Xu

papers.title: C-Phase-Aware Compilation for Efficient Fault-Tolerant Quantum Execution
papers.abstract: Achieving practical quantum advantage on fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) is fundamentally constrained by significant spatial and temporal overheads required to execute logical operations on physical hardware. Existing compilers fail to exploit the connection between algorithmic structure and fault-tolerant execution primitives, leaving substantial optimization opportunities unrealized. Additionally, they often rely on coarse-grained, slice-based abstractions that ignore microarchitectural overheads, leading to poor resource utilization. We present a microarchitecture-aware compilation approach that integrates algorithmic structure directly with lattice surgery (LS) execution. By leveraging the commutativity of C-Phase operations, the method transforms inherently sequential gate sequences into concurrent multi-target interactions, effectively removing artificial dependencies and exposing significant instruction-level parallelism. To enable this, we design a dynamic, event-driven scheduling strategy that accurately models spatial layout and routing constraints, allowing operations to overlap in time while minimizing contention. Compared to the state-of-the-art compiler, our work achieves up to 24.5$\times$~(geomean~3.7$\times$) reduction in execution time, up to 20.8$\times$~(geomean 2.9$\times$) reduction in space-time volume, and up to 2.7$\times$~(geomean 2.4$\times$) reduction in program-failure probability across three regimes of magic-state production. By co-optimizing the circuit reordering and LS primitives, we make executing fault-tolerant programs faster, cheaper, and more reliable on the same hardware.
papers.authors: Dhanvi Bharadwaj, Siddharth Dangwal, Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: Classifying double copies and multicopies in AdS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we draw a parallel between solutions of pure three-dimensional gravity with a negative cosmological constant and classical double copies in four dimensions. In the former case, topological solutions, such as the BTZ black hole, deficit angles, and naked singularities, emerge from identifying points in AdS using elements from its isometry algebra $so(2,2)$. The type of solution corresponds one-to-one with the orbits of $so(2,2)$. We demonstrate how various double copies of four-dimensional AdS gravity similarly arise from the $so(2,3)$ isometry elements, which also correspond one-to-one with their orbits through a Penrose-type transform. We classify all such elements and generate the corresponding double copies, which include AdS black holes, black branes, and many others. The double-copy isometries originate from the centralizer of a given AdS isometry, allowing us to define canonical coordinates associated with its Abelian part. Additionally, the two Casimir invariants of $so(2,3)$ feature in the metrics via the characteristic polynomial of the AdS symmetry parameter. Our classification naturally extends to higher spins, providing nonequivalent multicopies at the linearized level.
papers.authors: V. E. Didenko, N. K. Dosmanbetov

papers.title: An extensive theory of nonlinearly intercoupled pseudomodes for noise model reduction in circuit QED
papers.abstract: Superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamical (cQED) platforms present a persistent modeling challenge: the intrinsic nonlinearity of the Josephson potential couples to a dissipative electromagnetic environment in ways that resist both perturbative treatment and naive Markovian reduction. Standard approaches either scale poorly with system size or absorb undeclared approximations about the noise structure into their master equations. In this work, we generalize Garraway's pseudomode construction to accommodate nonlinearly intercoupled auxiliary modes, providing a nonperturbative and systematically reducible framework for open-system cQED dynamics. The key observation is that pseudomode elimination is not fundamentally tied to linearity but to representability: any eliminated sector whose influence on the retained subsystem admits a rational self-energy can be replaced by a finite set of damped auxiliary modes, independent of the internal nonlinear structure of the retained Hamiltonian. We develop the general theory in the Heisenberg picture via a Dyson equation for the retained-mode Green's function, then demonstrate closed-form elimination for two-, three-, and four-mode Kerr-coupled systems with bilinear exchange and three-wave mixing interactions. The resulting framework substantially reduces the computational overhead of open-system cQED modeling while remaining faithful to the underlying physics, provided the spectral description of the eliminated sector is chosen to match the experimentally measured response functions of the hardware.
papers.authors: M. Gabriela Boada G., Nicolas Dirnegger, Andrea Delgado, Prineha Narang

papers.title: Molecular Attoscope: Pulse Shape Spectroscopy of Electronic Coherence
papers.abstract: Tracking the coupled motion of electrons and nuclei on their intrinsic timescales is essential to understanding and controlling photochemical transformations. While attosecond techniques have provided unprecedented insight into electronic dynamics, they have largely been restricted to ionic systems, with nuclear motion often neglected or indirectly inferred. Here, we demonstrate a ``molecular attoscope", which uses shaped laser pulses in the deep ultraviolet to perform a coherent measurement of electronic and nuclear dynamics in an entangled wave packet in neutral benzene. This enables us to trace both the 856-attosecond-period electronic motion and the 36-femtosecond-period nuclear motion. We observe electronic coherence persisting over hundreds of optical cycles, modulated by nuclear dynamics. Our holographic approach is general, and lays the groundwork for coherent measurements capable of visualizing the evolution of the coupled electronic-nuclear wave function in real time.
papers.authors: Loc Thi-Hoang Ngo, Julia Codere, Javin Ohara, Brian Kaufman, Martin G Cohen, Scott Liguori, Varun Makhija, Tamas Rozgonyi, Philipp Marquetand, Matthew Bain, Brett J Pearson, Ruaridh Forbes, Thomas Weinacht

papers.title: Temporal State Tomography via Quantum Snapshotting the Temporal Quasiprobabilities
papers.abstract: Quantum tomography is a cornerstone of quantum information science, enabling the reconstruction of states and channels from experimental data. Here we introduce a new paradigm, temporal state tomography (TST), for reconstructing quantum processes across multiple times. Our approach is based on temporal quasiprobability distributions (TQDs), which, in the informationally complete setting, provide a complete description of multi-time quantum processes and uniquely determine temporal states. We formulate TST as a unified framework for reconstructing both density operators and quantum channels within a single scheme. We show that any TQD can be obtained via classical post-processing of measurement outcomes generated by a fixed set of quantum instruments, thereby establishing a direct operational route to accessing TQDs experimentally. For informationally complete TQDs, the associated temporal state can be reconstructed via a temporal Bloch-type representation. Leveraging this correspondence, we derive the sample complexity of TST, thereby quantifying its statistical efficiency.
papers.authors: Zhian Jia

papers.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
papers.abstract: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. Using the Fokker--Planck equation for the Gaussian mixing measure, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture and study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.
papers.authors: Xiao-Kan Guo

papers.title: Uncertainty Relations and Quantum Speed Limits for Lattice-Regularized Fractional Kinetic Operators
papers.abstract: We study a ``hybrid'' kinetic operator on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ that combines a lattice-regularized momentum, with lattice constant $a$, and a fractional (L\'evy-type) power $\alpha\in(1,2]$. It is a bounded Fourier multiplier whose symbol is a fractional power of the central-difference Laplacian symbol; equivalently, it is a long-range hopping model with algebraically decaying hops. We prove that the kinetic operator is bounded and self-adjoint with purely absolutely continuous spectrum $[0,E_{\max}]$ (for every $\alpha\in(0,2]$), and that $\hat K+V$ is self-adjoint on $\mathcal D(V)$. The main new technical result is an exact position--momentum commutator with domain control for the singular multiplier it produces when $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and the resulting Robertson-type uncertainty relation together with its joint weak-lattice, weak-fractionality expansion. For $\alpha=2$ the uncertainty relation reduces to a known lattice result, which we attribute. For quantum speed limits we recall the bandwidth bound $\tau_\perp\ge\pi\hbar/E_{\max}$, a direct consequence of the Mandelstam--Tamm bound, and evaluate the Mandelstam--Tamm and Margolus--Levitin bounds for Gaussian states in closed form, including their crossover as a function of $\alpha$. To leading order the lattice reduces the energy variance of a Gaussian state and therefore raises the Mandelstam--Tamm bound; the effect of the fractional order is controlled by the width of the state relative to a reference momentum $p_0$ through an explicit crossover width $\sigma_*$. For $\hat H=\hat K-F\hat x$ we show that $\ave{\hx}(t)$ is exactly periodic for every state, and discuss ion-chain realizations.
papers.authors: M. W. AlMasri

papers.title: Rotating End of the World
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics and interior structures of dynamical end of the world (EoW) branes in the rotating BTZ black hole. By mapping the induced metric of the branes to an effective Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) system, we derive the first law of thermodynamics for the boundary conformal field theory (BCFT), incorporating boundary degrees of freedom. To construct this thermodynamics, we adopt two frameworks of black hole chemistry and the duality between the JT black hole and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. In addition, we verify that the shadow entropy is equivalent to the boundary entropy via Hubeny-Ryu-Takayanagi (HRT) surfaces. Furthermore, we explore the possible interior configurations of the EoW brane inside the horizon. Two representative configurations, namely single and double-joint EoW branes, are considered. These disparate configurations share the same exterior brane configuration outside the horizon. By comparing their energies, we show that a transition could occur within the horizon.
papers.authors: Kyung Kiu Kim, Hwajin Eom, Jung Hun Lee, Yunseok Seo

papers.title: Visual Characteristics of a Rotating Black Hole in $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity with Thin Accretion Disk Under EHT Constraints
papers.abstract: This study investigates the visual characteristics of a rotating black hole (BH) within the fabric of $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity illuminated with two illumination models, such as a celestial light sphere and a thin accretion disk. To visualize the BH shadow images, we use a recent fisheye camera model and ray-tracing method. And then, we focus on investigating the impact of the coupling parameter $\alpha$ and the spin parameter $a$ on the shadow images. The results exhibit that the shadow radius decreases, while the shadow deviation increases with the aid of $\alpha$. However, with respect to $a$, the shadow radius is slightly increased compared to the corresponding shadow deviation. For a celestial light sphere, the increasing values of $\alpha$, lead to a decrease in the corresponding photon ring, while the space-dragging effect becomes more prominent with increasing $a$. For a thin accretion disk, we enhance its inner edge to the BH event horizon, and the particle motion is different in the regions inside and outside the innermost stable circular orbit. The result demonstrates that the shadow becomes progressively asymmetric with $a$, while the overall size of the inner shadow gradually decreases with the variations of $\alpha$. Subsequently, we also investigated the distinct features of red-shift configurations on the disk for both direct and lensed images. Additionally, we used the latest observational data from M87* and Sgr A* to impose certain parameter constraints on $\alpha$; the results depict the consistency of our considering the BH model.
papers.authors: Muhammad Israr Aslam, Manahil Ali, Sultan Hussain, Abdul Malik Sultan, Xiao-Xiong Zeng

papers.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
papers.abstract: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.
papers.authors: Adam Kmec, Lionel Mason, Romain Ruzziconi

papers.title: Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution with Majorana Memories
papers.abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) certifies secrecy from Bell nonlocality and has been demonstrated with ions, atoms, and photons. Majorana parity qubits are proposed as network memories, but their operations and noise have not been connected to device-independent security. We show that Clifford-only Majorana operations cannot violate the CHSH inequality on a heralded pair, so a node needs a non-Clifford resource, which we confine to one party's test rounds. Because quasiparticle poisoning flips the total island parity, a parity flag read before the inputs are drawn preserves device independence and turns the poisoning distance cutoff into a rate penalty; flag errors restore part of the loss in proportion to the miss probability. We derive closed-form Bell statistics for realistic heralding and anisotropic Majorana noise, instantiate a block-based finite-size key length, and find that 2025 tetron prototypes cannot yet certify a key. We identify the hardware milestones that would.
papers.authors: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Characterizing entanglement dynamics in QED scattering processes
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement among helicity degrees of freedom in quantum electrodynamics (QED) scattering processes at fixed momentum, modeled as quantum maps whose spectral structure determines the associated entanglement dynamics. We show that, for fermion-fermion scatterings, parity invariance preserves maximal entanglement and generically leads to entanglement saturation under iterations of the maps. The structure of the maps also provides an accurate description of the entanglement dynamics in processes involving both fermions and photons.
papers.authors: Massimo Blasone, Silvio De Siena, Gaetano Lambiase, Bruno Micciola, Kyrylo Simonov

papers.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-St\"ackel problem in the non-diagonal case
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--St\"ackel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.
papers.authors: Alexey V. Bolsinov, Andrey Yu. Konyaev, Vladimir S. Matveev

papers.title: Geometry of Critical Couplings, Quartic Binding, and Spectral Shift for Concentric $\delta$-Shells
papers.abstract: We study the first zero-energy resonance of finitely many attractive concentric spherical $\delta$-shells with fixed radii and variable strengths. The positive critical strengths form a smooth hypersurface in coupling space. For every nonzero tangent redistribution we calculate its second fundamental form as an explicit strictly positive quadratic form $C_a$ in cumulative weighted coupling changes. Along the straight perturbation $g_*+\varepsilon a$, the same coefficient determines the unique emerging bound state, $E_b=-C_a^2\varepsilon^4+O(|\varepsilon|^5)$, for either sign of $\varepsilon$, and the crossover of the canonically normalized total spectral shift on the scale $k\asymp\varepsilon^2$. We also give a global smooth parametrization of the positive critical surface by probability weights, determine the exact attainable interval of effective ranges, and reconstruct all critical strengths from individual threshold-pole responses. An exact coupling coordinate gives a uniform $O(k^3)$ spectral-shift normal form and a differentiated $O(k^2)$ estimate without a restriction on the ratio of coupling distance to wave number. The scattering determinant and general threshold exponents are established inputs. Our results give the model-specific curvature coefficient, its spectral consequences, and a complete local and global description of the first-critical configurations.
papers.authors: Masahiro Kaminaga

papers.title: Modeling the Disjunction Effect within Classical Probability: A New Decision Process Model and Comparison with Quantum-like Models
papers.abstract: In a Prisoner's Dilemma experiment, participants defected less often when the opponent's move was unknown than when they were told that the opponent had defected or that the opponent had cooperated. This disjunction effect has often been interpreted as a violation of the classical law of total probability and has motivated quantum-like models of decision making. We re-examine this interpretation and identify a strong assumption implicit in the conventional classical model. The conventional model uses the two informed conditions to represent the full range of participants' expectations and thus treats every participant as certain of the opponent's move even when that move is unknown. We relax this premise by introducing a continuous parameter for each participant's degree of expectation that the opponent will defect. Participants are grouped by expectation level, with the intermediate groups representing ambiguous expectations. A standard quantum-like model offers a different account of this same uncertainty about the opponent's move. In that model, ambiguity arises through superposition, and ambiguous pure states are generic (dense and of full unitarily invariant measure on the unit sphere), so certainty states are mathematically exceptional. Despite this difference in how ambiguity is represented, the proposed classical model can reproduce the observed strong disjunction effect while satisfying the classical law of total probability. More generally, we prove that it can exactly reproduce any triple of defection rates strictly between zero and one, including every such triple generated by the quantum-like model. The proposed model is therefore no less expressive than the quantum-like model for these three observable rates while remaining entirely within classical probability, and the substantive difference between the two lies in how they represent ambiguity and interpret events.
papers.authors: Ryo Nasu, Yoshihiro Maruyama

papers.title: Precision Spectroscopy of a Trapped Ion Using a Bath of Ultracold Atoms
papers.abstract: We perform laser spectroscopy of a trapped ion that is not directly laser cooled. An ultracold atomic bath continuously cools the internal degrees of freedom of the ion to its hyperfine ground state via spin-exchange collisions, while a cotrapped $^{174}$Yb$^+$ ion sympathetically cools the external degrees of freedom. Successful laser excitation is detected via state-selective charge transfer following a collision with an atom and subsequent ion loss. As a demonstration of this spectroscopic technique, we probe the $6^2S_{1/2}\rightarrow 6^2P_{3/2}$ transition at 329 nm in $^{173}$Yb$^+$ and measure the magnetic and electric hyperfine interaction constants for the $6^2P_{3/2}$ state to be A = -241(1) MHz and B = 1460(8) MHz, respectively. Our results are in agreement with a previous measurement obtained in a hollow-cathode discharge experiment but are a factor of 6-9 more precise. The techniques demonstrated in this work may be extended to perform precision spectroscopy on ions with complex level structures, with applications in fundamental physics.
papers.authors: Egor Kovlakov, Rene Gerritsma

papers.title: Analytical Solution of Spinning, Eccentric Binary Black Hole Dynamics at the Second Post-Newtonian Order
papers.abstract: Recent gravitational wave (GW) detections showing signatures of eccentricity and spin precession underscore the need to model binary black holes (BBHs) possessing these features simultaneously. Most efforts over the past fifteen years to model spinning BBHs and their corresponding GWs have relied on heuristically twisting waveforms from nonprecessing systems. This approach is based on empirical observations rather than first principles. This article aims to model the dynamics of spinning and eccentric BBHs from a first-principles approach using the post-Newtonian (PN) approximation within general relativity. Building on the already-existing 1.5PN solution, we construct an analytical solution for the time evolution of the relative separation vector, the individual black hole spin vectors, and the orbital angular momentum vector at 2PN order for BBHs with arbitrary spins and eccentricity. Such a solution is not fully 2PN accurate in that the tiny orbital timescale fluctuations in the solutions for the spins are only leading 1.5PN order accurate, instead of 2PN. However, it is shown that our new 2PN solution is still an order of magnitude improvement over the earlier 1.5PN solution, underlining the subdominant nature of the neglected next-to-leading-order oscillations in the spin solutions.
papers.authors: Tom Colin, Sashwat Tanay, Laura Bernard

papers.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.
papers.authors: Frederic Latremoliere

papers.title: Observational Signatures of Exact Black Hole Solutions in a Dark Matter Halo
papers.abstract: In this work, we derive novel exact solutions describing Schwarzschild-like black holes (BHs) embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter (DM) halo density profile and investigate their geometric, dynamical, and observational signatures arising from such geometries. We begin by analyzing the horizon structure and spacetime curvature invariants, as well as examining the energy conditions associated with the DM halo. Subsequently, we study the influence of the DM halo on both timelike and null geodesics in the resulting geometry. Finally, we obtain observational constraints on the DM halo parameters by comparing the model predictions with weak-field data from Mercury and the S2 star orbit, as well as with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) shadow measurements of M87$^\star$ and Sgr~A$^\star$, combined with the corresponding EHT and GRAVITY measurements of the BH mass and distance. Using Bayesian inference and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, we obtain the posterior distributions of the model parameters and derive 95\% upper limits on the DM halo parameters. For M87$^\star$, we obtain $\rho_s<11.83~M_\odot\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$ and $r_s<54.36~{\rm kpc}$. For Sgr~A$^\star$, the EHT, GRAVITY, and combined EHT+GRAVITY analyses give $\rho_s<31.56$, $16.76$, and $21.25~M_\odot\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$, respectively. We find that all three cases lead to similar constraints on $r_s$ for Sgr~A$^\star$. Our analysis provides valuable insight into probing the potential influence of DM halo environments on spacetime geometry and observable properties of astrophysical BHs, offering an alternative perspective on BH-DM interactions.
papers.authors: Azalbek Boltaev, Tursunali Xamidov, Sanjar Shaymatov

papers.title: How to find expressible and trainable parameterized quantum circuits?
papers.abstract: Whether parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) can be systematically constructed to be both trainable and expressive remains an open question. Highly expressive PQCs often exhibit barren plateaus, while several trainable alternatives admit efficient classical simulation. We prove that deciding whether a PQC family exhibits a barren plateau is undecidable in general. However, we derive a practical finite-sample, dimension-independent concentration bound for estimating the variance of a PQC cost function, yielding explicit trainability guarantees. Across commonly used ans\"atze, we observe an anticorrelation between trainability and expressibility, consistent with theoretical insights. Building on this observation, we propose a property-based ansatz-search framework for identifying circuits that combine trainability and expressibility. We demonstrate its practical viability on a real quantum computer and apply it to variational quantum algorithms. We identify quantum neural network ans\"atze with improved effective dimension using over six times fewer parameters, and for VQE on $\mathrm{H}_2$ we achieve UCCSD-like accuracy at substantially reduced circuit complexity.
papers.authors: Peter R\"oseler, Dennis Willsch, Kristel Michielsen

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang energy for a dilute gas of hard spheres: an upper bound
papers.abstract: We consider a quantum gas consisting of $N$ hard spheres with radius $\frak{a} > 0$, obeying bosonic statistics and moving in the box $\Lambda = [0;L]^3$ with periodic boundary conditions. We are interested in the ground state energy per unit volume in the thermodynamic limit, with $N, L \to \infty$ at fixed density $\rho = N / L^3$. We derive an upper bound for the ground state energy density, matching the famous Lee-Huang-Yang formula, up to lower order terms, in the dilute limit $\rho \frak{a}^3 \ll 1$.
papers.authors: Giulia Basti, Morris Brooks, Serena Cenatiempo, Alessandro Olgiati, Benjamin Schlein

papers.title: Integrability from Homotopy Algebras
papers.abstract: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in the study of field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. The semi-classical equivalence of the two theories is expected on general grounds, as the principal chiral model arises by eliminating trivial pairs and gauge fixing. We construct this equivalence explicitly as an off-shell, cyclic quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing the two theories, and show that it directly encodes the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.
papers.authors: Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles Alastair Stephen Young

papers.title: What is a minimum work transition in stochastic thermodynamics?
papers.abstract: We reassess the concept of transition at minimum work in classical stochastic finite-time thermodynamics, when the system dynamics is modelled by a diffusion process. We show that a well-posed formulation of the optimal control problem corresponding to the minimization of the mean work done on the system during a finite-time transition necessarily requires taking into account speed limits on control protocols. This fact has major qualitative consequences. First, it permits to discriminate between optimal swift engineered equilibration and transitions at minimum work. Second, it shows that in the limit when speed limits are removed, only transitions specified by generalized Schr\"odinger bridges admit a consistent physical interpretation. To illustrate these points, we focus on the simplest model problem: a levitating particle in a Gaussian moving trap.
papers.authors: Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi, Julia Sanders

papers.title: Mixed-state Phases from Higher-order SSPTs with Kramers-Wannier Symmetry
papers.abstract: Mixed-state phases have recently attracted significant attention as a generalization beyond their pure-state counterparts. Prominent examples include mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phases and the strong-to-weak symmetry breaking (SWSSB) phases. It has been shown recently that mSPT phases admit a holographic dual description in terms of higher-order subsystem SPT phases. In this work, we investigate the mixed-state phases obtained by tracing out the bulk degrees of freedom of higher-order subsystem SPT phases protected by non-invertible symmetries. We find that the resulting mixed-states exhibit the coexistence of the symmetry-protected topological order and SWSSB. We also use the interface as a probe to characterize the mixed-state phases, and specifically, when there is no local modification to preserve the symmetries across the interface, the two sides of the interface are in distinct phases.
papers.authors: Aswin Parayil Mana, Zijian Song, Fei Yan, Tzu-Chieh Wei

papers.title: Carrollian correlators in black hole perturbation theory
papers.abstract: In this note, we clarify the relationship between the two-point Carrollian correlator and massless scattering in a black hole background. It turns out that there are two types of Carrollian correlators at the null boundaries of each asymptotically flat spacetime. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ should be regularized by subtracting the flat-space analog, and it is the position space version of the reflection amplitude for massless scattering. On the other hand, the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to the future horizon $\mathcal H^+$ is absent in flat space, and it is the position space version of the transmission amplitude. The poles of the Carrollian correlators are governed by null geodesics from $\mathscr I^-$ to either $\mathscr I^+$ or $\mathcal H^+$, and these geodesics define two classes of classical equations in Carrollian space. These equations relate the Shapiro time delay to the deflection angle and are determined purely by the boundary data. We find that, for small deflection angles, the time delay for the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+/\mathcal H^+$ exhibits logarithmic/quadratic behavior. On the other hand, when the deflection angle is large, the time delay always increases linearly for both correlators. We further establish a relation between the low-frequency bulk scattering coefficients and the leading non-contact contributions at late times. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ features an inverse-square tail $\tau^{-2}$ with an explicit angular distribution $K_2$. We have numerically confirmed this angle-dependent late-time tail.
papers.authors: Jiang Long, Zhan-Jia Qu, Hong-Yang Xiao

papers.title: Landscape-Similarity-Guided Optimization in Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
papers.abstract: Divide-and-conquer strategies mitigate hardware constraints for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices by partitioning large interaction graphs into smaller, hardware-compatible sub-problems. However, this approach introduces a severe classical training bottleneck: a decomposition across $m$ boundary nodes generates $2^m$ distinct sub-problems that typically require independent optimization. In this work, we quantify correlations between reduced QAOA energy landscapes using a landscape-overlap measure $q$ and Pearson correlation $r$, and investigate their usefulness for parameter transfer. For $p=1$ on the studied long-range percolation graphs with $L=50$--$400$, the displayed $q(s)$ curves cross near $s\approx0.6$. This observation on finite systems does not establish a thermodynamic phase transition. Exploiting these correlations, we introduce Doubly Optimized QAOA (DO-QAOA), which fully optimizes one representative reduced instance and transfers its parameters to the remaining frozen assignments, with target-specific refinement when required. We evaluated DO-QAOA on more than 6,000 circuits under the realistic noise model, DO-QAOA uses approximately $285$--$386\times$ fewer quantum shots and has approximately $6.5$--$23.9\times$ shorter runtime than FrozenQubits, with equal or lower dataset-averaged Approximation Ratio Gap (ARG).
papers.authors: Sokea Sang, Leanghok Hour, Sanghyeon Lee, Aniket Patra, Hee Chul Park, Moon Jip Park, Youngsun Han

papers.title: Intractability of Witnessing an Entangled Measurement Device Independently
papers.abstract: Protocols have been previously proposed to certify that a measurement is entangled in a fully device-independent manner. Here, I provide models for these protocols in which the claimed measurement is not entangled, and demonstrate it is always possible to displace entanglement from a given measurement to the measured state for a general class of device-independent scenarios. This indicates that no black-box measurement scenario requires a specific chosen measurement to be entangled in order to replicate its behavior, which is relevant to our fundamental understanding of this phenomenon and how to witness it.
papers.authors: Peter Bierhorst

papers.title: Chaotic Dynamics around a Hairy Black Hole in Horndeski Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the chaotic dynamics of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmet- ric hairy black hole (BH) in Horndeski gravity, using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations closed by the Tulczyjew-Dixon condition. Bound orbits are identified by fixing the angular momen- tum and setting the energy according to the effective potential, so that the accessible parameter range is bounded by a critical hair parameter, hcrit, which varies non-monotonically with the spin. We analyze the resulting chaotic behavior using Lyapunov exponents, Poincare sections, and re- constructed attractors. We find that the response of these indicators to scalar hair is orbit- and spin-dependent rather than universally monotonic. An analysis of orbital frequency ratios shows that, at physically maximal spin (S = 1), an approaching 2:1 azimuthal resonance overlapping a persistent 1:1 polar lock amplifies chaos, while the hair-driven erosion of potential saddles tends to suppress it. At non-physical spin (S = 1.5), the Lyapunov exponent decreases monotonically. Gravitational waveforms constructed via the quadrupole formula inherit the same state-specific pattern: the correlation between the two polarization modes varies non-monotonically with h, in step with the Lyapunov exponent. These results show that chaotic indicators respond to scalar hair in an orbit- and resonance-dependent manner rather than through simple monotonic suppres- sion, and identify the spin-dependent resonance structure as an essential ingredient for interpreting chaos around hairy black holes.
papers.authors: Yang Yu, Ruo-Ting Chen, Shulan Li, Dan Zhang, Jian-Pin Wu

papers.title: Gradually opening Schr\"odinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics predicts that unobserved systems may exist in a superposition of states, yet measurement produces definite outcomes, a tension at the heart of the quantum-to-classical boundary. How the transformation between these opposing regimes unfolds as observation strength increases has remained experimentally elusive. Here, by continuously tuning the measurement strength on a superconducting qubit, we reveal that measurement-dominated dynamics emerge not gradually but through multiple sharp transitions marked by the halting of coherent oscillations, state freezing near an attracting state, and the onset of quantum Zeno dynamics. Decoherence, rather than washing out this structure, reshapes it, reordering the transitions and decoupling signatures that coincide in idealised models. These results establish that the passage from quantum dynamics to measurement-dominated behaviour unfolds through a sequence of distinct transitions governed by the interplay between observation and environment.
papers.authors: Barkay Guttel, Danielle Gov, Noam Netzer, Uri Goldblatt, Sergey Hazanov, Lalit M. Joshi, Alessandro Romito, Yuval Gefen, Parveen Kumar, Kyrylo Snizhko, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum

papers.title: A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
papers.abstract: We study single field inflation with the inverse exponential potential, which has one free parameter besides the energy scale. For a wide range of parameter space, its predictions for the scalar spectral index and the tensor to scalar ratio lie within the $1\sigma$ region of the combined SPA$+$BK$+$DESI data, and the wider family of inverse power law exponential potentials behaves similarly. We compare these predictions with those of the $R^2$ model, monomial potentials, $\alpha$-attractors, non-minimally coupled Higgs like inflation and a radiatively corrected plateau potential. The $R^2$ and monomial predictions lie near or outside the $2\sigma$ boundary of the same data, whereas the non-minimally coupled Higgs like and radiatively corrected plateau families overlap the favoured contours over part of their parameter space. To describe reheating, we add a steep exponential term that is negligible during inflation and, together with the inverse exponential term, creates a minimum about which the inflaton oscillates. The maximum reheating temperatures are $T_{\rm rh}\sim10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,{\rm GeV}$, consistent with the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis bound. Coupling the inflaton to a Dirac fermion through a Yukawa interaction, these temperatures require couplings comparable to the standard model charged lepton Yukawa couplings. Nonperturbative fermion production transfers negligible energy, and perturbative decay completes reheating. The same coupling induces a one loop correction to the inflationary potential, which limits the radiatively safe reheating temperature to $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}$.
papers.authors: Md. Wali Hossain

papers.title: Sublinear Time Quantum Algorithm for Attention Approximation
papers.abstract: Given the query, key and value matrices $Q, K, V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, the attention module is defined as $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)=D^{-1}AV$ where $A=\exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})$ with $\exp(\cdot)$ applied entrywise, $D=\mathrm{diag}(A\mathbf{1}_n)$. The attention module is the backbone of modern transformers and large language models, but explicitly forming the softmax matrix $D^{-1}A$ incurs $\Omega(n^2)$ time, motivating numerous approximation schemes that reduce runtime to $\widetilde O(nd)$ via sparsity or low-rank factorization. We propose a quantum data structure that approximates any row of $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)$ using only row queries to $Q, K, V$. Our algorithm preprocesses these matrices in $\widetilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1} n^{0.5} (s_\lambda^{3} + s_\lambda^{2} d + d) + \epsilon^{-2} s_\lambda d)$ time, where $\epsilon$ is the target accuracy and $s_\lambda$ is the $\lambda$-statistical dimension of the exponential kernel defined by $Q$ and $K$. Each row query can be answered in $\widetilde{O}(s_\lambda^2 + s_\lambda d)$ time. If every row sum of $A$ exceeds $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$, then with probability $1-1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ the answers have Frobenius-norm error $O(\beta\|D^{-1}\|(\epsilon\|A\|_F+\lambda\sqrt n)\|V\|_F)$. Here $\beta=(1-(\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n)\|D^{-1}\|)^{-1}\geq 1$ is close to $1$ when every row sum is much larger than $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$. To our knowledge, this is the first quantum data structure that approximates rows of the attention matrix in sublinear time with respect to $n$. Our approach relies on a quantum Nystr\"om approximation of the exponential kernel, quantum multivariate mean estimation for computing $D$, and quantum sampling of the rows of $V$ by their squared norms, with a median over independent samples, for the multiplication with $V$.
papers.authors: Zhao Song, Jianfei Xue, Jiahao Zhang, Lichen Zhang

papers.title: TopoLS: Lattice Surgery Compilation via Topological Program Transformations
papers.abstract: Lattice surgery is a leading approach for implementing fault-tolerant logical operations in surface code quantum computing. Current compilers largely treat lattice surgery as a layout problem downstream of a gate-level circuit; this circuit-centric view hinders a substantial optimization opportunity: lattice surgery computations are topological programs whose semantics are determined by connectivity, so different concrete space-time realizations may implement the same computation while offering different space-time volumes. Circuit-centric compilers, however, commit to fixed realizations throughout the program. We tackle this problem by presenting TopoLS, a topology-centric compiler that uses ZX diagrams as the intermediate representation (IR) for automated lattice surgery compilation. Compiler transformations on this graph preserve its semantics, and the backend must produce a valid pipe diagram, i.e., a 3D space-time layout of the lattice surgery program, with the same semantics. TopoLS first simplifies the graph and slices it into layers, and then uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to place the graph's nodes as cubes in a 3D grid and to route its edges as pipes. To scale to large circuits, TopoLS partitions the graph so that each search step routes a bounded number of connections. Across evaluated benchmarks, TopoLS reduces space-time volume by 46% on average over prior circuit-centric compilers, with improvements ranging from 25% to 90%, while exhibiting strong empirical scalability on large benchmark families.
papers.authors: Junyu Zhou, Yuhao Liu, Ethan Decker, Justin Kalloor, Mathias Weiden, Kean Chen, Costin Iancu, Gushu Li

papers.title: Modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the IKKT model
papers.abstract: The gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the IKKT or IIB matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the Yang-Mills-type matrix action with the induced Einstein-Hilbert action. This combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified Einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. In particular we find extra non-Ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.
papers.authors: Harold C. Steinacker

papers.title: Chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing via flux-mediated transmon mechanical coupling: Theory and device requirements
papers.abstract: Measurements of local gravitational acceleration support geophysics and inertial navigation. We develop a circuit-level model of a chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing head that longitudinally couples a nanomechanical beam in a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) loop to an independently flux-biased transmon. The interaction encodes changes in gravitational acceleration in the qubit Ramsey phase. We derive the phase response and evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the reduced qubit state and the classical Fisher information accessible through Ramsey readout. The model includes qubit relaxation and dephasing, mechanical damping, flux noise, readout infidelity, and cycle overhead. With other model inputs fixed, the competition between phase gain and responsivity-dependent decoherence yields a finite optimal transmon frequency responsivity to mechanical-loop flux. The decoherence model includes dephasing from low-frequency flux noise in the mechanical SQUID loop and coupling-dependent qubit dephasing from the mechanical bath. For the prospective integrated-device parameter set, Ramsey readout at the first mechanical revival gives a conditional projection of the sensing head's sensitivity of $1.1\times10^{-5}$ m s$^{-2}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ at an interrogation time of 10.0 $\mu$s. This estimate uses the single-cycle-equivalent Fisher-information rate for statistically independent cycles. A separate analysis identifies the joint mechanical, circuit, flux-noise, coherence, timing, and readout parameters needed within the model to reach $10^{-6}$-class internal sensitivity. These results specify the design tradeoffs and component requirements for Ramsey gravimetry in the proposed SQUID-transmon electromechanical sensing head.
papers.authors: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Spin-1 quantum annealing with anisotropy-controlled intermediate-state pathways
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing offers a promising strategy for solving complex optimization problems by encoding the solution into the ground state of a problem Hamiltonian. While most implementations rely on spin-$1/2$ systems, we explore the performance of quantum annealing on a spin-$1$ system where the problem Hamiltonian includes a single ion anisotropy term of the form $D\sum (S^z)^2$. Our results reveal that for a suitable range of the anisotropy strength $D$, the spin-$1$ annealer reaches the ground state with higher fidelity. We attribute this performance to the presence of the intermediate spin level and the tunable anisotropy, which together enable the algorithm to traverse the energy landscape through smaller, incremental steps instead of a single large spin flip. This mechanism effectively lowers barriers in the configuration space and stabilizes the evolution. These findings suggest that higher spin annealers offer intrinsic advantages for robust and flexible quantum optimization, especially for problems naturally formulated with ternary decision variables.
papers.authors: M. Haider Akbar, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

papers.title: Observational constraints on early time non-phantom behaviour of dynamical dark energy
papers.abstract: We investigate dynamical dark energy models in which the scalar field component is non-phantom at early times. The models include a single-exponential thawing field, a double-exponential scaling--thawing field, and extensions in which a steep exponential scaling field is combined with a cosmological constant, a constant-$w$ fluid, or a CPL fluid. We confront them with Planck PR4 CMB temperature, polarisation and lensing data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements and the Pantheon$+$ supernova sample. The background parameters are stable across all models, with $H_0 \simeq 67.7$--$68.3\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, so none of the models relieves the Hubble tension. The CPL parametrization prefers $w_0>-1$ and $w_a<0$ at $\sim\!2.7\sigma$ relative to $\Lambda$CDM, corresponding to phantom behaviour at low redshift. The constant-$w$ and thawing models remain consistent with a cosmological constant. When an early scaling phase is added, the data limit the peak early dark energy fraction to $f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.0075$ ($f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.015$ for SC$+$CPL). This requires a steep potential, $\lambda_2 \gtrsim 30$, and keeps the scalar-field density below the half-percent level at matter--radiation equality. Early scaling dynamics therefore cannot alter the sound horizon enough to address the Hubble tension. The scaling models fit the data as well as $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2_{\mathrm{min}}\lesssim 1.4$), but they are disfavoured by AIC and BIC because of their additional, weakly constrained parameters. Adding a scaling field to CPL does not improve the fit. Late-time evolving dark energy is mildly preferred by the data, while a simple early scaling phase offers no benefit.
papers.authors: Sk. Sohail, Sonej Alam, Md. Wali Hossain

papers.title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.
papers.authors: Ruiting Mao, Jeong Eun Lee, Matthew C. Edwards

papers.title: Entanglement, equivalence principle, and HBAR entropy, in a new bumblebee black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum correlations, atomic excitation, and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) entropy near a recently proposed bumblebee black hole with spacelike or lightlike Lorentz violating vacuum configurations. Using localized scalar field packets and the near horizon Rindler correspondence, we evaluate the logarithmic negativity and mutual information as functions of observer position, packet frequency, and geometric deformation. Configurations with the same geometry yield identical correlation measures. Positive geometric deformations partially counteract entanglement degradation, with the largest differences occurring at low frequencies. We also compute the excitation probability of a freely falling two level atom using the time coordinate normalized at spatial infinity. At leading near horizon order and within the frequency hierarchy adopted, its thermal factor agrees with the local flat spacetime acceleration radiation result. Finally, we derive the HBAR entropy flux and its relation to the radiative horizon area loss using the canonical conserved energy. The area coefficient depends on the causal character of the vacuum even for configurations with identical geometries: the spacelike case acquires a factor set by the bumblebee coupling, while the lightlike case gives the usual one quarter coefficient. These coefficients reproduce the corresponding thermodynamic entropy factors.
papers.authors: A. A. Ara\'ujo Filho, Wentao Liu

papers.title: Local causal consistency as a foundational principle for indefinite causal order
papers.abstract: Quantum processes with indefinite causal order challenge the description of physical experiments as globally ordered networks while retaining causality within each local laboratory. Whether and how this local causal requirement constrains the information flow in such quantum processes remains unclear. Here we formalize the principle of local causal consistency through experiments in which each laboratory performs two sequential operations and may use the earlier outcome to choose the later operation. The principle is equivalent to a set of parity-erasure conditions: the joint earlier outcomes for any set of laboratories reveal no information about the parity of the corresponding independent, uniformly random binary settings. We show that these conditions precisely characterize, via local process tomography, the multipartite channels representing valid quantum processes; characterize classical process-matrix correlations through local readout of outcome tables; and, together with the gentle-measurement property, constrain general quantum correlations with indefinite causal order. Moreover, these results extend naturally to a vast class of theories beyond quantum theory. Our findings provide an operational account of how causality within local laboratories shapes indefinite causal structure and the correlations it supports, revealing a fundamental constraint on information exchange through indefinite causal structure.
papers.authors: Zixuan Liu, Ognyan Oreshkov

papers.title: Analysis of LIGO glitches during the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
papers.abstract: This paper presents an analysis of noise transients observed in LIGO data during the first part of the fourth observing run, using the unsupervised machine learning technique t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) to examine the behavior of glitch groups. Based on the t-SNE output, we apply Agglomerative Clustering in combination with the Silhouette Score to determine the optimal number of groups. We then track these groups over time and investigate correlations between their occurrence and environmental or instrumental conditions. At the Livingston observatory, the most common glitches during O4a were seasonal and associated with ground motion, whereas at Hanford, the most prevalent glitches were related to instrumental conditions.
papers.authors: Tabata Aira Ferreira, Gabriela Gonz\'alez, Osvaldo Salas

papers.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
papers.abstract: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.
papers.authors: Zizhuo Zhao, Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, Jing Shu

papers.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.
papers.authors: Ming-Yu Lei, Bei Zhou, Xiaoyuan Huang

papers.title: IR/UV mixing from higher-order interactions in a Scalar Field
papers.abstract: The observed vacuum energy lies far below the usual quantum-field-theoretic estimate. We construct a preferred-frame reduced scalar Hamiltonian in which a nonlocal quartic field derivative interaction produces a wavevector dependence proportional to $|\vec k|^8$ for modes below a smoothly defined scale. Within the quartic oscillator regime, the ground-state energy and excitation gaps are $\propto |\vec k|^{8/3}$. The preferred frame is characterized by a timelike clock-field background. The Planck energy is reached at a substantially smaller value of the spatial wavevector due to its supra-linear mode-energy dependence. The proposed interaction is instantaneous in the preferred frame and yields a Hamiltonian bounded below. Normalizing the peak of the ground-state energy to the Planck scale, together with Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson (CKN) saturation, applied as a matching recipe rather than as an {\it {ab initio}} calculation, fixes the cutoff scale at $k_G\sim k_{Pl}^{1/3}k_{box}^{2/3}$. Modes above the smooth cutoff scale retain their ordinary scalar dynamics. We assume that the interaction-induced ground-state energy shift gravitates, as do other contributions. CKN saturation is imposed on the total vacuum energy, comprising this shift and the other vacuum contributions. Identifying the inferred infrared scale phenomenologically with the cosmic event horizon reproduces the holographic-dark-energy relation $\rho_{vac}\propto\frac{M_{Pl}^2}{R_h^2}$, provided the coupling tracks the horizon; the resulting holographic fluid has $w_0\simeq-0.89$.
papers.authors: Satish Ramakrishna

papers.title: Tensor ideals of abelian type and quantum groups
papers.abstract: We initiate a study of tensor ideals in linear rigid monoidal categories that are kernels of linear monoidal functors to abelian monoidal categories. We develop general methods and apply them to the category of tilting modules over quantum groups as well as to some representation categories of finite groups. In an appendix on Duflo involutions in monoidal categories, we make a connection between Duflo involutions in the affine Weyl group and tensor ideals for quantum groups, and prove some of Lusztig's conjectures for arbitrary Coxeter groups, at equal parameters, without invoking the boundedness hypothesis.
papers.authors: Kevin Coulembier, Pavel Etingof, Victor Ostrik

papers.title: Addressable gate-based logical computation with quantum LDPC codes
papers.abstract: Quantum computing relies on quantum error correction for high-fidelity logical operations, but scaling to achieve near-term quantum utility is highly resource-intensive. High-rate quantum LDPC codes can reduce error correction overhead, yet realizing high-rate fault-tolerant computation with these codes remains a central challenge. Lattice surgery remains the main approach for addressable logical computation but at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d)$ time overhead. Other approaches rely on low-rate code switching methods or high space overhead homomorphic CNOT. In this work, we introduce a gate-based protocol for addressable single- and multi-qubit Clifford operations on individual logical qubits encoded within one or more quantum LDPC codes. Our scheme leverages logical transversal operations via an auxiliary -- a Bacon-Shor code or an unrotated surface code -- to perform logical operations with constant time overhead enabled by teleportation. We demonstrate the implementation of an overcomplete logical Clifford gate set and perform numerical simulations to evaluate the error-correction performance of our protocol. Additionally, our scheme can also realize any joint Pauli product measurement natively. Finally, we observe that our scheme can be integrated with magic state cultivation protocols to achieve universal, gate-based, and fully addressable quantum computation.
papers.authors: Laura Pecorari, Francesco Paolo Guerci, Hugo Perrin, Guido Pupillo

papers.title: Secure PAC Learning: Sample-Budget Laws and Quantum Data-Path Admissibility
papers.abstract: Security in machine learning is fragile when data are exfiltrated or perturbed, yet existing frameworks rarely connect data-path security to learnability. In this work, we develop an operational theory of secure learning grounded in the probably-approximately-correct (PAC) viewpoint. An explicit stopping time combines the event that a trained hypothesis attains a target accuracy with the event that a run-based validation gate halts within a finite sample budget. We derive a closed-form sufficient budget requirement for this joint PAC-within-budget guarantee under an admissible random-classification-noise channel. We then specialize the construction to a BB84-like quantum label path. Under the stated ideal single-qubit, authenticated-classical-channel, memoryless, basis-symmetric, collective-attack, asymptotic, and one-way-reconciliation assumptions, the standard Holevo bound gives the protocol-specific information-advantage criterion $1-2h(\eta) > 0$, with the threshold $\eta_{\mathrm{BB84}} \simeq 0.11$. The quantum layer is not invoked to reduce distribution-free PAC sample complexity; rather, it turns a designer-chosen classical noise tolerance into a physically testable, protocol-dependent security condition by linking information acquisition to observable disturbance. Below the threshold, the PAC and information-advantage conditions provide complementary statistical and physical guarantees; at or above it, the present protocol and proof no longer certify the latter. Basis sifting is incorporated explicitly in the conversion from sifted-sample budgets to expected raw channel uses.
papers.authors: Jeongho Bang

papers.title: Localisation with on-shell supersymmetry algebras via the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism: Localisation as gauge fixing
papers.abstract: The Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism provides a powerful technique to deal with gauge and global (super)symmetries that may only hold on shell. We argue that, since global (super)symmetries and gauge symmetries appear on an equal footing in the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, similarly localisation with respect to global (super)symmetries appears on an equal footing with gauge fixing of gauge symmetries; in general, when the gauge-fixing condition is not invariant under the global symmetries, localisation (with respect to a localising fermion) and gauge fixing (with respect to a gauge-fixing fermion) combine into a single operation. Furthermore, this perspective enables supersymmetric localisation using only on-shell supermultiplets, dispensing with auxiliary fields, extending an insight first discovered by Losev and Lysov arXiv:2312.13999. We provide the first examples of on-shell localisation for quantum field theories (together with a companion paper by Arvanitakis arXiv:2511.00144).
papers.authors: Leron Borsten, Dimitri Kanakaris, Hyungrok Kim

papers.title: A Rigorous Quantum Framework for Inequality-Constrained and Multi-Objective Binary Optimization: Quadratic Cost Functions and Empirical Evaluations
papers.abstract: The prospect of quantum solutions for complicated optimization problems is contingent on mapping the original problem onto a tractable quantum energy landscape, e.g. an Ising-type Hamiltonian. Subsequently, techniques like adiabatic optimization, quantum annealing, and the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can be used to find the ground state of this Hamiltonian. Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) is one prominent problem class for which this entire pipeline is well understood and has received considerable attention over the past years. In this work, we provide novel, tractable mappings for the maxima of multiple QUBO problems. Termed Multi-Objective Quantum Approximations, or MOQA for short, our framework allows us to recast new types of classical binary optimization problems as ground state problems of a tractable Ising-type Hamiltonian. This, in turn, opens the possibility of new quantum- and quantum-inspired solutions to a variety of problems that frequently occur in practical applications. In particular, MOQA can handle various types of routing and partitioning problems, as well as inequality-constrained binary optimization problems.
papers.authors: Sebastian Egginger, Kristina Kirova, Sonja Bruckner, Stefan Hillmich, Richard Kueng

papers.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
papers.abstract: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.
papers.authors: Mu-Chun Chen, Yan Cao

papers.title: Classification of Thouless pumps with non-invertible symmetries and implications for Floquet phases
papers.abstract: We study symmetry preserving adiabatic and Floquet dynamics of one-dimensional systems. Using quasiadiabatic evolution, we establish a correspondence between adiabatic cycles and invertible defects generated by spatially truncated Thouless pump operators. Employing the classification of gapped phases by module categories, we show that the Thouless pumps are classified by the group of autoequivalences of the module category. We then explicitly construct Thouless pump operators for minimal lattice models with $\text{Vec}_G$, Rep($G$), and Rep($H$) symmetries, and show how the Thouless pump operators have the group structure of autoequivalences. The Thouless pump operators, together with Hamiltonians with gapped ground states, are then used to construct Floquet drives. An analytic solution for the Floquet phase diagram characterized by winding numbers is constructed when the Floquet drives obey an Onsager algebra. Our approach points the way to a general connection between distinct Thouless pumps and distinct families of Floquet phases.
papers.authors: Yabo Li, Matteo Dell'Acqua, Aditi Mitra

papers.title: Effective Dynamics for Weakly Interacting Bosons in an Iterated High-Density Thermodynamic Limit
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of weakly interacting Bose gases on a three-dimensional torus of arbitrary volume. The coupling constant is supposed to be inversely proportional to the density, which is considered to be large and independent of the particle number. We take into account a class of initial states exhibiting quasi-complete Bose-Einstein condensation. For each fixed time in a finite interval, we prove the convergence of the one-particle reduced density matrix towards the projection onto the normalised order parameter describing the condensate - evolving according to the Hartree equation - in the iterated limit where the volume (and therefore the particle number), and subsequently the density go to infinity. The rate of convergence depends only on the density and on the decay of both the expected number of particles and the energy of the initial quasi-vacuum state.
papers.authors: Daniele Ferretti, Kalle Koskinen

papers.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
papers.abstract: Given any K\"ahler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $\Omega^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem. As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.
papers.authors: Ruggero Bandiera, Seokbong Seol, Mathieu Sti\'enon, Ping Xu

papers.title: Resource-Efficient Quantum Reinforcement Learning on NISQ Devices with Dynamic-Circuit Qubit Reuse and Grover-Based Trajectory Search
papers.abstract: A resource-efficient quantum reinforcement learning framework for finite-horizon quantum Markov decision processes is presented, employing dynamic-circuit qubit reuse to reduce the interaction-workspace requirements of multi-step execution. The framework integrates quantum state-transition and reward encoding, dynamic-circuit execution, quantum return evaluation, and Grover-based trajectory search. Its central contribution is a dynamic execution model in which a fixed interaction workspace is reused across sequential agent-environment interactions through mid-circuit measurement, qubit reset, and next-state propagation. For the considered benchmark, this approach reduces the interaction-workspace requirement from 7T qubits under a static circuit to a constant seven qubits, independent of the interaction horizon T. This corresponds to a 66% reduction for the three-step benchmark and transforms the interaction-workspace complexity from O(T) to O(1). Trajectory returns are evaluated using reversible quantum arithmetic, and Grover's algorithm identifies the optimal trajectories, so that return evaluation and trajectory search are performed within a unified quantum-native pipeline. Ideal simulations demonstrate that the dynamic implementation preserves the valid trajectory structure of the static formulation, with quantitative comparisons assessing the agreement between their trajectory distributions. Finally, execution on an IBM Heron-class processor demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed dynamic-circuit architecture on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware.
papers.authors: Thet Htar Su, Shaswot Shresthamali, Masaaki Kondo

papers.title: Large scale dynamical response of interacting $1d$ Fermi systems
papers.abstract: We consider the dynamics of a class of weakly interacting, gapless $1d$ fermionic systems, in presence of small external perturbations slowly varying in space and in time. We consider the evolution of the expectation values of the charge density and of the current density, in the thermodynamic limit and for low enough temperatures. We prove the validity and the asymptotic exactness of linear response in the limit of vanishing space-time variation of the perturbation, and we provide the explicit expression of the response of the system. The proof relies on the representation of the real time Duhamel expansion in terms of Euclidean correlation functions, for which we provide sharp estimates using rigorous renormalization group methods. The asymptotic exactness of linear response holds thanks to a cancellation for the scaling limit of the correlations that is reminiscent of bosonization, and which is derived rigorously using emergent chiral Ward identities.
papers.authors: Marcello Porta, Giuseppe Scola, Harman Preet Singh

papers.title: Construction of Kochen-Specker Sets from Mutually Unbiased Bases
papers.abstract: We give a constructive analysis of Kochen-Specker (KS) contextuality at the level of complete orthogonal bases (contexts). In dimension three, three noncomputational mutually unbiased bases generate a union of 165 rays and 130 contexts. Exact provenance accounting gives a symmetric decomposition: the three 69-ray lineages share 21 rays and 10 contexts, while each contributes 48 exclusive rays and 40 lineage-specific contexts. Each 69-ray, 50-context lineage is a KS configuration; as a hypergraph it is the 69-50 KS set reported earlier by Pavicic and Megill. This framework clarifies the relation among the Yu-Oh, Harding-Salinas Schmeis, Pavicic-Megill, and Cabello constructions. In dimensions four and five, we give parametrized orthogonality gadgets whose connector contexts force a central ray to be maximally unbiased relative to the computational basis. For the concrete four-dimensional example, the 20-ray gadget and the Cabello 18-ray set are informationally equivalent subsets of the 24-ray Peres-Mermin eigensystem, although their context hypergraphs have different two-valued-state behavior.
