These results highlight the observational degeneracy between Damour--Solodukhin wormholes and Schwarzschild black holes in the small-deformation regime, while identifying the geometric and dynamical effects through which this degeneracy may be investigated.
papers.authors: G. Alencar, V. H. U. Borralho, T. M. Crispim, Marcos V. de S. Silva

papers.title: Accretion disks and photon rings in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate thin accretion disks and photon rings around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity, connecting thermal emission with the optical effects of the radial geometry. At fixed orbital mass and accretion rate, the local radiative flux scales as $1/\sigma$ and the effective temperature as $1/\sigma^{1/4}$, where $\sigma=\sqrt{1-q/2}$ and $q$ is the effective curvature coupling. The innermost stable circular orbit and the critical impact parameter share their Schwarzschild values, together with an emitted efficiency of approximately $5.72\%$. Moreover, photon trajectories admit an exact angular rescaling that determines the strong deflection coefficient and the exponential accumulation of successive disk images. We construct images of an opaque thermal disk and a transparent emitting sheet, taking into account gravitational frequency shifts, orbital motion, and radial emissivity. Positive $q$ increases the local thermal emission and accelerates the accumulation of successive images around the common critical curve. Under the universal coupling assumptions associated with the quoted Solar System bounds, the fractional corrections are of order $10^{-11}$ in flux and $10^{-12}$ in temperature.
papers.authors: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, N. Heidari, P. H. M. Barros, Carlos F. S. Pereira

papers.title: Degenerate wormhole as a topological oscillator
papers.abstract: A spherically symmetric, matter free degenerate wormhole is considered as a gravitational system with a single collective degree of freedom, the radius of its throat. The classical dynamics is determined by applying the equivalence principle to the motion of the throat, while canonical quantization reduces the dynamics to a spectral problem with the dynamical symmetry group \(SU(1,1)\). The exact solution of this spectral problem reveals two qualitatively different regimes. For subPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits Bohr type states characterized by a gravitational Bohr radius \(\hbar^2/(GM^3)\). For superPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits a semiclassical regime represented by the Einstein Rosen wormhole with Schwarzschild gravitational radius \(2GM/c^2\). Thus, the model connects the familiar quantum bound state behavior with the semiclassical geometry of a gravitational horizon.
papers.authors: Juri Dimaschko

papers.title: Direct inference of cosmological mass growth via timing of black hole - pulsar binaries
papers.abstract: Cosmologically coupled black holes (CCBHs) respond to the expansion of the Universe, independently of conventional astrophysical processes. Recent CCBH solutions in General Relativity demonstrate evolution of gravitating mass $m_{\rm BH}\propto a^\kappa$, where $a$ is the cosmological scale factor. This can be tested through the orbital period timing of black hole (BH) pulsar (PSR) binaries. In contrast to previous methods used to constrain $\kappa$, pulsar timing measurement baselines span decades instead of gigayears, allowing sources of bias to be well-controlled. As a test case, we analyze the globular cluster BH+PSR candidate J0514--4002E (spin $P\sim 5.6~{\rm ms}$, orbital period $P_{\rm b}\sim 7~\rm days$) under the assumption that the companion is a CCBH. Taking the difference between the observed orbital and spin period derivatives removes all kinematic effects, leaving only the pulsar's intrinsic spin-down $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ as unknown. Setting $\dot{P}_{\rm int} = 0$, its physical minimum, gives a robust upper bound $\kappa \leqslant 3.95$ at $95\%$ confidence. We estimate $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ through the population of millisecond pulsars matched in spin and infer $\kappa = 0.82 \pm 1.67$ and $0.75 \pm 1.54$, using $H_0 = 67.6$ and $73.5\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Adopting typical baseline scaling of timing precision, the value $\kappa = 3$, argued elsewhere to link energized vacuum BH interiors to accelerated cosmological expansion, can be excluded or detected for this $2.35^{+0.20}_{-0.18}\,M_\odot$ companion at $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ confidence by 2031 and 2036, respectively.
papers.authors: Kevin S. Croker, Gibson B. Bowling, Christopher Cain, Jake Summers, Duncan Farrah, Jeremy Coles, Hayley Williams, Chris Pearson, Joshua Grumski-Flores, Viktor T. Toth, Joshua Cohon, Rogier A. Windhorst, Leander Thiele, Gregory Tarl\'e, Gustavo Niz, James W. Rohlf, Nicolas Fernandez

papers.title: Extracting Energy from a Traversable Wormhole via Magnetic Reconnection: Circular Orbits and the Plunging Region
papers.abstract: Using the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism, we study energy extraction from the Teo traversable rotating wormhole at different orbital locations. This wormhole has no event horizon and cannot reduce to a Kerr black hole in any parameter limit. We compute circular orbits on the equatorial plane, the prograde photon sphere, and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). We find that below a certain spin, no circular orbit exists inside the ergosphere. Both the efficiency and power calculated from magnetic reconnection increase monotonically with angular momentum. Compared with a Kerr black hole under the same plasma parameters, the Teo wormhole has higher energy extraction power and efficiency. This is completely different from the Simpson-Visser rotating wormhole, which can reduce to a Kerr black hole, where the large spin makes efficiency and power decrease. We also extend magnetic reconnection to the plunging region. We find that when the spin is not particularly high, the energy extraction power and efficiency in the plunging region are higher than those in the circular orbit region, while for very high spin the situation is reversed. This conclusion also differs from that obtained from a Kerr black hole, where the power and efficiency in the plunging region are always higher than those in the circular orbit region.
papers.authors: Ke Wang, Wei Xu, Xiao-Xiong Zeng

papers.title: Geometric Formulation of Covariant Spin Operator
papers.abstract: In relativistic quantum theory, Lorentz boosts induce momentum-dependent Wigner rotations, complicating the coupling of particle spins in arbitrary frames. We describe particle spin spaces as fibers of an associate bundle over the velocity manifold, and different particle's spins residing at distinct fibers. Analogy to general relativity, we introduce parallel transport to bring spins at different velocities into a common frame, where they can be coupled. Using spinor-helicity variables, we construct the parallel transport operator along geodesics and show how it is uniquely determined by little group covariance. This construction gives explicit form of the covariant spin and orbital operators, and yields a covariant 3-point amplitude basis with definite spin and orbital angular momentum. Higher-point amplitudes can be constructively obtained and applied to the covariant partial wave expansion for amplitudes, form factors, and correlation functions, etc.
papers.authors: Yi-Ning Wang, Jiang-Hao Yu

papers.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
papers.abstract: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.
papers.authors: Damianos Iosifidis

papers.title: Spinning particle dynamics around a non-singular Schwarzschild black hole in conformal gravity
papers.abstract: Spinning test particles provide a precision probe of strong-field gravity, yet their dynamics around singularity-free black holes in conformal gravity remain poorly constrained. We investigate equatorial motion around the non-singular Schwarzschild black hole of conformal gravity, in which the conformal scale \(L\) removes the curvature divergence at the origin while preserving the event horizon at \(r=2M\) and recovering the Schwarzschild geometry as \(L\to 0\). Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations with the Tulczyjew spin supplementary condition, we derive the conserved energy and angular momentum in the conformally rescaled spherical spacetime and construct the radial effective potential for spinning particles. This allows us to determine the physical timelike spin bound, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), the degeneracy between \(L\) and the Kerr rotation parameter, and representative bound trajectories. We show that \(L\) strengthens the effective-potential barrier, decreases the ISCO radius, angular momentum and energy, and lowers the maximum admissible spin before the trajectory becomes spacelike. The orbital integrations reveal a clear division of roles: \(L\) governs the compactness of the bound orbit, whereas the particle spin governs the accumulated relativistic precession. These results establish spinning-particle dynamics as a sensitive diagnostic of conformally regular black-hole spacetimes and provide a possible route to distinguish the conformal Schwarzschild geometry from standard Schwarzschild background.
papers.authors: Shavkat Karshiboev, Bobur Turimov, Sulton Usanov, Ahmadjon Abdujabbarov, Chengxun Yuan, Hasanova Sumanbar, Gulhayo Hayitova

papers.title: Wegner model in high dimension: singular continuous spectrum from U(1) symmetry breaking and AAT self-consistency
papers.abstract: We analyze the energy-spectral decomposition of the Wegner one-orbital model in high lattice dimension using ideas from field theory and statistical mechanics. Most notably, we identify a local spectral measure of singular continuous type for the disordered model at the Anderson transition. The key mechanism that leads to a singular continuous spectrum is a novel scenario of spontaneous symmetry breaking, intimately connected to the non-compactness of the global symmetry group of the field theory. While that symmetry breaks down to a compact subgroup in the metallic phase, it spontaneously breaks down to a nilpotent subgroup at criticality. We describe the symmetry-breaking extremal states approximately, by applying the self-consistent theory of localization due to Abou-Chacra, Anderson, and Thouless. The thrust of our work is to provide a field-theoretical foundation for disorder phenomena associated with singular continuous spectra.
papers.authors: Julian Arenz, Martin R. Zirnbauer

papers.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,\mu\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop within $1\,\mu\text{s}$ while sustaining QPU-rate throughput. By introducing QuFrameISA, we cleanly decouple instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management. Execution is distributed across per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines (IREs) that resolve instructions against the frame via a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit enables independent, lock-free concurrent commits. To strictly guarantee the $1\,\mu\text{s}$ deadline, QuFrame pairs an asynchronous primary decoder with an on-chip fallback decoder that resolves in $144\,\text{ns}$, natively reconciling divergent updates in hardware without degrading logical error rates.
papers.authors: Aleksandra \'Swierkowska, Ilgaz Er, Emmanouil Giortamis, Pramod Bhatotia

papers.title: Stationary Quantum Time Series: Spectral Theory of Process Memory and Measurement Records
papers.abstract: Classical time series analysis converts temporal dependence into structure that can be learned from a single observed trajectory, through stationarity, ergodicity, spectral representation, and finite-memory models. Quantum experiments are naturally time series: every run is a sequence of interventions and outcomes, and the memory of an open system is written in its temporal statistics. However, the classical foundation cannot be translated directly: measuring a process and forgetting the outcome differs from not measuring at all, so no single family of joint probability distributions describes a quantum process. We develop a process-tensor framework for stationary quantum time series and establish its first structural theorems. For stationary combs of finite quantum Markov order l relative to a fixed informationally complete causal break, we construct a finite-dimensional causal transfer map of dimension at most d^{4l}, where d bounds the system Hilbert-space dimension at each step. ... These results supply the stationary foundation on which quantum spectral analysis, model identification, and single-trajectory inference can be built.
papers.authors: Hai Wang

papers.title: Topological signatures of criticality: the Ising case
papers.abstract: Topological properties of microscopic configurations may provide additional insight into phase transitions beyond conventional thermodynamic observables. We investigate this idea in the two-dimensional Ising model on square and triangular lattices by associating cell complexes with the positive and negative spin domains and constructing an Euler-characteristic observable from their difference. We provide the expression relating this quantity to conventional observables of the Ising model. This derivation allows us to understand its expected behavior physically. As a byproduct, we show that at any finite positive temperature the expectation of the Euler characteristic exceeds a positive, lattice-size-independent bound, hence disproving a previously suggested conjecture. Monte Carlo simulations combined with multihistogram reweighting show that this spin-odd topological observable exhibits order-parameter-like behavior near the ferromagnetic transition. Finite-size scaling of its susceptibility yields pseudocritical temperatures that converge to the known critical temperature for both lattice geometries. On the square lattice, the leading-order estimate of the critical exponent obtained from the topological observable depends more strongly on the fitting range than the magnetization estimate. This behavior is consistent with stronger subleading finite-size corrections, as supported by fits including an additional correction term. On the triangular lattice, the corresponding estimate remains consistent with the theoretical Ising value. Our study suggests that topologically defined quantities such as the Euler characteristic can provide an alternative way to locate order-disorder phase transitions in the systems considered here. Since the definition of these observables is purely geometrical, they can provide useful insights in cases in which order parameters cannot be constructed.
papers.authors: Tak-Shing Chan, Pawe{\l} D{\l}otko, Jacek Gulgowski, Biagio Lucini, Mateusz Mas{\l}owski, Davide Vadacchino

papers.title: Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite Qubit System
papers.abstract: Quantum Computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena, such as superposition and entanglement of quantum bits (qubits), to represent and manipulate information in multidimensional state spaces. This approach allows complex mathematical functions to be executed simultaneously rather than sequentially, making them much more efficient than classical computers. However, current quantum computers suffer from quantum decoherence, where small changes to their environment, such as thermal fluctuations and vibrations, affect the systems' fragile states. The goal of this study is to discuss the functionality of a proposed Fe$^{2+}$:forsterite qubit system by solving the unitary time-evolution of a quantum state vector for the system's Hamiltonian, using known axial and traverse anisotropy terms at temperatures up to 10 K. The system can effectively transfer population between its two lowest states at rates predicted by the Rabi half-period, with 99.9% fidelity. Additionally, it can hold the population at a desired state without docohering. The results remained consistent for temperatures up to 10 K, meaning, unlike many common qubit systems, the proposed qubit system could function without a dilution fridge and is not fragile to thermal noise.
papers.authors: Dishaanth S. Pillai, G. M. Wysin

papers.title: Proven optimality for LABS with quantum-classical branch and bound
papers.abstract: Low autocorrelation binary sequences (LABS) are the phase codes of pulse compression radar and the synchronization words of digital communication, and finding the sequence of a given length whose aperiodic autocorrelations have the smallest sum of squares is a hard binary optimization problem. The quantum optimization methods tested on LABS so far return good sequences, but they cannot show that a sequence is optimal or bound how far from optimal it may be. We show that a quantum optimization algorithm can deliver proven optimality. In our quantum-classical branch and bound, fixed-angle QAOA samples the Hamiltonians of the nodes of the search tree, its samples supply candidate sequences and the branching choice, and classical bounds prune the tree, so that the algorithm returns either a proof of optimality or, if it is stopped early, the best sequence found with a certified lower bound and gap. It works on the native quartic Hamiltonian without penalty terms, and its correctness does not depend on the sampler. With QAOA at depth p= 12 and at p= 1 and 1,000 shots per node, it proved the optima of all lengths from 2 to 30, where from length 27 on the root node is split without being sampled. Every run records both bounds against time, and its primal-dual integral measures its convergence. We claim no speedup.
papers.authors: Andr\'as Cz\'egel

papers.title: QCap: a physics-corrected graph neural network for the capacitance matrix of any planar superconducting device layout
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic simulations of device layouts to extract capacitance are computationally intensive, a major obstacle to accurate design of circuit devices. Machine learning models can bypass these simulations, but previous approaches have been restricted to layouts using only particular components, and require thousands of simulations of those same components as training data. We present QCap, a model that accurately predicts the Maxwell capacitance matrix of an arbitrary superconducting device layout in seconds, compared to minutes to hours of Ansys Q3D simulations. We develop a novel design-embedding algorithm that converts the layout into a universal graph format, allowing the model to work with any layout created with any tool. To achieve high accuracy, we obtain a coarse physics prior from a fast method of moments simulation of capacitance, then train the model to correct this prior. On 4,009 test designs withheld from training data the model outputs agree with Q3D simulations to a median error of 0.177%, and on never-seen component families it stays below 1% error. We demonstrate the model's scaling by obtaining the capacitance matrix of a 9-superconducting-qubit device in 12 seconds on a laptop (compared to 19.9 h and 228 GB of memory in Ansys) with sub-percent error, and capacitance of a (too large to simulate) 100-qubit, 781-conductor device in 3.4 min on a laptop. We provide the open-source models and data on SQuADDS and Hugging Face. Our results provide a powerful tool for large-scale accurate circuit design and guide the development of models to bypass other physical simulations.
papers.authors: Sadman Ahmed Shanto, Saikat Das, Eli M. Levenson-Falk

papers.title: Hyperk\"ahler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $\alpha$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $\sigma$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $\pi:\mathscr M\to\Lambda_0$ where $\Lambda_0$ encodes the admissible pairs $(\alpha,\sigma)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in $\Lambda_0$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(\alpha,\sigma)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.
papers.authors: Panagiotis Dimakis, Laura Fredrickson, Arya Yae

papers.title: Separation of gravitational perturbations of Myers--Perry black holes
papers.abstract: Gravitational perturbations of higher-dimensional rotating black holes generally obey coupled partial differential equations, making their separation a longstanding challenge. We separate linearized gravitational perturbations of nonextremal, asymptotically flat five-dimensional Myers--Perry black holes with two nonzero spins of unequal magnitude and arbitrary azimuthal numbers. The Killing--Yano symmetry induces a first-order angular operator that, together with a commuting second-order operator, determines the angular profiles of all five gauge-invariant curvature components. The joint angular harmonics form a complete basis at real frequencies, and all five components of each separated mode share a single radial amplitude satisfying a second-order scalar equation obtained through the Carter interchange. The corresponding metric perturbations can be reconstructed locally. We further extend this angular structure to Myers--Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions with nonzero spins of pairwise distinct magnitudes. Second-order symmetry operators associated with the Killing tensors induce mutually commuting angular operators on all curvature polarizations, with coefficients independent of radius. In odd dimensions, a Killing--Yano three-form generates an additional first-order angular operator commuting with this family. This common angular structure provides a route toward complete separation of gravitational perturbations in higher-dimensional rotating black holes.
papers.authors: Jun-Kun Zhao, Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Efficient $XX$ Placement Strategies for Energy-Gap Enhancement in Quantum Annealing
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing offers the prospect of a computational advantage over classical methods for certain classes of combinatorial optimisation problems. Its performance, however, is fundamentally constrained by the minimum spectral gap between the ground state and the first excited state encountered during the annealing process. When this gap closes exponentially with problem size, the runtime required to maintain adiabatic evolution can likewise grow exponentially, severely limiting the practical efficiency of the annealer. For problems including the maximum weight independent set (MWIS), previous work has shown that introducing $XX$ interactions along problem-graph edges can substantially enlarge the minimum energy-gap and thereby improve annealing performance. In practice, however, current quantum annealing hardware does not support these interactions natively and methods for implementing effective $XX$ couplings come with hardware overhead and connectivity constraints. These limitations motivate the use of only a limited number of $XX$ interactions. In this paper, we investigate $XX$ placement strategies for MWIS instances under both resource and topological constraints, and demonstrate that careful selection of the placements can substantially increase the minimum energy-gap. We evaluate these strategies through a detailed statistical analysis of both deliberately constructed hard MWIS instances and random Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs. Notably, these strategies are particularly effective for hard MWIS instances with initially small minimum gaps, where targeted placement yields the largest relative improvements.
papers.authors: Jennivine Chen, Natasha Feinstein, P A Warburton

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.
papers.authors: Rathindra Nath Karmakar, Samriddha Lahiry, Koichi Yamagata

papers.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
papers.abstract: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS $[[11,1,5]]_3$ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator. Its all-syndrome acceptance is distinct from the known $1/1728$ ideal acceptance of one-round strange-state Golay distillation. An accepted-run target-infidelity budget and a synthetic parameter protocol expose the remaining noise assumptions. Native charge-$4e$ syndrome extraction, material feasibility, a device threshold, and unconditional fault tolerance are not established.
papers.authors: Junhao (Eigen), Wang

papers.title: Buffer-Gas-Assisted Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Molecular Ions
papers.abstract: Sustained fluorescence detection of generic molecules has been challenging due to the lack of cycling transitions and limited photon budgets. We demonstrate a nondestructive method for continuous fluorescence of strongly rovibronically open molecular ions, $^{232}$ThF$^+$. Effective quasi-cycling transitions are established by room-temperature buffer-gas collisions, which replenish the population back to the laser-addressed states. In situ images and rotationally resolved spectra are obtained without optical repumping or auxiliary atomic readout ions. Combined with low-background spectroscopic detection, this approach achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 6 in a 1 s exposure on the P(1) line of $^{232}$ThF$^+$, despite a thermal population of only approximately 0.17% in the addressed state at room temperature. The ability to repeatedly interrogate trapped ions is particularly promising for scarce molecular samples, broadband spectroscopic searches, and in situ monitoring of molecular reactions.
papers.authors: Jinyue Jiang, Kenji Shu, Huaxu Dan, Xing Fan

papers.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).
papers.authors: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

papers.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities
papers.abstract: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.
papers.authors: Alessio Caddeo, Oscar Henriksson, Carlos Hoyos, Mikel Sanchez-Garitaonandia, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez

papers.title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
papers.abstract: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.
papers.authors: Sriram Akella

papers.title: Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism
papers.abstract: Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper examines the premise of that claim: whether Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra. We first survey five coproducts for coassociativity and a connected grading: the Connes-Kreimer coproduct $\Delta_\rho$, MCB's two coproducts $\Delta_d$ and $\Delta_c$, the contraction coproduct of Marcolli and Skigin (2025), and the coproduct of Xiao (2026). $\Delta_d$ is not coassociative. For $\Delta_c$, MCB gives no rule for the labels of trace leaves in trees that already contain trace leaves; under the literal extension it is not coassociative, but once a rule and a grading are supplied it yields a graded connected Hopf algebra. The coproduct of Xiao is coassociative, and so is that of Marcolli and Skigin once its definition is extended to trees with trace leaves. These properties do not tell the coassociative coproducts apart; what distinguishes them is the representation that movement leaves behind. We then review how generative grammar has treated moved elements, and confirm that semantic interpretation requires two things of the representation that results from movement. Retention requires that the structure the lower position had before movement be recoverable; Identifiability requires that, in interpreting the lower position, it be determinable which upper element, if any, corresponds to it. None of the five coproducts meets both conditions: Retention is met only by $\Delta_c$, and there only in the form of a label, and Identifiability by none. In light of the results on coassociativity, we also reassess the Birkhoff factorization that MCB employs at the syntax-semantics interface. Finally, we indicate at least three directions for algebraic Minimalism.
papers.authors: Daisuke Bekki (Ochanomizu University)

papers.title: Holographic warped CFTs on AdS$_3$, parity violation and unitarity
papers.abstract: We consider recently introduced boundary conditions for General Relativity on AdS$_3$, whose canonical generators span the warped conformal algebra, in the case of the Einstein-Hilbert action supplemented by parity-odd terms that do not modify the field equations in vacuum. The canonical generators are shown to acquire nonlinear contributions, and their algebra remains being the semidirect sum of Virasoro and $u(1)$ Kac-Moody, but with shifted central extensions. Thus, for suitable values of the parity-odd coupling, the Kac-Moody level can be nonnegative ($k_\text{KM}\geq 0$), admitting unitary representations. Nevertheless, requiring the black hole entropy to be nonnegative, implies $k_\text{KM}\leq 0$, in agreement with the established understanding of holographic warped CFTs. Compatibility of both requirements (entropy and unitarity) then singles out the case $k_\text{KM}=0$. However, the field equations degenerate in this case, which can be amended by imposing vanishing torsion as a constraint. The theory then precisely becomes Topologically Massive Gravity (TMG) at the chiral point, suggesting the extension of our boundary conditions to accommodate nontrivial logarithmic branches.
papers.authors: Kristiansen Lara, Ricardo Troncoso

papers.title: Towards a recursive construction of string scattering amplitudes
papers.abstract: We construct open superstring scattering amplitudes from three-point data using the Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten (BCFW) recursion and four-dimensional spinor helicity variables. We compute the contributions of selected leading and subleading Regge families to the color-ordered four-gluon amplitude by sewing their cubic couplings and summing over intermediate polarizations. The four-dimensional description makes helicity selection rules explicit and reduces the massive polarization sums to SU(2) little group contractions. The resulting residues are expressed in terms of Jacobi and Legendre polynomials, yielding explicit sums over mass levels. We construct a differential operator relating the two polynomial kernels, including their level-dependent normalizations. These results provide a concrete starting point for organizing the infinite intermediate-state sum and investigating whether relations among Regge families can support a recursive reconstruction of the full string amplitude.
papers.authors: Arkajyoti Manna

papers.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.abstract: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.
papers.authors: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal

papers.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
papers.abstract: We determine the monochromatic three-arm exponent for critical planar percolation through the exact spectral threshold of an explicit positive integral operator family with elementary kernels, obtaining $\xi_3=0.76928375\cdots$. Unlike the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) event, the three-arm event can be obstructed by two distinct white clusters, so a Markovian exploration must retain the past connections. We introduce a two-point boundary observable that records these connections. Using the coupling between conformal loop ensemble (CLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG), this observable satisfies a renewal equation in terms of quantum boundary lengths, and yields the explicit operator whose spectral information determines $\xi_3$. Our approach also gives an explicit spectral characterization of monochromatic $n$-arm exponents for all $n\ge4$.
papers.authors: Gefei Cai

papers.title: Gauge-parameter cancellation and finite form factors in one-loop quark scattering in the refined Gribov-Zwanziger framework
papers.abstract: We calculate the one-loop amplitude for distinct-flavor massless quark scattering in a local BRST-invariant refined Gribov-Zwanziger theory with minimally coupled quarks. The constraint determinant and two dynamical quark flavors are included in the action and loop sum. Retaining the RGZ masses in the free field matrix, we combine the mixed self-energy insertion, complete vertex and box corrections, and external-leg residues. The difference between a general linear covariant gauge and a reference gauge vanishes symbolically after removal of the Stueckelberg regulator in the specified dimensional prescription. We separate ultraviolet and infrared poles, including contributions hidden by scaleless integrals and the order of mass and dimensional limits. Local modified-minimal-subtraction counterterms cancel the ultraviolet poles, and the remaining infrared poles cancel in the stated nonzero-mass domain. The finite result is supplied as eight color-spin form factors over a thirty-entry scalar integral inventory, with all 144 finite-function coefficients provided electronically. Physical-region benchmarks evaluate the scalar functions on a common analytic sheet. Along a specified common-mass scaling path, the four physical color-helicity coefficients approach the QCD finite hard amplitudes numerically at three scattering angles after an explicit infrared conversion. Infrared helicity differences isolate color-dependent mass corrections beyond a universal rescaling of the Born exchange. A low-momentum expansion identifies an effective contact-interaction scale and clarifies the suppression relative to massless exchange. The result defines a partonic amplitude on a specified analytic branch; it does not establish a unitary colored-state S matrix or an inclusive next-to-leading-order cross section.
papers.authors: Wan Wu

papers.title: Beyond Robustness of Magic: Quantifying Quantum State Convertibility
papers.abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, magic states provide essential resources for implementing non-Clifford operations. The robustness of magic (RoM) quantifies the magic contained in a quantum state and is closely related to the cost of classical simulation. However, knowing how much magic two states contain is not sufficient to determine whether one can be converted into the other using free operations. In this work, we develop a geometric framework in which RoM is represented as half the distance to the set of free states, and extend this framework to state conversion. We introduce a directed conversion deficiency that measures how far a target state lies from the states freely reachable from a given input. This quantity vanishes exactly when free conversion is possible and, beyond being a mathematically well-defined measure, has an operational interpretation in terms of stabilizer quasiprobability. Furthermore, our framework provides lower bounds on the additional magic states required for conversion that can be strictly stronger than conventional RoM-based bounds. We demonstrate this distinction analytically by constructing a continuous family of mixed single-qubit states with identical RoM for which free conversion is possible in one direction but impossible in the reverse. Our results reveal that the usefulness of magic for quantum state conversion depends not only on its amount but also on the specific transformation being performed.
papers.authors: Satoshi Kanno, Yoshi-aki Shimada

papers.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days
papers.abstract: We present an end-to-end resource estimation of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, from its mathematical description to the allocation and scheduling of physical qubits on a chip layout. We review modern versions of Shor's algorithm for RSA, ECDLP and FFDLP, and make their logical circuits and trade-offs explicit. We compile the dominant subroutines down to physical-qubit operations on two architectures: one based on repetition cat codes and one on LDPC cat codes. We design a parity-Cnot gate for cat qubits, extend a multi-target Cnot gate to the LDPC-cat architecture, and adapt an active injection procedure to cat qubits. Building on these primitives, we adapt to cat qubits the adder from Gidney's 2025 resource estimate for factoring RSA-2048. We combine our adder compilation and a coarser estimate for the phaseup with the factory designs and lookup compilation from the FeMoco resource estimation of Kroell et al. Together, these lead to chip layouts and schedules for factoring RSA-2048. Assuming a 1$\mu$s error-correction cycle time, a 10$\mu$s reaction time, circuit-level phase-flip noise with probability $p_Z = 5 \times 10^{-4}$ and no bit-flips, factoring RSA-2048, the configuration we compile in full, requires about 23 000 cat qubits and 3.14 days. Reusing the compiled operations, solving ECDLP on secp256k1 requires at most 30 000 cat qubits and 1 hour, and FFDLP-512, which we propose as an intermediate benchmark, about 6 700 cat qubits and 21 minutes. Trading space for time, RSA-2048 runs in 1.25 hours on about 611 000 cat qubits. The no-bit-flip requirement (a bit-flip time of about 100 years) can be relaxed to a bit-flip time of about one hour by adding a concatenation layer with a distance-3 bit-flip code, in which case RSA-2048 needs about 45 000 cat qubits.
papers.authors: Axel Pappalardo, Dahmun Goudarzi, Victor Hertz, Hugo Jacinto, Larissa Kroell, Andr\'e Schrottenloher, Peter Shanahan, \'Elie Gouzien, R\'emi de la Vieuville, Vivien Londe

papers.title: Electron-photon entanglement in real space from quantum electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the entanglement between an electron and the photon it scatters, resolved in real space and time. Starting from nonrelativistic QED in Fermi's oscillator representation, we write Fock's coupled equations for components with fixed photon number in the photon configuration space, in the length gauge, where the photon is created around the atom through a nonlocal kernel. Truncated at one photon, the equations are solved numerically without the rotating-wave approximation for a one-dimensional model atom in a waveguide with a single transverse mode and enhanced coupling. The atom is driven by a short, off-resonant laser pulse, with the electron and photon represented on real-space grids. The global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient. It peaks during the pulse and decreases as the polarized electron cloud returns to the core, leaving a state close to a product of the electron state and a superposition of the field vacuum with a single scattered photon. Local entanglement, obtained from walkers sampled across both photon-number components, exhibits opposite spatial patterns for the two particles. The electron entropy is smallest at the nucleus and maps the local strength of the dipole coupling, whereas the photon entropy is largest near the atom, where photons are created and absorbed, and smaller in the outgoing wave packets.
papers.authors: Ivan P. Christov

papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.
papers.authors: Priyanka Grover, Hemant K. Mishra, Sarishti Singh, Temjensangba

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $X_f=\{f=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model. We define the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\C^n/\Z_n$ as a modification of the torsion-type invariant introduced by Fan and Fang, and prove that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension. The proof depends on a holomorphic anomaly formula for families of LG models and a uniform estimate for the torsion near a one-node degeneration of $X_f$.
papers.authors: Xinxing Tang, Junrong Yan

papers.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
papers.abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.
papers.authors: Kamran Behnia

papers.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string integrals from the intersection matrix
papers.abstract: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.
papers.authors: Yi-Xiao Tao, Shijie Zhang

papers.title: The Pre-Optimization Structure of QAOA: Polynomial Equivalence of Average and Optimal Probabilities
papers.abstract: We develop a theoretical framework connecting problem structure and variational parameter optimization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). We derive a general bound on how much variational optimization can improve the probability of measuring configurations in arbitrary subsets of computational basis states, relating the maximum probability to its average over variational parameters. For NPO-PB problems at constant depth and with polynomially many distinct mixer eigenvalues, optimization improves the average probability by at most a polynomial factor. This raises the question: to what extent is variational optimization necessary for sampling desirable solutions? Under suitable efficiency assumptions, randomly parameterized QAOA can achieve cumulative success probabilities comparable to variationally trained QAOA, with only polynomial overhead in circuit executions. In particular, under these conditions, efficient sampling of desirable solutions can be achieved without variational training whenever variationally optimized QAOA achieves inverse-polynomial success probability. Beyond its algorithmic implications, the mean--max bound reveals that, under polynomial mean--max proximity, a pre-optimization structural layer determines the asymptotic scaling of optimal measurement probabilities up to polynomial factors. For single-layer QAOA initialized in a uniform superposition, we explicitly characterize this layer for the measurement probability of a reference state using an exact expression for the average probability that captures the interplay between problem structure and mixer dynamics through the overlap of a problem structure matrix and a mixer-dependent matrix. We derive a mixer-dependent capacity bound and identify cancellations between constructive and destructive contributions as a mechanism for additional superpolynomial suppression relative to this capacity.
papers.authors: Guilherme Adamatti Bridi, Franklin de Lima Marquezino, Andris Ambainis

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for all sufficiently large $d$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.
papers.authors: Yucheng Liu, Leonardo T. Rolla, Yuliang Shi

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.
papers.authors: Ben Gripaios

papers.title: A Cauchy Busemann function approach to the geometry of cosmological spacetimes with applications to Bartnik's conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of future timelike complete spacetimes admitting a compact Cauchy hypersurface. Future timelike completeness is compatible with an initial singularity and disregards the incompleteness expected inside black holes, so it is a reasonable large scale idealization for a Universe without final singularity. Given a compact Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$, we introduce the future Cauchy Busemann function $b^+$. Its finiteness domain, the future cosmological development, and its boundary, the future cosmological horizon, do not depend on $\Sigma$. For spacetimes with an initial singularity, namely with regular cosmological time, we obtain a canonical Cauchy Busemann function and a canonical calibrating semi-flow. Using a product trick we show that $b^+$ is the graph function of a Cauchy horizon in $M\times \mathbb{R}$: $b^+$ is locally Lipschitz and locally semi-concave on the future development, the future horizon is a $C^0$ null hypersurface, and through every point of the development passes a calibrated timelike ray, an observer who ages maximally into the far future. We give a foliation-free formula for $b^+$ as a minimal asymptotic clock defect. Under the timelike convergence condition (TCC) the level sets of $b^+$ are mean convex in the support sense. We apply these results to Bartnik's splitting conjecture for timelike complete spacetimes satisfying the TCC. If the future and past cosmological developments intersect, which happens whenever $b^+$ is $C^1$ on its finiteness domain, then the spacetime contains a timelike line and hence splits. Therefore any counterexample contains a non-empty closed causally convex set, the cosmological wall, separating the two developments; some component of the future horizon contains a lightlike line, and if the wall has empty interior it coincides with both horizons and is ruled by lightlike lines.
papers.authors: E. Minguzzi

papers.title: QuasiStim: Scalable Accurate Non-Pauli Noise Simulation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computer design relies on simulating noisy quantum error correction (QEC) circuits with hundreds to thousands of physical qubits and large circuit depths. High-throughput stabilizer simulators, such as Stim, are the de facto tools for this regime. However, these simulators typically support only Clifford gates and stochastic Pauli noise. As a result, more realistic device noise models, such as coherent control errors and thermal relaxation, are often approximated using Pauli twirling. This replacement offers speed but can introduce substantial inaccuracies. To address this, we propose QuasiStim for scalable, accurate QEC simulation of realistic noise, with QuasiFold as a compiler frontend and DeltaFrame as a sampling backend. QuasiFold lowers sampling overhead by opportunistically merging non-Pauli noise sites in the quantum circuit without changing the circuit output. DeltaFrame samples the resulting stabilizer trajectories by reusing precomputed predicted references instead of resimulating the full tableau for each shot. In our evaluation, QuasiFold can reduce the number of shots by over $1000\times$ on bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes under coherent $R_{ZZ}$ noise. Compared to a per-shot tableau simulator, DeltaFrame is $190\times$ to $1479\times$ faster on rotated surface-code memory as $d$ grows from 5 to 35. QuasiStim also makes the PTA bias measurable: the gap is non-trivial and varies with noise strength, decoder, and circuit schedule.
papers.authors: Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: Percolation of Data Constraints and Reorganization of Boolean Function States in Parity Learning
papers.abstract: We study how a neural network reorganizes its learned function as training proceeds and as previously unseen parity data accumulate. The trained model is itself a Boolean function on binary strings of finite length. We then evaluate it on all data, inside and outside the training set, and read off its complete sign table. Its $\pm1$ entries are the amplitudes of a normalized state, dubbed the function-state, whose inverse subsystem purity $K_f=1/\textrm{Tr}(\rho_A^2)$ is an effective Schmidt rank. We find that small data additions broaden the Schmidt spectrum, whereas larger additions reconcentrate it in the target mode. The former is called differentiation because the model distinguishes inputs more sharply. The latter is called target-selective recoherence, where the model settles on the single rule shared by the added data. As the dataset grows, the connectivity of the constraint graph defined by the training set increases monotonically, whereas the learned inverse purity changes nonmonotonically. On a fixed connected dataset, as learning proceeds, the Schmidt spectrum begins to reorganize, followed by gains in target alignment and later by improvement in predictive accuracy. This ordering distinguishes three aspects of learning: constraint identifiability, function-state organization, and predictive accuracy. At fixed data size, a function that has already been learned can re-differentiate, an event we call retreat, without changing graph connectivity. Recovery reconcentrates the Schmidt spectrum in a similar target-selective pattern, without exact recurrence of the Boolean state. Thus the percolation of data constraints fixes the identifiable support, while the reduced state produced by training continues to reorganize even after that support stops changing.
papers.authors: Han Ma

papers.title: Collective Shortcuts for Preparing Identical Qubits
papers.abstract: Allowing two qubits to interact during preparation can reduce the total cost relative to preparing them independently. We characterize this advantage for two copies of any pure qubit state, starting with each qubit in $|0\rangle$ and measuring the cost by the sum of the absolute Pauli rotation angles. Independent preparation is optimal precisely for targets on the four meridian arcs joining the north pole of the Bloch sphere to the eigenstates of $X$ or $Y$. Every other pure qubit state admits a collective shortcut. For example, the equatorial states $|+\rangle$ and $|T\rangle$ differ only in their relative phase, by $\pi/4$. The cost is additive for $|+\rangle$, whereas a four-pulse preparation of two $T$ states costs $13.4\%$ less than the optimal independent preparation. Collective control can also reduce the cost while keeping the qubits unentangled throughout a continuous preparation.
papers.authors: Lin Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang, Shenggen Zheng

papers.title: Multiscale Renormalization of Weighted Networks
papers.abstract: Recent progress in network renormalization has identified various ways to transform network representations consistently across resolution levels. In particular, the renormalization flow describing how random graph models transform under node aggregation has identified a fixed point corresponding to an aggregation-invariant model that preserves the form of the connection probability across arbitrary scales. While this probabilistic multiscale approach has successfully been used to model real-world networks, construct latent-space node embeddings, and reconstruct finer-grained versions of aggregate network data in a principled resolution-invariant way, it has so far been restricted to binary graphs. Here we reformulate multiscale network renormalization for weighted random graphs. Via a generating-function approach, we identify a weighted multiscale model whose full probability law, encoding both link creation and weight assignment, has an invariant compound-Poisson form under arbitrary node aggregation. The renormalization rules that transform parameters across aggregation levels allow the ensemble to be calibrated at one level and applied at another, enabling consistent modeling and reconstruction of weighted networks across arbitrary scales.
papers.authors: Mattia Marzi, Frank P. Pijpers, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Bouncing-ball modes in ergodic billiards
papers.abstract: We show that for a horizontally stretched Bunimovich billiard, for almost every stretching parameter, there exists a sequence of eigenfunctions concentrating in the rectangular part. Thanks to the work of Markarian--Oliffson Kamphorst--Pinto de Carvalho, we know that for an open set of parameters such billiards are ergodic. The proof is a result of interaction with ChatGPT 6: we were curious if it could establish the existence of bouncing ball modes for Bunimovich or Sinai billiards. That was not successful until we suggested varying the wings. That produced an essentially complete argument for the existence of quasimodes. We then suggested using Hassell's parameter-variation argument which led to the result about eigenfunctions. The argument was then significantly simplified and clarified by the authors.
papers.authors: Zhenhao Li, Maciej Zworski

papers.title: Magnetostatics as a Stress Theory in $\mathbb R^3$: Free and Bound Currents, Gauge Invariance, and Mechanical Interactions
papers.authors: Vladimir Gol'dshtein, Wolfgang H. M\"uller, Reuven Segev

papers.title: Divergences in Nonpolynomial Quantum Field Theories
papers.abstract: The structure of divergences in several nonpolynomial scalar quantum field theories are investigated. Various $n$-point Green functions for nonpolynomial theories are calculated and their renormalization is analyzed, with special regard for the nonpolynomial $\left|\phi\right|^{3}$ theory in $4$ spacetime dimensions.
papers.authors: Galib Hoq, Thomas Curtright

papers.title: Four-Point String Monodromy from Six-Point Supersymmetric Consistency
papers.abstract: Can finite-particle consistency determine an infinite string amplitude? For four-dimensional planar tree-level $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills effective theories with a specified scalar parity condition, we derive all-order constraints directly from physical six-point Ward identities and local factorization. An overlapping-channel limit forces a scalar cocycle, while an explicit differential Ward functional eliminates all relevant five- and six-point contact freedom and fixes the four-point kernel by $q''=-6c_{00}q$. Its normalized branches are linear, trigonometric, and hyperbolic, and the target amplitude obeys the associated four-point monodromy. If its entire pole-subtracted axis sequence additionally admits one common nonzero positive moment measure, the trigonometric branch is selected and the complete Veneziano low-energy germ is unique up to scale. The result separates a formal low-energy necessity theorem from its conditional analytic-germ uniqueness corollary; no worldsheet or auxiliary KLT-module membership is assumed for the physical theorem.
papers.authors: Jianqi Sheng

papers.title: Improved Separations between Quantum and Classical Communication Complexity of Total Functions
papers.abstract: We refine Gavinsky's framework (arXiv:2608.18784) for exponential separations between quantum and randomized communication complexity of total functions and obtain larger separations: polylogarithmic quantum communication versus $\tilde\Omega(\sqrt n)$ randomized communication with two quantum messages, and versus $\Omega(n^{1-\varepsilon})$ for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$ with more quantum messages. Our main technical contribution is a general conversion from quantum versus randomized communication separations for partial functions to separations for total functions. Our construction combines the communication lookup construction of Anshu, Belovs, Ben-David, G\"o\"os, Jain, Kothari, Lee, and Santha (FOCS 2016), the fully linear PCPs of Boneh, Boyle, Corrigan-Gibbs, Gilboa, and Ishai (CRYPTO 2019), and a linear seeded extractor with a short seed based on the construction of Raz, Reingold, and Vadhan (JCSS 2002). The key idea is to use the extractor to compress the lookup table into a single cell, thereby reducing the input length.
papers.authors: Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall

papers.title: Phonon Scharnhorst effect: Acoustic analogue of the vacuum-fluctuation-boosted speed of light
papers.abstract: The Scharnhorst effect in quantum electrodynamics predicts a superluminal velocity shift $\delta c>0$ at low photon frequencies due to vacuum fluctuations between two mirrors. Although theoretically robust (no causality violation), the effect is extraordinarily small ($\delta c/c\approx 10^{-32}$ for mirrors $1\,\mu{\rm m}$ apart) and outside current experimental reach. Here we propose a condensed matter analogue, replacing the photons in the electromagnetic vacuum by phonon excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate. In an idealized geometry, the two-dimensional surface of a cylinder (circumference $L$) at zero temperature, the axial speed of sound is increased due to zero-point fluctuations of the condensate by $\delta c/c\simeq 5\times 10^{-3}\,\tilde{g}$ at $L\simeq 2\,\xi$, to first order in the dimensionless interaction constant $\tilde{g}\simeq 10^{-1}$ of the Bose gas of healing length $\xi\simeq 1\,\mu{\rm m}$. This is 28 orders of magnitude larger than the photonic effect at a comparable confinement length, basically because phonons have a self-interaction while photons only interact via massive electrons. When $L$ drops below $1.19\,\xi$ the velocity shift changes sign, signaling the crossover to a one-dimensional Bose gas. We discuss the prospects for observation of the acoustic Scharnhorst effect. The main obstacles are the nK temperature requirement and the need to separate the vacuum-fluctuation shift from a mean-field geometric correction.
papers.authors: C. W. J. Beenakker

papers.title: Solving wave propagation problems via geometric quantum state preparation on dispersion manifolds
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for solving partial differential equations through a linear-system formulation, focusing on wave propagation problems described by the discretized Helmholtz equation in frequency domain. Although quantum linear-system solvers offer exponential compression of the system degrees of freedom, their runtime complexity is generally governed by the condition number of the discretized operator. Exploiting the analytic structure of the differential operator can provide an alternative to explicit matrix inversion, as illustrated for the screened Poisson equation through an explicit quantum circuit. For the Helmholtz equation, however, the inverse operator becomes singular on the dispersion surface $k^2=\omega^2/c^2$, rendering direct Fourier-space state-preparation methods exponentially inefficient. We address this challenge by directly preparing quantum states supported on the resonant manifold and encoding source locations through Fourier phases. The resulting algorithm eliminates the exponentially large overhead associated with post-selection on the resonant manifold, yielding a success probability that depends linearly on the number of sources and is independent of the computational domain size. More generally, our approach applies to hyperbolic differential equations whose Fourier-space solutions possess singular support on dispersion manifolds, recasting their solution as a problem of geometric quantum state preparation.
papers.authors: Yakov Solomons, Lee Peleg, Netanel Barel, Jonathan Nemirovsky, Amit Ben-Kish, Yotam Shapira

papers.title: Forward gain tracks the mean-response share of the Fisher information in non-Hermitian bosonic ladders
papers.abstract:
Non-Hermitian lattices are proposed as sensors because non-normal amplification turns a small frequency shift into a large output, yet whether this increases precision at fixed photon number remains contested. We evaluate the classical Gaussian-state Fisher information of the intracavity field, split into mean-response and covariance-response terms, for a single bosonic chain and a two-chain opposing-skin ladder across 
um{34560} points under a Hurwitz stability margin. Over the 
um{15432} configurations passing both the margin and an independent covariance check, the mean-response share of the clean-cavity benchmark tracks forward gain along one curve in both architectures ($R^2=
um{0.978}$; architecture increment $\Delta R^2=
um{0.0012}$), falling from 
um{0.97} below zero gain to below 
um{2e-3} above \qty{60}{\dB}. Inter-chain coupling shifts the accessible gain range without raising the share at matched gain. Amplification thus relocates information into an ill-conditioned noise covariance, making the mean--covariance split and covariance conditioning the decisive metrics.
papers.authors: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

papers.title: Higher-Spin dS/CFT beyond minimal type-A, and the doubled nature of de Sitter space
papers.abstract: We study the holographic duality between free vector models and Higher-Spin Gravity in 4-dimensional de Sitter space. On both the bulk and boundary sides, we introduce new reality conditions, which allow us to include odd spins in the bulk, and to extend the duality from type-A to type-B (i.e. from boundary scalars to spinors). The new reality conditions are closely related to a higher-spin-symmetric Hilbert-space norm for the single-particle (super)multiplet in de Sitter space. We construct two alternative viewpoints on the type-A and type-B theories. In one view, the two co-exist in "parallel universes", specifically in even vs. odd antipodal identifications of de Sitter space. In the other view, type-A and type-B are Legendre-transformed descriptions of the same twistor-space theory in Euclidean AdS (this involves the observation that the higher-spin partition function is Legendre-dual to itself). In this way, higher-spin holography reconciles the two-boundary nature of de Sitter space with the one-boundary nature of Euclidean AdS. The supersymmetric theory that unifies type-A and type-B with bulk fermions fails to be consistent under the appropriate reality conditions.
papers.authors: Julian Lang, Yasha Neiman

papers.title: Euler Topological Metals in 1D
papers.abstract: We give a rigorous one-dimensional formulation of Kane's transport proposal for probing the Euler characteristic of a Fermi sea. For a clean, translation-invariant continuum Hamiltonian with real-analytic dispersion, a Fermi sea confined to a finite momentum range, and nonzero Fermi velocity at every Fermi point, we analyze a particular regularized transport response (obtained by tracing over the Fermi sea) and prove that its large-time limit equals the Euler characteristic. We derive an explicit finite-time formula, show that quantization requires the large-time limit, and obtain a convergence rate under additional nonstationarity assumptions. We also prove the lattice analog, where the commutator of the spatial switch with its time evolution is trace-class and a completely filled band contributes zero. Finite-volume calculations illustrate the prescribed order of the thermodynamic and large-time limits.
papers.authors: Yichen Hu, Jacob Shapiro

papers.title: Black holes from a Higgs-like field in the radiation era
papers.abstract: Light spectator fields during inflation can acquire superhorizon fluctuations that cross a potential barrier between positive and negative regions of their potential. Motivated by the Standard Model Higgs instability, in this work we study the subsequent evolution of patches where this occurs in the radiation era after inflation ends for a Higgs-like spectator field. We utilise fully nonlinear, spherically symmetric numerical relativity. Across the black hole forming configurations in our investigation we find a robust two-stage evolution. First, the central negative potential region reverses its expansion, becomes kinetic dominated, and forms a primordial black hole that hides the runaway core. The positive potential barrier that survives outside this first horizon then determines one of two late-time branches. In the subcritical branch the original apparent horizon grows smoothly and engulfs the remaining scalar structure. In the supercritical branch, however, the potential energy of the barrier dominates the local evolution. The result is a transient wormhole throat, a bifurcating trapping horizon, and an inflating child universe branch. In both branches the parent radiation dominated universe is ultimately left with an ordinary primordial black hole whose subsequent growth is governed by radiation accretion.
papers.authors: Ethan Milligan, Luis E. Padilla, David J. Mulryne

papers.title: Kerr-Newman and genuine Kerr black holes in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field
papers.abstract: We present a spacetime that describes a rotating and charged black hole immersed in an external magnetic (or electric) field which is oriented along the rotational axis. This solution is characterized by four physical parameters, namely the black hole mass $m$, its charge $e$, Kerr-like rotation $a$, and the value of the external field $B$. Such exact solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations has a surprisingly simple form. Moreover, for $B=0$ it reduces to standard Kerr-Newman metric, while for $m=0$ and $e=0$ we recover the Bertotti-Robinson universe with a uniform (electro-)magnetic field. We also show that the Kerr-BR solution presented in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 181401 (2025)] has a special charge, and we identify a genuine uncharged Kerr black hole immersed in the magnetic field. In the weak-field limit, it gives the Wald solution. We analyze the main physical properties of the new family, namely singularities, horizons, regularity of axes, charges, entropy, and temperature.
papers.authors: Hryhorii Ovcharenko, Jiri Podolsky

papers.title: Physics-guided machine learning for sim-to-real calibration of NV diamond magnetometers
papers.abstract: Ensemble nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond enable robust magnetometry in unshielded environments, yet deployment remains bottlenecked by complex calibration and a reliance on external references. Conventional statistical machine learning requires massive training datasets and suffers from severe simulation-to-reality mismatches. To address this, we introduce a physics-guided hybrid machine learning framework that embeds Zeeman splitting directly into the learning pipeline. In an ablation study, our model demonstrates a nearly 3-fold improvement in precision and a 372-fold reduction in mean prediction bias over a purely statistical baseline. Furthermore, anchoring scalable synthetic data generation with just 49 sparse experimental seeds circumvents physical data scarcity while incorporating real-world non-idealities. Evaluated across a hybrid dataset of over 19,000 spectra spanning a 400 G dynamic range, the framework bridges the simulation-to-reality gap and achieves robust scalar field prediction, transferring effectively to raw, uncalibrated experimental data. Operating with minimal computational overhead on standard commercial hardware, the model achieves sub-4 ms inference times per spectrum, demonstrating strong viability for real-time edge deployment.
papers.authors: Jonathan Daniel, Sangwoo Lee, Jesse Hernandez, Emanuel Suarez, Jinhee Lee, Je-Hyung Kim, Martin Y. Kim

papers.title: Multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: Angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
papers.abstract: The angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated M1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses and mass ratios. The main analysis is restricted to merger remnants that do not collapse to a black hole within the simulated time intervals. The angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. Following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. The dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. The degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. Superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. The associated half frequency, $f_{\mathrm{dom}}/2\simeq0.6$--$0.7\,\mathrm{kHz}$, is compared with local rotation rates in the simulated remnant--disk systems, suggesting a possible dynamical association between the remnant structure and neutrino variability. Finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. The polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron rich and below equilibrium.
