By measuring two input-output relations only having different moments of inertia, we can rigorously recover the relaxation function. Thus, we note a clear link between the characteristic roots and the poles. Numerical experiments reconstruct the relaxation function from synthetic angular displacements corresponding to two given moments of inertia based on our inversion method. The results show the effect of measurement noise on the recovered characteristic roots and relaxation function.
papers.authors: Yu Jiang, Takayuki Kurokawa, Ching-Lung Lin, Gen Nakamura

papers.title: Development of a Discrete Variable Representation of a Field-Adaptive Hermite Basis for Accurate Modeling of Magnetically Confined Systems
papers.abstract: Accurate magnetic-field evolution of spectra requires a common wavefunction representation that consistently describes multiple states across different field regimes. Discrete Variable Representation (DVR) methods combine accurate basis-based kinetic-energy evaluation with flexible real-space potential representation, enabling arbitrary non-analytic potentials to be treated. Here, we develop a magnetic-field-dependent Hermite function-based (Hermite-B) DVR that adapts naturally to magnetic confinement, efficiently representing compressed wavefunctions across a wide range of field strengths while remaining centered in regions relevant to the scalar confinement potential. This ensures accurate treatment of the field-dependent kinetic energy while addressing two key challenges: maintaining accuracy from the Zeeman to Landau regimes and accommodating diverse confinement potentials. We also introduce a spatial restriction scheme that confines Hermite DVR grid points to a fixed-length domain, enabling compact representations for smooth potentials. The method is benchmarked for two-dimensional quantum dots in perpendicular magnetic fields against analytical models and compared with finite-grid, sine DVR, and field-free Hermite DVR calculations. The performance of field-independent DVR methods for magnetically confined systems is also investigated for the first time. Excellent agreement with exact analytical spectra and wavefunctions is obtained, with Hermite-B requiring the fewest basis functions and smaller Hamiltonian matrices, improving computational efficiency. Applications to arbitrary confinement potentials and tilted magnetic fields demonstrate its versatility beyond analytically solvable systems. The proposed method offers a robust, accurate, and efficient framework for large-scale calculations of realistic semiconductor nanostructures and molecular systems in external magnetic fields.
papers.authors: Athul Tom, Pratyush Bhattacharjya, Sangita Sen

papers.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
papers.abstract: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times. Circuit-level noise models contain many error mechanisms but few firings per shot at low physical error rates, making exhaustive per-shot scanning inefficient. We present CHEQ, an FPGA platform integrating on-chip sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to sample firing locations from detector error models and amortize mechanism traversal across shots within each batch. Under independent random draws and exact geometric sampling, the shot distribution is invariant to batch size, enabling a memory-throughput tradeoff. A throughput model guides joint selection of the Sampling Unit count, batch size, and decoder count under FPGA resource constraints. Across evaluated conditions, the pooled one-sided 95% upper bound on the weighted root-mean-square relative firing-rate difference from Stim is 0.16%. At a batch size of 4,096, a Sampling Unit uses only 4.8%-11.2% of a Helios decoder's LUTs for code distances 7, 9, 11, and 13. On an AMD VCU118 FPGA at code distance 7 and physical error rate 10^-3, two Sampling Units supply 20 Helios decoders at 49.2 million shots/s, completing 10^10 shots in 3.4 minutes without host-side shot generation.
papers.authors: Sechan Park, Kyeongwon Lee, Mundo Jung, Chaebin Jung, Woojoo Lee

papers.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers.abstract: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. Stabilizer-assisted elimination further removes rotations certified to be invisible to all future measurements. A circuit-dependent schedule is computed once and shared across shots, while adaptive caching of conditional Born probabilities and batched execution reduce repeated sampling work while preserving the measurement-record distribution. Across 19 QEC benchmarks, MASQ reduces peak active width by up to 40 active virtual qubits and achieves up to 8,098-fold CPU throughput speedup over Clifft on multi-round circuits.
papers.authors: Chaebin Jung, Sangmin Jeon, Kyeongwon Lee, Sechan Park, Woojoo Lee

papers.title: Generalized Schrieffer-Wolff transformation
papers.abstract: The Schrieffer-Wolff transformation (SWT) is a cornerstone of effective-Hamiltonian theory. However, the SWT is predominantly used for weak-coupling problems, while a systematic counterpart for strongly coupled regimes remains largely unexplored. A general closed-form SWT generator and a clear physical principle for gauge fixing remain elusive, obscuring the transformation's underlying structure. We introduce the dual SWT to deal with the strong-coupling problems. The generalized SWT (gSWT) is formulated for any Hermitian operator and block partition. We establish the geodesic principle for its canonical gauge. Furthermore, we derive an exact closed-form solution of the gSWT generator at every order as a finite nested-commutator sum whose only input is the active gap set. Both the geometric and algebraic aspects of the SWT physics are revealed. The gSWT framework is illustrated in two quantum many-body models, the collective spin model and the transverse-field Ising model.
papers.authors: Tie-Cheng Guo

papers.title: Distrustful entanglement-based Quantum Key Distribution
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is the one of the most explored application of quantum information theory. While practical QKD systems are being deployed around the world, a major issue of these setups are that one has to trust the measurement devices of both parties. On the other hand, the most secure among such schemes are called device-independent (DI) QKD protocols, where no component of the setup is assumed to be trusted. However, due to their high technological demand, their loophole-free version currently remain out of practical reach. Inspired by the real world, we consider the traditional QKD in a distrustful measurement setting, that is, the measurement devices can only be trusted upto some level of confidence, which might still be large but not completely trusted. We then derive a general lower bound on the asymptotic key rate in this scenario. Then considering perfect detectors and source, and the entanglement-based BB84 (BBM) protocol, we show that to obtain secure keys one needs to trust their devices more than 92 %. However, we observe that such a protocol can not be realised with any level of distrust using the realistic detectors and sources at the current technology. Finally, we also consider the BBM protocol with arbitrary dimensional systems and observe that they are more robust to distrust than qubit systems. Consequently, with the same level of distrust, along with same detector and source efficiences, one can get better key rates with high-dimensional systems.
papers.authors: Shubhayan Sarkar

papers.title: Dynamical theory of the East model. I. A review on the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism
papers.abstract: The East model is a paradigmatic kinetically constrained spin model in one dimension that exhibits glassy dynamics. This review surveys the progress on the theoretical description of the dynamics of the East model, focusing on the spin time correlation function and the relaxation time. We summarize rigorous results on the super-Arrhenius scaling of the relaxation time in the low-temperature limit. We then present a unified derivation of the Zwanzig-Mori projection-operator formalism for both the fluctuation and domain bases. Within this formalism, an infinite hierarchy of coupled equations for the time correlation function and memory kernels emerges---a structure reminiscent of generalized mode-coupling theory developed for supercooled liquids. We review the analytical approximations obtained by truncating or closing the hierarchy at first or second orders and compare them against Monte Carlo simulations. Although these approaches perform reasonably at moderate temperatures, they universally fail in the low-temperature regime: mode-coupling closure schemes in the fluctuation basis introduce spurious ergodicity-breaking transitions, while truncations in the domain basis discard slower modes and fail to capture the asymptotic divergence of the relaxation time. The loss of analytical tractability beyond second order remains the central obstacle, underscoring the fundamental difficulty of describing hierarchical relaxation even in this ``simplest'' model of glassy dynamics.
papers.authors: Chong Zha, Yuliang Jin

papers.title: Live Noise Fingerprints for Quantum Program Analysis
papers.abstract: Quantum programs are probabilistic in nature, and noisy execution due to current imperfect hardware further complicates their analysis. In this paper, we study abstract semantics for analysing quantum programs under these conditions. We introduce noise fingerprints, compact descriptions of the observable effects of noise relative to a finite interface of input states and output measurements. We use them to define our abstract domain with respect to the concrete noise-related behaviour. We relate the concrete and abstract domains through a probabilistic Galois connection, extending the Galois-connection framework to distribution-valued interpretations. We study the resulting abstraction in terms of observational soundness, conciseness, efficiency, and ability to adapt to changing noise. We show that polynomial-size interfaces yield exponentially smaller fingerprints than full noise models while preserving the chosen observations, and that fingerprint distance characterises the largest observational discrepancy over the chosen interface. Further, we develop ChanShadow, which reuses noise fingerprints of commonly used short program fragments to analyse noisy execution of whole programs and provides a uniform finite-sample error bound. We construct working examples showing how fingerprints support program analysis. We evaluate fingerprint precision, representation cost, measurement requirements, and behaviour under noise drift. On a synthetic benchmark, fingerprints retain $(99 \pm 1)\%$ of the noise strength information of a full noise model. On simulated noise drift, reusing earlier measurements reduces the number of fresh measurement rounds needed to reach an error tolerance of $0.10$ by a factor of $2.3$ at $95\%$ confidence and by a factor of $27$ under the median-error criterion.
papers.authors: Avner Bensoussan, Karine Even-Mendoza, Debalina Banerjee, Elena Chachkarova, Sophie Fortz, Vasileios Klimis, Mohammad Reza Mousavi

papers.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
papers.abstract: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.
papers.authors: Avani Vivrekar, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen

papers.title: Probing the QCD Conformal Window with Four-Quark Operators
papers.abstract: The infrared fate of QCD-like theories and their conformal window for different numbers or flavours and colour remains an open question with applications ranging from high-energy to condensed-matter systems. A hallmark of phase transitions from a conformal to symmetry breaking phase can be the presence of classically irrelevant operators that provide relevant deformation in the infrared. We investigate this scenario by computing anomalous dimensions of all four-quark operators, with or without chiral symmetry, at four-loop order as well as the dimension-six gluonic operator at three loops in Veneziano QCD. Scaling dimensions are derived in a systematic conformal expansion. These results are improved with various resummation techniques and we estimate their uncertainties. We find no concrete evidence for a composite operator effectively describing a merger with the QCD fixed point.
papers.authors: Junchen Rong, Emmanuel Stamou, Tom Steudtner

papers.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
papers.abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb Z_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern--Simons--Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf8_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf8_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.
papers.authors: Yuxuan Guo

papers.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate. Equivariant quantum circuits are usually compared with architectures that also differ in gates, structure or size. Here, we investigate the role of invariance in a controlled setting, classifying images whose labels are invariant under the dihedral group $D_4$. We compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and number of trainable parameters, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras, and benchmark invariant implementations against non-invariant ones in terms of generalization error, robustness to shortcut learning and resilience to a realistic noise model. On four binary tasks, including MNIST and two scientific data sets of galaxies and red blood cells, the invariant models trained on a few tens of images show better generalization than non-invariant ones. Invariance also makes the models immune to orientation shortcuts: when trained with a class-dependent corner watermark, the non-invariant models learn the watermark and often drop to chance level when it is moved. We show that the gain in accuracy of invariant models persists also under a realistic noise model.
papers.authors: Giuseppe D'Ambruoso, Giovanni Gramegna, Domenico Pomarico, Giuseppe Magnifico, Cosmo Lupo

papers.title: Where can Gauss--Bonnet scalarization begin in neutron and quark stars, and when do stars carry scalar charge?
papers.abstract: In scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, with a coupling $\zeta(\phi)\mathcal G$, the Gauss-Bonnet invariant $\mathcal G$ sources the scalar when $\zeta'(0)\neq0$ and sets the sign of the effective mass squared of its perturbations when $\zeta$ is quadratic, so the surface on which $\mathcal G$ changes sign inside a star organises both the scalar flux and the regions in which spontaneous scalarization can begin. A regular static star with continuous density contains a surface $\Sigma$ on which $\mathcal G$ vanishes whenever its surface density is below half its mean density, and $\Sigma$ is unique when the density profile steepens outward and $p/\rho$ decreases. Neutron-star models without density discontinuities therefore have one, but self-bound stars need not: in the MIT bag model $\mathcal G<0$ inside every stable quark star, for any bag constant. For a quadratic coupling the tachyonic region is then, in a quark star, either the whole interior or the whole exterior, according to the sign of $\zeta''(0)$, whereas in a neutron star it includes part of the interior for either sign. In the Newtonian limit $\Sigma$ lies where $\rho=\bar\rho/2$ in every dimension. Over a whole slice the lapse-weighted integral of $\mathcal G$ equals the lapse-weighted Gauss-Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically in three dimensions, so regular stars carry no scalar charge when $D=4$. Above four dimensions every star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole given by an interior integral weighted by $\rho+p_r$. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of $\zeta'(0)$ for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild-Tangherlini black hole at the same order, and its size relative to the exterior contribution is of first post-Newtonian order.
papers.authors: Sudan Hansraj

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Corrections to Taub-NUT-AdS Black Holes and Their Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We investigate cubic curvature corrections to four-dimensional Taub-NUT-AdS black holes and their thermodynamics. We construct the complete analytic solution to the first order in the higher-derivative couplings, and derive the corrected Hawking temperature and Wald entropy. The NUT potential remains unchanged, while reconstructing the NUT charge and Gibbs free energy through the Maxwell relation leaves just one undetermined function of the NUT parameter. We then independently evaluate the Gibbs free energy using two improved Reall-Santos methods, based on either the field redefinition or the background subtraction. After matching the thermodynamic variables, both methods yield identical results and fix the undetermined function, providing a consistent determination of the mass and NUT charge. Our work therefore establishes that the thermodynamics of Taub-NUT-AdS black hole withstands the higher-derivative corrections.
papers.authors: Yu-Qi Chen, Hai-Shan Liu, H. Lu

papers.title: One Measurement, Many Fronts in Kitaev and Cluster Chains
papers.abstract: A projective measurement of one site in the ground state of a quantum chain disturbs the chain in two ways: learning the outcome shifts distant expectation values at once, through ground-state correlations, and the measurement erases the correlations between the measured site and the rest. Both changes travel outward. We solve this problem exactly for the Kitaev chain, the cluster chain in a transverse field, and the Kitaev chain with power-law couplings, and we find that far from the measured site every quadratic observable responds through a front. Where the front is and how fast it broadens depend only on the quasiparticle dispersion. How strong it is depends on two operators: how strongly the measured one creates the fastest quasiparticles and how strongly the observed one detects them; if either factor vanishes, the front is weaker and decays faster. One measurement therefore launches many fronts, one per observable, with a common position and width but different decay laws. In the Kitaev chain the density and the bond energy, the two terms of its nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian, respond to one density measurement with decay laws that trade places between the topological and the trivial phase; in the cluster chain, measuring a symmetry-odd spin instead of a symmetry-even one changes the critical decay law at a fixed Hamiltonian; and with power-law couplings the width law itself changes. All decay laws and profiles are obtained in closed form.
papers.authors: Nicholas Musat, Stephan Haas, Rishabh Jha

papers.title: Geometric limits of quantum recovery across an Ising transition
papers.abstract: How many physical spins must a receiver retain to recover an unknown qubit? Four Ising duality defects encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed charge sector. We vary that state at fixed defect geometry and optimize over preselected spins and joint decoders, taking the infinite-chain limit before increasing defect separation. At every fixed finite positive reference field, exact recovery costs the central spacing plus the shorter outer spacing to leading order. For an error falling as any fixed inverse power of separation, the leading cost is the central spacing in the ordered phase, the shorter outer spacing in the disordered phase and their sum at criticality. Order and disorder records in discarded spins explain the contrast. In a critical benchmark, single-spin measurements, a one-way classical message and an output correction preserve reference entanglement on two separated blocks at budgets where every connected interval is entanglement breaking.
papers.authors: Yi Liang

papers.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
papers.abstract: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical and magnetic counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.
papers.authors: Carlos Herdeiro, Eugen Radu

papers.title: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
papers.abstract: We apply Functional Dimensional Regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $1\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap, Fuzzy Sphere and Non-Perturbative Renormalization Group. This demonstrates that, in the context of non-unitary theories, FDR retains the efficiency and rapid convergence to accurate critical exponents already observed in the Ising and O(N) cases.
papers.authors: Piero Beretta, Carlos A. S\'anchez-Villalobos, Alessandro Codello

papers.title: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.
papers.authors: Nikita Markarian

papers.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.
papers.authors: G. Militaru

papers.title: Ground-state energy estimation compiled on cat qubits: 6 808 qubits for FeMoco-54 in 23.6 hours
papers.abstract: We provide a detailed resource estimate of the state-of-the-art sum-of-squares block encoding algorithm for electronic structure Hamiltonians of Low et al. on superconducting cat qubits. To achieve this, we present compilations with closed-form costs of the dominant subroutines such as skew-tree Qrom, a Swap network and a Phaseup for both a repetition-cat and an LDPC-cat architecture. Our compilation represents algorithmic qubits in the $X$ basis, taking advantage of the asymmetric cost of $X$ and $Z$ access that the concatenation of cat qubits with phase-flip classical code brings. Additionally, we provide a protocol for $\vert i \rangle$-state distillation and a two-level Toffoli-like $\vert \text{C}_X\text{C}_X X \rangle$ magic state distillation protocol, including three factory layouts. To minimize the cost of Clifford corrections induced by magic state injections we tailor injection gadgets to each subroutine. Combining our compilation work with the adder compilation from the companion work Pappalardo et al., we provide global layouts for the block encoding in both architectures which we use to obtain resource estimates for ground-state energy estimation for the benchmarks of FeMoco-54 and FeMoco-76. Assuming a cycle time of 1$\mu$s, a reaction time of 10$\mathrm{\mu}$s, a phase estimation precision of 1 mHa and circuit-level phase-flip noise with probability $p_Z = 5 \times 10^{-4}$ with negligible bit-flip error, FeMoco-54 requires fewer than $7\,000$ cat qubits with an expected runtime of under one day for a single phase estimation run using an LDPC-cat architecture. Relaxing the bit-flip requirement to $p_X = 10^{-11}$ with an additional layer of elevator codes raises this to an estimated $12\,100$ cat qubits.
papers.authors: Larissa Kroell, Hugo Jacinto, Victor Hertz, Axel Pappalardo, Adel Ben Moussa, Manuel Rispler, Peter Shanahan, \'Elie Gouzien, Christophe Vuillot, Vivien Londe

papers.title: Six-Degree-of-Freedom Rotor-Load Cross-Spectral Density from Rotor-Plane Turbulence Cross-Spectra
papers.abstract: A frequency-domain response analysis of a wind turbine rotor requires the complete hub-load spectrum, but the customary scalar thrust and torque spectra retain neither the four in-plane components nor the coupling between them. This paper derives the full six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) rotor-load cross-spectral-density (CSD) matrix from the IEC Kaimal turbulence model. By decoupling the spatial order of inflow coherence from the temporal Doppler shift, the formulation introduces a two-index rotational-sampling kernel. Rotor symmetry and azimuthal averaging constrain the observed Doppler carrier strictly to blade-passing harmonics $pBf_{\mathrm{rot}}$, while the azimuthal aerodynamic transfer shifts the spatial coherence order to $pB+s$. A convergence study of the retained azimuthal order $s$ shows that $\lvert s\rvert\le4$ suffices, the assembled CSD then deviating from the full-band result by less than $10^{-5}$ in relative norm. The formulation is compared with OpenFAST simulations of a rigid floating wind turbine over nine wind speeds: the six auto-spectral densities agree closely below 1~Hz, and the present theory over-predicts the spectra near the 6P and 9P rotational harmonics.
papers.authors: Haoran Yang, Zhaolong Han

papers.title: Cellular Algebra of A2 webs
papers.abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. By self-duality of $V^+\oplus V^-$, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.
papers.authors: Azat M. Gainutdinov, Jesper Lykke Jacobsen, Yueheng Li

papers.title: Runaway entanglement between a semiclassical background and parametrically-enhanced quantum fluctuations
papers.abstract: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.
papers.authors: Roxane Th\'eriault, George Zahariade

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a magnetic spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal has a maximum at $2k_c$ and, as expected from momentum conservation, has a sharp cutoff at that scale. We apply this analysis to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160$ MeV the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-10 MeV on such viable models.
papers.authors: Abdias Aires, Tatsuya Daniel

papers.title: Chameleon Gravity with an Environmental Frequency Dependent on Density
papers.abstract: Scalar field theories of modified gravity are strongly constrained by the absence of detectable long range fifth forces in laboratory and Solar System environments. The chameleon mechanism addresses this problem by making the equilibrium value and effective mass of the scalar field dependent on the ambient matter density. In this work, we investigate an effective phenomenological extension of the chameleon framework in which the scalar potential contains an additional quadratic environmental contribution characterized by a density dependent background frequency. This background frequency is distinct from the frequency of scalar perturbations and parametrizes unresolved environmental effects beyond the conventional matter coupling. For an inverse power law scalar potential, we derive the modified equilibrium configuration and identify a frequency dominated regime in which the environmental contribution controls the density dependence of the field. Linear perturbations about the environmental minimum obey a Klein Gordon dispersion relation with a density-dependent effective mass, and the absence of tachyonic instability requires a positive environmental coupling. We further derive analytical consistency conditions associated with frequency dominance, thin shell screening, fifth-force suppression, and the weak field approximation. Numerical illustrations for representative parameter choices demonstrate how the modified density scaling can enhance fifth-force suppression relative to the conventional chameleon case.
papers.authors: Raziyeh Zaregonbadi, Nasim Saba

papers.title: On-shell renormalization of sine-Gordon by the quantum inverse scattering method
papers.abstract: In the quantum inverse scattering method the sine-Gordon model is solved on a lattice. Sklyanin, Takhtajan and Faddeev observed that the continuum and infinite-volume limits of the vacuum quasiparticle density become uniform only after the length of the box is rescaled, which absorbs the dependence on the cut-off up to a finite ambiguity in the mass scale. We develop this obser- vation into a renormalization of the spectrum internal to the method: since all the eigenvalues of the monodromy operator depend on the lattice only through the vacuum density, the uniform limit removes the cut-off, and an on-shell condition on the lightest breather fixes the remaining ambiguity. We show explicitly that the results coincide with those of normal ordering and of conformal perturbation theory: the dependence on the cut-off is the multiplicative renormaliza- tion of the cosine, with the exponent fixed by its scaling dimension, the masses scale with the bare coupling with the same power, and the spectrum agrees with the semiclassical one and with the exact S-matrix. Since the procedure requires neither a free field nor a conformal point, it provides an alternative, non-perturbative route to renormalization, internal to the quantum in- verse scattering method, which applies wherever an ultralocal lattice regularization is available, including asymptotically free sigma models.
papers.authors: Francesco Beccarini, Claudio Conti

papers.title: A Noise Operator Approach to Quantum Query Complexity and Time-Space Tradeoff Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel method based on the noise operator for showing that time-bounded quantum query algorithms only have exponentially small success probability. We use this to prove strong quantum time-space tradeoff lower bounds that seem out of reach by other methods. Applying our noise operator method involves purely classical arguments, making it straightforward to use. We use our quantum noise stability bound to prove that, for any pairwise independent hash function family $H$ from $n$ bits to $m$ bits, almost all $h \in H$ require a quantum algorithm with at most $S$ qubits of memory to make $\Omega(nm/S)$ queries to input $x$ in order to compute $h(x)$, even with very small success probability. Such a lower bound was not previously known even for classical algorithms. Previously, Mansour, Nisan, and Tiwari had used their hash mixing lemma to show the same quantitative bound for classical algorithms that have as input both a description of $h$ and its input $x$. Our noise operator method allows us to use a related but simpler property of hash functions to prove our bounds. As one consequence of this lower bound we derive the first optimal time-space tradeoff lower bounds for quantum algorithms computing integer multiplication. We also use this method to prove the first nontrivial fully general quantum time-space tradeoff lower bound for sorting. All previous quantum time-space tradeoff lower bounds for sorting are limited to proving output-oblivious lower bounds (i.e. the lower bounds only apply to algorithms with a non-adaptive output schedule). By combining our quantum noise stability bound with quantum recording query methods, we prove that every quantum algorithm that sorts $n$ numbers from $[n^2]$ using at most $S$ qubits of memory requires $\Omega(n^{4/3} (\log \log n)/(S^{1/3} \log n))$ quantum queries to the input.
papers.authors: Paul Beame, Blake Holman, Niels Kornerup

papers.title: Thermodynamics and phase transitions of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of static, nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings and compare them with the corresponding canonical EsGB solutions. The phantom lower branches have higher Wald entropy at fixed mass and lower free energy at fixed temperature than Schwarzschild black holes. The phantom exponential primary branches develop negative entropy at small horizon radii. Positive heat capacity occurs between the mass and temperature extrema. The phantom field reverses their order, the direction of free-energy crossings, and the signs of the entropy and mass jumps. For both couplings, the phantom lower branches and portions of the primary branches are therefore thermodynamically preferred over Schwarzschild black holes.
papers.authors: Ming Zhang, De-Cheng Zou, Yun Soo Myung, Bo Liu, You Long, Lina Zhang

papers.title: Accelerating systems as probes of Lorentz violation
papers.abstract: We investigate the Fulling-Davies-Unruh effect in a local Lorentz-violating effective field theory, focusing on the quantum-field response of accelerated detectors. We canonically quantize a real scalar field exactly in the coefficients for Lorentz violation. The dispersion relation, Hamiltonian, and massless and massive Wightman functions are obtained. We determine the conditions under which the scalar dynamics preserves boost symmetry and distinguish these from the weaker conditions required for stationarity along a single accelerated worldline. The Wightman functions are used to construct the finite-time Unruh-DeWitt response for a uniformly accelerated detector. For generic coefficients the response is nonstationary and depends on both the duration and temporal location of the measurement. The spectrum, which is the resulting excitation rate as a function of the energy level difference in the detector, is obtained numerically. It shows discernable differences with the usual massive thermal spectrum for dimensionless coefficients on the order of $10^{-7}$. Experimental implications of the result are discussed. As an alternative viewpoint, we place Lorentz violation in the point-particle sector, derive the exact trajectory generated by a constant electric field, and study the proper-time Fourier response of a conventional scalar wave along the modified trajectory.
papers.authors: Quentin G. Bailey, Nils A. Nilsson, Sawyer J. Star

papers.title: Asymptotic quasi--local structure induced by Magnetic field
papers.abstract: We introduce a magnetic coherent--state frame over the Landau levels of the two--dimensional Landau Hamiltonian, indexed by a discrete metric space combining spatial and energy degrees of freedom. Although overcomplete, the frame is almost--orthogonal, and we use it to endow the CAR $C^*$--algebra over the one--particle Hilbert space with an \emph{asymptotic quasi--local} (AQL) structure, in which graded commutators of observables localized on disjoint index sets decay exponentially rather than vanish exactly. By means of a family of conditional expectations onto the resulting local subalgebras, we construct a Fr\'echet $*$--subalgebra of almost--local observables, invariant under the discrete group of lattice translations, which act on it by continuous automorphisms. For the full continuous group of magnetic translations we establish a quantitative control on how local observables spread through this almost--local algebra, and we show that this control {exhibits the compatibility of the AQL structure with graded asymptotic abelianness under the entire continuous translation group. The dependence on the volume of the localization regions of the constants in the AQL bound is left as an open problem.} The results provide a discrete--continuum dictionary intended as the starting point for extending Lieb--Robinson--type techniques from lattice systems to interacting continuum electrons in a magnetic field.
papers.authors: Giuseppe De Nittis

papers.title: Strong Selective and List-Decoding Direct Product Theorems for Quantum Query Complexity
papers.abstract: Quantum strong direct-product theorems for specific functions have been known for nearly two decades. These have been extended to general results for function computation and state generation. The proofs of these results use a version of the multiplicative adversary method that does not naturally extend to relations. Standard strong direct-product theorems apply when algorithms must correctly answer every given question. Prior work extended them to equivalent threshold direct-product theorems, which require answers to all questions but only require that most answers are correct. We focus on two further generalizations. Strong selective direct-products apply to algorithms that adaptively choose, based on what they learn from queries, which questions from a large list to answer. This generalization is relational and useful for proving time-space tradeoffs. We prove a quantum strong selective direct-product theorem for all functions using a relational formulation of the multiplicative adversary method by Jeffery and Zur which we prove, via an equivalent formulation, satisfies a strong selective direct product property and captures any query lower bound for functions proven by negative-weights adversaries. The second generalization is list-decoding direct product problems introduced by Ben-David and Blais for classical query complexity. These allow an algorithm to produce a large list of possible output vectors such that one of them is fully correct. They proved that such theorems hold for randomized complexity of all Boolean functions. We prove a quantum analogue of this theorem for all partial Boolean-valued functions. We show that strong list-decoding direct-product theorems are implied by a special case of multiplicative adversaries which we show, via a new reduction, can be obtained from negative-weights adversaries for any Boolean-valued function.
papers.authors: Paul Beame, Niels Kornerup, Michael Whitmeyer

papers.title: Circuit Hypernetworks for Quantum-Augmented Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Improving pretrained language models with limited adaptation data calls for computational modules that are both effective and scalable. Parameterized quantum circuits offer expressive transformations for language modeling, yet existing quantum-enhanced language models apply the same predefined circuit design to every token in an input sequence, regardless of its content. This limitation is particularly acute in masked-diffusion language models, where token representations evolve across iterative denoising steps while the circuit design remains fixed. We introduce HyperQ, a quantum-augmented masked-diffusion language model that dynamically synthesizes token-specific quantum circuits. Built upon an IQP-inspired architecture, HyperQ employs a lightweight circuit hypernetwork to generate rotation angles and measurement bases conditioned on each token's hidden state. The resulting quantum expectation values are projected back into the frozen language-model backbone through a residual connection. To support wider quantum registers, HyperQ bounds circuit interaction degree, maintaining per-qubit gradient scale and readout cost independent of register width. Across six zero-shot benchmarks, scaling HyperQ from 16 to 64 qubits improves average accuracy from 47.65 to 54.30, surpassing the frozen backbone's 49.59 by 4.71 points while using only one tenth of the fine-tuning data used by classical baselines. We further execute the generated circuits on an IBM 156-qubit superconducting quantum processor, demonstrating their feasibility on physical quantum hardware.
papers.authors: Xiaoqiang Wang, Mengyang Xiong, Jun Dai, Bang Liu

papers.title: Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
papers.abstract: We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Entropy is a 1-cocycle in information cohomology; we generalize this to the quantum setting via Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. For an inclusion of von Neumann algebras N contained in M with a faithful normal state w admitting a cyclic and separating vector, and a conditional expectation E: M -> N (whose existence is equivalent to modular invariance of N by Takesaki's theorem), we construct the entanglement complex as the image of the transgression map tau_w on the relative cyclic complex, where A is a dense *-subalgebra of M and B = A intersect N. Our main result identifies entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map HC*(A) -> HC*(B), up to the connecting homomorphism d of the long exact sequence of the pair (A,B); when d = 0, the identification is exact. The relative modular cocycle u_t = (Dw : D(w|_N) o E)_t generates explicit entanglement classes when E is not w-invariant, with the Araki relative entropy as its infinitesimal generator. The framework accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, and leads to a holographic proposal: a subspace of H^1_ent is conjecturally dual to linearized modular Hamiltonian perturbations of the bulk entanglement wedge. We verify the construction in finite-dimensional, type II_1, and type III_1 examples.
papers.authors: R. C. Rashkov

papers.title: Edge observables in Maxwell theory on null boundaries
papers.abstract: We study edge observables in three-dimensional Maxwell theory on null boundaries using a Hamiltonian formulation adapted to null foliations. We consider three backgrounds: Minkowski spacetime, the BTZ black hole, and de Sitter space, where the relevant boundaries are, respectively, null infinity, the black hole horizon, and the cosmological horizon. In all three cases we find, besides the usual $\mathrm U(1)$ charge, a second edge observable associated with a shift transformation intrinsic to the null boundary. The two charges are well defined quasilocally. They form a centrally extended algebra which, in Fourier modes, becomes two independent Abelian Kac--Moody algebras with opposite levels. Thus, the same centrally extended edge structure appears at both asymptotic and finite distance null boundaries. The phase space also admits charge-conjugation twisted configurations, in which the modes of the algebra are half-integer. Finally, in Minkowski spacetime we find an exact radiative solution in this twisted sector, with both charges nonvanishing.
papers.authors: Du\v{s}an {\DJ}or{\dj}evi\'c, Olivera Miskovic, Antonia Montecinos, Tatjana Vuka\v{s}inac

papers.title: NAQsim: Full-Stack Architecture Simulation Framework for Fast and Space-Efficient Neutral Atom Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Technological advances in neutral-atom platforms have opened a new path toward designing efficient protocols for fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC). However, each physical operation is still orders of magnitude slower than on other platforms, such as superconducting qubits. Therefore, architects must identify fast and efficient FTQC architectures, which require reliable modeling tools to explore various design choices across the software, classical hardware, and quantum device stacks of neutral-atom platforms. In this paper, we propose NAQsim, an open-source simulation framework for neutral-atom FTQC architectures based on transversal gates. As its key feature, NAQsim enables detailed full-stack architecture evaluation that opens opportunities to explore previously overlooked performance bottlenecks. As a first use case for NAQsim, we identify one such bottleneck, patch rotations, perform full-stack co-optimization, and finally derive a near-rotation-free architecture (D3-ROT). For practical FTQC benchmark workloads, D3-ROT achieves a 2.27x speedup from this single bottleneck alone, with minimal footprint overhead. These results point to a much broader space of full-stack optimizations that NAQsim makes accessible for transversal surface-code architectures and beyond.
papers.authors: Yosuke Ueno, Shinichi Sunami, Toshihide Hinokuma, Yasunari Suzuki, Akihisa Goban, Hayata Yamasaki, Teruo Tanimoto, Ilkwon Byun

papers.title: Multiparameter quantum bounds for entanglement-assisted aperture synthesis
papers.abstract: Entanglement-assisted optical interferometry promises diffraction-limited imaging over baselines where light cannot be physically combined, but its estimation-theoretic bounds exist only for a single visibility on one baseline. This work formulates the multiparameter quantum estimation problem for an M-station array. A reduction lemma shows that the multimode quantum Fisher information (QFI) equals the mean photon number times the QFI of a single delocalized photon, making the problem finite-dimensional. The local photon-number superselection rule erases all phase information from the bare state; shared entanglement restores a fraction f(r)=r/(1+r) of the QFI on a baseline supplied with r pairs, a benchmark that applies to every pair of the array. The QFI matrix and its mean Uhlmann curvature show numerically that a point source is measurement-compatible, whereas every extended-source model examined is incompatible; a semidefinite-programming evaluation shows that the Holevo bound exceeds the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative bound by up to ~24% for three stations and by 4-8% for larger arrays and for CHARA. An explicit collective receiver, a numerically optimised global linear-optical network with photon counting, attains a weighted variance within 2-9% of the Holevo bound, over an order of magnitude below an explicit pairwise receiver, and a noisy-resource threshold gives the break-even baseline (~22 km for illustrative parameters) beyond which distributed entanglement beats direct transmission. Finally, allocating a finite entanglement budget has a closed-form proportional (square-root-law) solution for a per-baseline fringe cost, whereas for the source-parameter variance under an explicit photon budget the routing of photons matters far more than the entanglement split. These results recast quantum aperture synthesis as collective multiparameter estimation, illustrated on CHARA.
papers.authors: Kalaga Madhav, Pieter Kok, Nic Scott

papers.title: Fermionic Casimir memory from an anisotropic gravitational pulse
papers.abstract: We investigate the late-time energy deposited by a weak, spatially homogeneous anisotropic gravitational pulse in a massless Dirac field confined between two static parallel plates. The field satisfies MIT bag boundary conditions, while the prescribed geometry approaches Minkowski spacetime in both asymptotic time regions. Using a tetrad formulation, we show that the linear spin-connection contribution cancels for the traceless anisotropy, leaving a coupling to the shear component of the Dirac stress tensor. The pulse produces real fermion--antifermion pairs, whose deposited energy is evaluated through the corresponding Bogoliubov coefficients. Subtracting the production in unbounded space isolates a finite boundary-dependent contribution governed by the pulse duration relative to the characteristic spectral timescale set by the MIT gap. This contribution is negative in the adiabatic regime, where confinement suppresses excitations relative to the continuous free spectrum, and approaches zero from above in the impulsive limit. The late-time force on the plates is obtained separately from the normal stress $T^{zz}$ of the produced pairs, evaluated at fixed occupation numbers, with the field and the pulse present on both sides of each plate. The resulting pressure correction is the difference between the interior and exterior normal stresses. It reinforces the attractive Casimir force for both slow and fast pulses and reduces it in an intermediate window, so that it exhibits two sign changes. Unlike the bosonic vacuum-polarization memory previously obtained for the same class of backgrounds, the present effect is a dissipative fermionic memory carried by gravitationally created pairs. Here, memory denotes the persistent late-time modification of the quantum state after the pulse has vanished.
papers.authors: Celio R. Muniz, Herondy F. Santana Mota

papers.title: Quantum information spreading via higher-order operator correlators
papers.abstract: We provide an exact analytical benchmarks into measuring the quantum information spreading by introducing N-operator correlators. Leveraging the idea from N-point correlation function from cosmology, we formulate a generalized Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlator (OTOC), called N-Operator Correlator (NOC). Such formulation can reduce the effect of restricted analysis associated with selecting only two operators for OTOC. NOC can take into account a larger set of measurement probes in measuring the degree of quantum information spreading. We demonstrate these concepts with two analytically tractable systems with computing thermal averages of operator time evolutions at a finite temperature: a single qubit in longitudinal field and isotropic XXX model with a transverse field, two-qubit system. Our analytical benchmark serves as a basic introduction to generalized operator correlators in quantum mechanics.
papers.authors: M S\"uzen

papers.title: Frequency-domain extended-effective-source gravitational self-force for eccentric Schwarzschild orbits
papers.abstract: Effective-source formulations provide a practical route to gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations when singular retarded fields cannot be handled directly mode by mode. Before this work, frequency-domain effective-source calculations of the first-order GSF had been performed only for circular Schwarzschild orbits. We construct and implement a frequency-domain extended effective-source (EES) formulation for first-order Lorenz-gauge GSF on eccentric orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. The central obstacle is that radial libration forces the physical puncture and effective source to switch between interior and exterior branches, limiting their differentiability and producing slow spectral convergence. We overcome this obstruction by analytically extending both branches across the libration region and solving the coupled Lorenz-gauge perturbation equations for the resulting smooth extended sources. This provides an end-to-end gravitational EES implementation for eccentric motion and validates a computational ingredient needed for extending frequency-domain effective-source calculations toward second order.
papers.authors: Xuchen Lu, Yungui Gong, Bokai Zhang, Chao Zhang, Wenting Zhou

papers.title: Investigation of global structure of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson spacetime
papers.abstract: We conduct an investigation of the global structure of Kerr-Newman-BR spacetime and its various subcases such as Schwarzschild-BR spacetime. In this work, we extend the result of our previous studies, where we found that $r\to \infty$ is not the proper conformal infinity. By using the reciprocal coordinate $y=1/r$, we show that the whole family of Kerr-Newman-BR spacetimes can be continuously extended through the surface $r\to \infty$. However, the conformal structure after passing $r\to \infty$ strongly depends on the type of spacetime one is considering (either rotation is present, or not) and on the polar direction one chooses to be fixed (namely, whether we consider generic polar angle $\theta$, or we focus on the behaviour near the equatorial plane $\theta=\pi/2$, or near the poles $\theta=0,\pi$). Physically this extension can be interpreted as kind of ``confinement box,'' created solely by the magnetic field. Finally, we discuss the universality of such a continuous extension.
papers.authors: Hryhorii Ovcharenko

papers.title: Near universality of nonlinear transverse and radial velocity responses in spherical collapse with arbitrary radial profiles
papers.abstract: The nonlinear relation between density and expansion is usually formulated for a homogeneous spherical top hat, which has a single local Hubble rate. A smooth spherical profile instead expands differently along and across the radial direction-a direct signature of radial inhomogeneity. We show that, for growing-mode pressureless matter with a cosmological constant, the complete shellwise response is nevertheless fixed by one top-hat function. Given the local and enclosed density contrasts, a transverse response and its derivative determine the transverse and radial expansion rates. The linear and second-order limits are algebraic maps whose only dynamical input is the usual growth rate. An exact equal-age construction supplies the nonlinear response without integrating an evolution equation. We check that it reconstructs full Lambda-Lemaitre-Tolman-Bondi profiles to numerical precision. We also provide a derivative-aware, cosmology-independent three-term symbolic fit that requires only the growth rate and the local and enclosed density contrasts. Across a representative set of matter-curvature-redshift combinations and for a shell located in the compensated transition, the maximum relative errors are 0.3% and 0.7% in the transverse and radial responses, respectively. This compact formulation separates the production of a density profile from its expansion response and makes the effect of radial gradients explicit.
papers.authors: Valerio Marra

papers.title: New RG flows between non-Unitary CFTs from exact massless scattering theories
papers.abstract: We construct complete solutions of the massless S-matrix bootstrap equations describing a new infinite family of integrable RG flows from the higher-fusion-level minimal models M(3,2n+3;n) to the non-unitary Virasoro minimal models M(2,2n+3), including a flow from M(3,5) to the Yang--Lee CFT M(2,5) when n=1. We provide strong evidence for this identification by matching conformal perturbation theory around the UV fixed points with the small-volume expansion of the corresponding thermodynamic Bethe ansatz equations. We further show that a family of non-invertible Verlinde defect lines is preserved along the flows.
papers.authors: Changrim Ahn, Zoltan Bajnok, Soma Elek

papers.title: Soft Scale Symmetry Breaking with Laguerre Explicit Regulators
papers.abstract: In this work, we search for explicit regulators that do not spuriously break scale invariance starting from conditions established by implicit regularization. There is a family of regulator functions that obeys the conditions and leads to soft breaking terms of the dilatation current. This family of functions is shown to be related to the Laguerre polynomials. We apply this approach by revisiting quadratic divergences in the context of the naturalness problem of the Standard Model and show that the quadratic dependence of the Higgs mass on the cutoff is not required by consistency of scale-symmetry breaking and can be removed within this class of regulators. Applications of these regulators beyond 1-loop order are also considered.
papers.authors: A. R. Vieira

papers.title: Beyond de Sitter: Longitudinal-Mode Instabilities and Spectral Evolution of Massive Vector Fields with Non-Minimal Curvature Coupling during Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate the inflationary dynamics and spectral energy densities of a massive spectator vector field non-minimally coupled to the Ricci scalar. We compare exact de Sitter (dS) and constant-slow-roll quasi-de Sitter (qdS) backgrounds, following transverse and longitudinal modes through an instantaneous transition to radiation domination. We initialize the modes deep inside the horizon with second-order WKB Bunch--Davies conditions and solve their equations numerically for representative comoving momenta and vector masses. The non-minimal coupling modifies the effective mass, canonical normalization, and effective-mass-crossing time, while leaving the horizon-crossing condition fixed by the prescribed background in the spectator-field approximation. At mass crossing, the transverse spectral energy density increases slightly and monotonically over 0 <= xi <= 10^{-6}, whereas the longitudinal density decreases monotonically, with an approximately 21% suppression from xi = 0 to 10^{-6} in both backgrounds. The qdS longitudinal values remain slightly above their dS counterparts, while the transverse results are nearly indistinguishable. Despite its suppression, the longitudinal contribution remains dominant, exceeding the transverse contribution by approximately three orders of magnitude. We also derive an all-momentum condition for a non-negative longitudinal canonical frequency in exact de Sitter space. For the representative mass considered, the required coupling lies outside the constant-coefficient heavy-scalar matching regime, so large-coupling solutions are formal rather than controlled effective-theory predictions. Our results distinguish kinetic positivity, canonical-frequency signs, bare spectral energy densities, and the validity domain of the effective description.
papers.authors: Ehsan Momeni, Fatimah Shojai, Hossein Khodabakhshi

papers.title: Experimental High-Dimensional Quantum Overlapping Tomography
papers.abstract: Large-scale quantum systems have advanced rapidly via the exploration of more particles and higher dimensions, offering great potential for developing quantum technologies. However, their characterization becomes prohibitive with increasing local dimensionality and particle number. Here we propose high-dimensional quantum overlapping tomography based on a graph-theoretic formulation, which allows one to efficiently reconstruct few-body marginals of multipartite high-dimensional quantum systems. We experimentally realize it on a photonic four-party entangled state in a $4 \times 4 \times 2 \times 2$ system. Using measurements in mutually unbiased bases, we reconstruct all six two-body marginals with only 25 projective measurement settings, compared with 94 and 225 settings for independent tomography of all two-body reduced states and full state tomography, respectively. The reconstructed marginals reveal a layered entanglement structure vital for high-dimensional quantum networks. We further show that these marginals enable more noise-resilient certification of multipartite high-dimensional entanglement than the fidelity-based criterion. Our work thus offers a scalable route for learning multidimensional quantum systems.
papers.authors: Haifei Wang, Rui Qu, Zhengning Yang, Xiaodan Lyu, Haotao Zhu, Zitong Xu, Lianzhen Cao, Joel Yang, Otfried G\"uhne, Weibo Gao

papers.title: de Broglie-Bohm Dynamics with Schr\"odinger Source Fields: A Framework for Subquantum Theory
papers.abstract: We extend de Broglie--Bohm (dBB) pilot-wave theory by introducing a complex source field into the Schr\"odinger equation and examining its effects on quantum equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics. In dBB theory, the physical particle distribution P, rather than the Born density $|{\psi}|^2$, carries the ensemble probability, so a source term may modify the pilot wave without violating conservation of total particle probability. We derive the source-modified Hamilton--Jacobi and continuity equations, the transport equation for the nonequilibrium ratio $f=P/|{\psi}|^2$, and an exact entropy-production formula. Three applications follow. First, suitably designed sources can drive exponential relaxation toward quantum equilibrium. Second, the entropy-production rate admits a Prigogine-type bilinear form, providing a basis for a subquantum thermodynamics with entropy-producing and entropy-extracting regimes. Third, a tuned source can exactly cancel the Bohmian quantum potential, yielding classical particle trajectories while the guiding wave retains nontrivial structure and the nonequilibrium ratio remains conserved. The resulting framework provides a unified setting for studying source-driven quantum nonequilibrium, entropy exchange, and classicalization, and motivates further investigation of the physical and ontological status of the source field.
papers.authors: Said Mikki

papers.title: Analytic Spread Complexity from Level Statistics: From Chaos to Integrability
papers.abstract: Spread complexity has emerged as a useful probe of quantum chaos, yet the microscopic spectral origin of its characteristic finite-time peak remains incompletely understood. We develop an analytic framework that relates spread complexity directly to local spectral statistics. Starting from an energy-space representation of the Krylov kernel, we show that the kernel is approximately banded, leading to a rapidly convergent diagonal expansion dominated by nearby levels in the ordered spectrum. Motivated by this structure, we propose an approximate kernel-universality hypothesis: after unfolding, the Krylov kernel is well approximated by that of a uniform lattice. Combining this universal kernel with local spectral statistics yields a simple analytic expression for spread complexity in terms of the Fourier transforms of the $k$-th nearest-neighbour spacing distributions. In particular, at leading order, the finite-time peak is controlled by the Fourier transform of the nearest-neighbour spacing distribution. The resulting framework describes both chaotic random-matrix ensembles and the integrable Poisson limit, identifies the spectral origin of the complexity peak and its late-time behaviour, and provides a direct connection between Krylov dynamics and spectral statistics.
papers.authors: Pallab Basu, Suman das, Bigboy Madlala

papers.title: Two-Parameter Ansatz for the Violation of Eigenstate Thermalization
papers.abstract: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides the prevailing framework for understanding quantum thermalization and ergodicity in isolated many-body systems. Yet, no general theory describes the continuous onset of ETH violation between the conventional ETH and its complete breakdown. Here, we introduce a two-parameter ansatz for ETH violation that unifies and distinguishes two mechanisms: fading ergodicity and trapped ergodicity. While fading ergodicity captures the established route to ergodicity breaking, trapped ergodicity describes a distinct scenario in which ETH is violated in finite systems but restored in the thermodynamic limit. We test this framework in the spin-1/2 $J_1$-$J_2$ chains with onsite disorder and a linear potential. In both cases, we find that the observed ETH violation is consistent with trapped ergodicity.
papers.authors: Kohei Ohgane, Lev Vidmar

papers.title: Delayed Formation of Landau Polaritons in Phase-Resolved THz Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling gives rise to polaritons through coherent and periodic energy exchange between electromagnetic cavity fields and material excitations. While this interaction is typically inferred from spectral mode splitting, its dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, using phase-resolved terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we observe vacuum Rabi oscillations of Landau polaritons formed by coupling the cyclotron resonance in a GaAs/AlGaAs two-dimensional electron gas with Fabry-Perot cavity modes. By employing cross-polarized spectroscopy and magnetic-field differential, we resolve the temporal beating of the cyclotron resonance oscillations. Supported by a quantum electrodynamic model, we show that the vacuum Rabi oscillations start after a delay corresponding to one cavity round-trip time. This demonstrates that the strong coupling regime sets up only after the formation of the cavity mode field. Our results provide direct insight into the dynamics of hybrid light-matter states in the THz regime.
papers.authors: Noureddine Charrouj, Nischal Gajurel, Yurii Ivonyak, Dmitriy Yavorskiy, Vladimir Y. Umansky, Jerzy Lusakowski, Wojciech Knap, Marcin Bialek

papers.title: QAdapt: Noise-Adaptive Neural Pre-Decoding for Surface-Code Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing relies on quantum error correction to protect logical information, requiring classical decoders that keep pace with syndrome generation. Heterogeneous, changing hardware noise and the distribution shift from simulation to experiment challenge the accuracy and robustness of fixed neural decoders. We present QAdapt, a noise-adaptive neural pre-decoding framework for surface-code quantum error correction. QAdapt learns local spatiotemporal correlations, continually adapts across noise environments, and passes the residual syndrome to a conventional global decoder. Online elastic weight consolidation limits forgetting as training moves between measurement, idle, CNOT, and Pauli-bias noise regimes. At distance nine, the HTNet pre-decoder reduces equivalent per-round logical error by 15.64% relative to Ising-Fast, with 28.75% fewer parameters and 9.07% less matching-backend time. Online EWC reduces average forgetting by 76.52% relative to sequential fine-tuning. With weights frozen, it reduces equivalent per-round logical error by 5.66% relative to continued base-environment training on a fixed valid domain of 331 unseen compound-noise conditions; whole-sequence failure probability falls by 2.54% over all 396 conditions. On native Willow records, the corresponding per-round reductions are 19.44%, 17.47%, and 17.95% at 10, 30, and 50 rounds, without target-domain fine-tuning. These results show how adaptive neural pre-decoding can improve logical accuracy, preserve performance across noise regimes, and reduce residual matching workload within an established decoding pipeline.
papers.authors: Ran Miao, Rui Luo, Xiaohan Shan, Xiaoming Sun

papers.title: From the Early Slope to Curvature: Future Prospects and challenges for Astrophysical Parameter Estimation Using the Core-Collapse Supernova High-Frequency Feature
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) signals from core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) contain both stochastic and deterministic components. Among these, the High-Frequency Feature (HFF), associated with Proto-Neutron Star (PNS) oscillations, has emerged as an observable for probing dense-matter physics. Previous studies of the HFF have primarily focused on its early-time slope as a diagnostic of PNS contraction and its dependence on the nuclear equation of state (EOS). In this work, we investigate recovering higher-order features of the HFF evolution, such as its curvature, from core-collapse supernova numerical simulations. By analyzing 2D and 3D waveforms injected into real interferometric noise, we apply the coherent WaveBurst algorithm in its cWB-XP implementation to reconstruct the HFF of recovered events. Comparing reconstructions at different signal strengths allows us to examine the extent to which the HFF remains accessible beyond its early linear evolution
papers.authors: Alejandro Casallas-Lagos, Marek Szczepa\'nczyk, Michele Zanolin, Anthony Mezzacappa

papers.title: Quantum Circuits for Quantum Spatial Search on $d$-Dimensional Hypercubic Lattices
papers.abstract: We propose an explicit quantum-circuit construction for quantum spatial search based on discrete-time quantum walks on $d$-dimensional hypercubic lattices and systematically evaluate its circuit-resource scaling. Although the algorithmic performance of quantum spatial search has been extensively studied, a systematic evaluation of its circuit-resource scaling remains limited. We implement the flip-flop shift operator using coin-controlled modular increment and decrement operations for position updates and a single $X$ gate for direction reversal. We compare four implementations of the position update based on the quantum Fourier transform (QFT), ripple-carry addition, multi-controlled $X$ (MCX) gates, and automatically synthesized arithmetic. The results show that the QFT-based implementation reduces circuit width and depth, while the ripple-carry implementation reduces the CX-gate count at the cost of additional ancilla qubits. We also extend the construction to non-periodic boundary conditions by introducing self-loops at lattice boundaries. We confirm that numerical simulations of the circuits reproduce the theoretical search dynamics for $d=2,3,4$, and $5$ under periodic boundary conditions and for $d=2$ under non-periodic boundary conditions. For $N=L^d$ lattice sites, the circuit width scales as $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$. We derive asymptotic upper bounds on the total circuit depth of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{N}\log^{5/2} N)$ for $d=2$ and $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{N}\log^2 N)$ for $d\geq3$, consistent with the numerical results. Furthermore, CX-gate depolarizing noise simulations show that reducing the CX-gate count improves noise robustness. These results provide guidance for efficient quantum-circuit design for spatial search on hypercubic lattices.
papers.authors: Rei Sato

papers.title: Distributed Topological Charge and Spinorial Holonomy in Yukawa-Regularized Graphene Disclinations
papers.abstract: Conical geometries provide the standard description of disclinations, but they concentrate the curvature at a singular apex. We introduce a Yukawa-type regularization that replaces this singularity by a smooth curvature distribution while preserving the asymptotic topology of the defect. Exact expressions are obtained for the conformal factor, curvature, and enclosed topological charge. The resulting geometry exhibits a scale-dependent topological charge and a corresponding radius-dependent holonomy, establishing a direct connection between distributed curvature and geometric phases. We further investigate the dynamics of massless Dirac quasiparticles in this background and show that the regularized core modifies the spin connection while preserving the asymptotic topological signature of the defect. These results provide a finite-core extension of the conventional conical description and offer a natural framework for studying geometric and topological effects in graphene-like systems.
papers.authors: A. M. de M. Carvalho, G. Q. Garcia, E. Brito, C. Furtado

papers.title: Relativistic bound-state solutions for a non-central Schi\"oberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular terms
papers.abstract: Singular interactions can reshape quantum spectra by changing admissible wavefunction domains. In this study, we investigate this mechanism in the Klein--Gordon equation for a non-central Schi\"oberg-type hyperbolic potential with double ring-shaped angular barriers. Equal scalar and vector couplings separate the radial and angular dynamics. We solve the angular equation exactly on each hemisphere with principal boundary conditions and treat the radial equation with the Greene--Aldrich approximation, obtaining Jacobi-polynomial wavefunctions and an implicit relativistic quantization condition. With this boundary realization, the equatorial inverse-square singularity splits configuration space into reflection-related sectors with identical angular spectra. Reducing the barrier to zero while retaining the equatorial wall selects the odd-reflection spectral branch of the regular full-domain problem; a single hemisphere has no intrinsic parity. The nonrelativistic limit recovers the corresponding Schr\"odinger formulation. State-resolved nonrelativistic and relativistic benchmarks quantify the centrifugal error. In a dimensionless relativistic example, the relative error in the remaining binding exceeds unity near threshold although the absolute energy error decreases.
