Whether causality in its strongest operational form -- non-disturbance under all physically realisable operations -- survives relativisation is left open. An upshot of our finding is that quantum field theories formulated relative to a quantum reference frame cannot rest on the traditional axioms, and some general relational axiomatisation must replace at least some of them by taking into account physically realistic properties of the frame.
papers.authors: Christopher J. Fewster, Leon Loveridge

papers.title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high even dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that the spherically symmetric $SO(d)$ Yang--Mills equation admits a third smooth self-similar profile, in addition to the two known explicit profiles, in every even dimension $d\geq 12$. This complements the analogous existence theorem in odd dimensions $d\geq 11$ (arXiv:2610.36784). In contrast to the odd-dimensional case, where the classification of smooth self-similar profiles reduces to counting roots of an explicit resonance polynomial [Phys. Rev. D 114, 064021 (2026)], the even-dimensional proof requires solving a nonlinear connection problem. In $d=10$, where one explicit profile degenerates to the zero solution, we give a formal argument for the existence of a second nontrivial smooth profile in addition to the single nontrivial explicit one.
papers.authors: Piotr Bizo\'n

papers.title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.
papers.authors: Jiahao Yan, Xuanying Lai, Xiaoshui Lin, Yizhou Wang, Changyu Yao, Guanghui He, Thomas Lewer, Chong Zu, Chuanwei Zhang

papers.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
papers.abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.
papers.authors: Mrinal Dasgupta, Alexander Fraley, Pier Francesco Monni, Saad Nabeebaccus

papers.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.
papers.authors: Blake J. Bottesi, James T. Liu

papers.title: Loss-Tolerant Quantum Correlations Between Atomic and Photonic Qubits
papers.abstract: Quantum physics forbids cloning of a qubit. Therefore, a qubit is irreversibly lost upon loss of the information carrier. To mitigate this physical loss, it has been proposed to distribute the logical information across an entangled set of physical qubits, some of which can be lost. Previous experiments illustrated this concept, but failed to demonstrate a gain in the information-retrieval efficiency. Here we address this challenge with photons for which the total loss, from generation to detection, is below the loss-tolerance threshold of $50\%$. Using two single-atom emitters in an optical cavity, we encode information into the photons of a graph state and observe an efficiency gain for retrieving quantum correlations between the atoms and the photons for single-qubit measurements in the Pauli $X$ and $Z$ bases. Although technical errors reduce the probability to obtain the \textit{correct} result, we achieve average fidelities as high as $\gtrsim\!70\%$ without and $\gtrsim\!75\%$ with error detection, demonstrating entanglement between the atomic and encoded photonic qubits. Lowering the encoding errors is a next natural step toward loss-tolerant photonic quantum-information processing.
papers.authors: Leonardo Ruscio, Love A. Pettersson, Philip Thomas, Stefano Paesani, Olivier Morin, Anders S. S{\o}rensen, Gerhard Rempe

papers.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
papers.abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level mechanisms by which complex structure moduli can generate fermion mass hierarchies and show analytically and numerically that both mechanisms are obstructed for previously studied tetra-quadric models. Motivated by these obstructions, we scan the existing databases of tens of thousands of complete intersection Calabi-Yau line bundle models and find a unique smooth quotient admitting a rank-three up-quark Yukawa matrix at tree level. Evaluating the physical couplings on this manifold and evolving them under the renormalization group, we obtain realistic mass hierarchies for the top, charm, up, and bottom quarks in the smooth supergravity regime.
papers.authors: Yuri Chervonyi, Fabian Ruehle, Nenad Tomasev

papers.title: Modular conjugations for thermal states and second worlds
papers.abstract: The modular conjugation $J$ maps an algebra of observables onto its commutant. For the vacuum on a Rindler wedge it is a spacetime reflection, but for thermal states in two-dimensional CFTs the known expressions involve chiral fields at the complex points $x\pm i\beta/2$, interpreted as belonging to a ``second world''. Here we compute $J$ for the geometric thermal state in explicit cyclic purifications, using either the vacuum vector, through the conformal map to a Rindler wedge, or a vector in the natural cone of a local algebra. The modular images are then fields at real points, and complex coordinates arise only when operators of the commutant outside the image of the thermal representation are written as fields on the original spacetime. For the chiral $U(1)$ current we also purify by doubling the Fock space, obtain explicit formulas for $J$, show that this purification coincides with Sorce's canonical purification, and treat all primary thermal states.
papers.authors: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau, Guillem P\'erez-Nadal

papers.title: Robust Passive Quantum Memory in Three Dimensions, Part I: Thermal and Zero-Temperature Perturbative Stability
papers.abstract: Whether a three-dimensional quantum many-body system with geometrically local, bounded-degree interactions can passively protect encoded quantum information has remained a central open question since Kitaev introduced topological quantum computation. Passive protection requires stability against both thermal noise at nonzero temperature and generic static Hamiltonian perturbations Balasubramanian, Davydova, and Lin (BDL) recently established unperturbed three-dimensional thermal self-correction using a recursively defined family of stabilizer Hamiltonians. However, they left open whether their construction remains stable against quantum perturbations, even at zero temperature. In this paper, we show that a slight variant of the BDL code family achieves stability along both boundary axes of the perturbation-temperature phase diagram as the system size grows. Following BDL, in the absence of perturbation it is thermally stable below a critical temperature, achieving a stretched-exponentially long memory lifetime when coupled to any local Markovian thermal bath generated by single-site system-bath interactions satisfying detailed balance with bounded coupling rates. At zero temperature under arbitrary weak, superpolynomially decaying quantum perturbations, the family maintains a uniform bulk spectral gap, superpolynomially small ground-space splitting, and a superpolynomially long closed-system unitary memory lifetime for quasi-locally dressed logical observables. To prove this zero-temperature stability, we establish local topological quantum order across the multiscale hierarchy using a linearly dilated relaxation of the usual Bravyi-Hastings-Michalakis criteria. In the companion paper, we combine the tools developed here with finite-temperature worldline cluster expansions to establish passive self-correction throughout the phase diagram's positive-temperature perturbed interior.
papers.authors: Patrick Hayden

papers.title: Restoring quantum neural network trainability through reusable calibration
papers.abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) rely on measured quantum observables to guide optimization, but hardware noise can suppress the parameter-dependent signals essential for learning. Here, we develop a structure-preserving error-mitigation framework that improves QNN trainability through reusable calibration of the quantum circuit's effective noise response. By calibrating a reference circuit with the same gate architecture as the trainable circuit, we construct regularized estimators of local quantum features that remain fixed throughout training. We quantify how calibration errors and response mismatches affect the recovery of both observables and their derivatives. Numerical simulations demonstrate enhanced loss-landscape contrast, faster convergence, and improved classification performance, and an IBM Quantum experiment confirms improved closed-loop variational optimization under hardware noise. We further demonstrate calibration reuse in a modular QNN comprising 25 independent four-qubit channels, corresponding to 100 qubits in aggregate. Our results establish reusable feature calibration as a practical approach to improving noise-limited quantum machine learning without repeated calibration at every training step.
papers.authors: Ruizhe Shen, Xianquan Yan, Kenji Kawaguchi, Ching Hua Lee

papers.title: Tunable Topological Charge Order in Magnetic Moir\'e Systems
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moir\'e superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $\nu_B=1$ in the presence of a moir\'e superlattice potential, with three electrons per moir\'e cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moir\'e bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moir\'e minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a N\'eel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.
papers.authors: Conor Smith, Yubo Yang, Shiwei Zhang, Miguel A. Morales

papers.title: Parametric and Universal Thouless Invariants in Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: We investigate the classification of continuous families of translation-invariant injective matrix product states on an infinite chain, parametrized by a paracompact Hausdorff space $X$ and subject to a compact Hausdorff symmetry $G$. We construct an invariant for phases of such families, valued in $\check{H}^1(X;\widehat{G})$, that generalizes the known $\widehat{G}$ phase invariant for $G$-symmetric Thouless pumps. The phase invariant is constructed as the pullback to $X$ of a single universal \v{C}ech cohomology class on a classifying space of $G$-symmetric translation-invariant injective matrix product states. Several examples are given over various parameter spaces where this invariant is nontrivial.
papers.authors: Leonardo Goller, Amartya H. Singh, Daniel D. Spiegel, Marco Venuti

papers.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
papers.abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.
papers.authors: Mohamed M. Anber

papers.title: A Proposal for Quantum Reference Frames in Quantum Field Theory and their Experimental Exploration
papers.abstract: We construct quantum reference frames (QRFs) in quantum field theory, using localized modes of a scalar field as frames for its shift symmetry. We import tools from relativistic quantum information to explicitly compute entropies and correlation measures of relational observables, investigating their frame dependence and the new features arising from the field-theoretic character of the system. Unlike QRFs for systems with finitely many degrees of freedom, localized field-theoretic QRFs are necessarily mixed in physically relevant states and generically correlated with the subsystems they describe. These aspects of QRFs for fields affect the properties of relational observables in a subtle way. Furthermore, we put forward a proposal for testing these predictions with existing quantum simulators based on ultracold atoms and quantum fluids, thus connecting QRF physics with analogue gravity platforms.
papers.authors: Ivan Agullo, Fabio M. Mele

papers.title: Modular Hamiltonian and modular flow of a massive scalar in an interval
papers.abstract: We obtain the vacuum modular Hamiltonian of a free massive scalar in an interval, for any $mL$. Its eigenvectors are superpositions of massive plane waves emitted from the two end points, with amplitudes given by a linear integral equation whose Neumann series is an expansion in reflections, and a normalization fixed by a Painlev\'e V transcendent. We follow the modular flow of initially localized wave packets inside the causal diamond. The flow is not geometric: the commutator profiles spread and can develop peaks ahead of the conformal trajectory.
papers.authors: Ra\'ul E. Arias, Daniel Fondevila

papers.title: Gravitational Mode Instabilities in Kerr-like Black Holes
papers.abstract: We identify exponentially growing modes of a homogeneous gravitational Teukolsky-like operator on highly spinning Kerr-like black holes subject to quasinormal mode boundary conditions. Specifically, we compute electromagnetic and gravitational quasinormal modes of a spacetime proposed by Konoplya, Rezzolla, and Zhidenko that parametrizes deformations from the Kerr geometry, including configurations with black hole spin parameter $a/M > 1$ that retain an event horizon. Using the continued fraction method, we find that the spin-weight $s=-2$ operator develops exponentially growing modes when the black hole spin and deformation parameters are sufficiently large, while the electromagnetic modes remain damped throughout the parameter space. We further compare the quasinormal mode predictions with an agnostic analysis of the GW250114 ringdown, identifying regions of the parameter space that are compatible with the spectrum inferred from the data.
papers.authors: Pedro Henrique Croti Siqueira, Rodrigo Dal Bosco Fontana, Maur\'icio Richartz

papers.title: Cyclic Boson Stars with Quantum Vortex Molecules
papers.abstract: We find a new type of stationary boson star with cyclic rotational symmetry in the minimal model of complex scalar field coupled to gravity. Unlike conventional axisymmetric spinning boson stars, these configurations can carry noninteger angular momentum per particle in units of the reduced Planck constant, revealing a new way for boson stars to carry angular momentum. We identify the vortex assemblies within these stars as self-gravitating quantum vortex molecules, in which gravity supports a stationary vortex arrangement despite internal circulation. These structures provide a relativistic realization of quantum vortex molecules studied in condensates and motivate possible laboratory analogues.
papers.authors: Xing-Yu Yang, Rong-Gen Cai

papers.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2\pi$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).
papers.authors: Vahid Reza Shajiee, Mohammad Mehdi Sheikh-Jabbari, Vahid Taghiloo

papers.title: Supersymmetric warped AdS$_3$ solutions in eleven-dimensional supergravity
papers.abstract: We construct new families of supersymmetric solutions of eleven-dimensional supergravity by deforming the half-BPS $\mathrm{AdS}_3\times \mathrm{S}^3_+\times \mathrm{S}^3_-\times\mathbb R^2$ background. We consider lightlike, spacelike and timelike warpings of the anti-de Sitter factor, accompanied by deformations of the two three-spheres, and determine the supporting four-form fluxes and the constraints imposed by the equations of motion. In particular, the deformation parameters of the two spheres are necessarily equal, although their radii need not coincide. We compute the conserved charges and determine the preserved supersymmetries and Killing superalgebras. Generic lightlike solutions preserve four real supercharges, whereas spacelike and timelike solutions preserve eight, with a Killing superalgebra containing a single exceptional $\mathfrak d(2,1;\alpha)$ factor.
papers.authors: Ruggero Noris

papers.title: Not All Holographic Entropy Inequalities Are Free of Area Law Ultraviolet Divergences
papers.abstract: In the AdS/CFT correspondence, linear constraints on subsystem entropies, which are necessary conditions for the validity of the Ryu-Takayanagi proposal, define the holographic entropy cone. We disprove a prior claim that all holographic constraints of this type are free of area law divergences (superbalanced). We analyze one explicit counterexample and explain how to easily find more; we report signatures of $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ counterexamples. Our findings invalidate multiple prior claims and conjectures.
papers.authors: Xin-Xiang Ju, Bartlomiej Czech

papers.title: Black holes as black boxes: a query lower bound on python's lunch decoding
papers.abstract: The python's lunch conjecture relates the complexity of bulk reconstruction in holographic tensor networks to an exponential cost associated with post-selection. We establish a tight query lower bound for this decoding problem in a Haar random oracle model, with a python's lunch circuit that applies Haar random unitary $U$ to a logical input and fixed ancillas, followed by post-selection on $m$ output qubits. Given one copy of the normalized encoded state and coherent oracle access to $U$ and $U^\dagger$, including controlled queries, we prove that recovering even a single logical bit with constant average advantage requires $\Omega(2^{m/2})$ queries. Together with the state-independent amplitude amplification upper bound for approximately isometric encodings, this establishes query complexity $\Theta(2^{m/2})$ at constant decoding accuracy. We also comment on the decoding cost for other "admissible'" ensembles of unitaries $U$ which give rise to families of approximately isometric holographic maps.
papers.authors: Chris Waddell, Michelle Xu

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.
papers.authors: Netta Engelhardt, Richard Nally

papers.title: 'Forward-backward' flows and integration cycles for semiclassical Euclidean gravity
papers.abstract: Integrating Euclidean semiclassical gravity over real Riemannian metrics is subtle due to the conformal factor problem. A perturbative prescription was given by Gibbons-Hawking-Perry (GHP) where the integration contour for the conformal perturbations is rotated to be imaginary. A potential non-perturbative remedy is that the integration cycles associated to semiclassical saddle points should be deformed into the space of complex metrics in the sense of Picard-Lefschetz theory. Here we propose a non-perturbative construction of such complex integration cycles. This employs a 'forward-backward' gradient flow of the Einstein-Hilbert action, starting at a saddle point, along which the action has monotonically increasing real part and constant imaginary part. The flow is not parabolic. In a neighbourhood of a saddle point, the real part of the conformal factor flows forward and that of the conformal class backwards, with the opposite true of their imaginary parts. Starting the flow at a saddle point, then roughly speaking, one specifies the real part of the conformal class and the imaginary part of the conformal factor at the end of the flow. Solving the flow one finds the complex metrics along a one parameter path within the integration cycle of that saddle, and varying this final data generates the integration cycle, the Lefschetz thimble of the saddle point. We find that near to a real saddle point this reproduces the GHP prescription. We characterise the neighbourhood of a saddle where such forward-backward flows may exist, finding a weaker restriction than that of Kontsevich-Segal-Witten. We numerically demonstrate flows explicitly for 4-dimensional gravity, constructing sections through the integration contours for the saddles given by Euclidean de Sitter, and for Schwarzschild in a cavity.
papers.authors: Nicholas M. K. Ross, Toby Wiseman

papers.title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.
papers.authors: Salvatore D. Pace, Sakura Schafer-Nameki, Carolyn Zhang

papers.title: An infrared-safe $S$-matrix for $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills
papers.abstract: Scattering amplitudes of massless gauge theories are not observables: they are infrared divergent, and the standard regulators are tied either to perturbation theory or the planar limit. We study $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory on rigid AdS$_4$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where the role of the amplitude is played by correlation functions of boundary operators. These are finite, and they are defined at any coupling and for any gauge group. Among them, the four-point function of the flavor-current supermultiplet is the counterpart of the $2\to2$ amplitude of the elementary supergluon states, and arguably the simplest non-trivial observable of the theory. In this paper, we compute it at weak coupling to one loop. The tree-level correlator follows directly from the microscopic theory, and the one-loop correlator, which we obtain from AdS unitarity, takes a remarkably simple form in Mellin space. In the flat-space limit, it reproduces the one-loop scattering amplitude, with the infrared divergences re-emerging as logarithms.
papers.authors: Maria Nocchi, Leonardo Rastelli

papers.title: Hidden wormholes from an action principle in $D=4$
papers.abstract: We present new black hole solutions for the class of gravitational effective field theories in four spacetime dimensions that extend General Relativity while retaining the graviton as the only degree of freedom of gravitational origin. We consider terms up to cubic order in curvature, solve the resulting field equations, and find one-way hidden wormholes as numerical solutions: these are regular black holes with an interior wormhole throat that is crossable in one direction and leads to a cosmological spacetime in its interior. They are regular and have no inner horizon, thus evading the mass inflation instability that afflicts conventional regular black hole geometries.
papers.authors: Francesco Del Porro, Alessia Platania, Samuele Silveravalle

papers.title: Isomorphisms of Class S Theories with IndexLab
papers.abstract: We use IndexLab to scan untwisted and twisted class $\mathcal{S}$ constructions based on ADE Lie algebras of rank up to seven, as well as $A_8$ and $E_8$. We consider surfaces of genus at most three with up to five punctures, covering 167,244,647 constructions in total. To find candidate pairs of isomorphic theories, we compare Schur and Hall-Littlewood indices, Weyl anomalies, Coulomb branch spectra, and flavor data. We set aside pairs explained by known mechanisms, leaving a catalogue of 5,278 candidate pairs. Recurring changes in rank, puncture labels, and twists suggest families of candidate isomorphisms. We group 99.58% of the pairs into 25 families and 6 finite families. IndexLab is available at superconformal.com.
papers.authors: Zhihao Duan, Zhenghao Zhong

papers.title: QEDist: Practical Exact Distance Certification for Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: We present QEDist, a method and software package that certifies the distance of qubit stabilizer codes. Building on tree-search methods, QEDist constructs candidate logical operators one qubit at a time, using sparse parity checks, stabilizer equivalence, and verified symmetries to reduce the work. For a cutoff $W$, a completed search either finds a nontrivial logical operator of weight at most $W$ or proves that none exists. Because satisfying one check can violate another, we use both satisfied and unsatisfied checks to lower-bound the weight needed to complete a logical operator, and prune branches whose bound exceeds the remaining budget, which substantially reduces net search time. We benchmark QEDist mainly on Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes; the same formulation extends to non-CSS codes and to the fault distance of syndrome-extraction circuits. For lifted-product (LP) codes, we further exploit the product structure to replace part of the full-code search with a smaller search on a classical constituent. We establish exact distances for codes with up to several thousand qubits, including Abelian and non-Abelian LP codes whose distances were previously reported only as upper bounds. In several seconds of search on one laptop core, QEDist certifies exact distances up to 20 for many of these codes and fault distance 10 for the syndrome-extraction circuit of the $[[144,12,12]]$ code. With orders-of-magnitude speedups over the tested exact solvers, QEDist makes exact distance certification a practical tool for selecting and optimizing finite-length quantum codes.
papers.authors: Jong Yeon Lee

papers.title: The Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic PBC clusters
papers.abstract: We construct and solve the three-colored Kitaev model on finite hyperbolic lattices with periodic boundary conditions. We describe a self-contained procedure which uses finite quotients of orientation- preserving triangle groups to generate regular maps on compact genus-g surfaces. From these, one can extract their lattice connectivity, plaquette structure, homology cycles and Wilson sectors while implementing consistent boundary conditions. On the example of {8, 3} and {12, 3} lattices, we enumerate a selection of quotients with up to 72 vertices, which constitute the discrete steps in a finite-size scaling analysis. For the isotropic point, corresponding to the spin-liquid phase in the thermodynamic limit, we identify the ground state superselection sectors, quantify their deviation from the homogeneous {\pi} flux sector and show how the selected flux background depends on the quotient geometry. We then discuss how the resulting ground state sector degeneracies are entirely generated by physical lattice symmetries acting on both the plaquette fluxes and non-contractible Wilson loops. Finally, we study the behaviour of the finite-size two-vison gap and matter fermion correlations. We find that the gap does not decrease monotonically with increasing system size, while one still recovers the expected algebraic decay of the correlations at the isotropic point, even for the considered modest system sizes.
papers.authors: Alberto Zorzato, Jiri Min\'a\v{r}

papers.title: CSS circuits are ICM circuits without magic states
papers.abstract: Gidney and Jones recently introduced ``CSS circuits'', generated by $X$, $Z$, $\MX$, $\MZ$ and CNOT, and showed that they can be sampled with $O(1)$ work per gate. They suspected that the class had been seen before. We point out that it is, up to a normal form, the initialisation--CNOT--measurement (ICM) form introduced in 2015 for compiling fault-tolerant circuits, restricted to $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{+}$ initialisations. The ICM construction answers constructively their question about ``non-CSS-ness as a resource'': every Clifford$+T$ circuit compiles to a CSS circuit acting on $\ket{Y}$ and $\ket{A}$ input states.
papers.authors: Alexandru Paler

papers.title: Remark on internal relaxation in large number qubit systems
papers.abstract: For a time $t_{c}$ of calculation in an $N$ qubit quantum computer that is much shorter than the intrinsic Heisenberg time $t_H$, $t_c\ll t_H$, the dynamics of the system is effectively irreversible and the couplings between the qubits give rise to a relaxation time scale $\tau_r$. If $t_H\gg t_c >\sim \tau_r$ one looses quantum coherence exponentially fast. Since $t_H$ scales exponentially with $N$ there is a threshold $N_c$ such that for $N\gg N_c$ one must be aware of possible intrinsic relaxation during calculation. As an order of magnitude estimation we find $N_c\approx \ln(\tau_r/T)$ where $T$ is a typical system specific oscillation time of a single qubit. $\tau_r$ can be estimated as the typical inverse transition rate between two parts of the system, one of which is treated as an environment of the other.
papers.authors: Martin Jan{\ss}en

papers.title: Renormalization-Group Foundation of Critical Modes in Correlation Matrices
papers.abstract: Based on the relevant scaling operators of renormalization-group theory, we establish a theoretical framework for constructing complete families of critical-sensitive fluctuation observables and their connected correlation matrices. The corresponding eigenstates of the correlation matrices reveal a hierarchy of multiscale critical correlation patterns and the leading normalized eigenvalues and their ratios show the finite-size scaling behavior. Applying this framework to the two-dimensional Ising model, the correlation matrices associated with both spin and energy operators are constructed. The resulting energy-sector eigenstate patterns, together with the scaling behavior of the leading eigenvalues, provide further support for the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss its potential extension to systems with unknown Hamiltonians.
papers.authors: Yanhua Zhang, Mingmei Xu, Jinghua Fu, Yuanfang Wu

papers.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.
papers.authors: Omar Pedraza, Erik D\'iaz-Bautista, L. A. L\'opez, Daniel O-Campa

papers.title: New traversable wormholes without invoking exotic matter in $f(Q)$ from the freedom of different connections
papers.abstract: Wormhole solutions in General Relativity can only exist in the presence of exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. In this paper, we investigate the possibility of constructing wormhole solutions in $f(Q)$ gravity in which the extra connection degrees of freedom contribute such that no exotic matter is needed. Considering the Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole as an example, we find that the system admits two families of connections consistent with the spacetime symmetries and the requirements of symmetric teleparallel gravity. For both families, we show that constant non-metricity scalar $Q$ is not merely a simplifying assumption but arises naturally from the field equations when $f_{QQ}$ is regular, and that the resulting exact analytic solutions can satisfy the null energy condition throughout the entire spacetime. For the second family, which possesses richer connection degrees of freedom, we further demonstrate that solutions with a spatially varying $Q$ exist when $f_{QQ}$ is allowed to diverge at a finite value of $Q$, and that these too can satisfy the null energy condition everywhere. Our results show that the nontrivial connection degrees of freedom in $f(Q)$ gravity can naturally be responsible for supporting wormhole geometries, without resorting to any exotic matter.
papers.authors: Ismael Ayuso, Mariam Bouhmadi-L\'opez, Che-Yu Chen, Konstantinos Dialektopoulos

papers.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
papers.abstract: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.
papers.authors: Albert J. Wakhloo, Sebastian Mizera

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution. However, existing approaches largely focus on improving general measurement capabilities, often overlooking the structure of specific sensing tasks and leaving potential performance gains untapped. Here, we develop an algorithmic approach to quantum sensing tailored to various spectroscopic tasks, providing new avenues for improvement. Specifically, we consider general time-varying signals supported on a known set of $N$ candidate frequencies, a setting we call discrete-frequency spectroscopy. We formulate three types of practically motivated sensing tasks---Detection, Search, and Learning---that require progressively more spectral information. For all tasks, we design optimal quantum sensing algorithms achieving a $\sqrt{N}$ speedup over conventional frequency-scanning approaches. Optimal Detection and Search need only a single-qubit sensor under $\pi$-pulse control, whereas optimal Learning provably requires coherent processing with a quantum computer. End-to-end numerical simulations incorporating various experimental imperfections predict up to two-orders-of-magnitude speedup in Detection. As an example, we analyze the feasibility of our Detection and Search algorithms for real-world molecular screening based on state-of-the-art nitrogen-vacancy centers. We also show how quantum-computing-enhanced Learning enables wireless communication in a weak-signal regime where conventional methods fail. Our results establish a practical route toward realizing quantum advantages via designing task-specific sensing algorithms.
papers.authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Richard R. Allen, Ruohan Shen, Bingtian Ye, Timothy T. Chang, Joonhee Choi, Soonwon Choi

papers.title: Astrophysical Constraints for Bosonic Dark Matter in and Around Quark Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure, stability, and mass-radius relations of compact stars composed of quark matter within the non-ideal MIT Bag Model mixed with self-interacting bosonic dark matter with a $\phi^n$ self-interaction potential. By solving the coupled two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations for boson masses between 200 MeV and 1 GeV and self-interaction strengths with $n=4$ and $n=40$, we show that strong self-interactions and higher boson masses enhance the stability of compact star configurations at high central pressures, though they reduce maximum overall masses. Ultra-compact solutions with $C \ge 1/3$ capable of mimicking black holes are significantly restricted compared to hadronic models, emerging only for strong self-interactions and dark matter fractions exceeding 90\%. Depending on the parameters, the compact stars form either extended dark matter halos or compact cores: stronger self-interactions and higher boson masses suppress the radial extension to favor compact cores of dark matter. Matching our models against observational constraints highlights PSR J1614$-$2230 and XTE J1814$-$338 as potential window of opportunity for dark matter detection. Notably, XTE J1814$-$338 could confirm a dark sector, given its requirement for light boson masses ($m_b \approx 200\text{--}300\text{ MeV}$) and strongly DM-dominated configurations.
papers.authors: J\'ulia Tartera Barber\`a, Sarah Louisa Pitz, J\"urgen Schaffner-Bielich, Laura Tolos

papers.title: Lifting asymptotic symmetries from metric to tetrad formulation
papers.abstract: Metric solution spaces defined by gauge and boundary conditions are associated with a residual symmetry algebra, consisting of the diffeomorphism generators whose action preserves these conditions. Describing a metric solution space in terms of tetrad variables adds a local Lorentz freedom. When part of this freedom is fixed by additional tetrad gauge and boundary conditions, metric residual symmetries must be supplemented by compensating Lorentz transformations. If a residual Lorentz freedom remains, there is an ambiguity in these compensating transformations. The most direct choices generally fail to realize the metric residual symmetry algebra as a subalgebra of the tetrad one, because of a field-dependent cocycle. We show that a reference tetrad, that is a section of the tetrad solution space seen as a principal bundle over the metric one, always provides a lift free of this cocycle, so that the tetrad residual symmetry algebra is the semi-direct sum of the metric one and the ideal of field-dependent residual Lorentz transformations. The construction is independent of the gauge conditions, of the residual group, of the first-order Lagrangian, and reduces to the Kosmann lift on metric isometry generators. We illustrate it on a Weyl BMS-type solution space with time-dependent boundary metric, described in tetrad variables with a residual U(1) Lorentz freedom, for which the cocycle of a naive lift is computed and then explicitly removed.
papers.authors: Antoine Vincenti

papers.title: What kind of quantum advantage is this?
papers.abstract: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity. Evaluating these claims requires distinguishing how an algorithm achieves an advantage from what is necessary for the separation and how strongly it is supported against classical alternatives. We propose a multi-label taxonomy that makes these distinctions explicit, classifying structural, interference, and coherent mechanisms while separately recording their necessity and the evidence for the classical comparison. Coherent mechanisms are further divided into memory and output, reflecting distinct restrictions on quantum information processing. A two-part entanglement-breaking test distinguishes loss of information from loss of algorithmic efficiency. The hidden subgroup problem illustrates the distinction: among the cases examined, cross-copy coherence is information-theoretically necessary only for the symmetric group. We present this as a diagnostic methodology rather than a theory of quantum advantage: for a new claim, it identifies the relevant adversary, separates the mechanisms a protocol uses from those shown to be necessary, and records the strength of the evidence and the quality of the advantage separately.
papers.authors: Christophe Pere

papers.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.
papers.authors: David Krejcirik, Vladimir Lotoreichik

papers.title: Relaxing the i.i.d. state preparation assumption with the block QKD protocol
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a novel approach to handling the independent and identically distributed assumption for the state preparation in prepare-and measure QKD protocols. Contrary to previous approaches, we do not prove the security using sub-protocols, and instead opt to guarantee security in the presence of correlations by dividing the communication into finite blocks of consecutive pulses, and adding an additional assumption of no dependence between each block. In turn we obtain a protocol which uses only a relaxed i.i.d. assumption and is easier to implement than subprotocol-style approaches since it does not require separate statistics for each sub-protocol, whose number grows with the correlation length of the underlying dependency.
papers.authors: Olgierd \.Zurek, Hoi-Kwong Lo

papers.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,\Omega)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1\Omega^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.
papers.authors: Naichung Conan Leung, YuTung Yau, Zhenyu Ye

papers.title: Equivariant Localization with Electric Monodromy in M-theory
papers.abstract: We extend equivariant localization for supersymmetric AdS$_3$ backgrounds of M-theory to solutions with nonzero electric flux periods. The associated local electric potential acquires additive monodromy, contributing to the warped volume alongside R-symmetry fixed points and outer boundaries. Using Killing-spinor identities, we relate the electric periods to magnetic flux and, for a class of compact backgrounds, the warped volume to the electric Maxwell charge. We also derive a relation between the gravitational anomaly and the electric flux. We apply these results to AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times S^3 \times T^2$ and AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times K3 \times S^1$, recovering their central charges and deriving the R-current levels of the former directly from eleven-dimensional supergravity. Finally, we study a noncompact half-BPS AdS$_3$ $\times S^3\times S^3$ geometry fibered over a periodic half-cylinder, where fixed-point, monodromy and outer-boundary contributions coexist.
papers.authors: Ji-seong Chae

papers.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
papers.abstract: We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4\pi m,4\pi(m+1))\times(4\pi k,4\pi(k+1))$, then \[ \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k =(1-x)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-y)^{\chi(M)-1}(1-xy)^{\chi(M)}, \] where $\chi(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block. At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4\pi,0)$ and $(8\pi,4\pi)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.
papers.authors: Youngae Lee, Haoyu Li, Juncheng Wei, Wen Yang, Lei Zhang

papers.title: Transient Information in Moving-Mirror Quantum Correlations
papers.abstract: We study how a finite dynamical history remains encoded in a quantum field after a moving mirror returns to a common thermal trajectory. Two compact deformations of the Carlitz--Willey ray map are related by reversal of a control parameter and share the same asymptotic null line and Hawking temperature. The pairing induces an exact even--odd grading of the peeling field and Bogoliubov transformation. The complex continuum covariance retains the transient sign at first order, while the leading monochromatic quadratic response is even under reversal. Finite-bandwidth wave packets convert this distinction into signed interference with the thermal reference covariance. In linear response, the signed squared correlation is quartic in bandwidth for the selected right-moving packets and cubic for matched Rindler/Milne packets. The relative cross-covariance phase has a linear bandwidth dependence, with its leading coefficient maximized in magnitude by the flat window among normalized real symmetric windows. Finite-amplitude corrections introduce an additional linear bandwidth term in the squared Rindler/Milne response. The distinguishing packets sample the transient history in retarded time, while both trajectories share the same asymptotic Hawking temperature.
papers.authors: M. Baran \"Okten, Asl{\i} S. Turan, Michael R. R. Good, Kuan-Nan Lin, Pisin Chen

papers.title: Efficient Iterative Symmetrization algorithm for quantum computing and hadron applications
papers.abstract: Efficient algorithms for the (anti)symmetrization of quantum registers are necessary for upcoming few- and many-body physics applications, from atomic to particle-physics scales. We propose a recursive algorithm (anti)symmetrizing the last particle added to memory, each time one is created or destroyed, respect to the rest of already (anti)symmetrized ones. Given a generalized Dicke state (GDS) of $(j-1)$ quantum registers, each assigned to a particle, the algorithm produces another GDS of $j$ registers (of $n_{qb}$ qubits each) using a mere $\mathcal{O}(j\log_2^2 j + j n_{qb})$ $\mathtt{CNOT}$ and single-qubit gates, and $3j+\lceil\log_2j\rceil+\mathcal{O}(\max(n_{qb},\log_2 j))$ clean auxiliary qubits. The (anti)symmetrizing operator constructed for this purpose depends on the quantum numbers of the additional particle being introduced or ``created''. The algorithm improves upon the construction presented in Appendix A of \cite{Galvez-Viruet:2024hry} by almost two powers of $j$ and is on par with the most efficient methods to date, while ideally suited for dynamical memory management with variable particle number. We exemplify its applicability with a small selection of problems from hadron physics which are expected to be addressable with upcoming quantum computers.
papers.authors: Nahia J. Dios-Bilbao, Adri\'an Casta\~no-Garc\'ia, J. J. G\'alvez-Viruet, Felipe J. Llanes-Estrada, Mario Logros\'an-\'Alvarez, Nicol\'as M. Arenaza

papers.title: Complexity and symmetry: The asymmetry factor approach
papers.abstract: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing so we resort to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the existence of any specific type of symmetry (e.g. a TKV), exclusively, for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process shows the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. Particular attention is paid to the relationship appearing between the TKV, and the complexity factor describing the degree of complexity of the fluid, bringing out for the first time a link between complexity and symmetry.
papers.authors: L. Herrera

papers.title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
papers.abstract: We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants.
papers.authors: M. A. Zubkov

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].
papers.authors: David Krejcirik, Petr Siegl

papers.title: Landau Theory of Black Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.
papers.authors: Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Model-family selection and recovery-gate design in generator-based noise tomography
papers.abstract: Family selection in generator-model noise tomography is a hypothesis test whose shot floor has closed form under a purely coherent noise model, $N^{*}=\lambda_{\mathrm{req}}/(r_{\mathrm{b}} S)^{2}$: set by the absolute bias $r_{\mathrm{b}} S$, not the relative residual, and computable from a calibration alone. The same computation prices the recovery gates, fingerprint and Fisher information coming off the same map, so there is no design-independent verdict and no family-independent design optimum. Whether a design can move that price is structural: a bias confined to the block every design measures identically is design-blind, one that reaches the code blocks is repriced by a factor of sixty-eight---from a dominated design to the cheapest, not between two optima---and the two platforms studied here are its extremes. At the reference point the floor is $1.1\times10^{7}$ and $6.7\times10^{6}$ shots per component, the easy corner of the sampled working points, whose median floor is eighty-three times dearer in one direction and less than twice in the other; at the $10^{5}$ shots a run spends, the power equals the level and the residual reported is shot noise. The design problem is conditioning, not rank: across the sixty-four placements the rms varies by factors of $2.7$ and $3.9$, while the optimal gate count is flat at two to four. At five qubits the whole sample moves to $10^{9}$--$2\times10^{10}$ shots, a design spread of twenty-one against nine at three qubits; on a measured three-qubit register the floor is a requirement on systematic control before it is a shot count, and where that control is missing no budget supplies it.
papers.authors: Long Huang

papers.title: Landau-Ginzburg Theory of a Holographic Superconductor: A Horizon Perspective on the Zero-Temperature Ground State
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of a quartic scalar self-interaction, $\lambda|\phi|^4$, on a holographic superconductor in which non-linear electrodynamic couplings generate a superconducting dome containing an extended Lifshitz regime. The quartic interaction leaves the linearized scalar dynamics around the normal phase unchanged while modifying the non-linear solutions where the scalar field is large. As $\lambda$ increases, the solutions within the dome pass through three stages. The Lifshitz region shrinks until its scaling solution disappears at $\lambda^*$, leaving a no-AdS region, beyond whose edge the flows end before reaching any asymptotic region, and above $\lambda_c$ the dome consists entirely of asymptotically AdS hairy black holes. At the bottom of the dome we identify the point where the horizon value of the scalar field is largest, which we refer to as the critical point. There this value lies at the deepest symmetry-breaking minimum that the horizon effective potential, of Landau-Ginzburg form, can have. Unlike a conventional Landau-Ginzburg description, this interpretation rests on the scalar field at the horizon rather than on the boundary order parameter. Below $\lambda^*$, the constant scalar of the Lifshitz fixed point sits instead at the minimum of the effective potential of its asymptotic scaling region.
papers.authors: Sejin Kim, Yunseok Seo

papers.title: Information--control limits for record-indistinguishable reset of a monitored qubit
papers.abstract: A qubit that is continuously monitored from the moment it is prepared in its excited state writes evidence of that preparation into its measurement record. We ask how much control is needed to reset such a qubit to its ground state while keeping its complete record statistically close to the record of an undriven ground-state qubit. The qubit is measured in $\sigma_z$ at rate $\Gamma_m$ with efficiency $\eta$ and has no relaxation. For feedback that acts causally on the record, distinguishability is the Kullback--Leibler divergence $D$ of the controlled record law from the reference law, and the control cost is the quadratic effort $J$, the integrated squared Rabi frequency. We prove that every open-loop drive leaves $D$ infinite and that every admissible control obeys $DJ\ge\Gamma_mU(\eta,D/\kappa_0)$, where $U$ is given by a one-parameter family of integrals and $\kappa_0=1-\ln2$. Our main result is the exact high-effort constant $\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\inf\{DJ/\Gamma_m: D\le\epsilon\}=K(\eta)$, where $K(\eta)=[\int_0^\pi\sqrt{2\eta(1+\cos\theta)^2+(1-\eta)\sin^2\theta}\,d\theta]^2$; an explicit sequence of two-phase feedback policies attains it. The first term of the integrand is the population evidence that the record receives while the qubit is rotated toward the ground state. The second is the price of the impurity created when the unrecorded part of the measurement dephases the coherence that the rotation needs; the record receives this evidence later, when the measurement repurifies the qubit. The global constant $c(\eta)=\inf DJ/\Gamma_m$ satisfies $K/2\le F_2\le c\le K$, where $F_2$ is again given by an integral; $c$ is known exactly at $\eta=1$ and in the limit $\eta\to0$. With any nonzero relaxation rate the unconstrained infimum of $DJ$ vanishes, so $c(\eta)$ is specific to the relaxation-free model.
papers.authors: Sinan Bugu, Fatih Ozaydin

papers.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
papers.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordstr\"om black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.
papers.authors: Hyunwoo Oh

papers.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
papers.abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.
papers.authors: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima

papers.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
papers.abstract: Repetition-code process tomography compares the logical channel of a code with a reference channel through a decoder almost always the standard minimum-weight one. We ask how many physical single-qubit Pauli gates that decoder needs when the measurement basis is fixed---the constraint that makes the count a resource. Exhaustive enumeration at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$, each rank decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order decoding and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, not which, so the problem splits into a budget and a placement; the placement decides identifiability, and more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and under a calibration-residual floor the $n=3$ precision curve is U-shaped. The three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ working points and better at every one of them, by $1.8$ to $88$ times; with the placement fixed in advance the factor falls to $6.9$, or to $3.1$ for the pre-commitment never worse, both medians over the same $40$ points. Because the full advantage needs per-point placement, we also certify two placements in parallel: they lose no direction either sees and, wherever either is identifiable and the calibration floor permits, reach a $10$\,mrad target within twice the shots. The optimal designs are not covariant under chain reversal.
papers.authors: Long Huang

papers.title: Pohlmeyer reduction of Newton-Cartan strings
papers.abstract: We develop a Pohlmeyer-type reduction for classical non-relativistic strings on string Newton-Cartan backgrounds. For strings on a two-sphere, we identify the invariant reduced field, show that its dynamics is integrable, and construct a Lax representation. We relate this intrinsic formulation to the non-relativistic expansion of relativistic strings and obtain a dictionary between non-relativistic string solutions and their reduced counterparts. The construction explicitly determines which relativistic solitonic configurations survive the non-relativistic limit and which decouple. Moreover, it provides a framework for applying integrability methods to Newton-Cartan string dynamics.
papers.authors: Aritra Banerjee

papers.title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Simulating strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials remains a central goal for quantum computing. A promising strategy uses quantum processors to prepare trial wavefunctions that guide classical quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, the enormous computational cost of repeatedly processing quantum measurements has severely limited the practical scalability of this approach. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by compressing quantum measurement data into machine-learning models that efficiently provide the wavefunction overlaps needed by QMC. This accelerates quantum-classical QMC by orders of magnitude, enabling chemically accurate simulations on up to 40 qubits, more than doubling the scale of previous hardware demonstrations with comparable accuracy. We demonstrate our approach on hydrogen chains and strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters using measurements from Google's Willow processor. By enabling efficient reuse of quantum-state information on the classical coprocessor, our framework addresses a fundamental bottleneck in hybrid quantum algorithms that will persist even into the fault-tolerant era.
papers.authors: Tong Jiang, Andrew Zhao, Shashwat Kumar, Jigyasa Nigam, Eliott Rosenberg, Ryan Babbush, Andrew D. Baczewski, William J. Huggins, Joonho Lee

papers.title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
papers.abstract: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, such as the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and are found to vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital geometry provides a promising unified framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.
papers.authors: Poulami Mukherjee, Chandrasekhar Bhamidipati, Sudipta Mukherji

papers.title: Helium States Inspired by Quantum Photonics Circuit
papers.abstract: We present a four-mode Fock-state photonics implementation of the variational quantum deflation (VQD) algorithm to calculate the ground-state and excited-state energies for the neutral helium atom in a CAS(2,2) Subspace. Its CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space is encoded into a bosonic Fock-space representation and subsequently optimized using a continuous-variable quantum circuit. The circuit architecture under study is constructed of single-mode phase shifts, beam splitters, and cross-Kerr interactions. The variational circuit is initialized in the Fock state $\ket{1100}$ and its performance is benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the active-space configuration-interaction (CASCI) Hamiltonian. We also extend the method to optimize from the first to three excited states of the helium atom with the aid of the variational quantum deflation $(VQD)$ method in a CAS(2,2). We then investigate the performance of this circuit architecture as a basis for implementing the VQD method. In the ideal noiseless simulation setting, we see that the survival probability of the ground and the excited states within the target $CAS$ subspace is unity, because the total photon number and the photon number in the two spin sectors $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are preserved. We demonstrate that the proposed approach enables the determination of the ground and excited-state energies within the CAS(2,2) electronic Hilbert space using a continuous-variable quantum circuit and the variational quantum deflation ($VQD$) algorithm, while satisfying the orthogonality conditions with negligible errors.
papers.authors: Forouzan Mirmasoudi, Badie Ghavami

papers.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
papers.abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The period of wall domination is manifested in the spectral shape of gravitational waves via a distinctive plateau replacing a peak, which is characteristic for the scenario with sub-dominant walls. The gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.
papers.authors: Sabir Ramazanov, Zhen-Min Zeng

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
papers.abstract: We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $\rho$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2\pi\rho(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\rho} + o(\sqrt{\rho}))$ as $\rho \to 0$, and the condensate fraction $\eta$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $\eta = 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrt{\pi}}\sqrt{\rho} + o(\sqrt{\rho})$ as $\rho \to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,\chi_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.
papers.authors: Mohamed El Hedi Bahri, Ian Jauslin

papers.title: Regge bounds and eikonal estimates in scalar effective field theory
papers.abstract: Positivity bounds are derived from twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which hold only if the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partial\phi)^4/\Lambda^4$ and $g_6(\partial\phi)^6/\Lambda^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. Matching the two regions gives the phase-model growth $s^{8/7}$ for the quartic sector and $s^{16/15}$ for the sextic sector, while a transition scale fixed by the cutoff gives the conditional bound $s^{7/4}$; in the forward limit the same construction gives only the marginal growth $s^2$, so that Regge boundedness remains an assumption on the completion. Under this assumption the $2\to 2$ and $2\to 4$ absorptive parts below the cutoff restrict the couplings to $0<g_4\le 80\pi^2/7$ and $-7.2\times 10^5\lesssim g_6\lesssim 6.9\times 10^5$.
papers.authors: Ji Li

papers.title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
papers.abstract: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.
papers.authors: Mikhail Gradov, Aleksei Ilin

papers.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
papers.abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics.
