At fixed $\lambda$ and $\langle\omega^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\int\omega^n\alpha^2F d\omega$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\int\alpha^2F d\omega$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint. The finite-dimensional core, including that conjecture, is formalized in Lean 4, and two computer-assisted proofs independent of the comparison principle confirm the Einstein bound.
papers.authors: Davis Rens

papers.title: On the equivalence of three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff models to the classical CBS equation
papers.abstract: We examine the three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff (CBS) models introduced by Wazwaz, Alhejaili, and El-Tantawy [Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ Plus \textbf{141}, 1218 (2026)]. Explicit invertible point transformations map the first model, and generically the second, to the classical CBS equation. The third model is generically equivalent to CBS with an additional spectator coordinate absent from the differential operator. We identify the exceptional parameter regimes and explain the reported exponential dispersion relations through these transformations. These equivalences show that the proposed models do not, in the generic parameter regimes, introduce new point-inequivalent CBS equations or genuine four-variable differential coupling.
papers.authors: Manjit Singh

papers.title: Quantum geometric spectroscopy with Schr\"{o}dinger cat states
papers.abstract: We propose a spectroscopic approach that reads out the quantum geometry of matter from the quantum decoherence of Schr\"{o}dinger-cat light, in the same way that optical absorption reads out the energy structure of matter. For a cat-state probe comprising a superposition of two coherent states, the interbranch coherence of the outgoing light encodes the overlap between the matter states driven by the two branches. We show that, when the electromagnetic fields of the two branches differ only slightly, cat-branch decoherence is quantified by dynamical quantum geometry, which characterizes infinitesimal displacements on the matter-state manifold. For frequency-selective kitten probes of equilibrium matter, we further establish a partition law for the quantum geometric tensor between light and matter, enabling optical readout of matter quantum metric and Berry curvature through, for example, the brightening of a stellar zero in the outgoing Husimi function. For nonequilibrium matter in a pure state, short-pulse cat probes also provide a time-resolved witness of multipartite entanglement through the transient quantum metric, which can be extracted from homodyne measurements of the outgoing light. By turning cat-state decoherence, conventionally regarded as a loss of quantum information, into a carrier of information about matter, this approach establishes a spectroscopic principle that directly probes quantum-state geometry and fluctuations alongside conventional response-based spectroscopy.
papers.authors: Shohei Imai, Marcelo F. Ciappina

papers.title: Repeated Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Binary Black Holes on Eccentric and Precessing Orbits around Spinning Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) from a stellar-mass binary black hole (BBH) orbiting a supermassive black hole (SMBH) can experience repeated gravitational lensing as the BBH passes behind the SMBH. Our previous studies of orbit-induced GW modulation motivate this investigation of repeated lensing in evolving hierarchical triple systems. We investigate how eccentricity, inclination, and relativistic precession of the outer orbit affect successive lensing events and parameter inference. The outer orbit follows post-Newtonian dynamics, and the inspiral waveform includes moving-source effects and de Sitter precession. An event-local point-mass lensing model tracks the changing source--lens alignment and GW frequency. For a one-year LISA observation, we examine lensing-event identification, Fisher-matrix estimates of parameter uncertainties, and waveform residuals when lensing is omitted. Our results show that outer-orbit evolution changes the timing and amplification of successive lensing events and can bring initially unfavorable configurations into the lensing region. A fixed circular, nonprecessing approximation misses all lensing events for a substantial fraction of the selected lensed systems. The median fractional reductions in uncertainty are largest for the outer-orbit inclination and SMBH spin. For some systems above the adopted detection threshold, lensing-induced waveform differences persist after local adjustments to the parameters of the unlensed model. Repeated lensing can thus provide complementary constraints on SMBH properties and outer-orbit geometry in LISA observations of hierarchical BBHs.
papers.authors: Jie Wu, Mengfei Sun, Jin Li, Zhoujian Cao

papers.title: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware. Here we introduce Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes whose algebraic structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The construction jointly enforces stabilizer commutation and correct parallel syndrome extraction, while admitting radial and circumferential couplings in crossing-free routing layers. We construct explicit codes with rates above 1/2, stabilizer weight 12, Tanner-graph girth 6, and distances from 12 to 16, with layouts on 5 or 6 hardware tiers. Compared with the Gross and Mitten codes at the same distances, the Armillary codes achieve encoding rates about 6 and 2.5 times those of the Gross and Mitten codes, respectively, while maintaining lower hardware-complexity scores. In circuit-level simulations, the \([\![8688,4348,16]\!]\) code approaches the teraquop regime, achieving a logical error rate of \(1.62\times10^{-12}\) per logical qubit per round at a physical error rate of 0.1\%. These results show that the rate-\(1/2\) regime of qLDPC codes can be extended from reconfigurable platforms to superconducting hardware, providing a route toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum processors.
papers.authors: Jiaxuan Zhang, Zhao-Yun Chen, Jia-Ning Li, Tian-Hao Wei, Qing-Yang Hou, Wei-Cheng Kong, Yu-Chun Wu, Guo-Ping Guo

papers.title: Collective coupling of over 100 individually trapped atoms to a single cavity mode
papers.abstract: Coupling optical tweezer arrays to high-finesse cavities provides a shared optical interface for neutral-atom registers. Scaling this interface to large tweezer arrays requires placing many traps within the coupling region of a single cavity mode while maintaining uniform trapping and site-resolved detection. Here we match a two-dimensional array of 192 optical tweezers to the coupling profile of a millimeter-scale Fabry-Perot cavity. To improve trap uniformity in the array generated by crossed acousto-optic deflectors, we combine optimization with optical feedback and atomic fluorescence feedback, achieving a mean cesium loading probability of approximately 58%. In each trial, fluorescence imaging determines whether each individual tweezer site is occupied, allowing the cavity transmission spectra to be grouped by atom number. The grouped spectra exhibit resolved normal-mode doublets, and the group with 120 imaged atoms yields an effective collective coupling of $G_{\mathrm{eff}}/(2\pi) = 21.30 \pm 0.23$ MHz. A model based on the calculated coupling profile and measured site loading probabilities predicts that the mean squared coupling per occupied site changes little between 97 and 120 atoms. The fitted collective coupling is therefore consistent with square-root scaling with atom number despite the spatial variation in single-atom coupling. These results provide an experimental basis for studying photon-mediated many-body dynamics and developing cavity-assisted readout and optical links between neutral-atom registers.
papers.authors: Shijun Guan, Guansheng Teng, Zhiguo Huang, Zhihui Wang, Pengfei Yang, Pengfei Zhang, Gang Li, Tiancai Zhang

papers.title: Phase-conjugate Gaussian encoding for continuous-variable quantum key distribution with a single phase-sensitive amplifier
papers.abstract: Phase-conjugate encoding is naturally compatible with shared phase-sensitive amplification and joint detection, offering a compact optical receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD). Here, we develop a unified encoding and security framework for two-mode Gaussian CVQKD with tunable phase-conjugate intermode correlations matched to a joint receiver comprising a single phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) and one balanced photodetector. We present both coherent-state and squeezed-state prepare-and-measure protocols that use the same transmitted ensemble. The two preparations can be implemented through classically precoded Gaussian displacements of coherent sidebands or a directly generated two-mode squeezed vacuum, respectively, without an actual optical mode converter. The encoding and detection scheme separates low-variance joint quadratures for key generation from high-variance joint quadratures carrying private random modulation. This complementary modulation can reduce Eve's Holevo information without changing the Alice--Bob mutual information. Numerical results show that optimized correlated coherent-state encoding achieves higher asymptotic key rates at long distances and extends the positive-key range compared with optimized single-mode coherent-state modulation. The optimal intermode correlation increases with transmission distance, and the range advantage persists under the symmetric correlated two-mode Gaussian attacks considered here. These results provide a theoretical basis for the design and implementation of PSA-enhanced two-mode CVQKD with phase-conjugate encoding.
papers.authors: Zhenlin Zhao, Dawei Wang

papers.title: Lean-Verified No-Go Theorems for $R$-Symmetries and Modular Symmetries in 4D GUTs
papers.abstract: $R$-symmetries are instrumental in supersymmetric model building. However, a no-go theorem restricts us from using them in a large class of four-dimensional (4D) grand unified theories (GUTs). Specifically, it has been shown that a supersymmetric 4D GUT based on SU(5), with finitely many chiral multiplets, cannot be broken spontaneously to the exact minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) while preserving a discrete $\mathbb{Z}_M^R$, with $M \geq 3$, or continuous U(1) $R$-symmetry. We use Lean 4 to formalize this proof. In the process, we identify and close a gap in the general case of the published argument. Further, we discuss the implications for GUT models with modular symmetries. We point out that modular symmetries are inevitably $R$-symmetries in a supersymmetric framework that also describes gravity. At certain critical points in moduli space, discrete $R$-symmetries are linearly realized. In the context of 4D GUTs, the no-go theorem then implies that exotic states become massless at these points, provided the GUT-breaking vacuum preserves these symmetries. In the vicinity of these critical points, these exotics are parametrically light, which may spoil gauge coupling unification.
papers.authors: Mu-Chun Chen, Xiang-Gan Liu, Michael Ratz, Alexander Stewart

papers.title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
papers.abstract: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut. The eigenbasis is indexed by an $m$-tuple of partitions and an addable corner, whose content is the eigenvalue. We give an anti-normal factorization and prove that the Lax operator is self-adjoint for the transported Euler pairing. With unit framing weight, the rank-one specialization recovers the Nazarov-Sklyanin factorization. We then show that the Lax operator is conjugate to the companion matrix of a projected q-Miura operator of the deformed $W$-algebra of type $\mathfrak{gl}_m$. This also gives an explicit presentation of the $K$-theory of the Hecke correspondence.
papers.authors: Ryan Mickler

papers.title: Lower bounds for testing the completely depolarizing channel
papers.abstract: We study lower bounds to the query complexity of testing whether an unknown quantum channel mapping a $d_{\mathrm{in}}$-dimensional input to a $d_{\mathrm{out}}$-dimensional output is the completely depolarizing channel or is $\varepsilon$-far from it in diamond distance. We show that for this task (i) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, adaptive tester requires at least $\Omega(d_{\mathrm{in}}d_{\mathrm{out}}/\varepsilon^2)$ queries; (ii) any ancilla-assisted, coherent, non-adaptive tester requires at least $\max\{\Omega(d_{\mathrm{in}}^{1.5}d_{\mathrm{out}}/\varepsilon^2), \Omega(d_{\mathrm{in}}^{2}/\varepsilon^2)\}$ queries. We also show that these lower bounds apply to the more general problem of determining whether an unknown channel belongs to the set of all state-replacement channels or is $\varepsilon$-far from the entire set in diamond distance.
papers.authors: Hirak Ghosh, Andrew Jackson, Animesh Datta

papers.title: Triple Exchange at the Cosmological Collider in Closed Form
papers.abstract: Particles with masses near the Hubble scale leave a characteristic pattern in the primordial bispectrum, turning inflation into a cosmological collider. For light fields, where this signal is largest, no closed form is known for the full shape of the quasi-single-field triple exchange. Using Feynman-integral methods, we obtain the first closed-form results, exact in the momenta, as expansions in terms of multiple polylogarithms around the massless and conformally coupled limits. We show that the template used in Planck analyses overestimates the amplitude by up to a factor of 1.8 and underestimates the mass, whereas our new template recovers both, as needed for current and upcoming CMB and galaxy surveys. We also compute the collapsed trispectrum and, combining it with the bispectrum, find that at weak mixing it bounds the self-coupling more tightly.
papers.authors: Taushif Ahmed, Sumit Banik, Syed Mehedi Hasan, Andreas Rapakoulias

papers.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+\epsilon})$ gate cost
papers.abstract: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+\epsilon})$. Here $\epsilon>0$ depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a "policy" that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.
papers.authors: Anirudh Suresh, Joshua M. Courtney, Runzhou Tao, Yudong Cao

papers.title: Response-Threshold Framework for First-Peak Preservation in Noisy Grover Search
papers.abstract: Grover search is executed only after integer iterations, so noise can alter the stopping decision even when a continuous first peak remains visible. We develop a response-threshold framework separating continuous peak motion, stroboscopic geometry, and the discrete sampled-success argmax. For a Drude-Lorentz environment, linearized HEOM supplies an a priori timing coefficient and sampled-probability differentials. The first-order layer is used as a conservative screen: well-separated points retain the nominal step, whereas near-threshold points escalate to finite-$\lambda$ evaluation. Across 260 unique HEOM points drawn from five overlapping validation sets, it detects all 15 observed stopping changes with zero regret on the changed subset; its residual errors are 45 one-step-early calls on otherwise stable points; the 245-point stable subset has mean regret $4.42\times10^{-3}$. An empirically validated two-stage workflow escalates every observed change while avoiding 160 of 260 unique full-HEOM propagations. Same-bath NZ2 reduces early calls. A heterogeneous three-qubit circuit exhibits three stopping-transition scales, each replicated across eight marked targets, and finite-shot recovery is 96.18% overall, with failures localized to a near-degenerate boundary at $s=1.5$. A depth-refined transfer test supports the predicted local quadratic timing-to-loss relation.
papers.authors: Ge Zhong (Faculty of Information Technology, Monash University, Melbourne, Australia), Charith Jayasekara (Faculty of Information Technology, Monash University, Melbourne, Australia), Nisal De Silva (Faculty of Information Technology, Monash University, Melbourne, Australia), Chetan Arora (Faculty of Information Technology, Monash University, Melbourne, Australia)

papers.title: Ternary-Valued FDTD Method for Nonlinear Optics: Third-Harmonic Generation on a Multiplier-Free Solver
papers.abstract: I show that a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solver with field variables restricted to the ternary alphabet $\{-1,0,+1\}$ can reproduce nonlinear optical physics quantitatively on both CPUs and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Building on the general ternary-valued FDTD algorithm, in which each Yee cell stores an integer state that accumulates the discrete curl of neighbouring symbols without being drained, I extend the scheme to inhomogeneous and Kerr media and to Mur absorbing boundaries, without performing any multiplication operations. Dielectric contrast is implemented as a multiplexer, since the difference between ternary symbols takes only a few values, the instantaneous Kerr nonlinearity as a coefficient look-up table and the Mur boundary coefficients as canonical signed-digit shift--add chains. The scheme reproduces the third-harmonic conversion efficiency of a floating-point reference to within $1.4\%$. A symmetry of the governing physics, expressed through the even harmonics forbidden by centrosymmetric $\chi^{(3)}$, provides a reference-free self-check for both ternary and floating-point models. The complete solver fits on a small, low-cost FPGA and contains no multiplier anywhere in its datapath, placing nonlinear optical modelling within reach of embedded and autonomous platforms rather than of high-performance computers.
papers.authors: Ivan S. Maksymov

papers.title: Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.
papers.authors: Fil Simovic, Kenan Scavennec, David Kubiznak, Robert B. Mann

papers.title: Exceptional structure and Lifshitz criticality in a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain
papers.abstract: We study an exactly solvable non-Hermitian $N$-site Kitaev chain with unequal pair-creation and pair-annihilation amplitudes and vanishing intersite hopping. We show that the chain supports an exceptional point (EP) at which all the many-body energies collapse to zero and the largest Jordan block grows quadratically with $N$. By constructing an explicit positive metric for the associated $N$-dimensional one-body problem which admits an extension to the full many-body Hamiltonian, we demonstrate that this EP collapse can be approached through a continuous quasi-Hermitian path in the parameter space. Further, in a different regime with onsite energies alternating between two unequal positive values, we show that pairing amplitudes of opposite signs can lead to crossings between ground states of opposite fermion parity within a quasi-Hermitian regime. Their accumulation in the thermodynamic limit produces a Lifshitz transition, characterized by particle-/hole-pocket formation, quadratic critical dispersion, and a nonanalytic ground-state energy density. We show that this transition remains separated from the EP boundary and ceases to exist for balanced real pairing.
papers.authors: Aritra Ghosh, Akash Sinha, Miloslav Znojil

papers.title: Generalized Rotating-Wave Approximations Hierarchy for the Interacting Two-Qubit Rabi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate the two-qubit quantum Rabi model for identical qubits symmetrically coupled to a single bosonic mode and interacting with each other through transverse and longitudinal couplings. We extend the adiabatic, generalized rotating-wave (GRWA), and squeezed generalized rotating-wave (SGRWA) approximations to include the qubit-qubit interactions, including self-consistent and variational choices of the bosonic parameters. The resulting analytical hierarchy allows us to distinguish the interplay between both kinds of qubit-qubit interactions and the effects of displacement, neighboring-manifold mixing, and squeezing on the low-energy properties. We find that the transverse interaction mainly changes the collective-spin structure of the states, while the longitudinal interaction also modifies the displacement-dependent oscillator overlaps and introduces an additional two-boson coupling. We compare the analytical results with numerically exact diagonalization for the low-energy spectrum, ground-state energy, mean photon number, two-qubit concurrence, and spin correlations. The results provide a compact analytical description of how direct qubit-qubit interactions modify both the spectrum and the eigenstate structure beyond the rotating-wave approximation for few-qubit light-matter systems.
papers.authors: Ricardo Herrera Romero, Carlos Andr\'es Gonz\'alez-Guti\'errez, Miguel Angel Bastarrachea-Magnani

papers.title: Graph spectra and late-time concurrence in a lossy reservoir network
papers.abstract: We investigate how coupling the local environments of noninteracting qubits into a network changes their late-time entanglement dynamics. Each qubit interacts with a lossy bosonic memory mode, with coherent hopping between memory modes determined by an underlying graph. The initial state contains at most two excitations. We show that the graph spectrum selects the collective modes that survive longest, thereby controlling both the decay and spatial distribution of pair concurrence. At resonance, nonbipartite graphs generically approach a fixed pattern of relative concurrence determined by the Perron eigenvector, whereas bipartite graphs support interference between two equally damped modes. This interference can produce arbitrarily late entanglement revivals when it overcomes the exponential decay of the surviving modes. We derive explicit thresholds separating revival and eventual monotonic decay, and show that loss from two-excitation states can drive the system across these thresholds without changing the graph or the initial one-excitation state. Underlying these results is a general bound on the sector decay rates, $\gamma_2\ge2\gamma_1$, valid at arbitrary uniform detuning. We also identify an exceptional equal-rate regime in which coherence between the vacuum and two-excitation sectors contributes to the leading concurrence. Together, these results establish how the topology of a structured dissipative environment and the redistribution of excitations through loss determine the long-time behavior of entanglement.
papers.authors: Haoyuan Tian, Gourab Ghoshal

papers.title: Off-shell one-loop counterterms of Palatini gravity with an independent background connection
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop divergences of pure gravity in the first-order (Palatini) formulation, using the background field method in Goldberg variables, with a background connection independent of the background metric. Background Ward-Takahashi identities are verified at one loop. The divergences of the two-point functions, obtained in arbitrary dimension and gauge, require, besides the curvature-squared terms, invariants built from the nonmetricity of the background connection; in particular, the Gauss-Bonnet combination, which is not topological for a nonmetric connection, does not suffice. Three- and four-point functions in the Feynman-de Donder gauge complete the counterterm Lagrangian up to fourth order in the nonmetricity and provide parameter-free tests of it. All the counterterms vanish on shell, as in the metric formulation, and off shell they can be removed by field redefinitions.
papers.authors: F. T. Brandt, G. A. Menezes

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $\eta\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $\eta$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $\eta=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.
papers.authors: Boris Botvinnik

papers.title: Pre-amplification for Preserving Quantum Resources Through an Open-Air, Room-Temperature Microwave Channel
papers.abstract: We model a scenario where the pre-amplified signal mode of a two-mode squeezed vacuum (TMSV) state generated by a Josephson parametric converter (JPC) is transmitted through a room-temperature, open-air channel, while the idler is retained at low temperature. Before transmission, the state contains three quantum resources: (1) entanglement, (2) non-classicality, and (3) sub-vacuum conditional prediction of the signal quadrature. To preserve these resources through noise and loss, we consider two forms of quantum-limited pre-amplification of the signal mode: phase-preserving amplification (PPA) and phase-sensitive amplification (PSA). We identify three thresholds for a fixed amount of loss as noise increases from zero marking the loss of (1) entanglement, (2) non-classicality, and (3) sub-vacuum conditional prediction of the signal quadrature, respectively. We find first that entanglement is fatally sensitive to the noise and loss in our channel model and neither form of pre-amplification protects it. On the other hand, phase-sensitive pre-amplification is shown to significantly raise the thresholds at which non-classicality and sub-vacuum conditional prediction are destroyed. For a 3-meter link between room-temperature horn antennas at 5 GHz, the noise thresholds for these resources can be orders of magnitude above the thermal background. Further analysis shows that these conclusions are robust to limited phase misalignment and pre-amplifier-added noise, with the latter having the stronger effect. These surviving non-classical resources may support quantum-enhanced sensing, illumination, and metrology protocols even in regimes where entanglement itself is destroyed. Our results suggest that protocols that exploit these quantum phenomena are the most likely to succeed in microwave applications.
papers.authors: Jonathan N. Blakely, Drew S. Addison, Mark L. Adams

papers.title: feedback-grape: A JAX-based Python Package for GPU-Accelerated GRAPE with Feedback
papers.abstract: Modern quantum technology applications require accurate control of quantum systems, including a feedback loop in the control process. While open-loop control can be performed using well established gradient methods like GRadient Ascent Pulse Engineering (GRAPE), it was until recently unclear how to combine these with feedback from measurements, which are inherently non-differentiable. Recent work has successfully demonstrated how feedback can be incorporated into GRAPE using machine learning, resolving this issue. Following this progress, we have developed an efficient Python package implementing the method of ``feedback GRAPE''. In this hands-on tutorial, we discuss the package in detail based on concrete examples. Built on the GPU-accelerated JAX platform, our package offers a user-friendly interface inspired by the widely-used QuTiP library, including simplified treatment of multi-component systems.
papers.authors: Yousef Elbrolosy, Adrian Bories, Florian Marquardt, Pavlo Bilous

papers.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $\phi$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $\Delta_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.
papers.authors: Zhijin Li, Tinghong Shen

papers.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
papers.abstract: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.
papers.authors: David Wallace

papers.title: Energy and Radius Estimates for Molecules
papers.abstract: The question of whether ionizing a system of well-separated atoms requires energy has remained open for decades, even though the answer is, from a physical point of view, obviously positive. The analog question for a system of molecules is even more challenging, partly because the molecular geometry is not known a priori and may change when electrons are added or removed. In this work, we investigate and analytically solve the first problem in the special case of a mixture of hydrogen and helium atoms. As a consequence, the van der Waals law for a system of hydrogen and helium atoms, which was proven in [6] assuming our result, now follows as a corollary without assumptions. Moreover, we prove a new lower bound for the `size' of a stable molecule with several nuclei, which improves upon the lower bounds from [1] with even less assumptions. Using among others this lower bound, we prove that it costs energy to ionize a system consisting of an $H_2$ molecule and a perfectly conducting half-infinite plate, provided that they are well-separated. The long-range asymptotics of their interaction energy was analyzed in [3] assuming our result.
papers.authors: Ioannis Anapolitanos, Michael Hofacker

papers.title: Energy-flow bubbles at the Schwarzschild horizon and their Regge-pole clock
papers.abstract: For a circularly polarized plane wave scattered by a Schwarzschild black hole, the time-averaged energy flow on the side of the horizon facing the wave contains small, sealed recirculation cells. In the main family, pairs of zero circles are born on the axis and slide into the horizon in periodic frequency windows; at higher frequencies further cells appear off the axis. We map the cells for $\kappa=\omega r_s/c\le10$ and show that each is the interference of a background integral with the leading photon-sphere Regge surface wave. A cell can die only at a zero of the circularly polarized field on the horizon, and all sixteen measured deaths are such zeros. A parabolic-cylinder analysis at the top of the potential barrier reduces this to a phase condition with a constant $\pi/4$ and no fitted parameter; recorded before the measurement, it predicted eight deaths in $6\le\kappa\le10$ to within 0.012 in $\kappa$. Electromagnetic duality makes the core of each main-family cell a circle of linear polarization; inside such a cell, flow lines lie on nested tori and close into torus knots of one chirality.
papers.authors: Maciej Janowicz, Arkadiusz Or{\l}owski

papers.title: Quantum-Enhanced Passive and Active Radio-Frequency Photonic Imaging
papers.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) photonics enables broadband, phase-coherent sensing beyond the reach of purely electronic architectures, yet at a given optical carrier power its sensitivity is bounded by the standard quantum limit of the optical readout. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that this limit can be surpassed in both passive and active RF imaging modalities by encoding RF signals onto a bright phase-squeezed optical carrier and recovering them via balanced homodyne detection, while the RF front end, illumination, and image reconstruction remain classical. A unified measurement model shows that phase squeezing reduces the variance of the additive readout noise by a single factor $g$, yielding peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) gains of up to $2G$, where $G\equiv10\log_{10}(1/g)$: between $G$ and $2G$ for deterministic targets in active imaging when the classical noise of the echoes is negligible against the readout noise, and set by the ratio of scene noise to readout noise in passive imaging. We validate the model in an experiment in the 5--20 MHz band, in which synthesized RF scenes are replayed through a physical squeezed-light receiver. With 3 dB of squeezing, the PSNR improves by about 6 dB, close to $2G$, in the readout-noise-dominated regime of both modalities, and the model predicts the measured gains without free parameters. These results identify where squeezed-light readout benefits RF-photonic imaging: wherever the optical readout noise, rather than the scene or the RF front end, dominates the image error.
papers.authors: Visuttha Manthamkarn, Haowei Shi, Shuaifeng Guo, Christopher M. Jones, Quntao Zhuang, Zheshen Zhang

papers.title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
papers.abstract: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Yu Gao, Jiayu Qiu

papers.title: Two categorifications of the Kekul\'e relations
papers.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelul\'e relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.
papers.authors: Jernej Grlj, Ziyi Lei, Emmanuel Wagner

papers.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
papers.abstract: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.
papers.authors: Kohei Fukai

papers.title: Radar Waveform Design via Convex Semidefinite Relaxation
papers.abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) of a radar waveform describes its ability to resolve targets in range and Doppler. Designing a waveform that attains a prescribed AF magnitude is a phase retrieval problem with four trivial ambiguities, and a time- or band-limited pulse is determined up to these ambiguities by at most three times as many AF samples as it has time samples or frequencies. Existing solvers for the narrowband AF, however, are non-convex: they cannot guarantee that they reach the global minimizer, which is unique only up to the trivial ambiguities, so the recovered pulse depends on the starting point. This letter addresses this gap by lifting the problem to positive semidefinite matrices supported on the pulse band, where each AF sample becomes the magnitude of a linear functional. In the lifted space, recovery is formulated as a convex program, and a dual certificate provides a sufficient condition for exactness. The proposed algorithm, wavex, combines an initialization by relaxed reflections, convex semidefinite surrogate steps, and a local polish. Numerical experiments show that wavex accurately recovers band-limited pulses from complete AFs and from AFs with most of their samples removed, provided the remaining samples determine the pulse, and that its accuracy degrades gracefully as the noise increases. wavex is built on the open-source library invexapi, and the code that reproduces every result is available at https://github.com/samuelpinilla/waveX.
papers.authors: Samuel Pinilla

papers.title: Casimir-like wormholes
papers.abstract: We investigate spherically symmetric spacetimes sourced by matter with energy density $\rho \propto 1/r^{4}$ and equation of state $p_r = \omega \rho$. We derive the most general solution of Einstein's equations for this class of sources, obtaining black holes, naked singularities and traversable wormholes, parametrized by the integration constants and $\omega$. We show that only two classes of matter can support traversable wormholes: Casimir-type matter with $\omega > 0$ and phantom matter with $\omega < -1$, while quintessence and conventional dark energy are excluded by the flare-out condition. For the Casimir value $\omega = 3$, the transverse pressure approaches $p_t \to -\rho$ near the central singularity, so the full algebraic structure of the Casimir stress-energy tensor, $\rho \propto -1/r^{4}$, $p_r = 3\rho$, $p_t = -\rho$, is not imposed but emerges from Einstein's equations. Treating the amplitude of the energy density as a free classical parameter, we obtain wormholes with throat radii from microscopic to astrophysical scales. These Casimir-like configurations share the functional form of the Casimir tensor but are not generated by the physical Casimir effect; Garattini's Planck-scale Casimir wormhole is recovered when the quantum Casimir energy scale is imposed. The total amount of exotic matter is finite for arbitrary $\omega$ and scales linearly with the throat radius. Analyzing the traveler's acceleration, tidal forces and transit times, we show that radial free fall satisfies all human traversability conditions for $r_0 \gtrsim 10^{8}$ m. Finally, embedding diagrams illustrate three geometric regimes depending on $\omega$.
papers.authors: Mauricio Cataldo

papers.title: On Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes in Square-Root Nonlinear Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Inspired by exponential Maxwell models, we propose a new black hole solution in square root nonlinear electrodynamics. Using the analogy between black hole mechanics and thermodynamics, we investigate the corresponding stability, the P-v criticality and the phase transitions. As a result, we find that the obtained black hole exhibits Van der Waals behaviors without additional corrections which typically appear in universal ratio computations.
papers.authors: A. Belhaj, S. E. Ennadifi, M. Jemri, M. Nach

papers.title: Mixed-state topological transitions with hidden long-range correlations
papers.abstract: We study a decoherence-driven transition from a one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological state to a trivial product state. The decoherence acts onsite while preserving the protecting symmetry on average. Although conventional local correlations remain short-ranged across the transition, we uncover hidden nondecaying long-range correlations in a symmetry-twisted ensemble that weights states according to their symmetry charge. At the transition, the twisted correlation length diverges and the twisted partition function becomes singular. These signatures can be directly extracted from symmetry-resolved measurement outcomes, making the hidden critical behavior accessible on current quantum platforms at mesoscopic system sizes. We demonstrate this through numerical simulations of the measurement process.
papers.authors: Ze-Min Huang, Frank Pollmann, Sebastian Diehl

papers.title: Generative Models using Multi-layer Quantum Extreme Learning Machines
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) and the closely related quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) paradigm exploit the complex dynamics of an uncontrolled quantum system for machine learning, offering an alternative to variational quantum algorithms whose training is hindered by barren plateaus and costly circuit optimization. Because the quantum system itself is left fixed, learning reduces to fitting a linear readout of a set of measured observables, and no gradient is ever taken through the quantum device. In this work we repurpose this paradigm for generative modeling: a fixed, randomly initialized multi-layer QELM transforms a scalar latent variable into a rich vector of measured expectation values, and only a simple linear readout is trained to map these to samples of a target distribution. The readout is fitted by minimizing the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between generated and target samples. We show that this algorithm is capable of reproducing a range of one- and two-dimensional distributions. Moreover, encoding the class label on dedicated qubits enables conditional generation of different classes of distributions with the same linear readout. We show that this cannot be achieved by the linear readout alone, and that the reservoir dynamics play a role in the ability to distinguish the different classes of distributions. We also show that using a simple six-qubit reservoir one is able to generate handwritten digits from the Digits and MNIST datasets with high accuracy. Moreover, replacing the Haar-random dynamics by time evolution under several physical Hamiltonians leaves the performance unchanged, provided the evolution spreads the input across the register. Finally, we show that a classical random Fourier feature model of the same size performs equally well: at the sizes we study, the QELM offers no advantage over its classical counterpart.
papers.authors: Amir Azzam, M. Pilar Casado, Michele Grossi, Arnau Riera, Sofia Vallecorsa

papers.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
papers.abstract: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.
papers.authors: Ahmed Gamal, Yasutaka Wada, Walid Gomaa, Norhan El-Sayed, Keiji Kimura, Salem F. Hegazy, Kazunori Ueda, Ahmed El-Mahdy

papers.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
papers.abstract: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying L\"uscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.
papers.authors: Zhiyao Lu, Shu-Heng Shao

papers.title: Readout errors limit how far adaptive quantum circuits can entangle
papers.abstract: Measurement and feedforward let quantum circuits entangle arbitrarily distant qubits in constant depth if measurement records are perfect and classical communication is instantaneous. We allow each reported bit to flip independently with a fixed probability between zero and one half, keeping all gates ideal. Consider a square-lattice device with a unique path between the endpoints and a bounded number of qubits per site. Beyond $\exp[O(D^3)]$ steps along that path, every depth-$D$ circuit starting from a product state leaves the endpoints exactly separable in every record, however rare. By copying outcomes onto spare qubits beside the path before readout, we attain a reach of $\exp[\Theta(D^3)]$ for a nondestructive parity measurement at fixed accuracy without postselection. On a one-dimensional chain, the optimal reach for the same measurement is $\exp[\Theta(D^2)]$. On any interaction graph, a constant-depth circuit starting from a product state needs $\Omega(L\ln L)$ qubits to entangle endpoints at graph distance $L$. The reliability of local readout thus limits the depth advantage of adaptive circuits for long-range entanglement.
papers.authors: Chenfeng Cao, Ruge Lin

papers.title: Imperfect Cavities Select Better: Enantioselectivity Beyond Pure Helicity
papers.abstract: Single-handed light appears ideally suited to select a preferred handedness of matter. For chiral molecules in a cavity, we show that this intuition fails. Hybridization of light and matter reshapes the optical resonance through a self-energy that mixes opposite helicities. As a result, the difference in power absorbed by opposite enantiomers is generically maximized by light of mixed, rather than pure, helicity. We clarify why chiral selection admits such mixed-helicity optima in more general light--matter systems. For a concrete set of cavity modes, we find that molecular localization at a weak helicity bias considerably outperforms helically pure designs, thus identifying spatial control as a promising design direction for devices previously thought to be ``imperfect''.
papers.authors: David Dams, Karolina S\l{}owik

papers.title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
papers.abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.
papers.authors: Rinat Kashaev

papers.title: Hardware-Aware Realization of Deterministic Quantum-Walk Search on Complete Bipartite Graphs
papers.abstract: Complete bipartite graphs offer a canonical platform for deterministic quantum search with quadratic speedup. We report the first experimental realization of deterministic discrete-time quantum-walk search over complete bipartite graphs, enabled by high-fidelity operations and a dynamical-phase compensation scheme, using a digital gate-based processor rather than an evolution-based platform. By compiling the search circuits to the native gate set and square-lattice topology, we implement full-space encoding to realize instances of graph sizes $N = 4$ and $8$, with success probabilities of 97.6% and 70.8% for finding the marked vertex, respectively. We also realize resource-efficient exact instances up to size $N = 16$, the largest achieving 66% success probability. Separately, a reduced invariant-subspace encoding preserves the dynamics of the deterministic search algorithm on two qubits for nominal problem sizes up to $N = 256$, with the success probability approaching 50%. Resource analyses of logical, hardware-compiled, and fault-tolerant-gate-set-synthesized circuits show that circuit depth and size scale as $\sqrt{N}$, with hardware overheads entering only as constant prefactors. For application-scale graphs ($N \sim 10^5$), an effective gate-fidelity model requires per-gate infidelity near $10^{-7}$. These results establish a concrete algorithm-to-hardware pathway for deterministic structured quantum search on gate-based quantum processors.
papers.authors: Tao Rong, Meng Li, Xin Tong, Jianbin Cai, Yu Li, Naibin Zhou, Shaowei Li, Sirui Cao, Yuan Li, Yu Xu, Fusheng Chen, Ming Gong, Xiaoming Sun, Chen Zha

papers.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong \int^{M} M \otimes M^\prime, \] where $M$ ranges over restricted $V$-modules. Finally, the connection between $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ and the regular representation $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$ constructed in \cite{Li02} is established, where $\xi \in \C^{\times}$. In particular, if $V$ is a $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra and $W$ is a restricted $V$-module, then $\mathcal{R}(W^\prime)$ is also a restricted $V \otimes V$-module and is canonically isomorphic to $\mathfrak{D}_{\xi}(W)$.
papers.authors: Xu Gao, Chao Yang

papers.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
papers.abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.
papers.authors: Konrad Walus

papers.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$. Unlike the case of ordinary $q$-Schur algebras, the submatrix formed by taking the row index set to be the same as the column index set need not be invertible. We determine that the row index set should be chosen as $H_{\min\{m,n\},\max\{m,n\}}(r)$ for $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$, and as the preimage of $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ under the Glaisher correspondence for $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$.
papers.authors: Li Luo, Senlei Yu

papers.title: Probing superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational wave observations
papers.abstract: We investigate superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations. Under the adopted cloud formation and survival conditions, the $\lvert322\rangle\rightarrow\lvert31-1\rangle$ fine transition can imprint phase corrections in the LISA band, while Bohr transitions occurring after the milli-Hertz band observation can be probed through shifts in the merger time. Modeling the coupled cloud-orbit evolution, we find that cloud depletion can begin before resonance and that ionization can advance rather than delay coalescence. For a representative nearby binary, a vacuum injection-recovery analysis yields a cloud-mass-fraction posterior concentrated at $M_c^i/M\lesssim10^{-6}$. Comparing the LISA-predicted coalescence time with a subsequent ground-based measurement provides a complementary test of later cloud evolution. These results motivate complementary searches for ultralight bosons with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations.
papers.authors: Si-Tong Peng, Anson Chen, Si-Yang Pu, Jun Zhang

papers.title: Efficient AOD-Transport Compilation for Neutral-Atom Arrays
papers.abstract: Neutral-atom quantum computers execute two-qubit gates by shuttling atoms between storage and entanglement zones with acousto-optic deflectors (AODs). The efficiency of these movements determines circuit fidelity via transport overhead, idle-atom crosstalk, and atom-transfer errors. Additionally, AOD hardware constraints limit parallel atom movements, so efficient qubit placement and routing are essential. We present NEAT (Neutral-atom Efficient AOD-Transport compiler). Its transport-informed placement evaluates each decision by its incremental equivalent time, a single cost combining transport time, atom-transfer loss, and crosstalk. Its partial-progress routing allows conflicting moves to advance concurrently via intermediate waypoints. NEAT also schedules gates to maximize parallelism and uses a staggered atom array whose trap geometry preemptively avoids AOD violations without extra moves. On standard benchmark circuits, NEAT outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) compilers in fidelity, circuit duration, and compilation time. On scalability benchmarks of up to 1,000 qubits, it shortens circuits by 1.9x, reduces the negative log-fidelity by 1.5x, and compiles 6.6x faster than SOTA compilers on average. Overall, NEAT is a lightweight yet effective compiler for efficient and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing. The code is available at https://github.com/HaydnCheng77/NEAT.
papers.authors: Haydn Cheng, Zhiding Liang

papers.title: Unstable Periodic Orbit Localization in a Nonlinear System-Environment Model
papers.abstract: The role of unstable periodic orbits (UPOs) is investigated in the chaotic dynamics of a nonlinear system-environment model composed of a central two-level system coupled to an environment of two-level systems. Families of UPOs embedded in chaotic regions are identified and their local instability is characterized. Their behavior is examined under variations of the environment size, energy, and system symmetry, allowing the model to serve as a controlled testbed in which the dimensionality and dynamical conditions can be systematically modified. Characteristic UPO-based dynamical quantities are used to assess the influence of these periodic orbits on nearby chaotic trajectories, including occupation of the UPO tube, its persistence at late times, return fidelity enhancement, and recurrence timing. Across the different model variations considered, trajectories initialized close to the UPOs retain statistically detectable spatial and temporal signatures associated with the periodic orbits. These results indicate that unstable periodic orbits can retain a measurable organizing influence on surrounding chaotic trajectories across changes in dimensionality, energy, and system symmetry, giving rise to scar-like dynamical signatures in a simple nonlinear system--environment model.
papers.authors: Daniel Martinez-Gil

papers.title: Pulse-timing errors in exchange-only spin qubits: how one control imperfection propagates to VQE, QAOA and fault-tolerance primitives
papers.abstract: In an exchange-only (EO) spin qubit every gate is a sequence of Heisenberg exchange pulses whose only continuous parameter is the pulse area. We ask how an error in that area propagates to an algorithm's result. On up to six encoded qubits we compile VQE for H$_2$ and LiH, QAOA MaxCut, Grover search, phase estimation and a distance-3 repetition code into exchange pulses and perturb every pulse with a systematic fractional error $\varepsilon$, an offset or per-pulse jitter. For circuits whose first-order response is negligible at the threshold, the useful regime ends at $\varepsilon$ of a few $10^{-3}$: chemical accuracy is lost at $\approx6\times10^{-3}$ for both molecules and 5% of success probability between 3 and $9\times10^{-3}$ for 498-1216 pulses. A systematic error accumulates as the square of the depth and biases the answer; jitter accumulates linearly and, within statistics, does not bias phase estimation. Leakage from inter-block pulses is a third of the CNOT error, survives variational re-optimisation and a leakage-controlled entangler, and makes a leakage-blind repetition-code round worse than its uncorrected data by a factor 38-93 at $\varepsilon=10^{-2}$ in three of four compilations; in the fourth the uncorrected data already fail. The compilation moves the thresholds by a factor of two to eight. Measured over-rotation and exchange noise put devices at the edge of this regime, and with the measured 3.5 $\mu$s $T_2^*$ a quasi-static magnetic gradient limits thousand-pulse circuits unless $J/h$ reaches several hundred MHz with continuous areas, because a duration grid of 2-5% of the SWAP time starts to cost chemical accuracy. As a bit budget, a common-mode area error needs 8-10 significant bits and a 6-bit significand for the durations suffices in the tested circuits; half-precision words and picosecond timers exceed this; older devices had 6-8 bits of analog stability.
papers.authors: Yuichiro Minato

papers.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
papers.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. These results constitute a step forward in practical implementations of quantum teleportation in future fiber-based quantum networks.
papers.authors: Raphael Joos, Michelle Pfahl, Ponraj Vijayan, Michal Vyvlecka, Michael Jetter, Simone L. Portalupi, Peter Michler

papers.title: Neumann zero modes and the locality of the derivative expansion
papers.abstract: The derivative expansion (DE) provides a useful approximation to the Casimir interaction energy between two close surfaces. It has the form of a local functional, obtained from a zero momentum expansion. However, when the system involves a massless field satisfying Neumann conditions, that expansion may develop nonanalytic terms. We present here a study on how this property reflects itself in the need to add to the DE some novel, nonlocal terms. These are, we argue, akin to the ones introduced in effective theories because of the presence of massless particles in loops. We pinpoint the mode responsible for this effect, and construct the effective action due to its fluctuations, showing that it reproduces known nonanalytic contributions, and present the corresponding nonlocal addition to the DE. We also predict a new nonanalyticity: Neumann conditions in $3+1$ dimensions at zero temperature produce a term of order $|{\mathbf k}_\shortparallel |^3$, with a parameter-free coefficient, between the (local) second and fourth orders of the expansion. We show that, for a cylinder in front of a plane, the zero-mode loop adds to the local expansion a term of relative order $(L/R)^{3/2}$, with a coefficient that we compute explicitly, showing that it accounts for the behaviour of the existing numerical fits for that geometry.
papers.authors: C. D. Fosco, F. D. Mazzitelli

papers.title: Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
papers.abstract: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.
papers.authors: Sven Krippendorf, Magdalena Larfors, Zhimei Liu, Andreas Schachner, Moritz Walden

papers.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
papers.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.
papers.authors: Kazuhiro Hikami

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
papers.abstract: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $\Lambda=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $\Lambda=0$. For $\Lambda=0$, sixth order WKB values with Pad\'e resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $\beta$ raises both. In our convention $\beta>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $\beta$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $\Lambda<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.
papers.authors: Semra Gurtas Dogan, Abdullah Guvendi, Hassan Hassanabadi

papers.title: Deterministic preparation of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states with arbitrary size and squeezing
papers.abstract: We introduce a scheme for the deterministic preparation of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states based on reservoir engineering. Our proposal relies on the linear and quadratic coupling of an oscillator mode to an auxiliary mode that decays into a vacuum reservoir. For suitable couplings, we show that the system unconditionally relaxes into a pure steady state. We derive an analytical expression for the steady state in terms of the coupling constants, and show that it corresponds to a displaced and squeezed finite superposition of Fock states. Numerical simulations further confirms that this state is reached with unit fidelity from a thermal initial state, without measurement, feedback or post-selection. Additionally, we derive analytical expressions for the non-Gaussianity and the Wigner function of the steady state. Our results reveal that states exhibiting maximal non-Gaussianity are excellent approximations of squeezed Schr\"odinger cat states, with fidelities exceeding $0.996$. The optimal squeezing stays close to 3dB, while the squared cat size scales proportionally with the highest Fock state occupation number in the finite superposition of the steady state. These maximally non-Gaussian states also maximise the Wigner logarithmic negativity. Finally, by selecting the appropriate ratios of the couplings, our scheme can generate cat states subject to arbitrary squeezing and displacement.
papers.authors: Oussama Houhou, Hamza Adnane

papers.title: Bowed-String-Mechanism-Inspired Quantum Dissociation Control of Molecules
papers.abstract: Inspired by Guettler's mechanics of accelerating Helmholtz motion, we present a predictive laser pulse-shaping strategy to rapidly initiate the multiphoton dissociation of vibrationally excited diatomic molecules. In intense infrared fields, NO molecules often exhibit unpredictable control windows due to the chaotic fragmentation of intensity thresholds. By incorporating a bowing-analogue transient shaper enforced by a boundary-matching constraint with symmetric derivative slope transitions and vanishing initial boundary conditions ($T(0) = 0, T'(0) = 0$), we demonstrate that a pulse engineered with non-linear front-flank acceleration reduces the multi-valued threshold topology into a single, predictable linear dissociation corridor. Wigner quasiprobability distributions confirm that this temporal acceleration trajectory opens cantori bottlenecks and suppresses wave-packet fragmentation, restricting the quantum non-classicality index to $M_{\text{nc}} \le 0.15$. Our simulations verify that this trajectory engineering preserves wave-packet localization and maintains high dissociation yields ($P_{\text{diss}} > 0.95$) even under Markovian thermal dephasing ($\delta/\omega_0 = 10^{-4}$) and frozen rotational variations up to $J = 5$. Comparison with contemporary ultrafast spectral phase modulation protocols demonstrates that conventional smooth pulse envelopes, despite advanced phase-chirping, exhibit limitations in restricting non-hyperbolic cantori stickiness due to insufficient sub-picosecond acceleration. In contrast, our boundary-constrained shaper enforces a deterministic, single-valued dissociation corridor under equivalent few-picosecond control windows.
papers.authors: Julian Juhi-Lian Ting

papers.title: A hybrid log-likelihood-ratio statistic for single-detector SPIIR gravitational-wave searches
papers.abstract: Periods with only one detector operating accounted for 13.3 percent of the third LIGO-Virgo observing run (O3) and 29.7 percent of the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a). We present the first dedicated single-detector implementation of the Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) merger searches. Our hybrid log-likelihood ratio combines signal-consistency models for non-Gaussian glitches with a profile likelihood ratio for the signal-to-noise ratio under a Gaussian-noise model. We calibrate the glitch model by source category and trigger-rate class. We assign false alarm rates (FARs) using the measured background from the same detector and analysis chunk, extrapolating its high-ranking tail. We check the FAR assignments by comparing observed and expected cumulative background counts for BNS in O3a and NSBH in O3b at LIGO Hanford (H1) and LIGO Livingston (L1). Using O3 data and the GWTC-3 injection set, we find that, at a threshold of one false alarm per two months, the BNS sensitive distances are $136.5^{+2.9}_{-3.0}$ Mpc in L1 and $120.2^{+3.1}_{-3.3}$ Mpc in H1. These central estimates are approximately 24 and 38 percent higher, respectively, than the GWTC-3 GstLAL values of $110.5^{+3.2}_{-3.4}$ Mpc and $87.2^{+3.6}_{-3.9}$ Mpc over the same data and injection parameter ranges. GstLAL provides the only published single-detector results in GWTC-3. For NSBH, SPIIR reaches $164.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc in L1 and $134.9^{+6.3}_{-7.0}$ Mpc in H1, compared with $165.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc and $156.0^{+5.9}_{-6.4}$ Mpc for GWTC-3 GstLAL, respectively. Targeted searches recover triggers associated with GW190425, GW200105_162426, and GW230529_181500 with assigned FARs below the same threshold.
papers.authors: SPIIR Collaboration, Weichangfeng Guo, Sunil Choudhary, Victor Oloworaran, Linqing Wen, Jayden Doan, Qingyuan Liang, Tim Davies, Luke Davis, Irina Dvorkin, Apratim Ganguly, Shang-Jie Jin, JeongCho Kim, Yu-Chiung Lin, Ngai-Chun Lung, Alistair McLeod, Khun Sang Phukon, Andreas Wicenec

papers.title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
papers.abstract: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.
papers.authors: Xiuwen Zhang, Jia-Xin Xiong, Alex Zunger

papers.title: On $\iota$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
papers.abstract: We consider the $\iota$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A.
