papers.title: Coxeter Rigidity and ADE Classification of Fibonacci-Generated Tensor Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a program to classify tensor categories generated by prescribed seed tensor categories. We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\mathbb{C}$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.
papers.authors: Huixuan He, Zhengwei Liu

papers.title: Distilling Knowledge from Search: Decoder Model Factory for Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: We introduce GraphMP, a learning-based message-passing decoder for quantum low-density parity-check codes that transfers without fine-tuning across code families, code sizes, physical error rates, and noise models. Its local message passing keeps computation scalable as the decoding graph grows. We further embed GraphMP in a beam-search algorithm that progressively refines candidate error patterns, trading additional decoding time for lower logical error rates. To turn this decoding effort into lasting improvements, we propose the decoder model factory, a paradigm for training successive models on data collected by earlier models during decoding. In our implementation, verified search trajectories provide reusable training data for distilling knowledge into subsequent models. Across generations, the model factory yields a search-enhanced decoder that is broadly competitive with Relay-BP. On the largest code block, which encodes $4612$ logical qubits, it achieves a lower logical error rate and about $20$ times the decoding throughput of the standard Relay-BP baseline. These results motivate a coupled quantum-classical architecture with two interacting cycles: rapid decoding protects quantum information, while slower learning adapts the models to changing noise conditions. The long-term vision is a scalable decoder model factory that continually produces high-performance, low-latency decoders for evolving quantum hardware.
papers.authors: Anil Bilgin, Wanda Hou, Pranav Srinivas Murali, Yi-Zhuang You

papers.title: Universal quantum control in biorthogonal framework
papers.abstract: As a paradigm for describing the open-quantum-system dynamics, the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation generally modifies the state norm, impeding the coherent control over the system. With a general instantaneous representation spanned by biorthogonal ancillary bases, we develop a biorthogonal quantum-control theory for finite-dimensional systems under a general time-dependent non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. In particular, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for extracting the transitionless pathways that transport parallel in both ket and bra states. When this condition is satisfied by a set of projectors constructed with biorthogonal basis states, the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian becomes diagonal in the relevant biorthogonal subspace, enabling arbitrary initial state to evolve as a superposition of several transitionless passages. Our theory is justified by the bidirectional population transfer, a non-Hermitian holomonic quantum gate implemented in a three-level system, and chiral state conversion. For the bidirectional transfer and the holonomic gate, we can further identify the parametric constraints under which a unitary transformation is formed to link the initial and target states. As a result, the final state is automatically normalized even though the transitional dynamics is nonunitary. In population transfer, controlled gain and loss cut the required coherent pulse area, delivering shorter transfer times than the Hermitian benchmark at equal average Rabi frequency. For the chiral state conversion, we find that a closed parametric loop along opposite directions leads to distinct final state, which is irrelevant to encircling the exceptional point or not. Our work integrates the universal quantum control into the biorthogonal framework, displaying full-rank coherent control in non-Hermitian systems.
papers.authors: Chen-yi Zhang, Jun Jing

papers.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.
papers.authors: Pietro Dall'Olio, Cristian Del Gobbo, Kh\'epani Raya, Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez-Quintero

papers.title: Quantum-Walk Inspired Spectral Metrics for Evaluating QAOA Mixers
papers.abstract: QAOA mixers play an important role in enabling exploration of the exponentially large solution space of binary optimization problems. However, the choice of mixer Hamiltonian is typically guided by convention and implementation or circuit constraints, rather than by a graph-topology-aware criterion. In this work, inspired by quantum-walk mixing theory, we propose two complementary spectral heuristics for characterizing QAOA mixer topologies. The first is the normalized minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer Hamiltonian $H_M$, while the second is the long-time averaged minimum eigenvalue separation of the mixer unitary $U_M(\beta)=e^{-i\beta H_M}$. Both quantities are invariant under any positive rescaling of the mixer Hamiltonian and provide Hamiltonian- and unitary-level characterizations of the mixer's spectral structure. We use them as heuristic indicators of the mixer dynamics relevant to amplitude redistribution during QAOA evolution. We derive exact expressions and asymptotic bounds for the complete graph, hypercube, cycle, and balanced 2-D torus, revealing a broad spectral separation between the studied topology classes. We then compare these separations with empirical QAOA performance. For random permutation-invariant cost Hamiltonians, the observed performance ordering is broadly consistent with the spectral characterization. In contrast, for structured 1-D and 2-D Ising QUBOs, this ordering breaks down, indicating that mixer-cost alignment can become important. These results illustrate both the usefulness and the limitations of topology-level, cost-agnostic spectral heuristics for QAOA mixer selection.
papers.authors: Jasjyot Singh Gulati, Tharrmashastha SAPV

papers.title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
papers.abstract: The choice of mixer is central to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), yet no single structural measure captures every limitation of a shallow circuit. We study two complementary properties: configuration-space transport, which constrains probability concentration, and finite-depth causal reach, which limits the problem information available to local observables. In the transport analysis, first-order bounds in the small-$\beta$ and small-$\gamma$ regimes reduce to the same cost-weighted Dirichlet energy on connected regular mixer graphs. A non-perturbative $\ell_1$-spreading bound also gives a problem-dependent restriction on the expected objective and on the spreading required for a target approximation ratio. For MaxCut, we augment the transverse-field mixer with graph-aligned two-qubit interactions and establish a causal-radius bound of $(k+1)p$ at depth $p$. Numerical experiments at $k=1$ on cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs show higher best-found approximation ratios for $X+XX$ and $X+YY$ than for standard $X$ at equal depth. Although these augmentations have the same causal-radius bound, $X+YY$ performs better in every tested setting, highlighting the role of operator structure alongside causal reach.
papers.authors: Jasjyot Singh Gulati, Tharrmashastha SAPV

papers.title: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices
papers.abstract: We extend the generalized transfer-matrix method introduced in [H. Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Phys.\ Rev.\ B \textbf{107}, 125155 (2023)] to one-dimensional spinful non-Hermitian tight-binding lattices with matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings. We derive a minimal channel-resolved transfer matrix and identify its eigenvalues with the generalized Bloch factors. The same transfer matrix determines the periodic- and open-boundary spectra, generalized Brillouin zone, skin localization, and finite-sample scattering conditions. In the Abelian limit, the model separates into fixed spin sectors, yielding exact spectral results and closed finite-length transport expressions in terms of Chebyshev polynomials. These results reveal bipolar spin-dependent skin localization and distinguish the reciprocal hopping scale, which governs poles, zeros, and reflectionlessness, from the directed-amplification factor controlling transmission asymmetry, transparency, and invisibility. For non-Abelian gauge fields, noncommuting link matrices coherently mix the spin sectors, such that four transfer eigenmodes jointly determine the non-Bloch spectrum and transport eigenchannels. We show that this mixing produces spin-hybridized lasing and coherent-perfect-absorption channels, Zeeman-tunable lasing thresholds, and direction-dependent reflectionless transport accompanied by pronounced spin conversion. The resulting boundary-condition criteria describe lasing, coherent perfect absorption, reflectionlessness, transparency, and invisibility, while identifying spin polarization and conversion as experimentally accessible signatures that distinguish Abelian from non-Abelian non-Hermitian transport.
papers.authors: Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Janis N\"otzel

papers.title: Gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
papers.abstract: The conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free Dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the Einstein$-$Cartan theory of gravity. In spacetime with torsion, the Dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. Under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. A Dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. We use the spinor connection formalism to derive the Dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. We determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. Consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. We also derive the Einstein$-$Cartan$-$Dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.
papers.authors: Nikodem Pop{\l}awski

papers.title: Homodyne versus heterodyne detection near Gaussian states: Fraction of the quantum Fisher information recovered
papers.abstract: Homodyne and heterodyne detection are the standard measurements of an optical mode. Which of them yields more information is known only for particular tasks, with opposite answers for displacements and tomography. We compare them for every small change of a Gaussian state by their efficiency, the recovered fraction of the quantum Fisher information. We prove that near any Gaussian state of any number of modes the quantum Fisher information and the Fisher information of any Gaussian measurement are sums over the Hermite orders of the change, each term fixed by the covariance matrix and the measurement. A fixed Gaussian measurement measures no change more efficiently than the best displacement. Near a thermal state of one mode closed-form efficiencies reconcile the known comparisons, and homodyne detection at a uniformly random phase recovers at most one half, a bound raised by squeezing. Near a coherent state both detections recover exactly one half for every change of finite quantum Fisher information (the largest possible average). At the two-mode squeezed vacuum, homodyne detection of both modes at uniformly random phases is as efficient as heterodyne detection for every such change. On simulated records of one set of distant states, a likelihood-ratio observer shows a heterodyne advantage under Gaussian noise and none under loss, as the theory predicts. Under dephasing it shows none. Neural networks on reconstructed Wigner functions can show a heterodyne advantage absent from the records. For random non-Gaussian changes of up to seven photons near a thermal state the median efficiencies of both detections lie between 0.04 and 0.19, 5 to 25 times below the optimal measurement.
papers.authors: Franciszek Grzywa, Sebastian Dolata, Karol Bartkiewicz

papers.title: Magnetic billiards: duality and magnetic Radon property
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.
papers.authors: Michael (Misha), Bialy

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
papers.authors: Dean Wang

papers.title: Conditional Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
papers.abstract: Open quantum sensors work either in a transient regime with finely timed readout or in a steady-state regime with robust but weaker sensitivity. To overcome this trade-off, we ask whether repeatedly resetting a probe to a fixed state, even a suboptimal one, can outperform the optimal single-shot transient protocol. We prove that blind resets, triggered by an external clock, cannot do so even with memory. Conditional resets, triggered by the probe's own state, break this no-go result by capturing parameter-dependent quantum jumps or by recycling heralded losses, for parameters encoded in dissipative rates and Hamiltonians alike. A three-level thermometer capturing thermal excitations outperforms the optimal no-reset protocol in both transient and steady-state regimes, even with a $40\%$ preparation error. Conditional resets can even saturate the ultimate bound of nonequilibrium thermometry with a single readout. Heralded recycling enables steady-state frequency estimation to outperform optimal transient Ramsey interferometry. The advantages extend to interacting probes and to elapsed-time estimation, and both mechanisms can be realized using established experimental techniques.
papers.authors: Silan Li, Qingjun Tong, Ruicheng Bao

papers.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
papers.abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided. Moreover, we show that it is a braided module category over a suitable monoidal subcategory.
papers.authors: Liao Wang, Zbigniew Wojciechowski

papers.title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
papers.abstract: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in nitrogen-rich diamond dephase on the electron spins of the substitutional nitrogen (P1) centres. If the paramagnetic nitrogen is instead converted into NV$^-$ centres, the laser that initializes the sensor also pumps the bath into $m_s = 0$, a state with no moment along its own axis. Using cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations with a dynamical mean field, combined with an exact solver for probe-bath exchange and with no adjustable parameter, this paper asks whether such an optically polarized NV$^-$ bath dephases a sensor more slowly than a P1 bath of the same density. The answer is set by the field. In a field along [111], three quarters of the bath centres lie off the field axis, and the moment of their $m_s = 0$ state along the field grows from 0.04 at 25 G to 0.46 at 300 G and 0.81 at 800 G. At 25 G the polarized bath is therefore nearly silent: at 0.57 ppm the dephasing time $T_2^*$ of a separately addressed $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe is 112 $\mu$s, six times the 18.0 $\mu$s of a P1 bath, and still 2.4 times at 90% polarization; an ensemble measurement gains a factor of two. At 300 G the advantage over P1 shrinks to 1.4, and at 800 G the polarized bath dephases faster than P1. The field dependence of every bath, P1 included, follows the mean moment of its centres along the field. For the Hahn echo, bath relaxation ($T_1$ = 6 ms) caps the gain: a $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe in a polarized bath reaches 1.5 times the P1 value at 25 G and 1.14-1.16 times at 300 and 800 G. Driving a single $^{14}$N hyperfine line at 25 G lengthens the ensemble $T_2^*$ to 38 $\mu$s ppm, four times the experimental P1 value, implying a 3.5-12-fold dc sensitivity gain over conventional diamond with 10-30% NV$^-$ conversion. Optical polarization of an NV$^-$ bath at low field therefore offers dephasing times beyond the P1 limit of nitrogen-rich diamond.
papers.authors: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
papers.abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.
papers.authors: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez

papers.title: Single-photon time qubit: Quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time
papers.abstract: Treating the arrow of time as a controllable quantum variable rather than a fixed external parameter is a central challenge in quantum physics. Recently, Bloch~\cite{Bloch2025} proposed the theoretical concept of a \emph{time qubit}, a two-level control space $\mathcal{H}_T=\mathrm{span}\{\ket{+},\ket{-}\}$ that selects between opposite Hamiltonian evolutions $\hat{H}_{\pm}=\hat{H}_0\pm\hat{V}$, but this paradigm has remained experimentally unrealized. Here we formulate the quantum-optical theory of a single-photon time qubit---uncovering quantum-vacuum control and complementarity of the arrow of time---and experimentally probe and validate its predictions using phase-resolved single-photon interferometry from two coherently seeded entangled nonlinear biphoton sources~\cite{Lee2018,Yoon2021}. First, we show theoretically and verify experimentally that a controlled $\pi$ pump--seed phase inversion during pair creation from the quantum vacuum flips the stimulated displacement generator $\hat{V}\to -\hat{V}$ on top of the spontaneous two-mode squeezing background $\hat{H}_0$, reversing the stimulated evolution time [$\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},-}(t)=\hat{U}_{\mathrm{stim},+}(-t)$] and enabling universal single-qubit $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ control and postselection-free first-order tomography on the temporal Bloch sphere. Second, we prove that spontaneous idler vacuum fluctuations record complete which-branch (temporal-direction) information whereas the shared coherent seed erases it without cascading or aligning the idler beams, establishing an exact wave--particle complementarity law $|\bm{r}|=\mathcal{V}=|\alpha|^2/(1+|\alpha|^2)$ for the purity of the arrow of time and enabling direct first-order measurement of the Loschmidt time-reversal echo.
papers.authors: Tai Hyun Yoon

papers.title: High-cadence GW astrometry in the $\mu$Hz gap
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of a dedicated, fast-spinning astrometric survey to a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) in the microhertz gap between pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and LISA. Spinning the satellite faster samples each star more often, raising the Nyquist frequency and opening higher frequencies at no cost in noise: the shorter, noisier exposures are exactly compensated by their number, so the white-noise floor of each position stream is independent of cadence. High frequencies are where astrometry is most competitive, because the deflection measures the strain directly: its strain noise is white, whereas the equivalent noise of pulsar timing grows as $f^2$. With a cross-correlation estimator over $N$ reference stars and the astrometric overlap computed in the distant-source limit, we find that a Gaia-like satellite scanning the ecliptic poles, with $N\sim10^4$ bright stars over $10$~yr, falls short of the background measured by PTAs by a factor $\sim\!60$. A larger, $8$-m-class aperture, or a constellation of satellites covering the whole sky, reaches it, while extending the reach continuously across the $\mu$Hz band.
papers.authors: Giorgio Mentasti, Carlo Contaldi

papers.title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
papers.abstract: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation \`{a} la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.
papers.authors: Jian-Rong Li, Tomasz Przezdziecki

papers.title: Self-organizing recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field
papers.abstract: Foraging recruitment is modeled as a contagion: an agent finding a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade on the group's communication network. Because activation is degree-normalized, crowding shuts the cascade off, causing the swarm to aggregate on a resource and then disperse to explore again. Acting on the cascade moves agents in space, rewiring the network; recruitment and exploration are thus one coupled process, and removing this coupling alone abolishes self-limitation. Recruitment spreads only within a connectivity window bounded below by percolation onset and above by degree-blocking. The swarm self-organizes to the near-critical edge of this window--self-organized quasi-criticality--hovering near but below the critical point without settling onto a size-invariant critical state, with a finite-correlation-time activity spectrum (Lorentzian-like, not 1/f) consistent with local criticality. Recruitment raises harvest up to 2.7x over solitary search on sparse, clustered fields and loses (down to 0.37x) on abundant or uniform ones; because resources generically aggregate, the favourable regime is the common one. The Levy search and resource field are both least-committal: a maximum-caliber walk coupled to a maximum-entropy point process whose generic sign is clustered, with the optimal search exponent tracking the field's fractal dimension. Heavy-tailed Levy exploration crosses sparse voids while recruitment cascades exploit clusters by switching agents to short local steps, binding exploration and recruitment into a single self-organizing cycle.
papers.authors: Galen J. Wilkerson

papers.title: Optimal robust single-qubit gates in superconducting quantum processors
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires high-fidelity quantum gates that are resilient to control errors and device imperfections. Here, we develop energy-optimal control pulses for single-qubit gates that are simultaneously robust against frequency detuning and waveform inhomogeneities while also suppressing leakage outside the computational subspace. Combining the optimized pulse envelopes with an adaptive control scheme, we experimentally demonstrate optimal robust gates on a superconducting quantum processor. For a gate duration of 90ns, we achieve fidelities above 99.9% for the X gate and 99.6% for Hadamard-type gates. For the X gate, we maintain fidelities above 99.5% for simultaneous drive-amplitude variations up to 20% and qubit detuning up to 4 MHz. This robustness outperforms that of conventional Gaussian pulses by an order of magnitude, without much difference in peak gate fidelity. These results establish a route towards robust single-qubit control in large-scale quantum processors, advancing the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing.
papers.authors: Tangyou Huang, Anuj Aggarwal, Jingjun Zhu, Akshay Gaikwad, David Niepce, Marcus Rommel, Andreas Nylander, Amr Osman, Janka Bizn\'arov\'a, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, St\'ephane Gu\'erin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, Anton Frisk Kockum, Giovanna Tancredi

papers.title: Designing Robust Quantum Gates
papers.abstract: For given control channels, quantum control theory determines whether quantum gates can be realized, but not their resilience to errors. We address this problem by establishing existence criteria for robust gate implementation in $d$-level systems. Our criteria reveal that implementability of all gates is not enough: a universal family of robust gates exists if and only if, in addition, the driven Hamiltonian operators share no common symmetry. When these criteria hold, we can make every gate resilient to any combination of static perturbations, uniform Hamiltonian rescaling, perturbations at a finite set of selected frequencies, and perturbations with arbitrary selected waveforms. We can impose robustness conditions broadly with limited information about errors, e.g., against any static perturbations; we can also tailor these conditions to the platform, e.g., against environment-induced noise with dominant spectral peaks, requiring no spectral details beyond the peak frequencies. We numerically construct explicit protocols for robust gates, reducing average gate infidelity by approximately two to seven orders of magnitude under Hamiltonian perturbations and environment-induced noise. Together, our existence criteria and numerical constructions provide practical guidance for evaluating the potential of quantum platforms and designing robust quantum gates.
papers.authors: Yuanxing Hao, Marin Bukov

papers.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
papers.abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point. Direct experimental observation of the two-point functions across the exceptional point could be achieved in two hyperbolic electric circuits with a non-reciprocal coupling, through the voltage response between their edge nodes.
papers.authors: Zuo Wang, Liang He

papers.title: Thermal activation of photon catalysis in difference-intensity Mach-Zehnder interferometry with squeezed thermal light
papers.abstract: Realistic non-Gaussian operations, which can be implemented by mixing a nonclassical Gaussian state with a Fock state at a beam splitter and then heralding on a photon-number-resolving detector, are known to improve phase estimation in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The existing studies have considered the single-mode squeezed vacuum for difference-intensity and parity detection, and the two-mode squeezed thermal state for parity detection alone as the initial Gaussian resources. However, a real squeezer in the lab actually produces single-mode squeezed thermal light, which has not been studied in a coherent-plus-resource interferometer. We take up this case and using the phase space Wigner picture, we obtain the heralded state produced by photon subtraction, addition and catalysis on a single-mode squeezed thermal resource, and evaluate the corresponding phase sensitivities. Single-photon catalysis, which is useless on squeezed vacuum, becomes a useful operation for any thermal occupation above $\nth\simeq0.2$, and since it heralds with a probability near one-half, it turns out to be the best success-weighted operation over the whole thermal range. In the vacuum limit our results reproduce the known hierarchy, where two-photon catalysis is the best operation. The quantum Fisher information computations confirms that thermal noise enhances the phase information encoded in the catalyzed state, demonstrating that difference-intensity detection closely approaches the ultimate precision bound across most operational regimes, and, together with a loss analysis, verifies the robustness of the effect.
papers.authors: Kirtpreet Singh, Arvind

papers.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
papers.abstract: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.
papers.authors: David Trestini, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather

papers.title: A compact six-beam 3D magneto-optical trap based on multifunctional metasurface chips
papers.abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs), indispensable to cold-atom-based quantum computing and quantum precision measurement, are increasingly desired in compact and stable form. Particularly, the six-beam 3D-MOT, distinguished by symmetric geometry and superior trapping performance, finds particularly broad applications. Conventional implementations, however, rely on complex and bulky free-space optics, hindering miniaturization, practical assembly, and long-term stability. Here, we demonstrate a compact six-beam 3D-MOT system that employs two multifunctional optical metasurface chips to implement the optical-field functionalities required for cooling and trapping atoms. By combining two metasurface chips and a vacuum cell, a photonic-integrated cell module (PICM) is implemented as the core assembly and the volume is only" 73*73*107 mm^3" . In success, 1.3 * 10^3 Rb atoms are trapped and cooled to the temperature of ~183 {\mu}K. It should be noticed that the laser beam is guided to the metasurface through optical fiber, thus such fully fiber-coupled architecture enables straightforward and stable operations. We believe that this work would pave a practical route toward compact and portable 3D-MOT.
papers.authors: Chen Qing, Huijie Sun, Yize Liu, Yuxuan Liao, Yongzhuo Li, Dengke Zhang, Xue Feng, Yidong Huang

papers.title: Reversible Higgs Bundles
papers.abstract: We study reversible Higgs bundles on a compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g\geq 2$, that is, $G$-Higgs bundles $(E,\Phi)$ with $(E,\Phi)\cong(E,-\Phi)$. Using the non-abelian Hodge correspondence, we show that the moduli space of reversible Higgs bundles carries the structure of a real affine algebraic set. We then describe reversibility through spectral data: in even rank, for a smooth spectral curve, reversible Higgs bundles correspond to line bundles invariant under the involution $\eta\mapsto-\eta$; in odd rank, under natural genericity assumptions for which the spectral curve is nodal, we give a gluing criterion together with an explicit polystability condition. Finally, for $SL(2n,\mathbb{C})$ we construct a relative Fourier--Mukai transform over the regular locus of the Hitchin base and prove that it maps the structure sheaf of the reversible locus to an object whose support is exactly the regular degree-zero $PSp(2n,\mathbb{C})$-locus in the Langlands dual $PGL(2n,\mathbb{C})$-moduli space. This support is of type $(B,B,B)$.
papers.authors: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Tathagata Nayak

papers.title: Adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
papers.abstract: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. The Klein-Gordon equation separates into a modified Mathieu equation in time and a confining Schr\"odinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. We impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. For the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. Analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. The spectrum is algebraic rather than Planckian.
papers.authors: Victor M Villalba

papers.title: Euler's thirty-six officers need not all be entangled: real AME(4,6), families and classification
papers.abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled states of four six-level systems, AME$(4,6)$, are the quantum solutions of Euler's problem of the thirty-six officers. Until recently all reported solutions were complex, and it was conjectured that no real orthogonal 2-unitary matrix of order $36$ exists. We give real AME$(4,6)$ states with $60$ non-zero coefficients in $\{\pm1,\sqrt2\}/\sqrt{72}$. Of their thirty-six officers, $12$ are classical, as some must be whenever fewer than $72$ coefficients are non-zero. They lie in the $-1$ eigenspace of an order-$4$ local symmetry, and on their support the AME conditions become linear. We derive two closed-form families of AME$(4,6)$ states that meet at one of these states: a $10$-parameter family that is supported on $72$ basis states, and an $11$-parameter family on $60$ basis states. At each of its two ends the first family loses $12$ coefficients, and the AME states on the remaining $60$ basis states form an $11$-parameter family: the second family at one end, and an analogous family at the other. These two $60$-term families contain $4096$ real AME states up to diagonal local unitaries, $1024$ of which are limits of the first family. They fall into exactly $20$ classes under local unitaries and permutations of the parties, and we certify their separation with interval arithmetic.
papers.authors: Palash Pandya

papers.title: Bell's go theorem: regaining local causality with a new notion of realism
papers.abstract: Bell's theorem is popularly stated as the inconsistency of quantum theory with local realism. Realism is here formalized by the ontological models framework, where elements of reality are points of a measurable space and probabilities obey the Kolmogorov axioms. In the Bell scenario, locally causal ontological models posit a common cause supporting a global valuation, a joint assignment of outcomes to all measurements at once, across incompatible contexts. Within this notion of realism, Bell's theorem makes any realist explanation of the quantum predictions conspiratorial: any mechanism, whether superluminal, superdeterministic, or retrocausal, must be finely tuned so as never to manifest operationally. We redefine realism through a new ontological framework that generalizes the standard one. The elements of reality, which we call records, are no longer points but relational parts of a point-free generalization of a topological space (sublocales of a locale). A record shared by two incompatible contexts establishes the sameness of a measurement across them, without such pairwise identities composing into a global valuation, and the common cause is then a web of such records. Within this framework, Bell's no-go theorem becomes a go theorem: local causality, restated for records, is no longer at odds with the quantum statistics. This is possible because modularity, the inclusion-exclusion law of classical probability, fails across incompatible contexts, so that the probability theory generalizes Kolmogorov's. We exhibit explicit models reproducing several quantum strategies, including the optimal CHSH violation. More broadly, locally causal models of this kind attain every Bell-CHSH value up to the algebraic maximum. A realist explanation of the quantum predictions need not be conspiratorial; every causal influence posited by these models is reflected in the operational predictions.
papers.authors: Lorenzo Catani, Nesta van der Schaaf, Rui Soares Barbosa

papers.title: Analytic parity-violating greybody factors of a dynamical Chern-Simons black hole
papers.abstract: We study the low-frequency scattering of gravitational and pseudoscalar waves off a non-rotating black hole in dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) gravity, where the axial (odd-parity) gravitational sector is irreducibly coupled to the dynamical pseudoscalar while the polar sector remains general relativistic. Working to first order in the dimensionless coupling zeta = (l_CS/M)^4 and using matched asymptotic expansions, we obtain, for the quadrupole (l=2) channel, an exact closed form for the graviton-to-pseudoscalar conversion probability and a high-precision analytic reconstruction of the absorption (greybody) asymmetry. Both reduce to combinations of pi^4, pi^2, and rational numbers, with no ln2 or odd-zeta terms in the reconstructed basis; the transmission-phase sector, by contrast, is governed by an analytically derived static integral involving Apery's constant zeta(3), with its matching prefactor identified numerically. The parity-violating reflection-phase asymmetry is strongly suppressed at low frequency -- well below the parity-even general-relativistic reflection phase -- so that any polarization rotation imprinted on the reflected wave is negligible, while a subleading O(omega*zeta) asymmetry remains in the transmitted phase. These effects are intrinsically strong-field and low-frequency: the normalized flux asymmetries are consistent with a 1/(M*omega)^2 falloff in the geometric-optics limit, where the leading remaining flux effect is conversion loss. The matched-asymptotic results are checked against direct two-channel integration, and the integral determining the absorption asymmetry is evaluated to high precision within an analytically controlled transcendental basis. The coefficients provide analytic targets linking dCS parity violation in absorption and mode conversion to the axial/polar quasinormal-mode splitting.
papers.authors: Abhishek Rout (University of South Carolina)

papers.title: QuSema: Detecting Silent Bugs in Quantum Libraries via Quantum-knowledge-enhanced Agents
papers.abstract: Quantum libraries are now critical infrastructure for quantum algorithm development, yet their correctness remains difficult to test. Existing testing techniques mainly rely on failure-based or comparison-based oracles, exposing bugs only when executions fail, violate runtime checks, or disagree with another implementation. Their applicability is limited when suitable execution-based oracles are unavailable, leaving some silent bugs undetected. Such missed bugs can produce incorrect results that propagate into experimental conclusions, simulation studies, and algorithmic designs. Here we present QuSema, an autonomous testing agent for finding silent bugs in quantum libraries. QuSema uses constraints from quantum semantics and documentation as a source-level semantic oracle to assess whether implementation logic can produce invalid outputs from valid inputs. It operates through an agentic loop that repeatedly inspects library API documentation and source code, reasons about the intended behavior of quantum operations, identifies potential semantic deviations, and validates them by generating executable tests through library APIs. Guided by quantum-domain reasoning, QuSema turns high-level behavioral mismatches into concrete, user-triggerable bug reports, enabling it to uncover non-crash defects. We implement QuSema for Qiskit and PennyLane. On a benchmark of 20 historical silent bugs, QuSema achieves higher mean bug relocation counts than Claude Code and Codex, with the DeepSeek configuration costing less than Claude Code. QuSema also discovers 40 previously unknown bugs confirmed by the developers, including 30 silent bugs.
papers.authors: Yujin Song, Kaining Zhang, Qixin Zhang, Shuai Wang, Pingchuan Ma, Yuxuan Du

papers.title: Chiral Extensions of Cotangent Yangian
papers.abstract: We construct chiral extensions of the cotangent Yangian using vertex algebroids. At zero level, the construction yields a vertex algebra with a compatible coproduct, whose Zhu reduction recovers the cotangent Yangian of Abedin and Niu. We also construct vertex algebra extensions at non-zero levels and study level-additive coproducts. The zero-level vertex algebra admits two natural quasi-conformal structures. We compute the corresponding sphere one-point conformal blocks and equip each block space with an associative product induced by the coproduct. For the first quasi-conformal structure, the blocks space can be identified with the dual of a certain Lie algebroid homology; for the second, we describe the block algebra and its classical limit in terms of mini-twistor geometry.
papers.authors: Keyou Zeng

papers.title: Fault-tolerant resource estimation for ground-state preparation via Lindblad simulation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in algorithms for simulating Lindblad dynamics have clarified their theoretical potential for state preparation, but their practicality in the early fault-tolerant regime and beyond remains uncertain. In this work, we address this by investigating the cost of preparing ground states of the fermionic Hubbard model, following the single-ancilla approach of [Phys. Rev. Research 6, 033147 (2024)]. We derive rigorous error bounds including constant prefactors, and compare to empirical error behavior and practical convergence parameters obtained from circuit-level simulations. We find that empirically chosen parameters can reduce the required resources by orders of magnitude, resulting in an estimated $7.7 \times 10^8$ T gates to perform one unit of time evolution targeting the low-energy subspace of a 36-site fermionic Hubbard model. We identify the accurate filtering of energy transitions as the main source of this cost.
papers.authors: Marius Bothe, Patrick Schoepf, Nick S. Blunt

papers.title: Rounded Clocks and Finite Precision: A Transfer Principle Between Continuous and Discrete Quantum Dynamics
papers.abstract: I present a short approach to discretizing continuous unitary evolution in finite dimensions. For a time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(s)$ with $s\in[0,1]$ and an integer $T\ge1$, let $U(T)$ be the evolution of $H(t/T)$ over time $T$, and let $W_T=e^{-iH((T-1)/T)}\cdots e^{-iH(0)}$ be the product of the unitaries generated by its samples. With a half-step phase at each end, $V(T)=e^{-iH(1)/2}W_Te^{iH(0)/2}$ is the evolution generated by $H(\lfloor t+1/2\rfloor/T)$, where $\lfloor t+1/2\rfloor$ is a rounded clock, time at finite precision. Whereas Duhamel's formula only bounds $\|V(T)-U(T)\|$ by a constant, I show that $\|V(T)-U(T)\|=O(1/T)$ in operator norm, with explicit constants, whenever $H'$ is Lipschitz and every sample has eigenvalue differences at most a fixed width below $2\pi$. The gain comes from cancellation within and between time steps. This general transfer theorem assumes neither adiabaticity nor a spectral gap, and any operator-norm bound for $U(T)$ transfers to $V(T)$ with an added $O(1/T)$. Nonetheless, discrete adiabatic theorems for $W_T$ follow from continuous ones, because the end phases commute with the spectral projectors of $H(0)$ and $H(1)$. For a product of samples of a $C^2$ unitary family, a continuously moving arc of fixed length $\vartheta$ that avoids the spectrum determines a Hermitian logarithm meeting the width condition, and the $O(1/T)$ bound has coefficients $O(\vartheta^{-3})$. In the easier direction, Duhamel's formula shows that rounding the clock to midpoints and truncating the entries of a regulated time-dependent Hamiltonian at a fixed binary place gives a product within $T$ times the error of the rounded, truncated Hamiltonian.
papers.authors: Michael Jarret

papers.title: Shallow Quantum Circuits for Geometrically Local Lindblad Dynamics
papers.abstract: Open-system dynamics govern decoherence, transport, and engineered dissipation in quantum many-body systems. We propose a quantum algorithm for simulating time-independent, finite-range Lindblad dynamics with bounded local strength on a constant-dimensional lattice of $n$ sites, allowing noncommuting jump operators. For time $T\ge1$ and diamond-norm error at most $\epsilon$, it has depth $O(T\operatorname{polylog}(nT/\epsilon))$ and gate count $O(nT\operatorname{polylog}(nT/\epsilon))$. These results extend the HHKL spatial decomposition to open systems. The main obstacle is that the reversible overlap corrections used for unitary dynamics have no direct analogue for dissipative channels. We overcome this by retaining the environment in a shared unitary dilation, keeping information lost from the system coherently available and making the spatial corrections reversible. We prove exponential occupation bounds for the environmental states generated by the decomposition, allowing compact representation and coherent simulation of local factors on the inputs that arise. The construction reduces each short-time evolution to a constant number of parallel layers on regions of logarithmic diameter, using nearest-neighbour gates and polylogarithmic auxiliary density. We also prove unconditional worst-case lower bounds using time-independent, purely dissipative processes that transport quantum information. For circuits with local quantum and classical communication, the lower bounds are $\Omega(nT)$ for the expected gate count and $\Omega(T)$ for depth on time scales up to the lattice diameter. They match the upper bounds' leading time and volume dependence up to polylogarithmic factors. At fixed time and sufficiently small fixed error, we further prove a depth lower bound of $\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)$, showing that global accuracy can require increasing depth as the lattice grows.
papers.authors: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang

papers.title: From Critical Zero Modes to Interior Dynamics in Holographic Superconductors
papers.abstract: We study how the critical behavior of holographic superconductors controls the interior geometry of charged black holes. Although the exterior condensate vanishes at criticality, the critical zero mode develops logarithmic oscillations near the Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, rendering the interior critical limit nonuniform. We show that the transmitted critical-mode amplitude, together with local Cauchy-horizon quantities, fixes both the leading Einstein--Rosen collapse $\Delta z_{\rm ER}$ width and the phase $\Theta_J$ in the subsequent Josephson regime. If the condensate obeys $t\equiv1-T/T_c\propto\epsilon^{2r}$, then $\Delta z_{\rm ER}\propto t^{1/r}$ and $\Theta_J\propto t^{-1/r}$. This Josephson phase is transferred to the first Kasner epoch, producing oscillatory Kasner exponents and an accumulation law $t_n\sim n^{-r}$ for successive zeros of the scalar velocity. The critical zero mode fixes the leading collapse and phase coefficients, which are quantitatively confirmed by fully nonlinear solutions in both the ordinary and tricritical cases. At low temperature, the interior instead depends on the infrared completion of the zero-temperature geometry. Thus near-critical scaling is governed by critical-mode transmission, whereas the low-temperature behavior is controlled by the infrared endpoint.
papers.authors: Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu

papers.title: Two-center Dirac equation in a Gaussian basis set
papers.abstract: A method for solving the two-center Dirac equation using a Gaussian-product basis set tailored to the axial symmetry of diatomic systems is presented. For the ground state of H$_2^+$ at an internuclear distance $R=2.0~a_0$, we obtain a relativistic energy with relative precision at the $10^{-18}$ level. The properties of the basis set allow for an analytic Fourier transform of the wave function. As a first application we evaluate, for the first time, the zero-potential contribution to the one-loop self-energy for H$_2^+$ in Feynman and Coulomb gauges. Although this contribution is not separately gauge invariant, its calculation provides a proof of principle for the use of the present framework in prospective QED calculations.
papers.authors: D\'avid Ferenc

papers.title: Rank-One HCIZ Integrals and Multiplicative Convolutions
papers.abstract: We study how spectral averaging interacts with the logarithm in large-dimensional rank-one Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber (HCIZ) integrals. For independent bi-unitarily invariant matrices $A,B$ with uniformly bounded deterministic singular values and weakly convergent empirical spectral measures of their Gram matrices, the integral for $(BA)^*(BA)\otimes\mathbf{1}_N$ has two limiting descriptions at speed $N^2$ for small real parameters: averaging its logarithm gives free multiplicative convolution, whereas taking the logarithm after averaging gives classical multiplicative convolution. We also prove an exact finite-dimensional equality between this annealed integral and the one for $(A^*A)\otimes(B^*B)$. For any fixed $k\ge3$ factors under the hypotheses stated for $A,B$, the annealed limits at speed $N^k$ generally differ for small positive parameters, and we characterize the equality cases. For tensor products with any fixed number $k$ of factors, global Haar vectors at speed $N^k$ and product-state vectors at speed $N$ yield classical and free multiplicative convolution, respectively, for small real parameters under the corresponding hypotheses. We also derive the known multiplicativity of the $S$-transform.
papers.authors: Beno\^it Collins, Nicolas Delporte, Manasa Nagatsu, Reiko Toriumi

papers.title: Toward an Optimal Quantum Algorithm for Geometrically Local Hamiltonian Simulation
papers.abstract: Understanding the dynamics of interacting quantum systems is a central goal of quantum simulation. For geometrically local Hamiltonians, locality suggests that digital simulation should retain much of the parallelism of the underlying dynamics. For a target accuracy $\epsilon$, we construct a nearest-neighbor quantum circuit that simulates the dynamics of an $n$-qubit, time-independent, finite-range Hamiltonian with normalized local interaction strength on a fixed-dimensional lattice for time $T\ge1$, with circuit depth $O(T\log(nT/\epsilon))$ and gate count $O(nT\log(nT/\epsilon))$. This reduces the polylogarithmic overhead of Haah, Hastings, Kothari, and Low to a single logarithm. On logarithmic-scale blocks from the Lieb--Robinson decomposition, a shallow but highly accurate implementation is essential for reducing the circuit depth. Our key observation is that spatial localization also controls the cost of high precision. In each block, the error of a constant-order product formula is compensated for by a correction, yielding exponential accuracy. The correction can be implemented with depth proportional to the block diameter, introducing no additional asymptotic depth scale beyond that required by spatial localization. Furthermore, we prove an unconditional circuit-depth lower bound for uniform XXZ Hamiltonians: at fixed evolution time $T$ in the stated regime and sufficiently small fixed error $\epsilon$, any nearest-neighbor quantum circuit simulating these dynamics requires depth $\Omega(\log n/\log\log n)$. This matches our $O(\log n)$ upper bound up to a doubly logarithmic factor, establishing near-optimal circuit depth for lattice Hamiltonian simulation in this regime. Together, these results clarify the role of locality and precision in determining the circuit complexity of quantum dynamics and suggest broader principles for spatially constrained quantum computation.
papers.authors: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Penghui Yao, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang

papers.title: When the electrons go marching in: Resonances and accuracy of pairwise approximations in multiterminal Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions connect three or more superconductors through a common weak link. We quantify when their equilibrium currents admit a pairwise description. Multiterminal irreducible harmonics are energy components that depend jointly on three or more terminal phases and cannot be reduced to a sum of pair couplings. In microscopic planar-junction models, pairwise terms can capture nearly all energy variation while leaving appreciable current errors: phase differentiation amplifies the omitted harmonics. A terminal-independent Fourier projection quantifies this effect while allowing arbitrary nonsinusoidal pair couplings. Shared normal-region resonances provide a means of controlling the error. Selecting a mode from normal-state data and shifting it with a gate while retaining a frozen background reproduces the normalized error trends in the tested devices; prediction of the complete current waveform also depends on the background contribution. Finite-gap calculations retain the gate dependence at substantially lower absolute currents. An analytic single-level model supplies a sufficient detuning for pairwise accuracy. Together, these results connect normal-resonance control to a quantitative, current-based criterion for pairwise modeling.
papers.authors: A. Bar{\i}\c{s} \"Ozg\"uler

papers.title: MADGRAV: a multilevel anomaly-detection pipeline for gravitational-wave searches applied to LIGO data
papers.abstract: We present the results of \textbf{MADGRAV}, a deep-learning-based search for high-mass compact binary coalescences, applied to the data collected by the LIGO interferometers during the third observing run and during the first and second part of the fourth observing run. The \textbf{MADGRAV} pipeline consists of a series of sequential convolutional neural networks that perform anomaly detection, glitch classification, coherence testing, and signal ranking. Data from the Hanford and Livingston LIGO detectors are studied (both individually and in coherence) by way of 1 second Q-transform windows. Of the candidates that survive every stage of the pipeline, 48 reach the significance threshold, and we report 47 gravitational wave detections characterised by a false alarm rate below $1\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro}>0.9$. Of the 47 detections, 44 are shared with the minimally modelled coherent WaveBurst search. The observed total source-frame masses, extracted from official gravitational wave transient catalogues, are in the $14-236 M_{\odot}$ range with a median of $69 M_{\odot}$, and a median SNR of 16. We note that the recovered fraction of confident detections rises with mass: for LIGO detectors network SNR $>10$ the pipeline recovers $8.1\%$ of confident catalog events below $30 M_{\odot}$, $39.8\%$ between $30$ and $100 M_{\odot}$, and $53.3\%$ above $100 M_{\odot}$, corresponding to $33.3\%$, $45.5\%$ and $53.3\%$ of the events detected by coherent WaveBurst in the same bins. These results suggest that anomaly detection pipelines can serve as an independent detection channel complementary to matched filtering in the high-mass high-SNR regime.
papers.authors: Gianluca Inguglia, Huw Haigh, Ulyana Dupletsa, Alessandro Longo

papers.title: Conserved currents associated with conformal symmetry in linearized gravity
papers.abstract: Extending a previous work on the energy-momentum tensor of the linearized gravitational field in Minkowski background, conserved currents in linearized gravity associated with Lorentz transformations, dilatations and special conformal transformations are explored in the framework of Lagrangian field theory. Both outstanding special cases and general parametric families of currents are considered. Regarding the former, the distinguished energy-momentum tensor $T_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$ we found earlier, guided by similarities between linearized gravity and electrodynamics, is supplemented with an angular momentum tensor $M_{\mathrm{lg}}^{abc}$ and a dilatation current $D_{\mathrm{lg}}^a$, associated with Lorentz and dilatation symmetries. Concerning special conformal transformations, a generalization of Noether's theorem that is useful if additional conditions (such as gauge fixing conditions) are imposed is formulated, it is shown that special conformal transformations are Noether symmetries of linearized gravity in the generalized harmonic gauges, and a special conformal tensor $C_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$, accompanying $T_{\mathrm{lg}}^{ab}$, is obtained using the generalized Noether's theorem. The angular momentum tensor, dilatation current and special conformal tensor accompanying two other notable energy-momentum tensors are discussed as well. General multi-parameter families of $M^{abc}$, $D^a$ and $C^{ab}$ tensors accompanying a general family of energy-momentum tensors, which was found earlier and includes canonical energy-momentum tensors, are also determined, and local balance equations that are relevant if matter is present are derived for them. Their members do not depend on higher than first derivatives of the linearized metric.
papers.authors: Gabor Zsolt Toth

papers.title: Inverse-Designed Nanobeam Cavities for High-Cooperativity Spin-Photon Interfaces in Silicon
papers.abstract: Telecom-band spin defects in silicon offer a compelling platform for integrated quantum networks by combining scalable silicon photonics with spin-based quantum memories and multiqubit registers. The T center and recently demonstrated Al1 center are particularly promising, but their limited coherent zero-phonon emission requires strong cavity enhancement for efficient spin-photon interfaces. Here, we inverse-design silicon nanobeam cavities for both centers using a unified adjoint-optimization framework targeting Purcell enhancement, resonance alignment, and photon extraction. For each emitter, symmetric cavities maximize Purcell enhancement, while asymmetric cavities provide directional coupling to an integrated waveguide. Three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain simulations yield loaded quality factors up to 3.25 x 10^6, Purcell factors up to 7.49 x 10^5, and cooperativities of approximately 1.4 x 10^3 to 2.6 x 10^4, corresponding to cavity-coupled emission fractions exceeding 99.9%. The asymmetric cavities direct approximately 90% of emitted power into a single on-chip waveguide while maintaining cooperativity above 1.4 x 10^3. Under nanometer-scale fabrication perturbations, all four designs remain within the high-cooperativity regime, and high cooperativity persists when the cavity quality factor is constrained to a realistic absorption-limited value of 10^5. This unified, fabrication-compatible framework establishes a scalable cavity-design route for silicon telecom spin-photon interfaces and, to our knowledge, the first cavity designs for the Al1 center.
papers.authors: Nail Letty, Md Sakibul Islam, Wayesh Qarony

papers.title: Causal Query Compression for Lindblad Dynamics: Optimal Queries and Nearly Linear Local Simulation
papers.abstract: We construct a causal query compiler for time-dependent Lindblad dynamics and establish query and gate bounds under distinct input models. With coherent block encodings of the Hamiltonian and individual jump operators, a Lipschitz generator can be simulated to diamond-norm error $\varepsilon$ using $O(1+\tau+\log(1/\varepsilon)/\log(e+\log(1/\varepsilon)/\tau))$ controlled queries, where $\tau=T(\alpha_H+\sum_\mu\alpha_\mu^2)$. This bound is independent of the time-grid size and is worst-case optimal for $\tau\ge1$. Weak active entry and clean return yield a factorial history tail; combining two reuse lengths removes the auxiliary input. A three-call polar correction supplies the Lindblad cells. The compiler also characterizes the minimum oracle action of bounded adaptive Markovian protocols by quantum query complexity and the general adversary bound, up to constant factors. For finite-range dynamics on $n$ lattice sites, efficient coherent evaluation of the local matrices and fixed local parameters give $O(n(T+1)\operatorname{polylog}X)$ elementary gates, where $X=\max\{e,n(T+1)(1+K_t+B)/\varepsilon\}$, for piecewise H\"older generators with fixed exponent, local variation bound $K_t$, and at most $B$ breakpoints per term. The jumps need not commute. This gate bound includes evaluation, arithmetic, selection, routing, and environment storage. Its proof combines a spatial decomposition on a common bath, compilation on occupied inputs, and routing on compressed records. Reusing bath storage between short segments gives depth $(T+1)\operatorname{polylog}X$ and space $n\operatorname{polylog}X$.
papers.authors: Jacob Kitchen

papers.title: Reduction technique for expanding the Feynman diagrams in AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We formulate the reduction technique for expanding the $n$-point AdS Feynman diagrams in two dimensions into the Wilson line networks. The technique applies to any $n$-point tree diagram, expressing it as several series of the matrix elements of Wilson line network operators, and employs the Wilson network expansions of the $(n-1)$-point AdS$_2$ Feynman diagrams, which can in turn be obtained using the same technique. Consequently, the complexity of this technique does not increase with $n$, provided that the expansions of the $(n-1)$-point diagrams are known. To demonstrate the reduction technique, we apply it to all topologically distinct five-point AdS$_2$ Feynman tree diagrams. The resulting expansions near the conformal boundary reproduce the known decompositions of the corresponding five-point Witten diagrams into conformal blocks.
papers.authors: V. S. Khiteev

papers.title: Optical and Dynamical Signatures of Pad\'{e} Approximated Wormholes in $f(T)$ Gravity
papers.abstract: We construct traversable wormhole solutions in the linear teleparallel model $f(T) = \alpha T + \beta$, adopting Pad\'e approximants of order [1/0] and [0/1] as shape functions together with the redshift function $\Phi(r) = -M/r$, and derive the corresponding source terms from the modified field equations. We assess the physical viability of both configurations through the energy conditions, Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equilibrium, the volume integral quantifier, thin-shell junction matching to an exterior Schwarzschild geometry, embedding diagrams, proper radial distance, the gravitational energy and the active mass. We then examine the observational signatures of each geometry by analysing equatorial null geodesics and the photon-sphere structure, computing shadow maps and radial intensity profiles, ray-tracing relativistic images of a geometrically thin accretion disc, and integrating timelike rosette orbits. Finally, we study the dynamical stability of both wormholes through a third-order WKB quasinormal-mode analysis across scalar, electromagnetic, and axial gravitational perturbations, cross-checked against time-domain evolution and the eikonal photon-sphere correspondence, and examine the parameter dependence of the mode spectrum together with the possibility of trapped-mode echoes.
papers.authors: Sneha Pradhan, Paras Balani, P. K. Sahoo

papers.title: Black Holes and Scalar Propagation in Three-Dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Gravity
papers.abstract: We derive an analytic black-hole family in three-dimensional scalar--tensor Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling. A single implicit equation determines the static circular metric and a scalar linear in time. We show that these solutions exhaust regular nonextremal exteriors with the stated AdS boundary conditions and a fixed nonzero coefficient of time in the scalar. The coupled metric and scalar perturbations have one propagating degree of freedom. On one branch, its kinetic coefficient is positive, its equation is hyperbolic throughout the exterior, and its bulk spatial energy is positive for perturbations of compact support. Scalar signals can cross the metric horizon outward, so exterior evolution needs information from the interior. For linear perturbations with the original metric and scalar boundary values fixed, nonzero compact initial master displacements with zero velocity can evolve only until their first contact with the AdS boundary. We derive this restriction from the original metric and scalar equations.
papers.authors: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja

papers.title: Dynamical, thermal, and ground-state multiparameter quantum metrology: Fundamental limits and their attainability in magnetometry
papers.abstract: We study the simultaneous estimation of parameters in Hamiltonians $H_{\vec{\theta}}=H_{\vec{\theta}}^P+H^C$, with $H^C$ a control term, for unitary dynamics, thermal equilibrium, and ground states. In each case, we bound the quantum Fisher information matrix by the covariance matrix of the parameter generators, extending single-parameter bounds and identifying the conditions for saturation. At thermal equilibrium, a complementary lower bound quantifies the cost of non-commutativity. For vector magnetometry, we derive asymptotically tight bounds and identify many-body control Hamiltonians that approach them in all three settings.
papers.authors: Riccardo Pedroni, V\'ictor Izquierdo, Advay Burte, Paolo Abiuso, John Calsamiglia, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet

papers.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero
papers.authors: Jonathan Lozano-Mayo

papers.title: Unified spatiotemporal quantum states and spatiotemporal entanglement from Kirkwood-Dirac phase space
papers.abstract: The notion of a spatiotemporal quantum state extends the conventional concept of a spatial quantum state to the spatiotemporal domain. Such states are represented by unit-trace operators that encode correlations among quantum events distributed across space and time. In this work, we use the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space to provide a unified characterization of spatiotemporal quantum states. Spatiotemporal states obtained from Kirkwood-Dirac distributions are generally non-Hermitian and nonnormal; whereas those constructed from Margenau-Hill distributions are Hermitian. We provide a unification via (quasi)probabilistic mixture of Kirkwwod-Dirac spatiotemporal states which encompasses almost all existing formulations of spatiotemporal quantum states. We derive recursive expressions for spatiotemporal states and elucidate the relation between Kirkwood-Dirac nonclassicality and the temporality of spatiotemporal states. We further extend the construction to many-fold correlation functions and establish its connection with out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). We also develop a more general unifying framework based on (quasi)probabilistic mixture of $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states and establish their Petz time reversal and application in studying Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition in two-time setting. Finally, we apply this framework to characterize quantum entanglement in spacetime and analyze spatiotemporal entanglement using several complementary entropy measures.
papers.authors: Zhian Jia, Mei-Hui Xiao

papers.title: Charged Klein--Gordon modes on an Ellis wormhole: magnetic confinement and conditional Heun-polynomial solvability
papers.abstract: We study a charged Klein--Gordon field on the complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ellis wormhole, coupled to the pullback of a uniform ambient magnetic field. The induced gauge potential is regular, whereas the intrinsic magnetic pseudoscalar reverses sign across the throat. For $\alpha_B>0$, the radial operator is unitarily equivalent to a self-adjoint one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator with a smooth confining potential and discrete spectrum. The radial equation is reduced to confluent-Heun form, and polynomial solvability is shown to require two independent termination conditions. These conditions yield degree-zero Gaussian modes, degree-one states of both global parities, and representative degree-two even states. Exact Ellis-measure normalization is obtained for the degree-zero and degree-one modes. An independent fourth-order full-line finite-difference calculation validates the analytic benchmarks and determines the first eight eigenvalues and their parities. In the double-well regime, the forbidden-region action determines the leading semiclassical exponential of the even--odd level splitting.
papers.authors: Abdullah Guvendi, Omar Mustafa

papers.title: Optimal Joint Lower Bound for Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
papers.abstract: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number $\kappa$, the sparsity $s$ of the input matrix, and the target precision $\varepsilon$. The dependence on $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon$ is already well understood through the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity $s$ is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s})$ for constant error $\varepsilon$. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.
papers.authors: Dhrumil Patel

papers.title: Differential equations for Dotsenko--Fateev integrals: the case of degenerate fields $\Phi_{n,1}$
papers.abstract: We study higher-order differential equations corresponding to integrals of the Dotsenko--Fateev type and associated with four-point correlation functions with degenerate fields $\Phi_{n,1}$. We determine the general structure and coefficients of the equations in terms of the integral parameters $ \{ A,B,C,g \} $. In particular, special cases of these equations in CFT are used for verification. In addition, the relationship between higher-order differential equations and hypergeometric operators is established.
papers.authors: Aleksandra Ivanova

papers.title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the numerical geography and tangent geometry of very amply polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds $(X,H)$ through the positivity of the first jet bundle $J^1(H)$. Let $d=\int_X H^3$, $c=\int_Xc_2(X) H$, and $e=\int_X c_3(X)$. We obtain $e\ge-5d-c-c^2/(4d)$ by mixed intersections on $\mathbb{P}(J^1(H)^*)$, and $e\ge40d\left[(1-\frac{c}{10d})^{3/2}-1\right]$ by a volume estimate for a perturbed tautological class. In particular, the latter inequality shows $e+6c\ge0$, improving Sun's inequality $e+10c\ge0$. As consequences, we show (1) the uniform Hodge bounds $-4d-80\le h^{1,1}(X)-h^{2,1}(X)\le173d/66$, (2) the lower bound $\mathrm{deg} X^\vee\ge78$ for the dual hypersurface, and (3) the upper bound $d\le34$ in the critical case $X\subset\mathbb{P}^6$.
